Testing strategy taxonomy\n"},{"number":134,"text":"\n"},{"number":135,"text":"This member owns the product-assurance bounded context,\n"},{"number":136,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-assurance`, under the selected complete\n"},{"number":137,"text":"STDO basis, and within it the Product-level test-authority taxonomy.\n"},{"number":138,"text":"Module-derived unit-proof law stays owned by the design profile (the\n"},{"number":139,"text":"DESIGN_MODULE member); the shared context does not merge the two authority\n"},{"number":140,"text":"sources (P6).\n"},{"number":141,"text":"\n"},{"number":142,"text":"Every executable proof surface declares its authority source (P6). For\n"},{"number":143,"text":"ticketed work the immediate proof authority is the admitted ticket and its\n"},{"number":144,"text":"triage path: tests derive from the ticket's lawful re-entry point\n"},{"number":145,"text":"(SPEC_METHOD §4) and from the governing constitutional or realisation-law\n"},{"number":146,"text":"surfaces it cites; they never derive expected results from current\n"},{"number":147,"text":"implementation behaviour (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":148,"text":"\n"},{"number":149,"text":"Authority source is not execution breadth. A test may be small or broad,\n"},{"number":150,"text":"fast or slow, deterministic or live, and still derives from one of two\n"},{"number":151,"text":"primary authorities (P6, P1):\n"},{"number":152,"text":"\n"},{"number":153,"text":"1. design or module conformance tests; and\n"},{"number":154,"text":"2. UAT, or acceptance, tests.\n"},{"number":155,"text":"\n"},{"number":156,"text":"Design or module conformance tests derive from realisation authority: the\n"},{"number":157,"text":"governing design, module ownership, the carrier inventory the design\n"},{"number":158,"text":"declares (the design profile's irreducible architectural carrier set,\n"},{"number":159,"text":"[DESIGN_MODULE §6](DESIGN_MODULE.md#irreducible-architectural-carrier-set),\n"},{"number":160,"text":"or an equivalent), structural carrier diagrams where present, and boundary-local\n"},{"number":161,"text":"fail-closed law. They answer one question: did the implementation realise\n"},{"number":162,"text":"the module or design boundary correctly? Unit tests are design or module\n"},{"number":163,"text":"conformance tests. Module integration tests, negative tests and\n"},{"number":164,"text":"fail-closed tests may also be, when their proof target is a designed module\n"},{"number":165,"text":"boundary rather than a user scenario (P6).\n"},{"number":166,"text":"\n"},{"number":167,"text":"UAT or acceptance tests derive from constitutional user or product\n"},{"number":168,"text":"authority: requirements, acceptance criteria, declared scenarios or use\n"},{"number":169,"text":"cases, and product-level release or qualification claims. They answer one\n"},{"number":170,"text":"question: does the composed product satisfy the claimed requirement or\n"},{"number":171,"text":"scenario? (P6, P2)\n"},{"number":172,"text":"\n"},{"number":173,"text":"Under this method only sandbox tests, or an explicitly equivalent isolated\n"},{"number":174,"text":"composed-product proof lane, may be called UAT or acceptance tests. A\n"},{"number":175,"text":"sandbox test exercises the deployed, installed or otherwise runnable\n"},{"number":176,"text":"product form through declared application, public, runtime or control\n"},{"number":177,"text":"surfaces, and is driven by a requirement-sourced scenario or acceptance\n"},{"number":178,"text":"case. Direct source-level unit tests, helper tests and module integration\n"},{"number":179,"text":"tests may be valuable proof; they are not UAT and cannot close user\n"},{"number":180,"text":"acceptance by themselves (P6; EVALUATION §1, the weaker property never\n"},{"number":181,"text":"substitutes for the claimed one).\n"},{"number":182,"text":"\n"},{"number":183,"text":"Sandbox UAT has two lawful execution modes (P6, P1):\n"},{"number":184,"text":"\n"},{"number":185,"text":"- harnessed sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a\n"},{"number":186,"text":"  deterministic, fake, recorded or injected worker or result surface; and\n"},{"number":187,"text":"- live sandbox UAT exercises the full composed product path with a real\n"},{"number":188,"text":"  configured worker, tool, agent, service or other external probabilistic\n"},{"number":189,"text":"  transport where the product depends on that live boundary.\n"},{"number":190,"text":"\n"},{"number":191,"text":"Harnessed sandbox UAT proves composition, orchestration, control,\n"},{"number":192,"text":"projection, archive and scenario wiring without relying on live\n"},{"number":193,"text":"probabilistic execution; it is the lane for deterministic reproducibility.\n"},{"number":194,"text":"Live sandbox UAT proves that the same scenario can cross the real external\n"},{"number":195,"text":"probabilistic boundary and return evidence through the declared result,\n"},{"number":196,"text":"evaluation, provenance and projection surfaces. Where a product or release\n"},{"number":197,"text":"claim depends on live probabilistic compute, semantic green, unit green,\n"},{"number":198,"text":"module-integration green and harnessed-sandbox green are necessary and not\n"},{"number":199,"text":"sufficient for live acceptance (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":200,"text":"\n"},{"number":201,"text":"Terminology (P1):\n"},{"number":202,"text":"\n"},{"number":203,"text":"- `unit` names module or design conformance scope, not user acceptance;\n"},{"number":204,"text":"- `integration` names execution breadth, not authority source;\n"},{"number":205,"text":"- `sandbox` names composed-product acceptance execution;\n"},{"number":206,"text":"- `harnessed`, `fake`, `recorded` or `deterministic` name non-live sandbox\n"},{"number":207,"text":"  execution; and\n"},{"number":208,"text":"- `live` is reserved for real external worker or transport execution; a\n"},{"number":209,"text":"  status projection named \"live\" is not live UAT unless it crosses that\n"},{"number":210,"text":"  real boundary.\n"},{"number":211,"text":"\n"},{"number":212,"text":"A project that uses other local filenames or runner labels still maps each\n"},{"number":213,"text":"executable lane back to this taxonomy before claiming closure (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":214,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":235,"heading":"ASSURANCE/2. Testing strategy taxonomy/Fixture and proof portability","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F2.%20Testing%20strategy%20taxonomy%2FFixture%20and%20proof%20portability","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"840d4d0d22215aeb1215105b67825503c3a78a50074f59aeaa8282f5828d4e21","start_line":215,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":215,"text":"### Fixture and proof portability\n"},{"number":216,"text":"\n"},{"number":217,"text":"Required closure lanes are reproducible from the declared source boundary\n"},{"number":218,"text":"(P3, P6). A unit, semantic or\n"},{"number":219,"text":"module-design conformance lane does not depend on an undeclared local path,\n"},{"number":220,"text":"a sibling workspace, an operator home directory or a mutable external\n"},{"number":221,"text":"fixture.\n"},{"number":222,"text":"\n"},{"number":223,"text":"Where a proof needs external project evidence, one of these holds:\n"},{"number":224,"text":"\n"},{"number":225,"text":"- a minimal fixture is checked into the source boundary;\n"},{"number":226,"text":"- a fixture manifest declares the external source, version and\n"},{"number":227,"text":"  acquisition or binding rule; or\n"},{"number":228,"text":"- the test is classified as harnessed sandbox, live sandbox, reference\n"},{"number":229,"text":"  comparison or optional local evidence rather than required semantic\n"},{"number":230,"text":"  closure.\n"},{"number":231,"text":"\n"},{"number":232,"text":"A missing external fixture fails with a governed diagnostic that names the\n"},{"number":233,"text":"fixture authority and the lane; it never masquerades as a product semantic\n"},{"number":234,"text":"failure (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":235,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":253,"heading":"ASSURANCE/3. Test authority","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F3.%20Test%20authority","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"e3bfb8cf7bd87297081d1d952c2400239c92e767e8daf3916b8a7064fb58e0ff","start_line":236,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":236,"text":"## 3. Test authority\n"},{"number":237,"text":"\n"},{"number":238,"text":"Every live requirement has written test-case authority (P6). That authority may include scenario bundles,\n"},{"number":239,"text":"ordered test-case sequences, negative or control cases and other explicit\n"},{"number":240,"text":"evidence cases appropriate to the kind of truth being proved; it exists in\n"},{"number":241,"text":"written form and is traceable. Written authority includes the assertion\n"},{"number":242,"text":"provenance of each expected result: the owning obligation, its\n"},{"number":243,"text":"interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared dependencies, and\n"},{"number":244,"text":"whether the asserted predicate is the obligation, a necessary condition of\n"},{"number":245,"text":"it or part of a sufficient conjunction\n"},{"number":246,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation),\n"},{"number":247,"text":"[Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance))\n"},{"number":248,"text":"(P6). No live requirement is fully proved on\n"},{"number":249,"text":"informal operator confidence, ambient habit or an unlabelled test corpus\n"},{"number":250,"text":"(P6; EVALUATION §5, green labels are not acceptance). The derivation of\n"},{"number":251,"text":"each test case from admitted work authority is\n"},{"number":252,"text":"[TICKETS §7 Test case authority](TICKETS.md#test-case-authority).\n"},{"number":253,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":273,"heading":"ASSURANCE/4. Scenario bundle","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F4.%20Scenario%20bundle","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"880365198347582b4cec11f952834a984da461babb6b5b27a3b9a1f3086b7d8f","start_line":254,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":254,"text":"## 4. Scenario bundle\n"},{"number":255,"text":"\n"},{"number":256,"text":"Features are not proved by isolated assertions alone. Where a requirement\n"},{"number":257,"text":"claims meaningful system behaviour, the proving surface should be a scenario\n"},{"number":258,"text":"bundle or an equivalent ordered set of test cases that exercises that\n"},{"number":259,"text":"behaviour through a coherent sequence rather than as disconnected\n"},{"number":260,"text":"fragments (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":261,"text":"\n"},{"number":262,"text":"A scenario bundle shows the feature or use-case boundary being exercised,\n"},{"number":263,"text":"the test-case sequence that proves it, and the outcomes expected at each\n"},{"number":264,"text":"significant step. It is the layer that makes operational meaning\n"},{"number":265,"text":"inspectable (P6).\n"},{"number":266,"text":"\n"},{"number":267,"text":"Declared scenarios and use cases are not downstream decoration. They put\n"},{"number":268,"text":"pressure on feature intent and design decisions by forcing the project to\n"},{"number":269,"text":"name the real operational boundary, sequence, actors, controls and\n"},{"number":270,"text":"expected outcomes that matter. For that reason they are also the best\n"},{"number":271,"text":"source for identifying the significant code and control paths the proving\n"},{"number":272,"text":"surface must exercise (§6; P2).\n"},{"number":273,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":286,"heading":"ASSURANCE/5. Installed dev proof","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F5.%20Installed%20dev%20proof","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"9f60bd1c324d4f95b230ebc0c7c9feb9eb4034a18344eed780736817a3ef3286","start_line":274,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":274,"text":"## 5. Installed dev proof\n"},{"number":275,"text":"\n"},{"number":276,"text":"Where a system has an installable or runnable development form, the\n"},{"number":277,"text":"decisive proving lane runs against an installed development version as if\n"},{"number":278,"text":"it were an independent project or an externalised target, not only against\n"},{"number":279,"text":"the source tree in place (P6, P3). That\n"},{"number":280,"text":"proof should prefer a fresh sandbox or equivalent isolated environment, an\n"},{"number":281,"text":"installed or built development artifact, and execution through the same\n"},{"number":282,"text":"declared entry, control and runtime surfaces the real product uses. Direct\n"},{"number":283,"text":"source-level or unit-level checks may stay useful; they do not replace\n"},{"number":284,"text":"installed-dev proof of the system under test (P6; SPEC_METHOD §6 for the\n"},{"number":285,"text":"install and development-product roles).\n"},{"number":286,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":305,"heading":"ASSURANCE/6. Significant path coverage","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F6.%20Significant%20path%20coverage","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"3f9ad6ee6d16751949c0033999d06ce42614bbed8d052eec09bcac0f349c5744","start_line":287,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":287,"text":"## 6. Significant path coverage\n"},{"number":288,"text":"\n"},{"number":289,"text":"The proving surface declares and exercises the significant paths for the\n"},{"number":290,"text":"behaviour being claimed (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":291,"text":"Exhaustive proof does not mean every possible branch in every file; it\n"},{"number":292,"text":"means the project names the meaningful paths and proves them\n"},{"number":293,"text":"intentionally. The significant paths usually include, where relevant:\n"},{"number":294,"text":"\n"},{"number":295,"text":"- the intended success path;\n"},{"number":296,"text":"- the fail-closed or rejection path;\n"},{"number":297,"text":"- the boundary or control path;\n"},{"number":298,"text":"- the integration, dispatch or transport path; and\n"},{"number":299,"text":"- the recovery, retry or replay path.\n"},{"number":300,"text":"\n"},{"number":301,"text":"If the significant paths are not declared, scenario coverage cannot be\n"},{"number":302,"text":"judged. If they are declared and not exercised, the behaviour is not fully\n"},{"number":303,"text":"proved (P6; EVALUATION §1, a claim's scope cannot exceed its evaluated\n"},{"number":304,"text":"evidence).\n"},{"number":305,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":307,"heading":"ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F7.%20Product%20testing%20frame%20set","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"2c2f542f0543999afdff0d5fc7e9fe9b90ce9b82f91923bbfd8eacc06f7da98c","start_line":306,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":306,"text":"## 7. Product testing frame set/Terms","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F7.%20Product%20testing%20frame%20set%2FTerms","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"05caa3b91298d7c3f478265a0db5ad4858b630759fc9993403772b7004d172e5","start_line":308,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":308,"text":"### Terms\n"},{"number":309,"text":"\n"},{"number":310,"text":"A testing frame is a frame (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) whose evaluation executes\n"},{"number":311,"text":"or observes a declared subject to discriminate one exact claim through an\n"},{"number":312,"text":"explicit oracle, evidence population, path boundary and falsification\n"},{"number":313,"text":"condition. A test file, suite, runner, fixture, scenario label, coverage\n"},{"number":314,"text":"percentage or actor does not become a testing frame by existing. A testing\n"},{"number":315,"text":"frame's authority is bounded by the claim actually exercised; test count,\n"},{"number":316,"text":"assertion count, source coverage, runtime duration and framework category\n"},{"number":317,"text":"do not widen it (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":318,"text":"\n"},{"number":319,"text":"An authoritative Product path is the declared ordinary causal composition\n"},{"number":320,"text":"from a supported user or public entry, through the exact selected\n"},{"number":321,"text":"interfaces, owners, state transitions, effects, persistence and recovery\n"},{"number":322,"text":"boundaries, to the outcome projection the Product claim requires.\n"},{"number":323,"text":"Producing an expected output through a bypass, an obsolete executor, a\n"},{"number":324,"text":"test-only seam, an undeclared fallback or a competing authority falsifies\n"},{"number":325,"text":"path conformance even when the output value is equal (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":326,"text":"\n"},{"number":327,"text":"Material combinatorial complexity is the claim-relative population of\n"},{"number":328,"text":"independent dimensions and interactions whose combinations can change an\n"},{"number":329,"text":"outcome, violate an invariant, select another authority path or expose a\n"},{"number":330,"text":"failure. At unit altitude it includes module-owned laws, behaviour at the\n"},{"number":331,"text":"public module contract included, with their algebraic operators,\n"},{"number":332,"text":"calculation regimes, states, transitions, boundary classes and failure\n"},{"number":333,"text":"cases. Cross-participant interface, Product, persistence, configuration and\n"},{"number":334,"text":"user-role combinations belong to the integration, end-to-end or\n"},{"number":335,"text":"user-acceptance frames; they are not mocked away and counted as unit\n"},{"number":336,"text":"evidence (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":337,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":395,"heading":"ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/The set","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F7.%20Product%20testing%20frame%20set%2FThe%20set","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"832ce23dc5a0727777775763ee811f4a87627b0b6d5a09ae7b0ba3215b5461f4","start_line":338,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":338,"text":"### The set\n"},{"number":339,"text":"\n"},{"number":340,"text":"Where the governing frame configuration (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7) or the\n"},{"number":341,"text":"admitted work authority selects testing frames for a Product promotion,\n"},{"number":342,"text":"closure or release-assurance claim, testing is configured as a\n"},{"number":343,"text":"claim-relative set of testing frames. Placement in this member makes the\n"},{"number":344,"text":"set, and the law of §8 to §13 that serves it, available; it adopts nothing,\n"},{"number":345,"text":"and each activation is decided by ACTIVATION §1 (Applicability). The kind\n"},{"number":346,"text":"of runner does not select the frame; the evaluated claim, subject, path,\n"},{"number":347,"text":"population, oracle and falsification boundary do (P6, P2). Each frame's `invalidation` row,\n"},{"number":348,"text":"here and in §13, lists named instances of the material input change or\n"},{"number":349,"text":"the changed basis of\n"},{"number":350,"text":"[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); it adds no\n"},{"number":351,"text":"other kind of invalidator. The ordinary configuration holds four\n"},{"number":352,"text":"distinct frames:\n"},{"number":353,"text":"\n"},{"number":354,"text":"- user acceptance evaluates the Product outcome from the user's supported\n"},{"number":355,"text":"  frame;\n"},{"number":356,"text":"- end to end evaluates the complete runnable causal realisation of that\n"},{"number":357,"text":"  outcome;\n"},{"number":358,"text":"- integration evaluates one material composition boundary and its\n"},{"number":359,"text":"  interaction population; and\n"},{"number":360,"text":"- unit evaluates one module-owned law; internal combinatorial complexity\n"},{"number":361,"text":"  decides the proportional size and strategy of that evidence, not whether\n"},{"number":362,"text":"  the law is eligible for unit proof.\n"},{"number":363,"text":"\n"},{"number":364,"text":"They add no role, stage, authority or testing hierarchy. Their ordinary\n"},{"number":365,"text":"evidence topology assigns each claim to its congruent frame (P6, P4a):\n"},{"number":366,"text":"\n"},{"number":367,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":368,"text":"Product and accepted design\n"},{"number":369,"text":"  |- user-outcome claims -> user-acceptance frames\n"},{"number":370,"text":"  |- runnable causal-path claims -> end-to-end frames\n"},{"number":371,"text":"  |- composition-boundary claims -> integration frames\n"},{"number":372,"text":"  `- module-owned laws -> unit frames\n"},{"number":373,"text":"\n"},{"number":374,"text":"bound results -> declared conjunction -> Product or release disposition\n"},{"number":375,"text":"```\n"},{"number":376,"text":"\n"},{"number":377,"text":"The fan-out assigns claims to evidence; it is neither an authority\n"},{"number":378,"text":"hierarchy nor a claim that one frame decomposes into another. Evidence\n"},{"number":379,"text":"may relate through declared conjunction\n"},{"number":380,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),\n"},{"number":381,"text":"translation (REFERENCE_FRAME §6), falsification and re-entry (P4a). A\n"},{"number":382,"text":"broader frame cannot make a module-owned\n"},{"number":383,"text":"law true, and any number of narrower green frames cannot establish an\n"},{"number":384,"text":"unevaluated Product composition or user outcome (EVALUATION §1, the weaker\n"},{"number":385,"text":"property never substitutes for the claimed one).\n"},{"number":386,"text":"\n"},{"number":387,"text":"The frames may overlap, and one execution may supply evidence to several of\n"},{"number":388,"text":"them; every result stays bound to its own claim. A label such as `UAT`,\n"},{"number":389,"text":"`E2E`, `integration` or `unit` has no assurance value without the\n"},{"number":390,"text":"corresponding frame declaration (P1, P6). Each frame below is given in the\n"},{"number":391,"text":"shape of a frame declaration (REFERENCE_FRAME §13); \"core result\", here\n"},{"number":392,"text":"and in §13, is a value of the core result algebra of\n"},{"number":393,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), recorded with the\n"},{"number":394,"text":"predicate the frame's claim states.\n"},{"number":395,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":427,"heading":"ASSURANCE/7. Product testing frame set/User-acceptance frame","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F7.%20Product%20testing%20frame%20set%2FUser-acceptance%20frame","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"d0b1be8dcbb5d220048e90734000ff3b8a843a1fb8648f3739efb0deabac053c","start_line":396,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":396,"text":"### User-acceptance frame\n"},{"number":397,"text":"\n"},{"number":398,"text":"(P6, P2)\n"},{"number":399,"text":"\n"},{"number":400,"text":"| Frame element | User acceptance |\n"},{"number":401,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":402,"text":"| evaluation family | Can a declared user, with the user's admitted capability and information, obtain the exact Product-defined outcome through the supported ordinary Product surface? |\n"},{"number":403,"text":"| subject and basis | the exact deployed, installed or otherwise runnable Product form the claim names; current Product, requirement, UX, identity, policy and acceptance authority; the declared user role, environment, and harnessed or live sandbox mode (§2) |\n"},{"number":404,"text":"| material manifold | user goal, supported entry surfaces, permissions, inputs, Product configuration, ordinary dependencies, any declared external-worker or transport substitution boundary, user-visible state and outputs, refusal and recovery behaviour, and the acceptance interval |\n"},{"number":405,"text":"| coordinates | exact Product and artifact identity, install, user role, capability, configuration, dependency realisation, harnessed or live mode, data, workspace, invocation, time, outcome and scenario identity |\n"},{"number":406,"text":"| governing invariants | the applicable Product and requirement outcomes; supported-interface, identity, UX, safety, persistence and release law; RF-001 to RF-017; EVALUATION §1, §2, §3, §6 and §7 (proof target, evidence separation, assurance-boundary congruence, freeze and post-exposure revision, comparison, method qualification) |\n"},{"number":407,"text":"| authority | bounded evaluation only; the frame mints no Product meaning or acceptance authority, and an automated actor does not become the human or Product acceptance owner |\n"},{"number":408,"text":"| evidence | actual supported-surface requests and responses, user-visible projections, durable side effects where claimed, refusals, recovery observations, scenario records, exact-subject identity, and the declared live or substituted dependency identity |\n"},{"number":409,"text":"| capability envelope | ability to operate the Product as the declared user would, perceive the material outcome and refusal surfaces, and distinguish hidden setup or unsupported assistance |\n"},{"number":410,"text":"| exclusions | source imports, private APIs, direct Product-state injection, test-only endpoints, hidden administrator capability, undeclared fixtures or substitutes, a test double at a boundary claimed as real or live, compatibility bypasses, and internal success substituted for the user outcome |\n"},{"number":411,"text":"| result | one core result bound to the exact user-outcome claim, with witnessed paths, counterexamples, residual user populations and invalidation conditions |\n"},{"number":412,"text":"| invalidation | a material change of Product, supported interface, user role, capability, configuration, dependency or substitution mode, data contract, runnable subject, acceptance meaning or ordinary path |\n"},{"number":413,"text":"\n"},{"number":414,"text":"User acceptance is the primary Product-outcome evidence frame when the\n"},{"number":415,"text":"claim is that a user can use the Product. It may be automated only when the\n"},{"number":416,"text":"automation faithfully occupies the declared user frame and gains no path or\n"},{"number":417,"text":"capability that user lacks. Automation can execute acceptance evidence; it\n"},{"number":418,"text":"cannot assume acceptance authority (P6; EVALUATION §5).\n"},{"number":419,"text":"\n"},{"number":420,"text":"Where harnessed sandbox UAT is admitted (§2), a deterministic, fake,\n"},{"number":421,"text":"recorded or injected external worker or transport limits the result to the\n"},{"number":422,"text":"composed Product relations actually exercised; it does not prove that the\n"},{"number":423,"text":"live external boundary works. |\n"},{"number":479,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":480,"text":"| evaluation family | Does one module-owned law hold across its material combinations of algebraic operator, calculation regime, state, transition, public or private boundary class, and failure case? |\n"},{"number":481,"text":"| subject and basis | one exact module boundary, the accepted ontology and design, the active carrier inventory the design declares, module-owned requirements and public contracts, the implementation, and a module-bounded decidable oracle |\n"},{"number":482,"text":"| material manifold | module-owned public contracts, algebras, calculations, parsers, reducers, state machines, transition functions, combinators, admission predicates, conservation laws, invariants, numerical boundaries and failures |\n"},{"number":483,"text":"| coordinates | module and implementation revision, owned law, operator or function family, module state, input class, boundary class, expected relation, generated case, mutation and result identity |\n"},{"number":484,"text":"| governing invariants | the design profile's module-ownership and unit-proof law (DESIGN_MODULE); the accepted ontology, carrier inventory, domain, sequence, state, algorithm and error relations material to the module |\n"},{"number":485,"text":"| authority | bounded local evidence only; a unit result has no Product, installed, integration, user-acceptance, architecture, path-selection or release authority |\n"},{"number":486,"text":"| evidence | law-derived examples, equivalence classes, finite exhaustive cases where available, property-based or generative cases, metamorphic relations, calculation or algebra oracles, boundary cases and killed internal mutations |\n"},{"number":487,"text":"| capability envelope | competence to derive an oracle independently from the owned law, identify the module-bounded combination population, and tell an invariant violation from an implementation restatement |\n"},{"number":488,"text":"| exclusions | Product outcomes, cross-module composition, supported user paths, packaging or installation, real external participants, orchestration topology, mocked-away interface behaviour, incidental branches, private helper layout, assertion count, and source coverage used as broader assurance |\n"},{"number":489,"text":"| result | one core result limited to the exact module-owned law and the module-bounded population, with counterexamples, residual combinations and invalidation conditions |\n"},{"number":490,"text":"| invalidation | a material change of ontology, carrier inventory, module boundary, owned law, algorithm, state space, numerical regime, implementation, oracle, generator or module-bounded population |\n"},{"number":491,"text":"\n"},{"number":492,"text":"Unit testing is deliberately module-bounded. Every coded module requires\n"},{"number":493,"text":"the module-derived unit lane the design profile owns; public module\n"},{"number":494,"text":"contracts are valid unit-proof subjects. Internal combinatorial complexity\n"},{"number":495,"text":"decides the proportional size and strategy of that evidence. Its highest\n"},{"number":496,"text":"discriminating value is often in algebras, calculations, transformations,\n"},{"number":497,"text":"parsers, reducers, state machines, decision tables, admission predicates,\n"},{"number":498,"text":"conservation relations and bounded algorithms with strong independently\n"},{"number":499,"text":"derived oracles. A unit test whose oracle repeats the implementation, or\n"},{"number":500,"text":"whose cases follow incidental code branches, gives weak or circular\n"},{"number":501,"text":"evidence (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":502,"text":"\n"},{"number":503,"text":"Modules whose material complexity lies mainly in composition,\n"},{"number":504,"text":"orchestration, configuration, persistence, ownership or user interaction\n"},{"number":505,"text":"need integration, end-to-end or user-acceptance evidence at that actual\n"},{"number":506,"text":"boundary. Mocking those relations into a unit test does not turn their\n"},{"number":507,"text":"complexity into unit evidence (P6).\n"},{"number":508,"text":"\n"},{"number":509,"text":"This frame does not waive the module-derived unit lane. It binds the lane\n"},{"number":510,"text":"to module-owned law and the smallest congruent evidence population. Low\n"},{"number":511,"text":"internal combinatorial complexity justifies a small lane, not omission and\n"},{"number":512,"text":"not hundreds of implementation-shaped tests. Unit-test volume has no\n"},{"number":513,"text":"independent closure value (P2).\n"},{"number":514,"text":"\n"},{"number":515,"text":"No Product, user-outcome, installed-path, cross-module composition or\n"},{"number":516,"text":"release claim may be closed from unit evidence, whatever the test count,\n"},{"number":517,"text":"assertion count, source coverage, mutation score, runtime or historical\n"},{"number":518,"text":"pass rate. Combinatorial coverage and testing value\n"},{"number":522,"text":"\n"},{"number":523,"text":"Testing value is indexed first by the material combinations a frame can\n"},{"number":524,"text":"discriminate for its exact claim, not by test, assertion, file, line,\n"},{"number":525,"text":"branch, mock, snapshot or runner count (P2, P6). For one claim, the\n"},{"number":526,"text":"testing-value index considers at least:\n"},{"number":527,"text":"\n"},{"number":528,"text":"1. congruence between the claim and the evaluated subject;\n"},{"number":529,"text":"2. the number and materiality of independent claim dimensions;\n"},{"number":530,"text":"3. the interaction strength actually covered among those dimensions;\n"},{"number":531,"text":"4. the exactness of the authoritative path;\n"},{"number":532,"text":"5. oracle independence and precision;\n"},{"number":533,"text":"6. sensitivity to realistic faults, rival paths and historical failures;\n"},{"number":534,"text":"7. observability, reconstruction and reproducibility of the result; and\n"},{"number":535,"text":"8. explicit residual combinations and invalidation conditions.\n"},{"number":536,"text":"\n"},{"number":537,"text":"No universal scalar is required. A project may define one only through\n"},{"number":538,"text":"Product, requirement or accepted-design authority, and keeps the\n"},{"number":539,"text":"underlying coverage coordinates rather than flattening them into a score\n"},{"number":540,"text":"(P1, P6). A project-defined scalar is a quantified claim under\n"},{"number":541,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Quantified assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#quantified-assurance)\n"},{"number":542,"text":"and keeps its model and limits explicit (P6).\n"},{"number":543,"text":"\n"},{"number":544,"text":"At unit altitude the relevant dimensions are module-bounded. Unit-testing\n"},{"number":545,"text":"value normally rises with the internal combinatorial complexity of an\n"},{"number":546,"text":"algebra, calculation, state machine, transition relation or other\n"},{"number":547,"text":"module-owned closed domain, because local tests can cheaply discriminate\n"},{"number":548,"text":"many meaningful combinations against a precise oracle (P2).\n"},{"number":549,"text":"\n"},{"number":550,"text":"At integration, end-to-end and user-acceptance altitude, testing value can\n"},{"number":551,"text":"be multiplicative rather than additive: each material interface composes\n"},{"number":552,"text":"preconditions, postconditions, authority, state, configuration, failure and\n"},{"number":553,"text":"recovery with every other traversed boundary. The value comes from the\n"},{"number":554,"text":"interactions actually discriminated, not from touching many interfaces on\n"},{"number":555,"text":"one sunny path (P4a, P2). Material Product factors commonly include:\n"},{"number":556,"text":"\n"},{"number":557,"text":"- user role and capability;\n"},{"number":558,"text":"- supported operation and Product composition;\n"},{"number":559,"text":"- selected definition, owner, implementation and dependency;\n"},{"number":560,"text":"- lifecycle and persisted state;\n"},{"number":561,"text":"- configuration and version combination;\n"},{"number":562,"text":"- process, continuation, retry, re-entry and recovery mode;\n"},{"number":563,"text":"- success, refusal, malformed result, partial failure and competing-path\n"},{"number":564,"text":"  case;\n"},{"number":565,"text":"- fresh-process, replay, reconstruction and migration condition; and\n"},{"number":566,"text":"- user-visible outcome and projection.\n"},{"number":567,"text":"\n"},{"number":568,"text":"The activated frame declares the finite interaction population and why its\n"},{"number":569,"text":"covering set is adequate. Pairwise or other covering-array reduction is\n"},{"number":570,"text":"lawful only where the basis explains why the omitted higher-order\n"},{"number":571,"text":"interactions cannot change the claim, or keeps them as residuals.\n"},{"number":572,"text":"High-consequence authority, persistence, concurrency, recovery, migration\n"},{"number":573,"text":"and historically failure-prone relations normally need explicit\n"},{"number":574,"text":"higher-strength combinations (P5, P2; REFERENCE_FRAME §8, interaction and\n"},{"number":575,"text":"failure coverage).\n"},{"number":576,"text":"\n"},{"number":577,"text":"Source, line, branch and function coverage may diagnose whether code was\n"},{"number":578,"text":"visited. They do not establish semantic combination coverage,\n"},{"number":579,"text":"authoritative path selection, user-outcome coverage or the absence of a\n"},{"number":580,"text":"rival path (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":581,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":631,"heading":"ASSURANCE/9. Legitimate path and technical-debt erasure\n"},{"number":583,"text":"\n"},{"number":584,"text":"Every Product path claim needs two-sided evidence (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":585,"text":"\n"},{"number":586,"text":"1. required-path reachability: each required authoritative composition has\n"},{"number":587,"text":"   an exact witness in the deployed, installed or otherwise runnable\n"},{"number":588,"text":"   Product form through the supported ordinary path; and\n"},{"number":589,"text":"2. forbidden-path exclusion: each material superseded, duplicate,\n"},{"number":590,"text":"   fallback, bypass or otherwise forbidden production path is absent,\n"},{"number":591,"text":"   unreachable or refused at its declared boundary.\n"},{"number":592,"text":"\n"},{"number":593,"text":"A successor passing does not prove the predecessor removed. Technical-debt\n"},{"number":594,"text":"erasure evaluates two distinct, finite, subject-relative graphs (P3, P6):\n"},{"number":595,"text":"\n"},{"number":596,"text":"1. production closure: the exact deployed, installed or otherwise runnable\n"},{"number":597,"text":"   Product form and configuration, with its transitive imports, exports,\n"},{"number":598,"text":"   package paths, configuration switches, registries, fallbacks, consumers,\n"},{"number":599,"text":"   generated runtime artifacts, recovery paths and fresh-process\n"},{"number":600,"text":"   reconstruction. No obsolete, bypass, fallback or rival production path\n"},{"number":601,"text":"   may remain reachable inside this graph for the claimed scope; and\n"},{"number":602,"text":"2. assurance/source closure: the source consumers, fixtures, proof\n"},{"number":603,"text":"   scripts, generators, mutations and assurance tooling relied on for the\n"},{"number":604,"text":"   claim. No obsolete assurance consumer may falsely supply closure\n"},{"number":605,"text":"   evidence or reintroduce the removed production path into the Product\n"},{"number":606,"text":"   graph.\n"},{"number":607,"text":"\n"},{"number":608,"text":"A test-only seam is lawful when it is isolated from the Product\n"},{"number":609,"text":"distribution, excluded from ordinary-path evidence and declared in the\n"},{"number":610,"text":"assurance subject. Its presence outside the production graph is not a\n"},{"number":611,"text":"production-path failure. A retained obsolete test or proof consumer stays\n"},{"number":612,"text":"an assurance defect when it can falsely establish the claim or reintroduce\n"},{"number":613,"text":"the removed path (P6).\n"},{"number":614,"text":"\n"},{"number":615,"text":"Where proportionate and safe, assurance includes path-sensitive mutation or\n"},{"number":616,"text":"sabotage (P5, P2):\n"},{"number":617,"text":"\n"},{"number":618,"text":"- disabling the selected authoritative path prevents the Product scenario\n"},{"number":619,"text":"  from succeeding;\n"},{"number":620,"text":"- forcing or restoring a rival path causes refusal or a detected\n"},{"number":621,"text":"  counterexample rather than silent success;\n"},{"number":622,"text":"- corrupting a material interface or owner result is detected at the\n"},{"number":623,"text":"  owning boundary; and\n"},{"number":624,"text":"- removing an asserted obsolete path does not change the accepted Product\n"},{"number":625,"text":"  outcome except through the declared deletion relation.\n"},{"number":626,"text":"\n"},{"number":627,"text":"A Product outcome reached through a forbidden path is a falsified path\n"},{"number":628,"text":"claim, not a passing Product test. A negative-path test that mutates the\n"},{"number":629,"text":"exact subject without isolation, restoration and subject revalidation\n"},{"number":630,"text":"invalidates its own assurance basis (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":631,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":663,"heading":"ASSURANCE/10. Testing evidence composition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F10.%20Testing%20evidence%20composition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"e33956bece2cff81f17c9ee9cd796a80e2561745e22765664877c43723a78dc1","start_line":632,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":632,"text":"## 10. Testing evidence composition\n"},{"number":633,"text":"\n"},{"number":634,"text":"One execution may provide several bound results. A supported user scenario\n"},{"number":635,"text":"may supply user-acceptance evidence for the outcome, end-to-end evidence for\n"},{"number":636,"text":"the runnable causal path, integration evidence for selected seams and unit\n"},{"number":637,"text":"counterexamples for a module-owned algebra. Those claims stay distinct and\n"},{"number":638,"text":"combine only through the declared relations of REFERENCE_FRAME §6, whose\n"},{"number":639,"text":"result conjunction is\n"},{"number":640,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)\n"},{"number":641,"text":"(P4a, P6). Each bound result states which\n"},{"number":642,"text":"predicate it establishes; a result over a necessary condition does not\n"},{"number":643,"text":"establish the obligation, and the sufficiency of a conjunction is a claim\n"},{"number":644,"text":"of its own ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation))\n"},{"number":645,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":646,"text":"\n"},{"number":647,"text":"The default proof responsibilities are (P6, P2):\n"},{"number":648,"text":"\n"},{"number":649,"text":"- user acceptance proves the outcome from the user's supported frame;\n"},{"number":650,"text":"- end to end proves the complete authoritative runnable Product path;\n"},{"number":651,"text":"- integration proves material participant composition; and\n"},{"number":652,"text":"- unit proves module-owned laws, with evidence size and strategy\n"},{"number":653,"text":"  proportional to their internal combinatorial complexity.\n"},{"number":654,"text":"\n"},{"number":655,"text":"User acceptance alone may leave internal path singularity unevaluated.\n"},{"number":656,"text":"End-to-end success alone may leave unselected user populations or\n"},{"number":657,"text":"combinations unevaluated. Integration and unit results cannot stand in for\n"},{"number":658,"text":"either broader claim. When the Product claim requires all of them, a\n"},{"number":659,"text":"conflict or a missing result stays visible to the decision owner's\n"},{"number":660,"text":"disposition and cannot be hidden by aggregate green status (P5, P6;\n"},{"number":661,"text":"FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results, Survival; REFERENCE_FRAME §8,\n"},{"number":662,"text":"operational full coverage item 6).\n"},{"number":663,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":698,"heading":"ASSURANCE/11. Assurance subject acquisition and evaluation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F11.%20Assurance%20subject%20acquisition%20and%20evaluation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"ee207532c758bea8a1c159353626da822ba3078fdee8cc50511373616d2734c9","start_line":664,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":664,"text":"## 11. Assurance subject acquisition and evaluation\n"},{"number":665,"text":"\n"},{"number":666,"text":"Acquiring the assurance subject and evaluating it are distinct relations\n"},{"number":667,"text":"(P6, P1). Where a\n"},{"number":668,"text":"claim depends on owner-issued Product, runtime, lifecycle, admission,\n"},{"number":669,"text":"replay or projection truth, the testing frame acquires that truth through\n"},{"number":670,"text":"the exact runnable owner surface, validator, projection, receipt or\n"},{"number":671,"text":"reconstruction relation. A harness, fixture, expected-value builder, proof\n"},{"number":672,"text":"script, assurance evaluator or assessor does not reconstruct a parallel\n"},{"number":673,"text":"owner state from raw payloads, events, logs, filenames, labels or\n"},{"number":674,"text":"implementation fragments and then evaluate that self-authored state as if\n"},{"number":675,"text":"it were the Product subject. Where the acquired observation cannot\n"},{"number":676,"text":"separate two admissible subjects on which the assessed predicate takes\n"},{"number":677,"text":"opposite truth values, the frame returns further evidence, a justified\n"},{"number":678,"text":"narrower scope or `indeterminate`. The binding of the\n"},{"number":679,"text":"observation itself needs support\n"},{"number":680,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation),\n"},{"number":681,"text":"Observation sufficiency) (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":682,"text":"\n"},{"number":683,"text":"After lawful acquisition, an independently derived oracle may evaluate the\n"},{"number":684,"text":"governing claim. Generic assurance mechanics may compute bytes, digests,\n"},{"number":685,"text":"ordering, equality, set membership, completeness and conjunction over\n"},{"number":686,"text":"owner-issued evidence. Those mechanics stay evidence evaluators: they\n"},{"number":687,"text":"cannot mint owner carriers, choose the current history, select the\n"},{"number":688,"text":"authoritative path, interpret domain lifecycle or admission meaning, or\n"},{"number":689,"text":"become a runtime fallback (P6; EVALUATION §2).\n"},{"number":690,"text":"\n"},{"number":691,"text":"The rule does not require an evaluator to trust the implementation under\n"},{"number":692,"text":"test as its semantic oracle; the oracle derives from Product, requirement\n"},{"number":693,"text":"and accepted-design law. It requires the assurance subject to be the actual\n"},{"number":694,"text":"owner-issued subject rather than a second implementation of the owner's\n"},{"number":695,"text":"runtime meaning. If the required owner projection or observable seam is\n"},{"number":696,"text":"absent, the result keeps a named assurance or design gap; the proof harness\n"},{"number":697,"text":"does not fill it with rival semantics (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":698,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":740,"heading":"ASSURANCE/12. Counterexample localisation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F12.%20Counterexample%20localisation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"455d516c07b1b1b7693f6f01acc0823afb35364b24f3df5cff3594df61499fce","start_line":699,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":699,"text":"## 12. Counterexample localisation\n"},{"number":700,"text":"\n"},{"number":701,"text":"A testing counterexample is returned to its earliest supported causal\n"},{"number":702,"text":"frontier on the declared path. The frontier holds the causally minimal\n"},{"number":703,"text":"violated owner relations or seam coordinates the evidence establishes;\n"},{"number":704,"text":"earliest means minimal under the declared causal relation, not first in log\n"},{"number":705,"text":"or clock order (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":706,"text":"\n"},{"number":707,"text":"The localisation result represents exactly one of (P5, P1):\n"},{"number":708,"text":"\n"},{"number":709,"text":"- one unique violated locus;\n"},{"number":710,"text":"- a jointly established set of incomparable earliest violated loci whose\n"},{"number":711,"text":"  combined violation is necessary to the supported causal explanation;\n"},{"number":712,"text":"- unresolved alternative frontiers, when the evidence supports several\n"},{"number":713,"text":"  possible causal explanations but cannot establish which occurred; or\n"},{"number":714,"text":"- `indeterminate`, when the evidence cannot support a bounded frontier.\n"},{"number":715,"text":"\n"},{"number":716,"text":"The four forms are a refinement of the core under the rule of\n"},{"number":717,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), for the predicate \"the\n"},{"number":718,"text":"evidence establishes the counterexample's earliest violated loci on the\n"},{"number":719,"text":"declared path\". One unique violated locus and a jointly established set\n"},{"number":720,"text":"map to `satisfied`. Unresolved alternative frontiers map to\n"},{"number":721,"text":"`indeterminate`, naming the alternatives that further evidence must\n"},{"number":722,"text":"decide between. The fourth form is the core value `indeterminate` itself,\n"},{"number":723,"text":"naming the evidence a bounded frontier needs. The form travels with the\n"},{"number":724,"text":"value as the domain outcome, so a joint set stays distinct from a unique\n"},{"number":725,"text":"locus and unresolved alternatives stay distinct from an unbounded\n"},{"number":726,"text":"frontier. Purpose and material relation: a localisation combines with\n"},{"number":727,"text":"other results in the one core, and an unresolved causal explanation is\n"},{"number":728,"text":"never read as an established one (P5, P1, P6).\n"},{"number":729,"text":"\n"},{"number":730,"text":"Localisation records the subject, basis, frontier form and members, causal\n"},{"number":731,"text":"evidence, expected relations, the observed counterexample and the\n"},{"number":732,"text":"downstream claims it invalidates. It does not collapse a jointly\n"},{"number":733,"text":"established set into one arbitrary owner, and it does not report\n"},{"number":734,"text":"unresolved alternatives as a joint cause (P5, P4b).\n"},{"number":735,"text":"\n"},{"number":736,"text":"A localised frontier does not itself authorise broader test expansion,\n"},{"number":737,"text":"compatibility repair, another controller or a reinterpretation of unchanged\n"},{"number":738,"text":"upstream meaning. A resulting scope or design change follows the existing\n"},{"number":739,"text":"re-entry relation (SPEC_METHOD §4; P6).\n"},{"number":740,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":768,"heading":"ASSURANCE/13. End-to-end interface integration frame","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F13.%20End-to-end%20interface%20integration%20frame","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"af91b246fee17c377b87678eed734420d09cb76292c9fff47e352eeb084a552d","start_line":741,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":741,"text":"## 13. End-to-end interface integration frame\n"},{"number":742,"text":"\n"},{"number":743,"text":"`urn:stdo:reference-frame:end-to-end-interface-integration:v1` is a\n"},{"number":744,"text":"composite refinement whose identity resolves in\n"},{"number":745,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation` (owned by\n"},{"number":746,"text":"REFERENCE_FRAME) under the exact selected basis; its assurance law is\n"},{"number":747,"text":"stated here. It relates the evaluation of public boundaries, design,\n"},{"number":748,"text":"operators, owners and proof to the integration, end-to-end and\n"},{"number":749,"text":"user-acceptance frames of §7. Like the set, it is available and is\n"},{"number":750,"text":"activated only where the governing frame configuration or admitted work\n"},{"number":751,"text":"authority selects it. It adds no fifth testing type, role or\n"},{"number":752,"text":"universal activation gate (P2, P3).\n"},{"number":753,"text":"\n"},{"number":754,"text":"| Frame element | End-to-end interface integration |\n"},{"number":755,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":756,"text":"| evaluation family | Does one outcome stay constructable, understandable and correctly realised across its material interface chain, with sufficient participant context and conserved meaning, authority and cause? |\n"},{"number":757,"text":"| subject and basis | one Product outcome and an independently stated oracle; the governing requirements and design basis, exact source or workspace checkpoint, contracts and finite case population; for design claims, the declared participant roles, functional path, dependencies, configuration and capabilities; for claims over their realisation, the actual participants, callable selection, supported entry and exit, and the exact runnable artifact or install |\n"},{"number":758,"text":"| material manifold | the producers, consumers, transformations and effect owners, as declared for design claims or actually selected for realised claims; at each material seam, the functional preconditions and postconditions, value and reference domains, lifecycle and time, supplied context, mutable subject, refusals, observations and user-visible result |\n"},{"number":759,"text":"| coordinates and equality | distinct Product, artifact or install, workspace, observation, invocation, candidate, admitted result and evidence identities; exact revisions, domain, units, cardinality, ordering, empty, null or default meaning and validity interval; equal shape or output implies no equal meaning, provenance or authority |\n"},{"number":760,"text":"| governing invariants | the selected Product, requirement, design and interface law; REFERENCE_FRAME declaration and translation law; the conjunction of results of FOUNDATIONS §4; the claim boundaries and obligations below; the existing testing and assurance owners keep their laws |\n"},{"number":761,"text":"| authority | existing owners keep semantic, operation, admission and reserved decision authority; the activation grants bounded evaluation, with construction only under its existing exact operation grant; the declared decision consumer disposes the closed result |\n"},{"number":762,"text":"| evidence | source-linked contracts and both selected sides; for design claims, design relations and explicitly unresolved realisation facts; for claims over realised relations, the actual supplied request, context and response, callable and configuration identity, owner validation, effect and observation records and the ordinary caller's outcome; independently derived expected relations and disclosed substitution limits |\n"},{"number":763,"text":"| capability envelope | competence in the outcome, functional composition, domain and lifecycle semantics, participant capabilities and causal diagnosis; sufficient access to the exact subject and evidence without altering a reviewed subject; required independence stays claim-relative |\n"},{"number":764,"text":"| exclusions | hidden context or privilege, rival contract truth, inferred authority, undeclared substitutes, private or test-only paths for ordinary-path claims, candidate output treated as admission, fixture success treated as real user evidence, and unsupported whole-Product or all-future-case conclusions |\n"},{"number":765,"text":"| result and relations | each activated claim returns a core result with its exact evidence, coverage, causal findings and residuals; shared evidence is referenced once; mandatory claims compose only through a declared same-basis or lawful-translation conjunction (FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results) to the named decision consumer |\n"},{"number":766,"text":"| invalidation | a material change of contract, domain, participant, prompt or context, capability, callable path, configuration, translation, relevant workspace observation, lifecycle, oracle or evidence population invalidates the affected conclusions; unchanged valid evidence and owner rulings stay reusable |\n"},{"number":767,"text":"| qualification | the representative sensitivity and refusal cases below, bound to actual subjects, actor envelopes and independently stated expected relations; mechanical source checks supply no semantic or live-user qualification |\n"},{"number":768,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":794,"heading":"ASSURANCE/13. End-to-end interface integration frame/Claim boundaries","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F13.%20End-to-end%20interface%20integration%20frame%2FClaim%20boundaries","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"06b949af1e9ade0fafd33d24fdd628095b878659f1ec67661273bf323de52f7a","start_line":769,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":769,"text":"### Claim boundaries\n"},{"number":770,"text":"\n"},{"number":771,"text":"(P6, P1)\n"},{"number":772,"text":"\n"},{"number":773,"text":"| Claim | Evaluation and evidence boundary |\n"},{"number":774,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":775,"text":"| contract sufficiency | Can each participant determine and perform its responsibility from the declared interface and the available context? Source-grounded design evaluation may establish this claim without an implemented runtime; unresolved realisability or actor-context questions stay explicit. |\n"},{"number":776,"text":"| boundary congruence | Do the actual selected producers, transformations and consumers preserve the declared domains, meanings, lifecycle and authority? An actual-composition claim acquires both sides and their exchanges; design correspondence alone proves no implementation behaviour. |\n"},{"number":777,"text":"| path realisation | Does the exact runnable subject use the authoritative entry-to-outcome path through its material state, effect and observation boundaries? Matching output through another path is insufficient. |\n"},{"number":778,"text":"| user usability | Can the ordinary human, LLM or software caller obtain the selected outcome using only its declared context, access and supported surface? Internal success or validator-aware fixtures cannot establish this claim. |\n"},{"number":779,"text":"\n"},{"number":780,"text":"The activation selects claims from the work's applicability (ACTIVATION §1)\n"},{"number":781,"text":"and states the scope reason for each unselected claim; an unselected claim\n"},{"number":782,"text":"has no result. Design-only work\n"},{"number":783,"text":"does not require unavailable runtime evidence and does not report runtime or\n"},{"number":784,"text":"UAT satisfaction. An unknown material condition keeps its dependent claim\n"},{"number":785,"text":"unresolved: the claim's result is never `satisfied` and names the\n"},{"number":786,"text":"condition as what would decide it\n"},{"number":787,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Standing); omission\n"},{"number":788,"text":"cannot close it. A full end-to-end usability claim\n"},{"number":789,"text":"needs all four distinct results and their explicit conjunction\n"},{"number":790,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),\n"},{"number":791,"text":"in which an unselected claim is uncovered coverage. Transport,\n"},{"number":792,"text":"parse, admission, semantic satisfaction, operation completion and user\n"},{"number":793,"text":"success are not interchangeable (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":794,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":878,"heading":"ASSURANCE/13. End-to-end interface integration frame/Obligations","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F13.%20End-to-end%20interface%20integration%20frame%2FObligations","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"acd561b6405cce59325d2da8e142e34ae81923053bc02fe6581dc92cc7708f32","start_line":795,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":795,"text":"### Obligations\n"},{"number":796,"text":"\n"},{"number":797,"text":"Existing truth surfaces are reused. The working record adds only missing\n"},{"number":798,"text":"cross-interface relations; schemas, prompts, adapters, indexes and tests do\n"},{"number":799,"text":"not become another contract owner (P6, P2). For each material seam:\n"},{"number":800,"text":"\n"},{"number":801,"text":"1. Bind the functional input domain, producer success postconditions,\n"},{"number":802,"text":"   consumer preconditions, permitted effects, refusals and observable exit.\n"},{"number":803,"text":"   Direct successful handoff requires the producer's guarantees to meet the\n"},{"number":804,"text":"   consumer's preconditions. An interface may instead emit candidates:\n"},{"number":805,"text":"   candidate output, later admission and semantic assessment stay distinct\n"},{"number":806,"text":"   declared stages. A normal model refusal or an inadmissible candidate does\n"},{"number":807,"text":"   not by itself falsify an adequately declared candidate interface; the\n"},{"number":808,"text":"   exact promised outcome and refusal behaviour are evaluated (P4a, P5).\n"},{"number":809,"text":"2. Make material actor obligations and domains available through the\n"},{"number":810,"text":"   actual interface or context, or through an exact locator the actor can\n"},{"number":811,"text":"   lawfully resolve. Bind the LLM role, instructions, supplied context,\n"},{"number":812,"text":"   tools and model or transport configuration where material. Generic\n"},{"number":813,"text":"   governance access does not replace the Product-specific contract or\n"},{"number":814,"text":"   authorise inference of hidden validator rules. Existing deterministic\n"},{"number":815,"text":"   owners compute the available facts and expose their owned relation to\n"},{"number":816,"text":"   context and validation by reuse or a proven equivalent projection.\n"},{"number":817,"text":"   Semantic actors judge meaning within that domain; reserved owner\n"},{"number":818,"text":"   rulings, eligibility, authority and admission are not inferred from an\n"},{"number":819,"text":"   actor response or a frame label (P0, P6, P1).\n"},{"number":820,"text":"3. Preserve domain and temporal meaning through serialisation, parsing,\n"},{"number":821,"text":"   normalisation and adaptation. A lawful translation binds source and\n"},{"number":822,"text":"   target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance,\n"},{"number":823,"text":"   governing owner and refusal conditions. Distinguish proposed, admitted,\n"},{"number":824,"text":"   assessed and completed states; active input from historical context;\n"},{"number":825,"text":"   current validity from mere byte availability. Equal wire shape is no\n"},{"number":826,"text":"   translation proof (P1, P3; REFERENCE_FRAME §6).\n"},{"number":827,"text":"4. Observe the relevant current mutable workspace for each later\n"},{"number":828,"text":"   operation, and bind that observation separately from immutable\n"},{"number":829,"text":"   authority, artifacts, history and prior candidates. Changed support\n"},{"number":830,"text":"   invalidates dependent conclusions; unaffected accepted work stays\n"},{"number":831,"text":"   reusable. A snapshot does not replace the current subject, and a change\n"},{"number":832,"text":"   of actor alone is no reason to repeat still-valid work (P3, P4b;\n"},{"number":833,"text":"   ACTIVATION §7).\n"},{"number":834,"text":"5. Follow the actual callable path and the existing effect owners through\n"},{"number":835,"text":"   the selected exit and any required fresh observation. A hidden fallback,\n"},{"number":836,"text":"   state injection, manually repaired output, private entry or undeclared\n"},{"number":837,"text":"   retry cannot support an ordinary real-path claim. A pure function\n"},{"number":838,"text":"   acquires no new event lifecycle because this frame evaluates it (P6,\n"},{"number":839,"text":"   P3).\n"},{"number":840,"text":"6. Preserve diagnostic cause through wrappers and projections. Apply §12:\n"},{"number":841,"text":"   report the supported causal frontier, not merely the first log or clock\n"},{"number":842,"text":"   occurrence. Keep the originating seam, bounded field or path, expected\n"},{"number":843,"text":"   domain or basis, observed mismatch and evidence locator where available,\n"},{"number":844,"text":"   with downstream symptoms, successful work and the declared continuation\n"},{"number":845,"text":"   or block. Preserve joint causes, alternative frontiers and\n"},{"number":846,"text":"   indeterminacy; do not invent a unique cause. Product redaction rules\n"},{"number":847,"text":"   still govern sensitive content. Missing required diagnostic evidence\n"},{"number":848,"text":"   stays a named gap. Return the smallest supported owner or re-entry;\n"},{"number":849,"text":"   diagnosis grants no repair or retry (P5, P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":850,"text":"\n"},{"number":851,"text":"Evidence acquisition follows §11: owner facts are acquired through existing\n"},{"number":852,"text":"surfaces and evaluated with an independent contract-derived oracle.\n"},{"number":853,"text":"Computed facts, contextual judgments and reserved owner rulings keep their\n"},{"number":854,"text":"distinct owners and validity scopes (P6).\n"},{"number":855,"text":"\n"},{"number":856,"text":"For an LLM-interface usability claim, clean-room LLM UAT is used, with the\n"},{"number":857,"text":"ordinary supplied context and permitted tools and without private\n"},{"number":858,"text":"implementation knowledge or fixture assistance. Expected outcomes are\n"},{"number":859,"text":"recorded before responses are inspected. The sunny case and the ordinary\n"},{"number":860,"text":"ambiguity and negative cases material to the claim are included.\n"},{"number":861,"text":"Substitutes are disclosed; replayed or fabricated responses prove only\n"},{"number":862,"text":"their stated narrower relation, not live-provider usability. Responses are\n"},{"number":863,"text":"not edited, and nothing is silently retried until green. Live claims need\n"},{"number":864,"text":"live evidence under §2, not a new universal live-provider requirement\n"},{"number":865,"text":"during design (P6, P5; EVALUATION §3, expectations before exposure).\n"},{"number":866,"text":"\n"},{"number":867,"text":"An early sunny thread can establish bounded evidence while the unexercised\n"},{"number":868,"text":"claims stay open (the sequencing heuristic of SPEC_METHOD §8). This frame\n"},{"number":869,"text":"adds no exhaustive-hardening prerequisite, scenario quota, controller,\n"},{"number":870,"text":"runtime, generator, routine human approval, new ledger or automatic extra\n"},{"number":871,"text":"agent. Existing authority selects proportionate assurance and any further\n"},{"number":872,"text":"operation. The result returns, for each of the four claims, its core\n"},{"number":873,"text":"result or the scope reason it was not selected, the exact\n"},{"number":874,"text":"exercised subject and path, the supported mismatch, retained work,\n"},{"number":875,"text":"substitutions, residuals and invalidators in the existing work carrier; it\n"},{"number":876,"text":"is neither acceptance nor a grant of the next action (P2, P6; ACTIVATION\n"},{"number":877,"text":"§6).\n"},{"number":878,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":901,"heading":"ASSURANCE/13. End-to-end interface integration frame/Computational whole-path evaluation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F13.%20End-to-end%20interface%20integration%20frame%2FComputational%20whole-path%20evaluation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"b97655fda5851b36606b5cc4f22bb74a88a59f1fd7971c1a6c74f5d02f8df71a","start_line":879,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":879,"text":"### Computational whole-path evaluation\n"},{"number":880,"text":"\n"},{"number":881,"text":"For material computational composition or recurrence work, the selected\n"},{"number":882,"text":"interface claims are composed with evaluations of the path's operators,\n"},{"number":883,"text":"owners, reused foundations and proof, to evaluate one complete\n"},{"number":884,"text":"producer-to-consumer path under the design profile's computational\n"},{"number":885,"text":"realisation and recurrence law (DESIGN_MODULE). The evaluation binds fact\n"},{"number":886,"text":"establishment, each consumer, validity and invalidation, effects, retained\n"},{"number":887,"text":"alternatives and accumulated work. It evaluates equivalent computation\n"},{"number":888,"text":"across different domain names without assuming semantic equivalence.\n"},{"number":889,"text":"Qualification challenges the design's declared workload and operational\n"},{"number":890,"text":"assumptions, and preserves the independent scope, freshness and effect\n"},{"number":891,"text":"checks that serve distinct supported obligations (P4a, P1, P2).\n"},{"number":892,"text":"\n"},{"number":893,"text":"An identifiable complete-path result and its evidence return to the\n"},{"number":894,"text":"declared decision consumer; a collection of local successes cannot replace\n"},{"number":895,"text":"that result. Design-only evidence establishes only the design claim; claims\n"},{"number":896,"text":"about actual work need observations on the selected path. Valid unchanged\n"},{"number":897,"text":"results are reused, and affected reassessment is activated on a material\n"},{"number":898,"text":"change of path, basis or workload. This is a bounded composition of\n"},{"number":899,"text":"existing frames, not a permanent actor, an extra frame family, a per-helper\n"},{"number":900,"text":"review or a separate accounting ledger (P4b, P2).\n"},{"number":901,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":921,"heading":"ASSURANCE/13. Each selected\n"},{"number":906,"text":"case binds its own exact subject, oracle, evidence and claim scope (P6,\n"},{"number":907,"text":"P5; EVALUATION §7).\n"},{"number":908,"text":"\n"},{"number":909,"text":"| Case | Required discrimination |\n"},{"number":910,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":911,"text":"| empty and non-empty eligible domains | Ordinary context makes both domains usable; a universal empty-value workaround cannot replace the governing domain. A hidden required rule defeats contract sufficiency even when the validator correctly refuses. |\n"},{"number":912,"text":"| adequate candidate contract and rejected response | Legitimate refusal or admission filtering is told apart from an inadequate interface or a violated success guarantee; model variability alone is no frame failure. |\n"},{"number":913,"text":"| same-response or historical-only reference | Eligibility and lifecycle come from the owning domain; available or equal-looking references are not automatically current admissible inputs. |\n"},{"number":914,"text":"| individually valid but temporally mismatched carriers | Different observations or admission states can falsify boundary congruence despite matching shapes. |\n"},{"number":915,"text":"| meaning-changing translation | Loss of units, default, identity or ordering is detected against the independent outcome oracle, even when both shapes validate. |\n"},{"number":916,"text":"| fixture knows a hidden rule | Mechanical success leaves user usability unproved; it cannot hide missing ordinary actor context. |\n"},{"number":917,"text":"| expected output through a forbidden path | Path realisation is falsified; equal output does not discharge the actual-path obligation. |\n"},{"number":918,"text":"| changed workspace and reusable accepted work | Affected context and dependent evidence are refreshed while unaffected valid work is kept; history does not stand in for the current subject. |\n"},{"number":919,"text":"| wrapped or ambiguous failure | The supported originating causal frontier and its uncertainty are kept, not replaced by a downstream symptom or an invented unique cause. |\n"},{"number":920,"text":"| design-only sufficient contract | A bounded contract result can close while runtime and user claims stay unclaimed or unresolved according to their applicability; no runtime or UAT satisfaction is inferred. |\n"},{"number":921,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1013,"heading":"ASSURANCE/14.
