Design-to-module evidence route\n"},{"number":923,"text":"\n"},{"number":924,"text":"For a new or materially changed realisation boundary governed by a design\n"},{"number":925,"text":"profile (DESIGN_MODULE, tier 3, whose binding of the objects named here is\n"},{"number":926,"text":"declared in that profile), the canonical evidence relation is (P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":927,"text":"\n"},{"number":928,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":929,"text":"constitutional WHAT and owning requirements\n"},{"number":930,"text":"  -> accepted ontology, the carrier inventory the design declares,\n"},{"number":931,"text":"     target design, and the design's domain, sequence and state evidence\n"},{"number":932,"text":"  -> implementation and module-derived unit tests\n"},{"number":933,"text":"  -> reconciliation and acceptance\n"},{"number":934,"text":"  -> promotion and design-method closure\n"},{"number":935,"text":"\n"},{"number":936,"text":"implementation and module-derived unit tests\n"},{"number":937,"text":"  -> evidence, counterexample or falsification input\n"},{"number":938,"text":"  -> affected ontology or design relation\n"},{"number":939,"text":"```\n"},{"number":940,"text":"\n"},{"number":941,"text":"The first chain is semantic derivation. The second is evidence feedback\n"},{"number":942,"text":"and cannot select or accept the affected semantic answer (P6). The two\n"},{"number":943,"text":"chains are this member's instance of parallel derivation: expected results\n"},{"number":944,"text":"carry assertion provenance from the first chain and executions carry\n"},{"number":945,"text":"execution provenance from the second; agreement between them is\n"},{"number":946,"text":"compatible with a shared error, and disagreement requires diagnosis\n"},{"number":947,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance))\n"},{"number":948,"text":"(P6, P1). When the\n"},{"number":949,"text":"design's co-evolution condition holds, the two chains may proceed together\n"},{"number":950,"text":"without making implementation semantic authority; design still owns the\n"},{"number":951,"text":"structural HOW. Where the design is not decision-complete, the relation is\n"},{"number":952,"text":"design-gated at the smallest causally closed affected decision set and\n"},{"number":953,"text":"retained implementation follows its acceptance. An unchanged\n"},{"number":954,"text":"`realization_refactor` (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes) cites the accepted\n"},{"number":955,"text":"relation and proves no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not\n"},{"number":956,"text":"recreate the evidence (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":957,"text":"\n"},{"number":958,"text":"Where construction is probabilistic or agentic, the execution relation of\n"},{"number":959,"text":"ACTIVATION §1 governs the handoff from this accepted design basis into\n"},{"number":960,"text":"bounded construction, assessment, disposition, checkpoint and\n"},{"number":961,"text":"continuation. The design profile supplies the governing-frame,\n"},{"number":962,"text":"transformation-admission, invariant-reconstruction,\n"},{"number":963,"text":"computational-realisation and module evidence that relation consumes; it\n"},{"number":964,"text":"does not define a second execution protocol (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":965,"text":"\n"},{"number":966,"text":"Completeness requires (P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":967,"text":"\n"},{"number":968,"text":"- the final implementation is traceable to the accepted ontology;\n"},{"number":969,"text":"- the final implementation is traceable to design and module boundary\n"},{"number":970,"text":"  assets;\n"},{"number":971,"text":"- unit tests are traceable to module ownership, not only to helper\n"},{"number":972,"text":"  layout;\n"},{"number":973,"text":"- implementation-first discoveries are reconciled into the ontology and\n"},{"number":974,"text":"  the design's domain, sequence and state evidence before promotion or\n"},{"number":975,"text":"  closure; and\n"},{"number":976,"text":"- implementation may not compensate for an unrealised declared\n"},{"number":977,"text":"  constructor by introducing a hidden controller or alternative authority\n"},{"number":978,"text":"  path.\n"},{"number":979,"text":"\n"},{"number":980,"text":"Unit tests may be discovered from implementation behaviour, but the\n"},{"number":981,"text":"closure proof is re-expressed against module ownership rather than code\n"},{"number":982,"text":"helper shape. The module boundary is the intermediate reasoning surface\n"},{"number":983,"text":"that lets implementation and unit tests be audited against the same\n"},{"number":984,"text":"ownership cut; it does not outrank constitutional truth or ratified design\n"},{"number":985,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":986,"text":"\n"},{"number":987,"text":"The minimum complete evidence chain is (P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":988,"text":"\n"},{"number":989,"text":"1. constitutional WHAT;\n"},{"number":990,"text":"2. accepted ontology;\n"},{"number":991,"text":"3. target design;\n"},{"number":992,"text":"4. target module boundary assets and the ontology-derived carrier\n"},{"number":993,"text":"   inventory;\n"},{"number":994,"text":"5. accepted domain, sequence and state projections with axiom evaluation;\n"},{"number":995,"text":"6. implementation; and\n"},{"number":996,"text":"7. unit tests derived from the same ontology and module boundary.\n"},{"number":997,"text":"\n"},{"number":998,"text":"Where a reference realisation exists, the complete evidence chain becomes\n"},{"number":999,"text":"(P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":1000,"text":"\n"},{"number":1001,"text":"1. constitutional WHAT;\n"},{"number":1002,"text":"2. reference design;\n"},{"number":1003,"text":"3. accepted target ontology and reference-to-ontology mapping;\n"},{"number":1004,"text":"4. target design mapping;\n"},{"number":1005,"text":"5. target module boundary assets and the ontology-derived carrier\n"},{"number":1006,"text":"   inventory;\n"},{"number":1007,"text":"6. accepted domain, sequence and state projections with axiom evaluation;\n"},{"number":1008,"text":"   and\n"},{"number":1009,"text":"7. implementation and unit tests derived from the same ontology.\n"},{"number":1010,"text":"\n"},{"number":1011,"text":"If a change jumps from design or code straight to tests and never\n"},{"number":1012,"text":"reconstructs the module boundary, the proof surface is too weak (P6).\n"},{"number":1013,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1051,"heading":"ASSURANCE/15. Module-derived unit tests","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F15.%20Module-derived%20unit%20tests","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"0a500dfbf4f849a7426c968485c490120a067242e3cdc52a29097fd7ede028cd","start_line":1014,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":1014,"text":"## 15. Module-derived unit tests\n"},{"number":1015,"text":"\n"},{"number":1016,"text":"Within the product-assurance bounded context of §2, the two authority\n"},{"number":1017,"text":"sources stay distinct: the module-derived unit test and its proof relation\n"},{"number":1018,"text":"derive from realisation authority, which the design profile owns\n"},{"number":1019,"text":"(DESIGN_MODULE), and this section states that relation so both sources sit\n"},{"number":1020,"text":"in one member; that ownership does not extend to Product-level UAT or\n"},{"number":1021,"text":"acceptance meaning, which stays with Product authority under §2 (P6).\n"},{"number":1022,"text":"\n"},{"number":1023,"text":"Unit tests under the design profile are module-owned proof lanes. They\n"},{"number":1024,"text":"derive from module ownership evidence, not from code shape alone. A unit\n"},{"number":1025,"text":"test should be traceable to (P6, P2):\n"},{"number":1026,"text":"\n"},{"number":1027,"text":"- the accepted ontology and the applicable entity, lifecycle, authority,\n"},{"number":1028,"text":"  function, effect or projection law;\n"},{"number":1029,"text":"- the governing module design;\n"},{"number":1030,"text":"- the active carrier inventory the design declares, or an equivalent\n"},{"number":1031,"text":"  carrier inventory;\n"},{"number":1032,"text":"- the module-bounded domain, sequence and state projections; and\n"},{"number":1033,"text":"- the requirement families the module owns.\n"},{"number":1034,"text":"\n"},{"number":1035,"text":"Unit tests are not authored primarily from helper function boundaries,\n"},{"number":1036,"text":"private method layout, incidental branch structure, temporary\n"},{"number":1037,"text":"implementation decomposition, or mock convenience that hides the real\n"},{"number":1038,"text":"module contract. The required question is not \"what functions exist to\n"},{"number":1039,"text":"test?\" but \"what does this module own, and what proof does that ownership\n"},{"number":1040,"text":"require?\" This does not prohibit helper-level tests; it prohibits\n"},{"number":1041,"text":"helper-level tests from becoming the canonical proof surface for a module\n"},{"number":1042,"text":"boundary (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":1043,"text":"\n"},{"number":1044,"text":"Canonical rule (P6): module-owned unit tests are authoritative for module\n"},{"number":1045,"text":"proof; broader integration, scenario and sandbox lanes remain downstream\n"},{"number":1046,"text":"proof families; transitional slice-gating tests may exist, but they do not\n"},{"number":1047,"text":"replace module-derived unit proof. If a module has code but no\n"},{"number":1048,"text":"module-derived unit test lane, the module is not closure-ready under the\n"},{"number":1049,"text":"design profile. What such a lane claims, and what it never closes, is\n"},{"number":1050,"text":"the unit frame of §7.\n"},{"number":1051,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1099,"heading":"ASSURANCE/16. Module lifecycle confirmation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md#ASSURANCE%2F16.%20Module%20lifecycle%20confirmation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","sha256":"de8510483651ae24131201e42a022a66054ab6e0ae0f8e4543780097893c419d","start_line":1052,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ASSURANCE.md","lines":[{"number":1052,"text":"## 16. Module lifecycle confirmation\n"},{"number":1053,"text":"\n"},{"number":1054,"text":"Every designed module, function, application surface, runtime surface,\n"},{"number":1055,"text":"plugin surface, public interface, data surface, and published function or\n"},{"number":1056,"text":"module of a profile exists inside an operational lifecycle. Under the\n"},{"number":1057,"text":"design profile that lifecycle signal is confirmed at the realisation\n"},{"number":1058,"text":"boundary before design-method closure (P2, P6). The\n"},{"number":1059,"text":"canonical operational lifecycle chain is SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational\n"},{"number":1060,"text":"lifecycle sufficiency; this section consumes that chain and does not\n"},{"number":1061,"text":"redefine its phases. The checklist is not a release plan and does not\n"},{"number":1062,"text":"replace RELEASE; it is an ambiguity detector for ultimate intended use.\n"},{"number":1063,"text":"\n"},{"number":1064,"text":"For each governed boundary, the design evidence states, or points to a\n"},{"number":1065,"text":"surface that states (P6, P5):\n"},{"number":1066,"text":"\n"},{"number":1067,"text":"- the upstream intent and requirement authority;\n"},{"number":1068,"text":"- the build or realisation surface;\n"},{"number":1069,"text":"- the assurance and proof surface;\n"},{"number":1070,"text":"- the release or packaging posture;\n"},{"number":1071,"text":"- the deployment or install posture;\n"},{"number":1072,"text":"- the live usage or invocation posture;\n"},{"number":1073,"text":"- the observed telemetry, projection or monitoring posture;\n"},{"number":1074,"text":"- the retirement, revocation, supersession or decommission posture; and\n"},{"number":1075,"text":"- the owner, source truth and authority boundary for the lifecycle\n"},{"number":1076,"text":"  decisions.\n"},{"number":1077,"text":"\n"},{"number":1078,"text":"Each lifecycle phase takes one of the three answers that\n"},{"number":1079,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §2 Operational lifecycle sufficiency](SPEC_METHOD.md#operational-lifecycle-sufficiency)\n"},{"number":1080,"text":"owns, applied here to design evidence: answered by the active design,\n"},{"number":1081,"text":"requirement, release, deployment or telemetry surface; declared not\n"},{"number":1082,"text":"applicable with a reason; or recorded as a named `Gap:` or `Unanswered:`\n"},{"number":1083,"text":"item, which in design evidence also names its owning follow-up. A phase\n"},{"number":1084,"text":"list without answers, not-applicable reasons or named gaps is not\n"},{"number":1085,"text":"design-method evidence (P5, P6). The three are declared states of the\n"},{"number":1086,"text":"design evidence for a phase under that section, not result values; a\n"},{"number":1087,"text":"named gap is a residual\n"},{"number":1088,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology)) that remains until its\n"},{"number":1089,"text":"owning follow-up disposes it (P4b, P5).\n"},{"number":1090,"text":"\n"},{"number":1091,"text":"Implementation proves the selected lifecycle path only within the\n"},{"number":1092,"text":"authority it owns. Code, tests, generated artifacts or runtime fixtures may\n"},{"number":1093,"text":"confirm that a lifecycle claim is real, but they may not invent lifecycle\n"},{"number":1094,"text":"authority that the product, requirements, design, release or operational\n"},{"number":1095,"text":"surface did not declare (P6). If the checklist exposes missing release,\n"},{"number":1096,"text":"deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement truth, the module may still\n"},{"number":1097,"text":"proceed only when that gap is explicitly governed; it may not close by\n"},{"number":1098,"text":"relying on local convention, implementation precedent, mutable runtime\n"},{"number":1099,"text":"state, prompt prose or test-only fixture behaviour (P6, P5).\n"}]},{"end_line":15,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","sha256":"b23761fb783cdd92dd10a6288ae8a6afb9341fc583a745f7d3f1e7f69710f9f8","start_line":1,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","lines":[{"number":1,"text":"# AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS\n"},{"number":2,"text":"\n"},{"number":3,"text":"Tier 1. Owns the a_c theory in full: position and scope, the signature,\n"},{"number":4,"text":"the typed records, the laws AC-001 to AC-020, traversals and functor\n"},{"number":5,"text":"kinds, interpretation and models, the three governed layers, the law of\n"},{"number":6,"text":"calculus identity, the application boundary, external imports, exclusions\n"},{"number":7,"text":"and the conformance obligations of this member. Consumes the ontology of\n"},{"number":8,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md) (subject, representation, interpretation,\n"},{"number":9,"text":"context, object, claim, evidence, judgment, authority, residual, basis,\n"},{"number":10,"text":"material) and the core result algebra of\n"},{"number":11,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results); it states laws over\n"},{"number":12,"text":"those objects and defines none of them a second time. Each clause names\n"},{"number":13,"text":"the principle (P0 to P6) that requires it, as\n"},{"number":14,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §1](FOUNDATIONS.md#1-vocabulary-of-standing) requires.\n"},{"number":15,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":58,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/1. Position\n"},{"number":17,"text":"\n"},{"number":18,"text":"The STDO Axiomatic Calculus for Governed Symbolic Systems, written `a_c`,\n"},{"number":19,"text":"is this method's domain-specific, carrier-neutral constitutional calculus\n"},{"number":20,"text":"for representing and relating governed symbolic systems. Its stable\n"},{"number":21,"text":"concept identity is `urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:a-c`. This member\n"},{"number":22,"text":"owns that concept in the bounded context\n"},{"number":23,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:axiomatic-calculus`. Both identifiers are\n"},{"number":24,"text":"declared identities and do not change with the carrier or the directory\n"},{"number":25,"text":"that publishes them (P3).\n"},{"number":26,"text":"\n"},{"number":27,"text":"`a_c` is a separately identifiable calculus derived from the method's\n"},{"number":28,"text":"principles. It defines sorts, typed objects, relations, constraints,\n"},{"number":29,"text":"latitude, residual uncertainty, traversals, functor kinds, judgments,\n"},{"number":30,"text":"closure, projections, transformations, models and validity laws. Those\n"},{"number":31,"text":"definitions depend on no derivation-source record layout, no selected\n"},{"number":32,"text":"subject interpretation, no particular carrier, no model provider, no\n"},{"number":33,"text":"runtime and no repository topology (P1, P2).\n"},{"number":34,"text":"\n"},{"number":35,"text":"`a_c` claims no universal applicability, logical completeness,\n"},{"number":36,"text":"consistency, decidability, soundness or category-theoretic status except\n"},{"number":37,"text":"where an exact, separately identified proof establishes that claim for a\n"},{"number":38,"text":"declared fragment, model or relation; for category-theoretic status that\n"},{"number":39,"text":"proof is the demonstration of\n"},{"number":40,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra), Formal fragment (P6).\n"},{"number":41,"text":"\n"},{"number":42,"text":"The principles are the derivation provenance of the calculus. Application\n"},{"number":43,"text":"of the calculus to any exact subject is a separately owned downstream\n"},{"number":44,"text":"relation. The relations are distinct (P3, P6):\n"},{"number":45,"text":"\n"},{"number":46,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":47,"text":"exact local governing principles             -> derive    -> a_c\n"},{"number":48,"text":"a_c + exact subject X                        -> interpret -> a_c.X\n"},{"number":49,"text":"a_c.X + exact accepted semantic judgment J_X\n"},{"number":50,"text":"      + exact carrier C                      -> encode    -> a_c.X.C\n"},{"number":51,"text":"```\n"},{"number":52,"text":"\n"},{"number":53,"text":"The calculus, an interpreted model and an encoded carrier are distinct\n"},{"number":54,"text":"governed layers with separate content identities and proof boundaries\n"},{"number":55,"text":"(§7). A layer becomes a released Product only through separately\n"},{"number":56,"text":"authorised Product acceptance and release. Neither interpretation nor\n"},{"number":57,"text":"encoding can redefine the calculus (P6).\n"},{"number":58,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":129,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/1. (P6):\n"},{"number":64,"text":"\n"},{"number":65,"text":"- scoped identity and authority conservation:\n"},{"number":66,"text":"  [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology), Signature","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F2.%20Signature","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","sha256":"5e74619ee1056913c0c8d9dc17c0462f4a0203e462da50000b93c3d2754b16a7","start_line":220,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","lines":[{"number":220,"text":"## 2. Signature\n"},{"number":221,"text":"\n"},{"number":222,"text":"An `a_c` signature is (P3, P1):\n"},{"number":223,"text":"\n"},{"number":224,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":225,"text":"Sigma = (\n"},{"number":226,"text":"  RecordKind,\n"},{"number":227,"text":"  Sort,\n"},{"number":228,"text":"  RelationKind,\n"},{"number":229,"text":"  ConstraintKind,\n"},{"number":230,"text":"  ResidualKind,\n"},{"number":231,"text":"  FunctorKind,\n"},{"number":232,"text":"  JudgmentKind,\n"},{"number":233,"text":"  StopKind\n"},{"number":234,"text":")\n"},{"number":235,"text":"```\n"},{"number":236,"text":"\n"},{"number":237,"text":"`a_c` fixes this finite core record-kind set:\n"},{"number":238,"text":"\n"},{"number":239,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":240,"text":"RecordKind_ac = {\n"},{"number":241,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:semantic-object,\n"},{"number":242,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:typed-relation,\n"},{"number":243,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:constraint,\n"},{"number":244,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:latitude,\n"},{"number":245,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:residual,\n"},{"number":246,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:traversal,\n"},{"number":247,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:transformation,\n"},{"number":248,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:judgment\n"},{"number":249,"text":"}\n"},{"number":250,"text":"```\n"},{"number":251,"text":"\n"},{"number":252,"text":"Every `a_c` signature imports those identities unchanged. A model-family\n"},{"number":253,"text":"signature specialises their fields, value domains, reference domains and\n"},{"number":254,"text":"admissible kinds; it does not remove, rename, shadow or silently add a\n"},{"number":255,"text":"core record family. Another fundamental record family requires an explicit\n"},{"number":256,"text":"compatible calculus extension, never an extra subject sort (P3).\n"},{"number":257,"text":"\n"},{"number":258,"text":"Every signature member is a finite, closed identity set for one model\n"},{"number":259,"text":"family. The signature defines:\n"},{"number":260,"text":"\n"},{"number":261,"text":"- the fields and value domains of every sort and record family;\n"},{"number":262,"text":"- the reference domain and cardinality of every identity-bearing field;\n"},{"number":263,"text":"- the allowed source and target sorts for every relation kind;\n"},{"number":264,"text":"- the subject and predicate domains of every constraint kind;\n"},{"number":265,"text":"- the subject, uncertainty, consequence and re-entry domains of every\n"},{"number":266,"text":"  residual kind;\n"},{"number":267,"text":"- the input, output, evidence and stop contract of every judgment kind;\n"},{"number":268,"text":"  and\n"},{"number":269,"text":"- the functor kinds permitted for each traversal.\n"},{"number":270,"text":"\n"},{"number":271,"text":"Unknown kinds and fields are not extensions. They require a new signature\n"},{"number":272,"text":"or an explicit compatible extension relation (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":273,"text":"\n"},{"number":274,"text":"An `a_c` model over exact basis `b` is:\n"},{"number":275,"text":"\n"},{"number":276,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":277,"text":"M_b = (b, I, O, E, C, L, X, V, T, J)\n"},{"number":278,"text":"\n"},{"number":279,"text":"Population_M = {\n"},{"number":280,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:semantic-object  -> O,\n"},{"number":281,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:typed-relation  -> E,\n"},{"number":282,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:constraint      -> C,\n"},{"number":283,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:latitude        -> L,\n"},{"number":284,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:residual        -> X,\n"},{"number":285,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:traversal       -> V,\n"},{"number":286,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:transformation  -> T,\n"},{"number":287,"text":"  urn:stdo:concept:axiomatic-calculus:record-kind:judgment        -> J\n"},{"number":288,"text":"}\n"},{"number":289,"text":"```\n"},{"number":290,"text":"\n"},{"number":291,"text":"where `I` is the closed identity universe; `O` the finite set of typed\n"},{"number":292,"text":"semantic objects; `E` the finite set of typed directed relations; `C` the\n"},{"number":293,"text":"finite set of constitutional constraints; `L` the finite set of declared\n"},{"number":294,"text":"latitude records; `X` the finite set of residual uncertainty records; `V`\n"},{"number":295,"text":"the finite set of traversal records; `T` the finite set of transformation\n"},{"number":296,"text":"records; and `J` the finite set of judgment records.\n"},{"number":297,"text":"\n"},{"number":298,"text":"`Population_M` is a total function over `RecordKind_ac`. Every population\n"},{"number":299,"text":"is finite, every fundamental record belongs to exactly one population, and\n"},{"number":300,"text":"record identities are unique across their disjoint union. Let `Local_M` be\n"},{"number":301,"text":"that union. Then `I = Local_M disjoint_union External_M`, where every\n"},{"number":302,"text":"member of `External_M` is admitted only through one signature-declared\n"},{"number":303,"text":"external reference domain and exact resolution relation. A hidden record,\n"},{"number":304,"text":"an unpopulated extra record family, an identity occurring in two\n"},{"number":305,"text":"populations, or an identity in `I` with neither one local record nor one\n"},{"number":306,"text":"lawful external resolution refuses the model. A population may be empty\n"},{"number":307,"text":"only when the selected signature does not require a member of that record\n"},{"number":308,"text":"kind (P3, P5).\n"},{"number":309,"text":"\n"},{"number":310,"text":"The signature declares a finite reference-domain function:\n"},{"number":311,"text":"\n"},{"number":312,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":313,"text":"RefDomain_Sigma(record_kind, field)\n"},{"number":314,"text":"  -> (cardinality,\n"},{"number":315,"text":"      allowed_local_record_kinds,\n"},{"number":316,"text":"      allowed_semantic_object_sorts,\n"},{"number":317,"text":"      allowed_external_target_kinds,\n"},{"number":318,"text":"      required_basis_relation)\n"},{"number":319,"text":"```\n"},{"number":320,"text":"\n"},{"number":321,"text":"Every scalar or collection member that carries an identity reference is\n"},{"number":322,"text":"checked through that function. A local reference resolves across the exact\n"},{"number":323,"text":"`Population_M` family named by its target record kind; a reference to a\n"},{"number":324,"text":"semantic object also satisfies the declared target sort. An external\n"},{"number":325,"text":"reference resolves through exactly one declared external target kind and\n"},{"number":326,"text":"basis relation. No reference may resolve both locally and externally.\n"},{"number":327,"text":"Missing field domains, wrong-family targets, wrong-sort targets, ambiguous\n"},{"number":328,"text":"targets and dangling external identities refuse structural admission (P3,\n"},{"number":329,"text":"P6).\n"},{"number":330,"text":"\n"},{"number":331,"text":"The tuple is abstract. A carrier may use records, tables, terms, clauses,\n"},{"number":332,"text":"code or any other representation only when its encoding profile proves\n"},{"number":333,"text":"that every tuple relation is preserved or explicitly refused (P1, P4b).\n"},{"number":334,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":346,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/3. Typed records\n"},{"number":336,"text":"\n"},{"number":337,"text":"The following subsections define the exact shapes of five of the eight\n"},{"number":338,"text":"core record families. `SemanticObject`, `TypedRelation`, `Constraint`,\n"},{"number":339,"text":"`Latitude` and `Residual` populate `O`, `E`, `C`, `L` and `X`. The\n"},{"number":340,"text":"traversal record (§5), the transformation record (AC-013) and the judgment\n"},{"number":341,"text":"record (AC-014) populate `V`, `T` and `J`. A traversal, transformation or\n"},{"number":342,"text":"judgment is not placed in `O` merely by reifying its name as a semantic\n"},{"number":343,"text":"object. A subject model may independently represent the concept of a\n"},{"number":344,"text":"record kind, but that representation does not satisfy the core population\n"},{"number":345,"text":"law (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":346,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":368,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/3. It remains represented, is explicitly dispositioned by competent\n"},{"number":464,"text":"authority, or causes refusal (P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":465,"text":"\n"},{"number":466,"text":"`kind` resolves one declared `ResidualKind`. Its coordinates map to that\n"},{"number":491,"text":"identity as follows: the owner is the identity's authority, the type is\n"},{"number":492,"text":"its kind, and the member it resolves is what its value denotes; context,\n"},{"number":493,"text":"scope and basis are further coordinates, which IDENTITY §2 permits and\n"},{"number":494,"text":"`a_c` requires.
