It\n"},{"number":1365,"text":"selects, constructs, accepts or releases no concrete interpretation or\n"},{"number":1366,"text":"carrier. A downstream authority owns its exact subject population,\n"},{"number":1367,"text":"interpretation, carrier, judgments and Product or release status. The\n"},{"number":1368,"text":"downstream identity is never embedded back into the calculus or its\n"},{"number":1369,"text":"publication basis (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1370,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1379,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/9. Application boundary, imports and exclusions/External imports and specialisations","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F9.%20Application%20boundary%2C%20imports%20and%20exclusions%2FExternal%20imports%20and%20specialisations","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","sha256":"8e7a6b7aa5a17e7b5635565bab41e74ac02be928136ca661a7759a742b8f0234","start_line":1371,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","lines":[{"number":1371,"text":"### External imports and specialisations\n"},{"number":1372,"text":"\n"},{"number":1373,"text":"An application may declare a typed import, translation or specialisation\n"},{"number":1374,"text":"of an `a_c` concept under that application's own exact authority, context,\n"},{"number":1375,"text":"basis, scope, preservation, loss, refusal and invalidation law. Such a\n"},{"number":1376,"text":"relation is external to the calculus. It neither changes `a_c` nor enters\n"},{"number":1377,"text":"this member by being useful to an application (P6, P2). PROFILES §1 states the same\n"},{"number":1378,"text":"rule from the profile's side as the declared-binding rule.\n"},{"number":1379,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1464,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/9. Application boundary, imports and exclusions/Constraint surfaces","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS%2F9.%20Application%20boundary%2C%20imports%20and%20exclusions%2FConstraint%20surfaces","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","sha256":"d27b24dd5175339d053f718c4d9b1cd6348bc57d928559c8c6ba16573446fc78","start_line":1380,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","lines":[{"number":1380,"text":"### Constraint surfaces\n"},{"number":1381,"text":"\n"},{"number":1382,"text":"A constraint surface states, for a declared subject and work boundary,\n"},{"number":1383,"text":"the obligations and the permitted freedom of the work: its objects and\n"},{"number":1384,"text":"their meanings, the predicates and dependencies that bear on it, the\n"},{"number":1385,"text":"admissible operations, the required results, the authority, the evidence\n"},{"number":1386,"text":"and the conditions still unresolved. It constrains the work without\n"},{"number":1387,"text":"prescribing the worker's internal solution strategy beyond those\n"},{"number":1388,"text":"obligations (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1389,"text":"\n"},{"number":1390,"text":"An interpretation of a subject in `a_c` (§6) yields the constraint surface\n"},{"number":1391,"text":"of a task by projection. The task's declared subject and work boundary\n"},{"number":1392,"text":"are the seed set `Z`, with the dependency relation family `R` the task\n"},{"number":1393,"text":"declares, and the surface is `project(M_subject, Z, R)` (AC-011) over the\n"},{"number":1394,"text":"material closure of AC-010. Its parts come from the records of this\n"},{"number":1395,"text":"member:\n"},{"number":1396,"text":"\n"},{"number":1397,"text":"| Part of the surface | Records and laws that supply it |\n"},{"number":1398,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":1399,"text":"| objects and meanings | the semantic objects of `M_Z` (§3), with identity under AC-002 and provenance under AC-017 |\n"},{"number":1400,"text":"| predicates and dependencies | the constraints (§3, AC-007) and typed relations (AC-004) in the closure; a premise shared by several constraints is one record, and the closure imposes no tree shape and no execution order |\n"},{"number":1401,"text":"| admissible operations | the traversals and transformations in the closure (§5, AC-013), each with its preconditions and operation authority |\n"},{"number":1402,"text":"| required results | each constraint's judgment kind and its outcomes, mapped to the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) under AC-007 |\n"},{"number":1403,"text":"| permitted freedom | the latitude records (AC-008); what no obligation fixes and a latitude admits is the worker's choice |\n"},{"number":1404,"text":"| authority | the authority each record retains (AC-005); the surface grants none |\n"},{"number":1405,"text":"| evidence | the judgments (AC-014) and the evidence, provenance and basis coordinates of the records (AC-006) |\n"},{"number":1406,"text":"| unresolved conditions | the residuals in the closure (AC-009) and the seams recorded in `Boundary_Z` (AC-011) |\n"},{"number":1407,"text":"\n"},{"number":1408,"text":"Conditions on its use:\n"},{"number":1409,"text":"\n"},{"number":1410,"text":"1. **Standing kept.** Each element keeps the standing the interpretation\n"},{"number":1411,"text":"   records for it: premise, derived consequence, policy choice,\n"},{"number":1412,"text":"   observation or unresolved claim. A policy choice keeps its owner, and a\n"},{"number":1413,"text":"   preference is never read as an obligation. An element of the\n"},{"number":1414,"text":"   construction or assurance relations also keeps the kind of support\n"},{"number":1415,"text":"   the interpretation records for it, one of the five that\n"},{"number":1416,"text":"   [FOUNDATIONS §4 Formal representation](FOUNDATIONS.md#formal-representation)\n"},{"number":1417,"text":"   distinguishes: a stated formula is not read as discharged, and an\n"},{"number":1418,"text":"   externally assessed predicate keeps the source, scope and evidence\n"},{"number":1419,"text":"   that establish it.\n"},{"number":1420,"text":"2. **Unresolved blocks.** A residual, a `hold`, a `gap` or an external\n"},{"number":1421,"text":"   predicate not yet established keeps its source and its required\n"},{"number":1422,"text":"   acquisition, and it blocks every operation and result that depends on\n"},{"number":1423,"text":"   it until its premise is established. A missing premise or an omitted\n"},{"number":1424,"text":"   obligation never becomes permission or a satisfied result (AC-007,\n"},{"number":1425,"text":"   AC-009).\n"},{"number":1426,"text":"3. **Routes, not observations.** The surface carries the constraints and\n"},{"number":1427,"text":"   the acquisition routes of the material inputs the task needs. It\n"},{"number":1428,"text":"   supplies no observation, effect grant or task context: a step acquires\n"},{"number":1429,"text":"   those from the workspace and its selected authoritative inputs, at the\n"},{"number":1430,"text":"   acquisition step of\n"},{"number":1431,"text":"   [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),\n"},{"number":1432,"text":"   which is where a step uses a surface. The workspace stays the basis for\n"},{"number":1433,"text":"   reacquisition.\n"},{"number":1434,"text":"4. **Exact subject and basis.** The surface binds the exact subject the\n"},{"number":1435,"text":"   interpretation represents and, as a separate coordinate, the calculus\n"},{"number":1436,"text":"   basis and signature used to represent it. A projection from an\n"},{"number":1437,"text":"   interpretation bound to other subject bytes, or whose basis is not\n"},{"number":1438,"text":"   established, returns `refusal(basis)`, which is `invalid_basis` (AC-006,\n"},{"number":1439,"text":"   AC-011).\n"},{"number":1440,"text":"5. **A derived view.** The surface is a derived view of the owning prose,\n"},{"number":1441,"text":"   not a second owner. A surface that changes the permitted or required\n"},{"number":1442,"text":"   work is a fidelity defect (AC-017), repaired at the source or the\n"},{"number":1443,"text":"   derivation that caused it. An approximate surface declares its\n"},{"number":1444,"text":"   adequacy relation and its end-to-end bound.\n"},{"number":1445,"text":"6. **Separate claims.** Structural validity of a surface is a structural\n"},{"number":1446,"text":"   claim that a checker may decide (AC-019); its fidelity is a semantic\n"},{"number":1447,"text":"   judgment ([EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation), AC-018); its\n"},{"number":1448,"text":"   sufficiency for a task is shown only by actual use\n"},{"number":1449,"text":"   ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)). A mechanical\n"},{"number":1450,"text":"   projection runs only under a separately selected checking contract.\n"},{"number":1451,"text":"   None of these claims grants operation or acceptance authority.\n"},{"number":1452,"text":"\n"},{"number":1453,"text":"This section states how any interpretation yields a surface; under the\n"},{"number":1454,"text":"Application boundary above it selects, constructs and accepts no\n"},{"number":1455,"text":"interpretation. The downstream authority of a subject owns its\n"},{"number":1456,"text":"interpretation and which interpretation is current. Ordinary entry\n"},{"number":1457,"text":"selects the current exact interpretation with its limits, and an earlier\n"},{"number":1458,"text":"interpretation is identified as historical. Purpose and material\n"},{"number":1459,"text":"relation: an actor has to recover the constraints of one task within\n"},{"number":1460,"text":"finite context and attention (P0, P2); the surface carries them from\n"},{"number":1461,"text":"their owners with their dependencies, freedom and open conditions, so\n"},{"number":1462,"text":"the actor neither loads the whole model nor loses an uncertainty (P4b,\n"},{"number":1463,"text":"P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1464,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1479,"heading":"AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS/9. Conformance obligations\n"},{"number":1481,"text":"\n"},{"number":1482,"text":"Review and qualification of this member cover at least (P6):\n"},{"number":1483,"text":"\n"},{"number":1484,"text":"1. closed signature, `RecordKind_ac`, population, field, value-domain and\n"},{"number":1485,"text":"   reference-domain definitions;\n"},{"number":1486,"text":"2. well-typed positive and refusal examples for every fundamental law;\n"},{"number":1487,"text":"3. identity uniqueness and cross-context collision cases;\n"},{"number":1488,"text":"4. closure, projection, overlay, transformation and composition laws,\n"},{"number":1489,"text":"   including exact model identities, population partitions, basis\n"},{"number":1490,"text":"   equality, and byte-or-typed-equality preservation refusal;\n"},{"number":1491,"text":"5. strict separation of domain operations, functor kinds, actors and\n"},{"number":1492,"text":"   judgments;\n"},{"number":1493,"text":"6. residual and authority conservation through interpretation and\n"},{"number":1494,"text":"   encoding;\n"},{"number":1495,"text":"7. exact calculus-basis identity reconstruction;\n"},{"number":1496,"text":"8. direct-coordinate, cross-family reference, wrong-family,\n"},{"number":1497,"text":"   duplicate-family and dangling-reference refusal cases for every\n"},{"number":1498,"text":"   fundamental record family;\n"},{"number":1499,"text":"9. derivation-basis and publication-basis reconstruction with cyclic and\n"},{"number":1500,"text":"   same-carrier counterexamples; and\n"},{"number":1501,"text":"10. one neutral toy model demonstrating that the calculus has no hidden\n"},{"number":1502,"text":"    derivation-source record, application-profile or carrier dependency.\n"},{"number":1503,"text":"\n"},{"number":1504,"text":"No example, checker, model or carrier can qualify a law outside the exact\n"},{"number":1505,"text":"claim it evaluates (P6; EVALUATION §1).\n"}]},{"end_line":32,"heading":"CONFORMANCE","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/CONFORMANCE.md#CONFORMANCE","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/CONFORMANCE.md","sha256":"5463790ec7c6d7545354584f42fcdf8997ef1f6aae8e5d50405e2f7ac579345e","start_line":1,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/CONFORMANCE.md","lines":[{"number":1,"text":"# CONFORMANCE\n"},{"number":2,"text":"\n"},{"number":3,"text":"Tier 2. Defines conformance cases for the method's shared owners and their\n"},{"number":4,"text":"consumers. A discriminator is a situation whose expected distinction\n"},{"number":5,"text":"separates a conforming application from a defective one. Each expectation\n"},{"number":6,"text":"and its deciding local owner are stated here; this member imports the\n"},{"number":7,"text":"method's rules and defines no competing result algebra.\n"},{"number":8,"text":"\n"},{"number":9,"text":"A case names its subject, mechanism and expected distinction. An execution\n"},{"number":10,"text":"record separately binds the exact tested subject, basis, acquired context,\n"},{"number":11,"text":"observations, assessor and result. A run is not a pass; only an assessment\n"},{"number":12,"text":"against the declared predicate establishes one. The presence of a case or\n"},{"number":13,"text":"coverage map is no execution or qualification evidence (P6).\n"},{"number":14,"text":"\n"},{"number":15,"text":"A case passes when the expected distinction is observed and no coerced\n"},{"number":16,"text":"success appears anywhere in the result\n"},{"number":17,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed): the\n"},{"number":18,"text":"assessment returns a core value for that predicate, and the case passes\n"},{"number":19,"text":"only when the value is `satisfied`. A case that cannot be run with the\n"},{"number":20,"text":"declared subject is a planned evaluation that was not performed: it has no\n"},{"number":21,"text":"result ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed),\n"},{"number":22,"text":"and it is recorded as not run, never hidden.\n"},{"number":23,"text":"\n"},{"number":24,"text":"Result values. The values `satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`,\n"},{"number":25,"text":"`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` named in this member are core values of\n"},{"number":26,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). The values `re_enter`,\n"},{"number":27,"text":"`re_entry_requested(authority)`, `not_effected` and `completion_unknown`\n"},{"number":28,"text":"are refinements that\n"},{"number":29,"text":"[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition) defines and\n"},{"number":30,"text":"maps into that core. Construction trials\n"},{"number":54,"text":"\n"},{"number":55,"text":"| Case | Shared task | Expected distinction |\n"},{"number":56,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":57,"text":"| T-01 Context cap and decomposition | required basis exceeds one actor's declared cap; Cases for method discriminators\n"},{"number":82,"text":"\n"},{"number":83,"text":"Discriminators 32, 33, 38, 42 and 43 of §5, turn on what\n"},{"number":84,"text":"actors do during real work: how a configuration they belong to is judged\n"},{"number":85,"text":"and kept while they redistribute work, how a realisation is judged against\n"},{"number":86,"text":"its kind of executor, and whether an actor trusts a retained account over\n"},{"number":87,"text":"the workspace. The three cases below exercise them. Discriminator coverage\n"},{"number":120,"text":"\n"},{"number":121,"text":"A logical-review check is a reviewer's reasoned reading: the reviewer\n"},{"number":122,"text":"constructs a discriminator's situation against the text and finds whether\n"},{"number":123,"text":"the text yields the expected distinction, or finds a counterexample or a\n"},{"number":124,"text":"contradiction, without running anything (P6). A\n"},{"number":127,"text":"structural or mechanical check of the text does not establish it\n"},{"number":128,"text":"([EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation)), and it supplies no\n"},{"number":129,"text":"actual-use evidence ([EVALUATION §7](EVALUATION.md#frame-qualification)).\n"},{"number":130,"text":"\n"},{"number":131,"text":"Each row states the situation, expected distinction, local owning sections\n"},{"number":132,"text":"and checks. L-n identifies a logical-review check. UC-n identifies a construction case;\n"},{"number":239,"text":"AS-n identifies an assurance case. Each receives a logical-review check\n"},{"number":240,"text":"under its local owner, and applicable actual-use evidence where the claim\n"},{"number":241,"text":"requires it. A finite model can establish a property only within its\n"},{"number":242,"text":"stated model and population; mechanical validity supplies no semantic\n"},{"number":243,"text":"fidelity or whole-product conformance.\n"},{"number":244,"text":"\n"},{"number":245,"text":"| No. | Discriminator | Expected distinction | Member sections | Exercised by |\n"},{"number":246,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":247,"text":"| UC-1 | Internal tasks pass while a required end-to-end feature fails | Keep the outer failure and diagnose the affected join; local completion does not establish Z. | ACTIVATION §1 Composition boundaries; FOUNDATIONS §4 Preservation through construction; EVALUATION §1 | L-UC1 |\n"},{"number":248,"text":"| UC-2 | Every selected operation is lawful but the result fails the chosen outcome constraints | Preserve the distinction between admissible construction and delivered outcome. The specification supplies Z; a calculus or lawful execution supplies no automatic satisfaction or acceptance. | ACTIVATION §1 Binding A and Z (lawfulness establishes neither delivery nor optimality); SPEC_METHOD §11 | L-UC2 |\n"},{"number":249,"text":"| UC-3 | A report called a bug could concern implementation, requirements or missing observations | Apply one intake and causal diagnosis. Correct the supported affected relation, or acquire evidence and retain unresolved alternatives. The label supplies no repair class or permission. | ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis; SPEC_METHOD §4 Universal intake triage | L-UC3 |\n"},{"number":250,"text":"| UC-4 | A requirement is weakened until the current realisation passes | A change to Z needs its owning decision and downstream re-entry. Cost savings supply no waiver. Preserve incomparable alternatives and unsupported estimates explicitly. | ACTIVATION §1 Strategy; FOUNDATIONS §4 Quantified assurance (no waiver by a cheaper plan); EXECUTIVE_BASELINE Steel-thread delivery | L-UC6 |\n"},{"number":253,"text":"| UC-7 | Every recursive step preserves an invariant but the process does not deliver | Preservation alone proves no progress or termination. State the actual support for continuing or the unresolved stop; no generic termination proof is required merely to perform bounded work. | ACTIVATION §1 Preservation, progress and completion; FOUNDATIONS §3 Construction synthesis | L-UC7 |\n"},{"number":254,"text":"| UC-8 | A limit is exhausted, an observation exposes more work, or an ongoing maintenance loop continues | Distinguish attempt termination, useful discovery, continuing maintenance and delivered outcome. It retains supported local results. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Preservation through construction | L-AS1 |\n"},{"number":257,"text":"| AS-2 | A histogram has the right keys but incorrect counts; a key-only test passes | The check establishes only its target predicate. Assertion provenance identifies whether that predicate is a necessary condition or is sufficient for the claimed requirement. A faithful count assertion detects the count defect within its scope. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation (a check of a necessary condition); case AR-01 | AR-01; L-AS2 |\n"},{"number":258,"text":"| AS-3 | Two admissible states have identical acquired observations but opposite truth values for the asserted obligation | The checker cannot claim a sound complete decision from those observations. It acquires distinguishing evidence, justifies a narrower scope or returns an indeterminate judgment. Unavailable observation and not-performed evaluation retain their distinct meanings. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation, Observation sufficiency; case AR-02 | AR-02; L-AS3 |\n"},{"number":259,"text":"| AS-4 | A test copies its expected answer from the implementation and cites the requirement's digest | Execution provenance and text identity do not establish assertion fidelity or an independent upstream derivation. A supported local regression claim remains usable. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance (an implementation-derived decision supplies no independent justification) | L-AS4 |\n"},{"number":260,"text":"| AS-5 | A human or probabilistic checker can soundly return satisfied or indeterminate on the same observations | The model admits both outcomes. A universal soundness claim covers every admitted conclusion; a selected deterministic model retains its scope, and a probability claim needs its own distribution and evidence. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation (a universal soundness claim covers all admitted conclusions) | L-AS5 |\n"},{"number":261,"text":"| AS-6 | Two implementations or reviewers agree through the same wrong interpretation, fixture or received contribution | Agreement is not counted as independent evidence merely because actors differ. The original evidence and counterexample retain their subjects. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse; ACTIVATION §7; case AR-04 | AR-04; L-AS9 |\n"},{"number":265,"text":"| AS-10 | An implementation or environment dependency changes but the only selection relation is requirement-to-test provenance | Impact includes material execution and validity dependencies. Missing influence information cannot justify exclusion; new uncovered obligations generate work and mandatory gates remain applicable. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse (a requirements-to-test link is no impact model) | L-AS10 |\n"},{"number":266,"text":"| AS-11 | A local repair has supported isolation from an unchanged obligation and its evidence conditions | The applicable unchanged evidence may be retained alongside reassessment of affected claims. The method does not demand full re-execution solely because the subject has changed. | FOUNDATIONS §4 Change impact and evidence reuse (retention) | L-AS11 |\n"},{"number":267,"text":"| AS-12 | Selection is cheap but omits a material obligation, or selection overhead exceeds the saved execution | The plan accounts for required assurance, residual uncertainty and total relevant cost. The graph-execution and\n"},{"number":25,"text":"UX profiles ([ODD](ODD.md) and [UX](UX.md)) refine or bound this one where their own scope\n"},{"number":26,"text":"applies.\n"},{"number":27,"text":"\n"},{"number":28,"text":"This profile's own terms are Ontology (the engineering Ontology of one\n"},{"number":29,"text":"designed boundary, §5), Prime (§5, §6), the Irreducible Architectural\n"},{"number":30,"text":"Carrier Set (IACS, §6), Subordinate Payload, Promotion Test and Boundary\n"},{"number":31,"text":"Inflation (§6), carrier, three-view design asset (§7), module (§9) and the\n"},{"number":32,"text":"predicates `decision_complete(B)` and `co_evolution_admissible(B)` (§5).\n"},{"number":33,"text":"Binding declared under PROFILES §1: where ASSURANCE (tier 2) names \"the\n"},{"number":34,"text":"carrier inventory the design declares\", \"the accepted ontology and\n"},{"number":35,"text":"design\", \"the design's domain, sequence and state projections\" and \"the\n"},{"number":36,"text":"design's decision-completeness and co-evolution conditions\", a boundary\n"},{"number":37,"text":"governed by this profile binds them to the IACS, the accepted Ontology and\n"},{"number":38,"text":"target design, the three-view design asset and the two predicates of §5.\n"},{"number":39,"text":"Direction: profile to tier 2; preserved meaning: the tier-2 law applies\n"},{"number":40,"text":"unchanged to the bound objects; narrowed scope: boundaries this profile\n"},{"number":41,"text":"governs; invalidation: a change of this profile's definition of any bound\n"},{"number":42,"text":"object re-evaluates the binding (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":43,"text":"\n"},{"number":44,"text":"Results and design records. The Ontology verdict\n"},{"number":50,"text":"and the design verdict are dispositions under\n"},{"number":51,"text":"[ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition), as §7 Gate and\n"},{"number":52,"text":"retrospective work states. Its bias is\n"},{"number":83,"text":"toward low coupling, modular composition, immutable typed carriers, total\n"},{"number":84,"text":"or nearly total semantic transforms and explicit effect boundaries. The\n"},{"number":85,"text":"goal is not language ideology. The goals are to reduce ambiguity, reduce\n"},{"number":86,"text":"entropy, eliminate avoidable technical debt, increase refactorability,\n"},{"number":87,"text":"reduce hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift in realisation\n"},{"number":88,"text":"code, and preserve enough evidence that later reviewers can audit,\n"},{"number":89,"text":"refactor and reconstruct why the realisation took its current shape (P2,\n"},{"number":90,"text":"P6). The profile is therefore about realisation design and implementation\n"},{"number":91,"text":"shape.\n"},{"number":92,"text":"\n"},{"number":93,"text":"It does not mandate one optimal authoring path for every agent, worker or\n"},{"number":94,"text":"runtime. Agentic coders may sometimes move faster by deriving\n"},{"number":95,"text":"implementation and proof in the same work pass; that is acceptable only\n"},{"number":96,"text":"when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds under proportional design\n"},{"number":97,"text":"sequencing (§5) and the boundary reaches decision completeness before any\n"},{"number":98,"text":"design-method closure claim (P0, P2).\n"},{"number":99,"text":"\n"},{"number":100,"text":"One pillar of specification-driven development is bounded intermediate\n"},{"number":101,"text":"traversal. Specification gives the global WHAT; every intermediate\n"},{"number":102,"text":"traversal should have a finite, inspectable unit for reasoning,\n"},{"number":103,"text":"implementation, evaluation, proof and later refactor. A module boundary is\n"},{"number":104,"text":"one realisation-level tool for creating that unit; it is not the only\n"},{"number":105,"text":"possible bounded traversal. Without bounded units, reviewers and agents\n"},{"number":106,"text":"traverse too much context at once, and correctness depends on memory\n"},{"number":107,"text":"rather than on preserved structure (P0; ACTIVATION §1 Execution unit).\n"},{"number":108,"text":"\n"},{"number":109,"text":"The profile does not replace constitutional authority (SPEC_METHOD) and\n"},{"number":110,"text":"does not replace the graph-native law of the graph-execution profile\n"},{"number":111,"text":"(PROFILES §2). It governs how the Ontology, architecture and realisation\n"},{"number":112,"text":"modules should be derived once the project has decided the outcomes and\n"},{"number":113,"text":"capabilities it is building. A product decision that functionality is\n"},{"number":114,"text":"required does not decide how many entities, functions, public operations,\n"},{"number":115,"text":"carriers or modules should exist (P2, P6). For a product governed by the\n"},{"number":116,"text":"graph-execution profile, this profile does not authorise replacing a graph\n"},{"number":117,"text":"function, edge traversal or graph module with deterministic implementation\n"},{"number":118,"text":"modules; it governs the deterministic realisation shape inside or beneath\n"},{"number":119,"text":"those carriers (P6, §2).\n"},{"number":120,"text":"\n"},{"number":121,"text":"These rules apply to module boundaries, schema and carrier families,\n"},{"number":122,"text":"entity and record design, and interface contracts. They are not limited to\n"},{"number":123,"text":"one programming language or one runtime binding (P1).\n"},{"number":124,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":135,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/1. That means semantic meaning should live in typed carriers and\n"},{"number":128,"text":"explicit transforms; imperative coordination should be subordinate to\n"},{"number":129,"text":"admitted truth; side effects should be isolated to explicit boundary\n"},{"number":130,"text":"modules; and mutable shared state should be minimised and justified. The\n"},{"number":131,"text":"profile does not require a functional programming language; it does\n"},{"number":132,"text":"require a functional design discipline. A Python, Scala, TypeScript,\n"},{"number":133,"text":"Kotlin or Java implementation may each satisfy it if it keeps semantic law\n"},{"number":134,"text":"in explicit carriers and transforms rather than hidden orchestration.\n"},{"number":135,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":144,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/1. Boundary closure evaluators/Authority seam closure","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F3.%20Boundary%20closure%20evaluators%2FAuthority%20seam%20closure","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"b8f025e077ffcb8bdb44b10e578802e2c3380df7f3bb78ae897f8469b0b3abc4","start_line":317,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":317,"text":"### Authority seam closure\n"},{"number":318,"text":"\n"},{"number":319,"text":"Each change does not increase the number of truth surfaces; where\n"},{"number":320,"text":"duplicate or rival truth surfaces already exist, seam-closure work should\n"},{"number":321,"text":"reduce them (P6, P3). This means one\n"},{"number":322,"text":"authoritative carrier or contract at each semantic boundary; no\n"},{"number":323,"text":"controller-side reconstruction of already-admitted truth; no downstream\n"},{"number":324,"text":"surface silently rebuilding source truth from raw artifacts; and no raw or\n"},{"number":325,"text":"open payload trusted past ingress. The test: if the authoritative carrier\n"},{"number":326,"text":"were removed, would the system fail closed, or would another path silently\n"},{"number":327,"text":"reconstruct the same meaning? If meaning survives by reconstruction, the\n"},{"number":328,"text":"seam is not closed.\n"},{"number":329,"text":"\n"},{"number":330,"text":"For projection and query modules, seam closure also requires source\n"},{"number":331,"text":"coherence (P6, P1): the projection names the admitted carrier, runtime,\n"},{"number":332,"text":"event or source truth it derives from; reconstructed catalogue, ownership,\n"},{"number":333,"text":"route, status or closure truth is structurally compared against the\n"},{"number":334,"text":"admitted source carrier before publication; same-name but different-shape\n"},{"number":335,"text":"carriers fail closed unless an explicit migration design makes the\n"},{"number":336,"text":"divergence lawful; and negative tests cover structural drift, not only\n"},{"number":337,"text":"missing source truth.\n"},{"number":338,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":350,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/3. Boundary closure evaluators/Essential carrier consolidation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F3.%20Boundary%20closure%20evaluators%2FEssential%20carrier%20consolidation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"1e2d191f0670ca709739da9afcc91c949c1082cd240e6ccb0d02562b656ca0e1","start_line":339,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":339,"text":"### Essential carrier consolidation\n"},{"number":340,"text":"\n"},{"number":341,"text":"Each change should collapse the slice to the few real identity-bearing\n"},{"number":342,"text":"carrier families (P3, P2). This\n"},{"number":343,"text":"means declaring the IACS first (§6), keeping Subordinate Payloads\n"},{"number":344,"text":"subordinate by default, and avoiding fragment classes, interfaces or result\n"},{"number":345,"text":"records created only to satisfy typing, serialisation or convenience\n"},{"number":346,"text":"extraction. Progress is fewer, sharper carrier families, less duplicate\n"},{"number":347,"text":"authority and less boundary inflation; not one more wrapper layer, one more\n"},{"number":348,"text":"branch-local peer type, or one more public record that only mirrors\n"},{"number":349,"text":"payload detail.\n"},{"number":350,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":364,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/3. Boundary closure evaluators/Enforcement after proof","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F3.%20Boundary%20closure%20evaluators%2FEnforcement%20after%20proof","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"770498bd9fb20bc90ffee834ee551252520cefd87527019341741495b924b3de","start_line":351,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":351,"text":"### Enforcement after proof\n"},{"number":352,"text":"\n"},{"number":353,"text":"Typing, schemas, validators, contracts and codecs exist to lock in a seam\n"},{"number":354,"text":"that has already been made real (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":355,"text":"Parse, validate or construct first; admit and narrow the boundary\n"},{"number":356,"text":"explicitly; then use types or schemas to enforce the proved shape. It does\n"},{"number":357,"text":"not mean relabelling an open payload and calling it closed, wrapping loose\n"},{"number":358,"text":"data in a typed envelope while keeping the same authority path, or using\n"},{"number":359,"text":"casts, unchecked assertions or dynamic mutation as fake closure. The\n"},{"number":360,"text":"evaluator is language-agnostic: in one language it may be `mypy --strict`,\n"},{"number":361,"text":"in another a sealed algebraic type plus a schema parser, in another a\n"},{"number":362,"text":"compiler-enforced sum type plus decoder. The rule is the same: proof\n"},{"number":363,"text":"first, enforcement second.\n"},{"number":364,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":376,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/3. Boundary closure evaluators/Ingress collapse","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F3.%20Boundary%20closure%20evaluators%2FIngress%20collapse","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"9757f3bd200b1e5b4d60f5659186a2f05ef87a4b71f527cabc76ad1083470b17","start_line":365,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":365,"text":"### Ingress collapse\n"},{"number":366,"text":"\n"},{"number":367,"text":"Foreign, dynamic or weakly typed input is lawful only at ingress (P1, P5). Once admitted, it collapses immediately\n"},{"number":368,"text":"into local carrier truth before semantic transforms begin. The required\n"},{"number":369,"text":"shape: receive foreign input; parse, validate or normalise it once;\n"},{"number":370,"text":"construct local admitted carrier truth; consume only that local truth in\n"},{"number":371,"text":"semantic kernels. Not lawful seam closure: repeated parsing of the same\n"},{"number":372,"text":"loose payload in several modules; `from_dict(...).to_dict()` or equivalent\n"},{"number":373,"text":"round-trip ceremony that preserves the same open authority; loaders that\n"},{"number":374,"text":"merely relabel stored JSON or map data without validating it; semantic\n"},{"number":375,"text":"kernels that continue to inspect open payload fragments directly.\n"},{"number":376,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":378,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/4. Functional bias and typing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F4.%20Functional%20bias%20and%20typing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"f5e78daccb8761f3b665ea850766a89b1375526d842cb66a6030b0dab9f3ccd6","start_line":377,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":377,"text":"## 4. closed typed carriers over open dictionary or\n"},{"number":383,"text":"string protocols; parsing and admitting foreign data once at ingress;\n"},{"number":384,"text":"explicit return values over hidden mutation; explicit failure carriers\n"},{"number":385,"text":"over ambient exception-driven control flow where practical; and\n"},{"number":386,"text":"composition of small transforms over long controller procedures.\n"},{"number":387,"text":"\n"},{"number":388,"text":"They avoid: one giant mutable workspace object; one orchestration method\n"},{"number":389,"text":"that owns semantic law; hidden read and write coupling through globals,\n"},{"number":390,"text":"shared registries or mutable service state; typed envelopes over open\n"},{"number":391,"text":"payload truth; dynamic payload mutation at the semantic centre; effectful\n"},{"number":392,"text":"helpers that both decide meaning and perform writes; and proxy interfaces\n"},{"number":393,"text":"that partially imitate a new design while preserving the old authority\n"},{"number":394,"text":"path (P6, P4a; §10).\n"},{"number":395,"text":"\n"},{"number":396,"text":"Both lists bind. A project that adopts this profile prefers the first\n"},{"number":397,"text":"and avoids the second as an obligation of the profile, not as a\n"},{"number":398,"text":"description of practice: a realisation that takes an avoided shape, or\n"},{"number":399,"text":"forgoes a preferred one, does not conform unless a rule of this profile\n"},{"number":400,"text":"permits that departure and the realisation records the justification the\n"},{"number":401,"text":"rule requires. The permitted departures are those the owning rules state:\n"},{"number":402,"text":"mutable carrier state where it is materially necessary, under §10\n"},{"number":403,"text":"[Immutable carriers](#immutable-carriers), and the failure-carrier\n"},{"number":404,"text":"preference only where practical. Convenience permits no departure (P6,\n"},{"number":405,"text":"P2).\n"},{"number":406,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":438,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/4. Functional bias and typing/Python typing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F4.%20Functional%20bias%20and%20typing%2FPython%20typing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"073044c9d8c45aea0819f834e617a1ab652752371ce375eedbee49d538417169","start_line":407,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":407,"text":"### Python typing\n"},{"number":408,"text":"\n"},{"number":409,"text":"When this profile governs a Python boundary, repo-authored Python is fully\n"},{"number":410,"text":"typed (P1): every function, method and\n"},{"number":411,"text":"callable surface has explicit parameter and return annotations; semantic\n"},{"number":412,"text":"carriers are closed and typed; and repo-authored tests, scripts and\n"},{"number":413,"text":"support code are typed too, with no lower bar than production code.\n"},{"number":414,"text":"\n"},{"number":415,"text":"These do not count as typed semantic design (P1): untyped `def`; implicit\n"},{"number":416,"text":"`Any`; semantic `dict[str, Any]`; semantic `Mapping[str, Any]`; semantic\n"},{"number":417,"text":"`object` payloads used as carrier truth; unchecked JSON blobs passed\n"},{"number":418,"text":"through several layers and interpreted by `.get(...)` chains. For Python,\n"},{"number":419,"text":"`dict[str, Any]` at the semantic centre is untyped design debt, not an\n"},{"number":420,"text":"acceptable carrier.\n"},{"number":421,"text":"\n"},{"number":422,"text":"The required shape (P1, P5): use `dataclass`, `TypedDict`, `Protocol`, `Literal`,\n"},{"number":423,"text":"`Enum` or other closed typed forms for local carriers; parse and validate\n"},{"number":424,"text":"dynamic input at the boundary; narrow untyped external data into local\n"},{"number":425,"text":"typed carriers before semantic transforms begin; keep `Any` at foreign\n"},{"number":426,"text":"boundaries only, and collapse it immediately. `Any`, `cast(...)` and\n"},{"number":427,"text":"`# type: ignore` are allowed only when all of these hold: the boundary is\n"},{"number":428,"text":"genuinely foreign or dynamically typed; the local code cannot express the\n"},{"number":429,"text":"shape more precisely; the use is narrow, explicit and justified in place;\n"},{"number":430,"text":"and the imprecision does not cross into the semantic kernel as governing\n"},{"number":431,"text":"truth.\n"},{"number":432,"text":"\n"},{"number":433,"text":"Python boundaries under this profile are checked with a strict static\n"},{"number":434,"text":"typing pass such as `mypy --strict` or an equivalent strict checker\n"},{"number":435,"text":"configuration. If the checker cannot run cleanly on the adopted boundary,\n"},{"number":436,"text":"the boundary is not yet implementation-conformant under this profile (P1,\n"},{"number":437,"text":"P6).\n"},{"number":438,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":496,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"1084eac69d442ba1be2a0c72457692e23ab93ac44dc5c783afd623f5726c7a5d","start_line":439,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":439,"text":"## 5. Ontology-first design\n"},{"number":440,"text":"\n"},{"number":441,"text":"Every new or materially changed active semantic boundary derives its\n"},{"number":442,"text":"semantic model from one accepted Ontology (P1, P6). Before a new or changed entity, function,\n"},{"number":443,"text":"authority, effect, Prime-conformant carrier, module boundary, public\n"},{"number":444,"text":"operation or schema is promoted, the affected boundary first produces a\n"},{"number":445,"text":"candidate Ontology slice and carries it through the acceptance sequence\n"},{"number":446,"text":"below.\n"},{"number":447,"text":"\n"},{"number":448,"text":"The Ontology is the prior semantic-design authority for the boundary. It\n"},{"number":449,"text":"is subordinate to the constitutional WHAT: it derives from intent,\n"},{"number":450,"text":"product, requirements and the applicable graph or domain profile, and it\n"},{"number":451,"text":"does not invent product meaning. Once accepted, it governs semantic\n"},{"number":452,"text":"entities, relationships, invariants, lifecycle, authority, functions,\n"},{"number":453,"text":"composition and effects (P6, P2). It does not replace target architecture\n"},{"number":454,"text":"or module design: accepted design remains the structural HOW for topology,\n"},{"number":455,"text":"interfaces, carrier placement, module boundaries, algorithms and local\n"},{"number":456,"text":"realisation. Implementation and tests derive from requirements plus\n"},{"number":457,"text":"accepted design and preserve the accepted Ontology; they are not direct\n"},{"number":458,"text":"substitutes for either layer (P6; SPEC_METHOD §2 Constitutional chain).\n"},{"number":459,"text":"\n"},{"number":460,"text":"Ontology acceptance identifies the constitutional sources it derives from\n"},{"number":461,"text":"and the design authority that accepted it. It carries stable element and\n"},{"number":462,"text":"relation identities plus a version or basis that makes source change,\n"},{"number":463,"text":"staleness and the affected projection set decidable (P3; FOUNDATIONS §2,\n"},{"number":464,"text":"Basis). A reprice of a governing source invalidates only the affected\n"},{"number":465,"text":"Ontology relations and downstream projections until their impact is\n"},{"number":466,"text":"re-evaluated; the reprice is an instance of the material input change of\n"},{"number":467,"text":"[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), which owns the\n"},{"number":468,"text":"invalidators. Code, tests, generated schemas or a single implementing\n"},{"number":469,"text":"agent cannot self-ratify missing Ontology authority (P6). The Ontology\n"},{"number":470,"text":"verdict may live in the same design pack and acceptance record as the\n"},{"number":471,"text":"three-view verdict (§7); this rule does not require a second document,\n"},{"number":472,"text":"ticket or approval ceremony.\n"},{"number":473,"text":"\n"},{"number":474,"text":"Proportionality applies (ACTIVATION §6). A material semantic boundary is\n"},{"number":475,"text":"one whose change affects identity, authority, lifecycle, public contract,\n"},{"number":476,"text":"externally observable Product meaning, cross-module topology, or accepted\n"},{"number":477,"text":"effect or closure law. A `realization_refactor` wholly inside an accepted\n"},{"number":478,"text":"boundary may cite the existing Ontology and design basis and prove no\n"},{"number":479,"text":"Ontology delta; it does not require re-authoring or re-accepting unchanged\n"},{"number":480,"text":"evidence. A semantic or structural change publishes only the affected\n"},{"number":481,"text":"Ontology and design delta and its projection impact set. Unaffected\n"},{"number":482,"text":"maintenance and unrelated boundaries do not freeze merely because one\n"},{"number":483,"text":"source digest changed (P2, P0).\n"},{"number":484,"text":"\n"},{"number":485,"text":"For this profile (P1):\n"},{"number":486,"text":"\n"},{"number":487,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":488,"text":"Ontology =\n"},{"number":489,"text":"  entities + identities + relationships + invariants + lifecycle\n"},{"number":490,"text":"  + authority + atomic functions + higher-order composition\n"},{"number":491,"text":"  + effects + projections\n"},{"number":492,"text":"```\n"},{"number":493,"text":"\n"},{"number":494,"text":"A class inventory, schema list, endpoint list, command list or carrier\n"},{"number":495,"text":"census alone is not an Ontology (P1).\n"},{"number":496,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":567,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Proportional design sequencing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FProportional%20design%20sequencing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"6b6853f3db0cf6e436da046fbbcf62eb93522615f5833ffe359581574f6189f5","start_line":497,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":497,"text":"### Proportional design sequencing\n"},{"number":498,"text":"\n"},{"number":499,"text":"For one governed boundary `B`, let `M(B)` be its complete material-relation\n"},{"number":500,"text":"set (decision-complete symbolic design, below) and `U(B)` the unresolved\n"},{"number":501,"text":"members of that set (P2, P0):\n"},{"number":502,"text":"\n"},{"number":503,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":504,"text":"U(B) = unresolved(M(B))\n"},{"number":505,"text":"decision_complete(B) iff\n"},{"number":506,"text":"  U(B) = empty\n"},{"number":507,"text":"  and M(B) is jointly satisfiable\n"},{"number":508,"text":"  and every network admitted by M(B) is semantically equivalent under the\n"},{"number":509,"text":"      governing Product, requirements and accepted design relations\n"},{"number":510,"text":"co_evolution_admissible(B) iff decision_complete(B)\n"},{"number":511,"text":"design_gate(B) =\n"},{"number":512,"text":"  the smallest causally closed affected set needed to establish\n"},{"number":513,"text":"  decision_complete(B)\n"},{"number":514,"text":"```\n"},{"number":515,"text":"\n"},{"number":516,"text":"Design sequencing follows `decision_complete(B)`, not one global authoring\n"},{"number":517,"text":"order (P2, P6). Co-evolution is lawful only when `decision_complete(B)` holds:\n"},{"number":518,"text":"design still owns the structural HOW, but design, implementation and tests\n"},{"number":519,"text":"may evolve together and reconcile before promotion or closure.\n"},{"number":520,"text":"Design-gated sequencing is required when implementation would otherwise\n"},{"number":521,"text":"establish an unresolved or contradictory relation, or choose between\n"},{"number":522,"text":"materially non-equivalent networks, with durable consequences for future\n"},{"number":523,"text":"change: the affected design decision is accepted before retained\n"},{"number":524,"text":"implementation establishes it. A disposable spike may supply evidence\n"},{"number":525,"text":"without becoming the selected design.\n"},{"number":526,"text":"\n"},{"number":527,"text":"Neither mode is the global default; the same proportionality relation\n"},{"number":528,"text":"selects between them. Proportionality decides which relations are material\n"},{"number":529,"text":"and bounds the smallest affected gate; decision completeness is the\n"},{"number":530,"text":"resulting admissibility test (ACTIVATION §6). Where a bounded symbolic\n"},{"number":531,"text":"model can contract the material semantic alternatives within effective\n"},{"number":532,"text":"reasoning capacity, the code, runtime-state, test, review and\n"},{"number":533,"text":"reconciliation space it removes is counterfactual evidence of that\n"},{"number":534,"text":"contraction, not an independent reason for a design gate. Where no\n"},{"number":535,"text":"material alternative remains, a separate prior gate adds ceremony without\n"},{"number":536,"text":"disambiguation (P2).\n"},{"number":537,"text":"\n"},{"number":538,"text":"The bidirectional design-and-implementation relation is an evidence\n"},{"number":539,"text":"relation, not bidirectional semantic authority. Implementation may provide\n"},{"number":540,"text":"a counterexample, falsify a constraint or expose hidden ambiguity. It may\n"},{"number":541,"text":"not select the missing semantic answer, rewrite upstream truth to legalise\n"},{"number":542,"text":"itself, or ratify a material design decision after establishing it (P6).\n"},{"number":543,"text":"\n"},{"number":544,"text":"The selected relation and its basis belong in the existing work or design\n"},{"number":545,"text":"carrier; this rule requires no separate artifact. If implementation\n"},{"number":546,"text":"exposes previously hidden architectural ambiguity, the boundary switches to\n"},{"number":547,"text":"design-gated sequencing at the smallest causally closed affected decision\n"},{"number":548,"text":"set rather than retroactively invalidating unrelated work. Serial\n"},{"number":549,"text":"implementation repairs do not establish design acceptance. Repeated or\n"},{"number":550,"text":"cross-cutting material surprises are evidence for diagnosis under\n"},{"number":551,"text":"[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation),\n"},{"number":552,"text":"not a diagnosis. Where the diagnosis establishes that the affected design\n"},{"number":553,"text":"cut is underconstrained, so that `decision_complete(B)` fails, one bounded\n"},{"number":554,"text":"`design_reframe` follows (SPEC_METHOD §4 Change classes), and retained code\n"},{"number":555,"text":"remains provisional evidence until that reframe is accepted. Where the\n"},{"number":556,"text":"accepted design is decision-complete and the realisation alone deviates\n"},{"number":557,"text":"from it, the repair is a `realization_refactor`, however often the surprise\n"},{"number":558,"text":"recurs (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":559,"text":"\n"},{"number":560,"text":"This applies the governing proportionality law: a prior design gate is\n"},{"number":561,"text":"warranted when it removes material semantic ambiguity whose alternatives\n"},{"number":562,"text":"would establish materially different durable architecture, and that\n"},{"number":563,"text":"contraction justifies its reasoning load. It is disproportionate when\n"},{"number":564,"text":"upstream truth leaves no materially divergent architecture to adjudicate\n"},{"number":565,"text":"and a separate prior acceptance would add no disambiguation. Design still\n"},{"number":566,"text":"records and owns the resulting HOW before promotion or closure (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":567,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":612,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Decision-complete symbolic design","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FDecision-complete%20symbolic%20design","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"c174fc772b42ca20b0ddfebf7f1a300f1ea9b8c70e15d15c7eaafba8b7036b9c","start_line":568,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":568,"text":"### Decision-complete symbolic design\n"},{"number":569,"text":"\n"},{"number":570,"text":"For one governed boundary `B`, the complete material-relation set is (P1,\n"},{"number":571,"text":"P2):\n"},{"number":572,"text":"\n"},{"number":573,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":574,"text":"M(B) =\n"},{"number":575,"text":"  entities + identities + relationships + cardinalities + invariants\n"},{"number":576,"text":"  + authorities + authority transitions + functions\n"},{"number":577,"text":"  + higher-order composition laws + topology\n"},{"number":578,"text":"  + lifecycle states and transitions + public contracts\n"},{"number":579,"text":"  + externally observable Product meaning\n"},{"number":580,"text":"  + declared domains and admission conditions\n"},{"number":581,"text":"  + failure and refusal routes + effect and closure laws\n"},{"number":582,"text":"  + projections + module mappings + material algorithmic obligations\n"},{"number":583,"text":"```\n"},{"number":584,"text":"\n"},{"number":585,"text":"A design boundary is decision-complete when `U(B)` is empty, `M(B)` forms\n"},{"number":586,"text":"one jointly satisfiable constraint network, and every network admitted by\n"},{"number":587,"text":"`M(B)` is semantically equivalent under the governing Product,\n"},{"number":588,"text":"requirements and accepted design relations. This is the design gate's\n"},{"number":589,"text":"acceptance criterion: a boundary is ready for retained implementation\n"},{"number":590,"text":"without a prior gate exactly when it is decision-complete, and a gate that\n"},{"number":591,"text":"cannot reach decision completeness has not closed (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":592,"text":"\n"},{"number":593,"text":"Ontology, Prime contraction, IACS, target design, the domain, sequence and\n"},{"number":594,"text":"state views, public contracts, module boundaries, implementation and tests\n"},{"number":595,"text":"are projections of that one network at different reasoning altitudes.\n"},{"number":596,"text":"Their presence, section names, individual plausibility or mechanical\n"},{"number":597,"text":"validity does not establish decision completeness (P1, EVALUATION §1).\n"},{"number":598,"text":"\n"},{"number":599,"text":"The boundary is underconstrained whenever `decision_complete(B)` is false,\n"},{"number":600,"text":"including when implementation has to introduce a new material semantic\n"},{"number":601,"text":"decision, projections contradict one another, or two materially\n"},{"number":602,"text":"non-equivalent networks remain admissible. Local algorithm and layout\n"},{"number":603,"text":"choices may remain open only when every admitted choice is semantically\n"},{"number":604,"text":"equivalent under the accepted network. Contradictory projections make the\n"},{"number":605,"text":"design unsatisfiable and block promotion (P1, P5): an unsatisfiable design\n"},{"number":606,"text":"fails the design gate's acceptance criterion, so this block is a\n"},{"number":607,"text":"precondition of the gate (§7 Gate and retrospective work), not a decision\n"},{"number":608,"text":"on a review finding. Decision completeness\n"},{"number":609,"text":"does not require another document: the constraint network may be expressed\n"},{"number":610,"text":"through the existing Ontology, algebra, module mapping and views when those\n"},{"number":611,"text":"surfaces jointly carry the complete relation (P2).\n"},{"number":612,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":668,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Bounded frame conservation (UP-017)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FBounded%20frame%20conservation%20%28UP-017%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"d184c52a2d17c1f3a6c19e21bbf70860a13c1d4312c3c59594db47de63cce825","start_line":613,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":613,"text":"### Bounded frame conservation (UP-017)\n"},{"number":614,"text":"\n"},{"number":615,"text":"`M(B)` closes one governed boundary. A bounded local action is taken inside\n"},{"number":616,"text":"a design frame that derives from other accepted frames, and its lawfulness\n"},{"number":617,"text":"depends on relations the acting frame does not itself own (P4b, P0). Global and local are relative to\n"},{"number":618,"text":"the selected frame. Each material design frame identifies:\n"},{"number":619,"text":"\n"},{"number":620,"text":"- the governing frames and accepted relations from which it derives;\n"},{"number":621,"text":"- the bounded affected relation set of the proposed action;\n"},{"number":622,"text":"- the applicable inherited invariants;\n"},{"number":623,"text":"- the authority and composition seams crossing that set; and\n"},{"number":624,"text":"- the subordinate frames opened by unresolved material distinctions.\n"},{"number":625,"text":"\n"},{"number":626,"text":"A frame may derive from more than one governing frame. A persistence\n"},{"number":627,"text":"component belongs to an entity lifecycle boundary and an operational\n"},{"number":628,"text":"consistency boundary; an admission function belongs to a domain transition\n"},{"number":629,"text":"and a runtime-authority boundary; a shared callable may be consumed by\n"},{"number":630,"text":"several sibling domains without becoming subordinate to one. A single\n"},{"number":631,"text":"governing frame is lawful where the structure is genuinely hierarchical,\n"},{"number":632,"text":"and is not required. Governing frames form a constraint network for the\n"},{"number":633,"text":"same reason `M(B)` does (P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":634,"text":"\n"},{"number":635,"text":"The seam rule is [ACTIVATION §1 Execution unit](ACTIVATION.md#execution-unit)\n"},{"number":636,"text":"and [§4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement). Applied to a design\n"},{"number":637,"text":"frame, it makes the declared set testable against its own declared seams without a closure algorithm or\n"},{"number":638,"text":"recursive expansion through irrelevant relations (P0).\n"},{"number":639,"text":"\n"},{"number":640,"text":"The result is evaluated against every affected governing frame, preserves\n"},{"number":641,"text":"each applicable accepted relation, and updates only affected subordinate\n"},{"number":642,"text":"projections. A bounded local action conserves governing truth; it does not\n"},{"number":643,"text":"rewrite it. A result that changes a governing relation re-enters at that\n"},{"number":644,"text":"relation before acceptance (P4b; FOUNDATIONS §3 P4b, frame instance). A\n"},{"number":645,"text":"subordinate frame opens only when a material distinction cannot be\n"},{"number":646,"text":"resolved at the governing altitude; this rule does not require recursively\n"},{"number":647,"text":"documenting irrelevant descendants (P2). The law is false if a change is\n"},{"number":648,"text":"locally valid inside the selected frame but violates, duplicates or\n"},{"number":649,"text":"silently reinterprets an invariant in any affected governing frame.\n"},{"number":650,"text":"\n"},{"number":651,"text":"Discovered functionality is evidence about required behaviour, not yet an\n"},{"number":652,"text":"architectural operation. A discovered verb, screen action, endpoint,\n"},{"number":653,"text":"command, ticket phrase or use case is not promoted directly into a public\n"},{"number":654,"text":"operation identity, peer carrier, module or implementation function; it is\n"},{"number":655,"text":"first derived through the Ontology (P6, P2). The derivation order:\n"},{"number":656,"text":"\n"},{"number":657,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":658,"text":"constitutional functionality\n"},{"number":659,"text":"  -> candidate Ontology\n"},{"number":660,"text":"  -> logical completeness\n"},{"number":661,"text":"  -> whole-family Prime contraction\n"},{"number":662,"text":"  -> accepted Ontology basis\n"},{"number":663,"text":"  -> Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set\n"},{"number":664,"text":"  -> target design and domain, sequence and state projections\n"},{"number":665,"text":"  -> public contract and adapter projections\n"},{"number":666,"text":"  -> implementation and test projections\n"},{"number":667,"text":"```\n"},{"number":668,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":681,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Native constructability (UP-002)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FNative%20constructability%20%28UP-002%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"548eb7a1554f09d233d90549dbbacb513ec4c56a48082304d49d17c20d4e5c9e","start_line":669,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":669,"text":"### Native constructability (UP-002)\n"},{"number":670,"text":"\n"},{"number":671,"text":"A semantically coherent design is not acceptable when its selected\n"},{"number":672,"text":"substrate cannot natively construct the required identities,\n"},{"number":673,"text":"relationships, transitions, authority boundaries, effects, lifecycle,\n"},{"number":674,"text":"composition, publication and retirement behaviour (P2, P5). A missing\n"},{"number":675,"text":"substrate capability remains an explicit design gap or triggers lawful\n"},{"number":676,"text":"re-entry (SPEC_METHOD §4); it is not hidden behind a reference bridge,\n"},{"number":677,"text":"adapter, filesystem runner, test double or promised future feature (P6;\n"},{"number":678,"text":"SPEC_METHOD §7 Bridge prohibition). This is a constructability obligation,\n"},{"number":679,"text":"not a prescribed implementation; the consumer chooses the substrate and the\n"},{"number":680,"text":"evidence mechanism (P0).\n"},{"number":681,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":801,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Capability and foundation selection (UP-023)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FCapability%20and%20foundation%20selection%20%28UP-023%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"3cb515072564fe861dd5732e0ccd8323f161bf626ea4e08eaae60d3710727dd7","start_line":682,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":682,"text":"### Capability and foundation selection (UP-023)\n"},{"number":683,"text":"\n"},{"number":684,"text":"Native constructability proves that the selected substrate can realise the\n"},{"number":685,"text":"design; it does not prove that locally constructing another generic\n"},{"number":686,"text":"mechanism is the best realisation. Before constructing a material generic\n"},{"number":687,"text":"capability, common mechanic or algorithm, or selecting a material\n"},{"number":688,"text":"dependency, the active design boundary performs a proportional\n"},{"number":689,"text":"foundation-selection pass (P2, P6). Its governing law\n"},{"number":690,"text":"is [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra) Shared machinery; this\n"},{"number":691,"text":"section is its selection procedure.\n"},{"number":692,"text":"\n"},{"number":693,"text":"The pass first states the required capability without Product, domain,\n"},{"number":694,"text":"module, vendor, file or incumbent-implementation labels. It then\n"},{"number":695,"text":"distinguishes each irreducible semantic or authority-bearing relation,\n"},{"number":696,"text":"with its declared owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis and material\n"},{"number":697,"text":"lifecycle and refusal invariants, from the generic mechanics and\n"},{"number":698,"text":"foundation capabilities that may support those relations or realise an\n"},{"number":699,"text":"explicitly assigned role. This factoring concerns declared relations and\n"},{"number":700,"text":"roles, not source authorship (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":701,"text":"\n"},{"number":702,"text":"The bounded candidate population draws applicable compositions from:\n"},{"number":703,"text":"foundations already admitted in the current project; language, runtime,\n"},{"number":704,"text":"platform or standard-library capabilities; accepted predecessor or\n"},{"number":705,"text":"immutable-lineage realisations usable as evidence; maintained external\n"},{"number":706,"text":"foundations where the Product permits a dependency; and a bounded local\n"},{"number":707,"text":"implementation (P2).\n"},{"number":708,"text":"\n"},{"number":709,"text":"Candidate discovery is bounded, reproducible and explicitly\n"},{"number":710,"text":"non-exhaustive. For every candidate category the evidence record declares\n"},{"number":711,"text":"the sources or collections searched, cutoff time and relevant version\n"},{"number":712,"text":"basis, applicability and inclusion criteria, material exclusions,\n"},{"number":713,"text":"predecessor or incumbent status, discovered candidates and residual\n"},{"number":714,"text":"unknowns; a category not searched records `not_applicable` or a named gap\n"},{"number":715,"text":"with its reason. Discovery closes only for that declared basis and cutoff.\n"},{"number":716,"text":"A discovery gap that could materially alter the frontier prevents\n"},{"number":717,"text":"selection; an immaterial residual records why it cannot change the current\n"},{"number":718,"text":"decision. A later candidate that satisfies the applicability criteria and\n"},{"number":719,"text":"could materially alter the lawful frontier invalidates the affected\n"},{"number":720,"text":"selection evidence and re-enters this relation (P6, P5, P3); such a\n"},{"number":721,"text":"candidate is newly acquired admissible evidence material to the selection,\n"},{"number":722,"text":"an instance of the material input change of\n"},{"number":723,"text":"[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse).\n"},{"number":724,"text":"\n"},{"number":725,"text":"This relation operates inside the Product boundary and, where applicable,\n"},{"number":726,"text":"the migration strategy already admitted by their existing owners. It does\n"},{"number":727,"text":"not choose bounded evolution versus fundamental re-adoption or override\n"},{"number":728,"text":"the rebuttable strategy presumption of SPEC_METHOD §7 Constitutional\n"},{"number":729,"text":"migration options. A working predecessor may therefore constrain the\n"},{"number":730,"text":"admitted candidate set at migration altitude. Within that admitted\n"},{"number":731,"text":"boundary and the generic-capability decision, discovery may begin with the\n"},{"number":732,"text":"incumbent or an already installed dependency, but selection has no\n"},{"number":733,"text":"source-order, familiarity, sunk-cost, local-code or dependency-count\n"},{"number":734,"text":"preference. Candidate compositions are evaluated, not only individual\n"},{"number":735,"text":"packages: a lawful result may use a foundation for generic mechanics and\n"},{"number":736,"text":"may also use it to realise a semantic or authority-bearing role explicitly\n"},{"number":737,"text":"assigned by accepted design. Neither case changes who owns the declared\n"},{"number":738,"text":"relation (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":739,"text":"\n"},{"number":740,"text":"For every material candidate admitted to the bounded population, one\n"},{"number":741,"text":"evidence ledger or equivalent design record compares the dimensions that\n"},{"number":742,"text":"can change the decision, including: functional and constructability fit;\n"},{"number":743,"text":"semantic or operation-authority leakage; adapter, integration, migration,\n"},{"number":744,"text":"deletion and future-code cost; licence, maintenance, security, upgrade and\n"},{"number":745,"text":"supply-chain posture; package, runtime, startup, storage and operational\n"},{"number":746,"text":"cost; determinism, concurrency, failure, recovery, reconstruction and\n"},{"number":747,"text":"replay; proof and assurance burden; and exit, replacement and reversibility\n"},{"number":748,"text":"cost (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":749,"text":"\n"},{"number":750,"text":"A hard authority, Product-contract, safety, security, licensing or\n"},{"number":751,"text":"native-constructability failure eliminates a candidate. Unknown evidence\n"},{"number":752,"text":"remains unknown and cannot be converted into a favourable score. A\n"},{"number":753,"text":"universal scalar is not required. Lawful candidates that remain materially\n"},{"number":754,"text":"incomparable form an explicit undominated frontier (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":755,"text":"\n"},{"number":756,"text":"One lawful candidate composition dominates another on the current basis\n"},{"number":757,"text":"only when every material decision dimension is comparable or evidenced as\n"},{"number":758,"text":"non-discriminating between them, it is no worse on every comparable\n"},{"number":759,"text":"dimension, and it is strictly better on at least one. A material unknown\n"},{"number":760,"text":"that could reverse the relation prevents dominance and remains a gap. A\n"},{"number":761,"text":"dominated candidate cannot be selected unless new evidence or another\n"},{"number":762,"text":"material dimension invalidates the dominance relation; therefore a local\n"},{"number":763,"text":"rebuild of generic mechanics is inadmissible when an existing lawful\n"},{"number":764,"text":"foundation composition dominates it. Unused feature breadth alone does not\n"},{"number":765,"text":"establish dominance and may itself add lifecycle cost (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":766,"text":"\n"},{"number":767,"text":"The existing trade-off owner may select an undominated lawful composition\n"},{"number":768,"text":"only by applying priorities and risk tolerances declared for the exact\n"},{"number":769,"text":"Product and basis and recording how they resolve the frontier. If those\n"},{"number":770,"text":"priorities and tolerances do not resolve the frontier, the choice remains\n"},{"number":771,"text":"an explicit design gap. The selected construction is not necessarily the\n"},{"number":772,"text":"fewest dependencies, smallest immediate edit, lowest local line count or\n"},{"number":773,"text":"richest feature set. A rejected material candidate records the decisive\n"},{"number":774,"text":"evidence or falsifier. Unsupported preference is not design closure (P6).\n"},{"number":775,"text":"\n"},{"number":776,"text":"Reuse does not automatically confer or transfer semantic, admission or\n"},{"number":777,"text":"other operation authority (IDENTITY §6; an instance of\n"},{"number":778,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What\n"},{"number":779,"text":"creates no authority). A selected foundation may realise\n"},{"number":780,"text":"an explicitly assigned authority-bearing role when accepted design\n"},{"number":781,"text":"preserves the declared relation's owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis\n"},{"number":782,"text":"and material lifecycle and refusal invariants. Foundation capability,\n"},{"number":783,"text":"provenance or source authorship cannot widen or remint that role.\n"},{"number":784,"text":"Ownership belongs to the declared relation, not necessarily to locally\n"},{"number":785,"text":"written code; an irreducible Product or domain relation retains its\n"},{"number":786,"text":"declared owner whether local code, a reused foundation or their\n"},{"number":787,"text":"composition realises it. Generic local code is lawful only when it wins\n"},{"number":788,"text":"the same comparison; it is not the default (P6).\n"},{"number":789,"text":"\n"},{"number":790,"text":"If construction exposes another material generic subproblem, that\n"},{"number":791,"text":"subproblem recursively re-enters this selection relation before its\n"},{"number":792,"text":"implementation is retained. This prior selection pass is distinct from\n"},{"number":793,"text":"recurrence extraction (§10): recurrence review detects repeated\n"},{"number":794,"text":"realisation after patterns exist, while this rule prevents avoidable\n"},{"number":795,"text":"reproduction before construction (P2). Apply the pass proportionally. It\n"},{"number":796,"text":"is mandatory for material algorithms, common mechanics, new dependencies\n"},{"number":797,"text":"and locally rebuilt foundation capabilities. It does not require a package\n"},{"number":798,"text":"survey or ledger for a trivial helper whose choice cannot materially affect\n"},{"number":799,"text":"authority, Product behaviour, lifecycle cost or the accepted design network\n"},{"number":800,"text":"(P2; ACTIVATION §6).\n"},{"number":801,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":833,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Entity and lifecycle completeness","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FEntity%20and%20lifecycle%20completeness","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"88892303f72c817d654bd05cba18986590c93c30652a4538c39514a528696bde","start_line":802,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":802,"text":"### Entity and lifecycle completeness\n"},{"number":803,"text":"\n"},{"number":804,"text":"The Ontology enumerates the entities inside the active boundary, their\n"},{"number":805,"text":"identities, relationships, cardinalities, invariants, lifecycle states and\n"},{"number":806,"text":"authority owners (P3, P5). For\n"},{"number":807,"text":"each entity, design evidence provides this logical-completeness matrix or\n"},{"number":808,"text":"an equivalent closed representation:\n"},{"number":809,"text":"\n"},{"number":810,"text":"| Entity | Identity | Authority owner | Declare/create | Read/project | Update/transition | Delete/retire |\n"},{"number":811,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":812,"text":"\n"},{"number":813,"text":"The matrix applies to identity-bearing entities and independently governed\n"},{"number":814,"text":"value families (P3, P2).
