A Subordinate Payload or value object inherits the\n"},{"number":815,"text":"lifecycle and authority of its owning entity unless it passes the\n"},{"number":816,"text":"Promotion Test (§6); it does not require a ceremonial peer lifecycle row.\n"},{"number":817,"text":"\n"},{"number":818,"text":"The lifecycle columns are completeness questions, not a mandate for\n"},{"number":819,"text":"mutable CRUD: create may be declaration, construction, admission or\n"},{"number":820,"text":"materialisation; read should normally be a typed projection over\n"},{"number":821,"text":"authoritative truth; update should normally be an admitted transition or\n"},{"number":822,"text":"new version rather than in-place semantic mutation; delete should normally\n"},{"number":823,"text":"be retirement, revocation, decommission or supersession where history or\n"},{"number":824,"text":"identity has to remain true (P3). Every cell identifies a lawful function,\n"},{"number":825,"text":"declares `not_applicable` with a reason, or names a `Gap:` or\n"},{"number":826,"text":"`Unanswered:` item and owner. Silence is not logical-completeness evidence\n"},{"number":827,"text":"(P5, P6).\n"},{"number":828,"text":"\n"},{"number":829,"text":"This entity lifecycle is distinct from the operational module lifecycle of\n"},{"number":830,"text":"ASSURANCE §16: the Ontology describes what states and transformations\n"},{"number":831,"text":"exist for domain entities; ASSURANCE §16 confirms how the resulting\n"},{"number":832,"text":"realisation is built, released, deployed, observed and retired (P1).\n"},{"number":833,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":871,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Authority model","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FAuthority%20model","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"6590c06509f8faab8efba7474234ffbec90694c0055cfddcf1a1994d92e90210","start_line":834,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":834,"text":"### Authority model\n"},{"number":835,"text":"\n"},{"number":836,"text":"Authority is part of the Ontology, not metadata added to an operation\n"},{"number":837,"text":"after its shape has been selected (P6). For every\n"},{"number":838,"text":"Ontology function or lifecycle transition that crosses a semantic,\n"},{"number":839,"text":"authority, admission, effect, persistence or public boundary, design\n"},{"number":840,"text":"evidence provides this authority matrix or an equivalent closed\n"},{"number":841,"text":"representation:\n"},{"number":842,"text":"\n"},{"number":843,"text":"| Function or transition | Proposer | Evaluator | Verifier | Admitter | Executor | Projector | Retirement owner |\n"},{"number":844,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":845,"text":"\n"},{"number":846,"text":"The model distinguishes actor identity from authority; available\n"},{"number":847,"text":"capability from authority admitted for the current basis; proposal from\n"},{"number":848,"text":"evaluation, verification, admission, execution, projection and retirement;\n"},{"number":849,"text":"attribution from permission; and ownership of domain meaning from\n"},{"number":850,"text":"ownership of runtime effects (P6; FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds). One\n"},{"number":851,"text":"owner may lawfully occupy more than one role only when the governing\n"},{"number":852,"text":"authority explicitly says so; role coincidence is not inferred from\n"},{"number":853,"text":"implementation convenience. Pure subordinate helpers inherit the authority\n"},{"number":854,"text":"envelope of their owning Ontology function and do not require peer\n"},{"number":855,"text":"authority rows unless they cross one of those boundaries.\n"},{"number":856,"text":"\n"},{"number":857,"text":"What cannot create authority is stated once in\n"},{"number":858,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What\n"},{"number":859,"text":"creates no authority. This paragraph applies its items on composition,\n"},{"number":860,"text":"projection, labels, capability strings and payload shape to the Ontology's\n"},{"number":861,"text":"functions and adds only these design instances (P6; IDENTITY §6).\n"},{"number":862,"text":"Composition does not widen authority implicitly: a composed or\n"},{"number":863,"text":"higher-order function has no more authority than the authority law\n"},{"number":864,"text":"admitted for its inputs, constituent functions and current basis.\n"},{"number":865,"text":"Delegation, elevation, transfer or retirement authority requires a named\n"},{"number":866,"text":"typed transition and an owning admission boundary; these carry in the\n"},{"number":867,"text":"design the explicit authority decision that FOUNDATIONS requires and do not\n"},{"number":868,"text":"replace it. Projections cannot create authority, and downstream code\n"},{"number":869,"text":"cannot reconstruct an authority witness from actor labels, capability\n"},{"number":870,"text":"strings or payload shape.\n"},{"number":871,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":949,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Transformation admission completeness (UP-016)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FTransformation%20admission%20completeness%20%28UP-016%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"56d999daa5be981f745cd0cc404d672f2bc0966df9729d0baacee0a78c8f054d","start_line":872,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":872,"text":"### Transformation admission completeness (UP-016)\n"},{"number":873,"text":"\n"},{"number":874,"text":"The authority matrix names who admits; it does not by itself establish the\n"},{"number":875,"text":"relation that decides which candidate transformation becomes durable\n"},{"number":876,"text":"entity truth. Two designs can complete the matrix plausibly and still leave\n"},{"number":877,"text":"two materially different ways to admit the same transformation (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":878,"text":"\n"},{"number":879,"text":"For every consequential entity-transition domain, design evidence contains\n"},{"number":880,"text":"the complete transformation-admission relation over entity identity,\n"},{"number":881,"text":"predecessor basis, authority scope, candidate family, decision\n"},{"number":882,"text":"cardinality, admission predicate, resulting durable fact and supersession\n"},{"number":883,"text":"law, through the authority matrix or an equivalent closed representation\n"},{"number":884,"text":"(P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":885,"text":"\n"},{"number":886,"text":"| Entity transition domain | Predecessor basis | Candidate family | Admission relation | Durable result | Competing-path disposition |\n"},{"number":887,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":888,"text":"\n"},{"number":889,"text":"For every material admission relation, accepted design declares, in one\n"},{"number":890,"text":"compact relation or equivalent representation (P6, P4b, P3):\n"},{"number":891,"text":"\n"},{"number":892,"text":"- each admission owner and supported admission boundary;\n"},{"number":893,"text":"- the exact admission-valid basis identity, predecessor and currentness\n"},{"number":894,"text":"  continuity through admission, and any equal or coherent composite\n"},{"number":895,"text":"  multi-owner basis;\n"},{"number":896,"text":"- the complete enclosing relation, participant identities and equality\n"},{"number":897,"text":"  joins;\n"},{"number":898,"text":"- refusal and effect boundaries;\n"},{"number":899,"text":"- the complete semantic commit unit and its decomposability: every\n"},{"number":900,"text":"  materially distinct post-validation commit or publication boundary\n"},{"number":901,"text":"  capable of exposing a subset, or a design-declared dominance or\n"},{"number":902,"text":"  equivalence proof that named representative observations cover the\n"},{"number":903,"text":"  complete partial-failure surface;\n"},{"number":904,"text":"- reconstruction and the supported direct, composite and nested forms; and\n"},{"number":905,"text":"- competing-path disposition.\n"},{"number":906,"text":"\n"},{"number":907,"text":"The declaration binds the admission and standing-test semantics of\n"},{"number":908,"text":"ACTIVATION §4 (Complete enclosing-relation admission; Standing structural\n"},{"number":909,"text":"qualification), which solely owns them. Qualification is instantiated per\n"},{"number":910,"text":"owner and supported boundary. Unsupported composite or nested forms use\n"},{"number":911,"text":"`not_applicable` only when accepted domain or design excludes the form and\n"},{"number":912,"text":"the boundary has no weaker or competing admission path (P6, P4b). This\n"},{"number":913,"text":"obligation is false if a field, owner or supported boundary is missing or\n"},{"number":914,"text":"invented downstream; if basis continuity, partial-failure boundary\n"},{"number":915,"text":"coverage or its dominance or equivalence proof, or reconstruction is left\n"},{"number":916,"text":"to implementation inference; or if non-applicability is established only\n"},{"number":917,"text":"by a parser, helper or manufactured refusal.\n"},{"number":918,"text":"\n"},{"number":919,"text":"Singularity attaches to the complete decision relation, not to one actor,\n"},{"number":920,"text":"callable or component. Several actors, stages or implementations are\n"},{"number":921,"text":"lawful as constituents or disjoint instances of that relation. A relation\n"},{"number":922,"text":"may lawfully require one actor, several signatures, a quorum, a human\n"},{"number":923,"text":"step-up, delegated proxy authority or jurisdictional partitioning, provided\n"},{"number":924,"text":"its cardinality and adjudication law are declared (P6).\n"},{"number":925,"text":"\n"},{"number":926,"text":"Competing-path disposition does not imply deletion. An equivalent path may\n"},{"number":927,"text":"be a lawful constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent\n"},{"number":928,"text":"realisation, provided its relationship to the singular admission law is\n"},{"number":929,"text":"explicit. A superseded responsibility remains subject to SPEC_METHOD §7\n"},{"number":930,"text":"Core interface migration: retention requires a distinct supported purpose,\n"},{"number":931,"text":"not merely a path label or an existing test (P6, P2). A projection may\n"},{"number":932,"text":"produce a candidate transformation, but projection status does not confer\n"},{"number":933,"text":"admission authority; any consequential result re-enters the governing\n"},{"number":934,"text":"admission relation against its explicit predecessor basis, and a\n"},{"number":935,"text":"reconstructed projection state is not self-authenticating admission\n"},{"number":936,"text":"evidence (P6; projection is an item of\n"},{"number":937,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What\n"},{"number":938,"text":"creates no authority).\n"},{"number":939,"text":"\n"},{"number":940,"text":"This law is false if any of the following holds (P6, P4b): two materially\n"},{"number":941,"text":"non-equivalent admission relations remain reachable for the same governed\n"},{"number":942,"text":"transition domain on the same entity identity, authority scope and\n"},{"number":943,"text":"predecessor basis (disjoint scopes or identities are not a\n"},{"number":944,"text":"counterexample); a materially equivalent competing implementation remains\n"},{"number":945,"text":"reachable without being identified as a constituent, replica, replacement\n"},{"number":946,"text":"or deliberately independent realisation; or a projection-triggered\n"},{"number":947,"text":"reaction uses its own reconstructive state as self-authenticating\n"},{"number":948,"text":"admission evidence.\n"},{"number":949,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":986,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Atomic functions and higher-order composition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FAtomic%20functions%20and%20higher-order%20composition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"5c8e9dbd5e019aa1797cf206d0a847cc0502a4c6e1cec59c812700391fbd7027","start_line":950,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":950,"text":"### Atomic functions and higher-order composition\n"},{"number":951,"text":"\n"},{"number":952,"text":"The Ontology derives the smallest parameterised atomic function families\n"},{"number":953,"text":"that make the entity lifecycles logically complete. Variation that changes\n"},{"number":954,"text":"only an entity kind, projection kind, transition kind, policy or\n"},{"number":955,"text":"subordinate payload should normally be a typed parameter or closed variant\n"},{"number":956,"text":"of one function family, not another peer function (P4a, P3). The minimum\n"},{"number":957,"text":"function-derivation evidence is:\n"},{"number":958,"text":"\n"},{"number":959,"text":"| Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |\n"},{"number":960,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":961,"text":"\n"},{"number":962,"text":"Every row is one of: derived through an admitted atomic function; derived\n"},{"number":963,"text":"through a declared higher-order composition; deferred with an owner and\n"},{"number":964,"text":"re-entry condition; excluded by current product authority; or unresolved\n"},{"number":965,"text":"as a named gap (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":966,"text":"\n"},{"number":967,"text":"Where the boundary has higher-order behaviour, the Ontology names the\n"},{"number":968,"text":"governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories include unit\n"},{"number":969,"text":"or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold\n"},{"number":970,"text":"or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and\n"},{"number":971,"text":"projection. The design states the applicable identity, closure,\n"},{"number":972,"text":"associativity, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws rather\n"},{"number":973,"text":"than hiding them in controller flow (P4a, P6; FOUNDATIONS §4 Composition).\n"},{"number":974,"text":"This does not require monadic or category-theory vocabulary\n"},{"number":975,"text":"(SPEC_METHOD §2 Realisation shape). A product under the graph-execution\n"},{"number":976,"text":"profile may bind the requirement to GTL composition and ABG\n"},{"number":977,"text":"interpretation; another product may use another explicit algebra.\n"},{"number":978,"text":"\n"},{"number":979,"text":"Composition, effects and implementation may be discovered iteratively only\n"},{"number":980,"text":"when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds. Otherwise only a disposable spike\n"},{"number":981,"text":"may supply evidence across the affected unresolved, contradictory or\n"},{"number":982,"text":"materially non-equivalent relation before its design is accepted. Every\n"},{"number":983,"text":"retained result is reconciled into accepted design before promotion or\n"},{"number":984,"text":"design-method closure. No private helper, loop, adapter or endpoint may\n"},{"number":985,"text":"become an undeclared constructor (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":986,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1014,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Prime semantic atoms and admitted domain","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FPrime%20semantic%20atoms%20and%20admitted%20domain","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"9e8e8b45acf8e8d8e5bcb006fd29dbc73225b01a4ef8f73287c9b6d3ec81584e","start_line":987,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":987,"text":"### Prime semantic atoms and admitted domain\n"},{"number":988,"text":"\n"},{"number":989,"text":"A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic\n"},{"number":990,"text":"function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,\n"},{"number":991,"text":"topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed\n"},{"number":992,"text":"honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same\n"},{"number":993,"text":"meaning (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":994,"text":"\n"},{"number":995,"text":"Prime is decided at semantic-design altitude. A file, source function,\n"},{"number":996,"text":"class, schema record, public operation, diagram, module or owner category\n"},{"number":997,"text":"is not a Prime atom merely because it is small, typed, separately named or\n"},{"number":998,"text":"independently testable. One atom may project into several realisation\n"},{"number":999,"text":"units, and one realisation unit may implement several atoms, provided the\n"},{"number":1000,"text":"mapping is explicit and introduces no rival meaning or authority. An\n"},{"number":1001,"text":"atomic function is not proven Prime until the complete candidate family has\n"},{"number":1002,"text":"been contracted (whole-family Prime contraction, below; P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1003,"text":"\n"},{"number":1004,"text":"Every accepted Prime atom declares the admitted domain over which its law\n"},{"number":1005,"text":"holds, and within that domain it governs every admitted instance. A later\n"},{"number":1006,"text":"use case composes or parameterises the atom; it does not fork, shadow,\n"},{"number":1007,"text":"specialise or reinterpret the atom locally. An out-of-domain case may\n"},{"number":1008,"text":"justify proposing another candidate atom for design admission. An\n"},{"number":1009,"text":"in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and re-enters at that\n"},{"number":1010,"text":"atom's design boundary rather than authorising a feature-local replacement\n"},{"number":1011,"text":"(P3, P6). An atom without a declared admitted domain remains a candidate\n"},{"number":1012,"text":"atom; it cannot supply Prime acceptance or Prime-conformance to a\n"},{"number":1013,"text":"realisation projection.\n"},{"number":1014,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1042,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Whole-family Prime contraction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FWhole-family%20Prime%20contraction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"fab105e82bc57e27946a273a8514b70572fe2b3a786756bc65eff83fb041a8ce","start_line":1015,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1015,"text":"### Whole-family Prime contraction\n"},{"number":1016,"text":"\n"},{"number":1017,"text":"Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and\n"},{"number":1018,"text":"every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or\n"},{"number":1019,"text":"each atom in isolation. The family includes every proposed identity,\n"},{"number":1020,"text":"authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, function, composition\n"},{"number":1021,"text":"law, effect and closure law. A function-and-carrier-only pass does not\n"},{"number":1022,"text":"establish whole-family Prime (P3, P2). Before promotion, review asks:\n"},{"number":1023,"text":"\n"},{"number":1024,"text":"- can several proposed operations be typed parameters of one atomic\n"},{"number":1025,"text":"  function?\n"},{"number":1026,"text":"- are several commands lifecycle transitions over one entity?\n"},{"number":1027,"text":"- are several reads projections over one source truth?\n"},{"number":1028,"text":"- are several implementations applications of one higher-order function?\n"},{"number":1029,"text":"- does the candidate introduce independent identity, authority, effect,\n"},{"number":1030,"text":"  lifecycle, reuse or public pattern-match semantics?\n"},{"number":1031,"text":"- has every candidate atom kind entered the same contraction?\n"},{"number":1032,"text":"- does every realisation unit map explicitly to its accepted atom or\n"},{"number":1033,"text":"  atoms?\n"},{"number":1034,"text":"- does any realisation projection introduce, duplicate or reinterpret\n"},{"number":1035,"text":"  meaning or authority?\n"},{"number":1036,"text":"\n"},{"number":1037,"text":"A family of individually plausible functions is not Prime when one\n"},{"number":1038,"text":"parameterised template plus closed variants carries the same meaning and\n"},{"number":1039,"text":"authority. Recurrence is contracted during design when visible; the\n"},{"number":1040,"text":"post-implementation recurrence rule (§10) is not a substitute for this\n"},{"number":1041,"text":"prior pass (P2).\n"},{"number":1042,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1063,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Recursive Prime and root conservation (UP-003)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FRecursive%20Prime%20and%20root%20conservation%20%28UP-003%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"e5c5be408a5127a2bf347c43652365bde9069a08de65471b3478f6e5c246ed53","start_line":1043,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1043,"text":"### Recursive Prime and root conservation (UP-003)\n"},{"number":1044,"text":"\n"},{"number":1045,"text":"At a material semantic boundary, Prime contraction applies to each\n"},{"number":1046,"text":"candidate semantic atom and then to the complete family produced by those\n"},{"number":1047,"text":"contractions. A locally irreducible atom is not globally Prime when the\n"},{"number":1048,"text":"family duplicates identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology,\n"},{"number":1049,"text":"effect or projection meaning. Local Prime-conformance of realisation units\n"},{"number":1050,"text":"does not prove the semantic family globally Prime (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1051,"text":"\n"},{"number":1052,"text":"Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation.\n"},{"number":1053,"text":"Reducing files, functions, operations or authoring surfaces cannot\n"},{"number":1054,"text":"compensate for introducing another authority source or truth path (P6,\n"},{"number":1055,"text":"P4b). Prime evidence states the complete candidate semantic-atom family;\n"},{"number":1056,"text":"each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and\n"},{"number":1057,"text":"falsification condition; the whole-family contraction relation; retained\n"},{"number":1058,"text":"meaning and authority before and after contraction; accepted loss; and the\n"},{"number":1059,"text":"explicit total mapping from every proposed realisation projection to its\n"},{"number":1060,"text":"accepted atom or atoms (P4b, FOUNDATIONS §4 Conservation accounting). Work\n"},{"number":1061,"text":"inside an accepted boundary cites the existing Prime basis rather than\n"},{"number":1062,"text":"recreating it (P2).\n"},{"number":1063,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1089,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/5. Ontology-first design/Ontology projection","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F5.%20Ontology-first%20design%2FOntology%20projection","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"deaf8d609c21a1e7b8163718dc8e318472cda24b86dc89c09bbd53ce55e57866","start_line":1064,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1064,"text":"### Ontology projection\n"},{"number":1065,"text":"\n"},{"number":1066,"text":"The Ontology is one semantic truth (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1067,"text":"These preserve it and do not become independent semantic authorities:\n"},{"number":1068,"text":"class or domain diagrams; sequence diagrams; state and lifecycle diagrams;\n"},{"number":1069,"text":"authority and effect matrices; the IACS; public APIs, operation registers,\n"},{"number":1070,"text":"SDK and CLI surfaces; schemas, codecs, manifests and generated catalogues;\n"},{"number":1071,"text":"target architecture and module design; implementation modules through\n"},{"number":1072,"text":"accepted target design; and test and proof inventories through\n"},{"number":1073,"text":"requirements and accepted design.\n"},{"number":1074,"text":"\n"},{"number":1075,"text":"Each design projection identifies its Ontology source and the identity,\n"},{"number":1076,"text":"relationship, lifecycle, authority, function or effect law it preserves.\n"},{"number":1077,"text":"Any intentional omission or flattening declares accepted loss and a\n"},{"number":1078,"text":"failure condition (FOUNDATIONS §4 Reference versus body). Target design\n"},{"number":1079,"text":"may add structural HOW absent from the Ontology, but it may not originate\n"},{"number":1080,"text":"rival semantic meaning. Implementation and tests trace through that\n"},{"number":1081,"text":"accepted design rather than bypassing it (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1082,"text":"\n"},{"number":1083,"text":"If a public operation, sequence message, state transition, carrier or\n"},{"number":1084,"text":"effect cannot be traced through accepted design to the accepted Ontology,\n"},{"number":1085,"text":"it is ungrounded design and does not enter the active product line. An\n"},{"number":1086,"text":"implementation branch or test expectation traces to requirements plus\n"},{"number":1087,"text":"accepted design; it preserves, but need not be enumerated by, the\n"},{"number":1088,"text":"Ontology (P6; SPEC_METHOD §2 Trace closure and anti-drift).\n"},{"number":1089,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1141,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"9739a3fee19ad5acc3669400f6575b49cda5e69cc7ee377e88720dd5baa63f04","start_line":1090,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1090,"text":"## 6. Prime law\n"},{"number":1091,"text":"\n"},{"number":1092,"text":"Using the logically complete candidate Ontology, derive the Prime semantic\n"},{"number":1093,"text":"atoms before proposing top-level realisation units. Whole-family Prime is\n"},{"number":1094,"text":"part of the evidence used to accept the Ontology basis. Target design,\n"},{"number":1095,"text":"IACS, modules, source functions, schemas and tests project those accepted\n"},{"number":1096,"text":"atoms; they do not originate Prime meaning. Prime applies both to each\n"},{"number":1097,"text":"semantic atom and to the candidate family as a whole (P3, P2).\n"},{"number":1098,"text":"\n"},{"number":1099,"text":"Prime-conformance applies to these realisation projections: functions,\n"},{"number":1100,"text":"classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules. Typed\n"},{"number":1101,"text":"closure by itself is not sufficient reason to create a new top-level type.\n"},{"number":1102,"text":"The hard vocabulary of this law (P1):\n"},{"number":1103,"text":"\n"},{"number":1104,"text":"- Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set (IACS): the smallest lawful\n"},{"number":1105,"text":"  top-level carrier family required for one boundary;\n"},{"number":1106,"text":"- Subordinate Payload: payload detail that exists inside that boundary but\n"},{"number":1107,"text":"  is not top-level by default;\n"},{"number":1108,"text":"- Promotion Test: the explicit test a Subordinate Payload passes before it\n"},{"number":1109,"text":"  becomes a top-level type; and\n"},{"number":1110,"text":"- Boundary Inflation: the defect where subordinate payload detail is\n"},{"number":1111,"text":"  promoted into extra peer types without irreducible need.\n"},{"number":1112,"text":"\n"},{"number":1113,"text":"A top-level realisation unit is Prime-conformant only when it projects one\n"},{"number":1114,"text":"or more accepted Prime atoms without introducing, duplicating or\n"},{"number":1115,"text":"reinterpreting semantic authority. A topological or effect boundary is\n"},{"number":1116,"text":"first derived and accepted as a Prime atom. Source-code size and\n"},{"number":1117,"text":"one-to-one correspondence with an atom are immaterial (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1118,"text":"\n"},{"number":1119,"text":"Typical lawful reasons to introduce a new top-level realisation unit are a\n"},{"number":1120,"text":"new feature topology or branch in the admitted work graph, a new typed\n"},{"number":1121,"text":"carrier transformation, a new effect boundary, a new validation or\n"},{"number":1122,"text":"admission boundary, and a new projection boundary. A realisation unit is\n"},{"number":1123,"text":"not Prime-conformant when it exists only to: shorten a call site without\n"},{"number":1124,"text":"creating a new semantic boundary; aggregate unrelated behaviour for\n"},{"number":1125,"text":"convenience; preserve an old interface behind a new name; shuttle data\n"},{"number":1126,"text":"through one more wrapper layer; hide mutation, fallback or orchestration\n"},{"number":1127,"text":"that should remain explicit; name one more payload variation that carries\n"},{"number":1128,"text":"no independent authority; turn internal record detail into public schema\n"},{"number":1129,"text":"surface without an irreducible boundary; mirror another top-level carrier\n"},{"number":1130,"text":"with only small field variation; or respond to typing discomfort by\n"},{"number":1131,"text":"multiplying peer classes instead of closing one governing carrier family\n"},{"number":1132,"text":"(P3, P2).\n"},{"number":1133,"text":"\n"},{"number":1134,"text":"This is Occam's razor for design modules: prefer composition over\n"},{"number":1135,"text":"convenience extraction; prefer existing lawful functions over new\n"},{"number":1136,"text":"wrappers; prefer fewer, sharper boundaries over many vague helper\n"},{"number":1137,"text":"functions; prefer fewer, sharper carrier families over many payload-shaped\n"},{"number":1138,"text":"peer types. The purpose of the Prime law is not to minimise line count; it\n"},{"number":1139,"text":"is to stop semantic fragmentation and helper sprawl from becoming\n"},{"number":1140,"text":"architecture (P2).\n"},{"number":1141,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1155,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law/Boundary and governance cost (UP-005)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law%2FBoundary%20and%20governance%20cost%20%28UP-005%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"28d2d304e4a41e123aaeca619011784e14e9ba5bdcc186f3b825231d9fd80735","start_line":1142,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1142,"text":"### Boundary and governance cost (UP-005)\n"},{"number":1143,"text":"\n"},{"number":1144,"text":"The proportionality relation that weighs ambiguity removed against\n"},{"number":1145,"text":"reasoning complexity introduced is ACTIVATION §6; this clause applies it to\n"},{"number":1146,"text":"Prime contraction (P2, P0). Review cuts, realisation\n"},{"number":1147,"text":"units, runtime modules and work items are distinct boundaries. They may\n"},{"number":1148,"text":"relate many-to-one or one-to-many and are not forced into one-to-one\n"},{"number":1149,"text":"decomposition for administrative convenience. Prime review accounts for\n"},{"number":1150,"text":"governance cost as well as implementation count: contraction is not\n"},{"number":1151,"text":"successful when it increases authority centres, maintained truth surfaces,\n"},{"number":1152,"text":"acceptance boundaries, dependency cycles, manually reconciled projections\n"},{"number":1153,"text":"or review burden. Evidence remains proportional to semantic change and\n"},{"number":1154,"text":"risk; this rule does not require one artifact or review per concern.\n"},{"number":1155,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1202,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law/Irreducible architectural carrier set","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law%2FIrreducible%20architectural%20carrier%20set","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"9bbf3e897fdca8031484f933ea9522f393e8d0f1ddee7ce5cdd140f1cd0b405b","start_line":1156,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1156,"text":"### Irreducible architectural carrier set\n"},{"number":1157,"text":"\n"},{"number":1158,"text":"When defining a schema, carrier family or typed public boundary, derive\n"},{"number":1159,"text":"the IACS from the accepted Ontology before naming subordinate payloads or\n"},{"number":1160,"text":"implementation modules (P3, P6). The IACS is the smallest\n"},{"number":1161,"text":"set of carriers required to carry the real functionality and authority\n"},{"number":1162,"text":"flow of the boundary. It should be named before subordinate payload\n"},{"number":1163,"text":"records, helper result shapes or internal branch detail. It is the carrier\n"},{"number":1164,"text":"inventory the design declares, to which ASSURANCE §2, §7 and §15 bind\n"},{"number":1165,"text":"design and module conformance tests and unit proof (the binding declared\n"},{"number":1166,"text":"at the head of this member).\n"},{"number":1167,"text":"\n"},{"number":1168,"text":"Examples of irreducible architectural carrier roles (P3) include the source\n"},{"number":1169,"text":"truth carrier, admission carrier, execution carrier, yielded or recovery\n"},{"number":1170,"text":"carrier, effect plan carrier and public projection carrier. These do not\n"},{"number":1171,"text":"automatically justify a top-level carrier: one more branch-specific\n"},{"number":1172,"text":"payload shape; one more internal persistence detail; one more read-model\n"},{"number":1173,"text":"row shape; one more field grouping extracted only to make typing easier.\n"},{"number":1174,"text":"\n"},{"number":1175,"text":"The required carrier-set evidence (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":1176,"text":"\n"},{"number":1177,"text":"1. cite the accepted Ontology and function-derivation evidence;\n"},{"number":1178,"text":"2. declare the IACS;\n"},{"number":1179,"text":"3. map each carrier to the Ontology identity, lifecycle, function,\n"},{"number":1180,"text":"   authority, effect or projection law it carries;\n"},{"number":1181,"text":"4. declare which carriers are authoritative and which are downstream;\n"},{"number":1182,"text":"5. treat every other shape as a Subordinate Payload by default;\n"},{"number":1183,"text":"6. keep subordinate payload detail private unless it passes the Promotion\n"},{"number":1184,"text":"   Test; and\n"},{"number":1185,"text":"7. reconcile the typed implementation to that carrier set before claiming\n"},{"number":1186,"text":"   design-method closure.\n"},{"number":1187,"text":"\n"},{"number":1188,"text":"The IACS is a realisation projection of the Ontology. It does not replace\n"},{"number":1189,"text":"the Ontology or become the first surface on which entities, functions,\n"},{"number":1190,"text":"lifecycle or authority acquire meaning (P1, P6). If the accepted Ontology\n"},{"number":1191,"text":"or IACS has not been declared, the schema is not yet design-method\n"},{"number":1192,"text":"complete under this profile.\n"},{"number":1193,"text":"\n"},{"number":1194,"text":"When `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, Ontology, carrier-set evidence,\n"},{"number":1195,"text":"implementation and tests may develop together. Implementation may expose a\n"},{"number":1196,"text":"missing entity, relation, function or carrier, but it cannot self-ratify\n"},{"number":1197,"text":"that meaning. Before the affected boundary is promoted or claims\n"},{"number":1198,"text":"design-method closure, the Ontology and IACS are accepted and the typed\n"},{"number":1199,"text":"implementation is reconciled to them. Under design-gated sequencing, the\n"},{"number":1200,"text":"affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is\n"},{"number":1201,"text":"accepted before retained implementation establishes it (P6, P2; §5).\n"},{"number":1202,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1225,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law/IACS revision","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law%2FIACS%20revision","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"17e49cf33e2569e9b802ae54127fb22de23f3cc5e4a1167f8788cfd22cf205d2","start_line":1203,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1203,"text":"### IACS revision\n"},{"number":1204,"text":"\n"},{"number":1205,"text":"The IACS is not numerically frozen. Adding, removing, merging or splitting\n"},{"number":1206,"text":"a carrier is lawful through accepted Ontology and design re-entry (P6,\n"},{"number":1207,"text":"P4b). For every such revision, accepted\n"},{"number":1208,"text":"design:\n"},{"number":1209,"text":"\n"},{"number":1210,"text":"- re-derives the complete IACS and classifies every addition, removal,\n"},{"number":1211,"text":"  merge and split;\n"},{"number":1212,"text":"- reruns the Promotion Test and the Boundary Inflation prohibition over\n"},{"number":1213,"text":"  the full revised set, not only newly introduced carriers;\n"},{"number":1214,"text":"- updates every conformance or checker subject to the declared composite\n"},{"number":1215,"text":"  carrier relation under the assurance-boundary congruence law of\n"},{"number":1216,"text":"  EVALUATION §1 (with its freeze and revision in §3); and\n"},{"number":1217,"text":"- reconciles implementation to the revised set before promotion or\n"},{"number":1218,"text":"  closure.\n"},{"number":1219,"text":"\n"},{"number":1220,"text":"This obligation consumes that assurance law without restating it. A\n"},{"number":1221,"text":"prohibition without a lawful revision path is false. A revision is also\n"},{"number":1222,"text":"false if its gates inspect only new carriers, its assurance surfaces\n"},{"number":1223,"text":"retain a weaker or obsolete subject, or implementation is not reconciled\n"},{"number":1224,"text":"before closure (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":1225,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1248,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law/Promotion test","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law%2FPromotion%20test","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"cc6ef08810068d9c3a7c746b5b69744e2324ca739171fa77f0a5f415e04211e9","start_line":1226,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1226,"text":"### Promotion test\n"},{"number":1227,"text":"\n"},{"number":1228,"text":"A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record\n"},{"number":1229,"text":"justifies its existence as an architectural boundary, not merely as\n"},{"number":1230,"text":"payload detail (P3, P2). A Subordinate Payload may\n"},{"number":1231,"text":"be promoted to a top-level type only when at least one of these is true:\n"},{"number":1232,"text":"it is an authoritative source carrier; it is a public or persisted\n"},{"number":1233,"text":"contract boundary; it is an explicit variant of a public outcome family\n"},{"number":1234,"text":"that consumers pattern-match directly; it is reused across several modules\n"},{"number":1235,"text":"without semantic bleed; or it is versioned, published or admitted\n"},{"number":1236,"text":"independently.\n"},{"number":1237,"text":"\n"},{"number":1238,"text":"Promotion is not lawful when the candidate type is only internal record\n"},{"number":1239,"text":"detail of one larger carrier, a field grouping used once inside one\n"},{"number":1240,"text":"module, a temporary typing shim around an open dictionary, a private\n"},{"number":1241,"text":"payload variation that never crosses a true interface boundary, or a\n"},{"number":1242,"text":"mirror of another type with cosmetic or local field differences. Default\n"},{"number":1243,"text":"rule: if a shape does not need independent authority, independent reuse or\n"},{"number":1244,"text":"direct pattern-match semantics, it remains a Subordinate Payload and stays\n"},{"number":1245,"text":"nested, private or local to the carrier family. The burden of proof is on\n"},{"number":1246,"text":"promotion; designers and reviewers should assume a candidate type stays\n"},{"number":1247,"text":"subordinate until an irreducible boundary is shown (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1248,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1268,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law/Boundary inflation prohibition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law%2FBoundary%20inflation%20prohibition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"fd50c42552d3e7fe3528af804f7241b1d73677d50b0a9020942d6ff100632c47","start_line":1249,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1249,"text":"### Boundary inflation prohibition\n"},{"number":1250,"text":"\n"},{"number":1251,"text":"Schema work declares the IACS, which types are authoritative, which types\n"},{"number":1252,"text":"are downstream projections, which shapes are Subordinate Payloads, and\n"},{"number":1253,"text":"which Subordinate Payloads are intentionally deferred from promotion (P3,\n"},{"number":1254,"text":"P2). The rule exists to stop type\n"},{"number":1255,"text":"proliferation from turning one migration into many parallel schema\n"},{"number":1256,"text":"migrations. If a schema or ticket lists a wide family of types, it\n"},{"number":1257,"text":"distinguishes the IACS from the Subordinate Payloads; failing to make that\n"},{"number":1258,"text":"distinction is design drift. Typed closure does not excuse Boundary\n"},{"number":1259,"text":"Inflation.\n"},{"number":1260,"text":"\n"},{"number":1261,"text":"Boundary Inflation exists when payload detail is promoted into peer types\n"},{"number":1262,"text":"because the code feels hard to type; internal records are turned into\n"},{"number":1263,"text":"public schema surface without a new authoritative boundary; many\n"},{"number":1264,"text":"near-identical top-level types appear for one boundary where one carrier\n"},{"number":1265,"text":"family would suffice; or one migration ticket silently becomes several\n"},{"number":1266,"text":"parallel schema migrations. Boundary Inflation is design debt, not\n"},{"number":1267,"text":"progress (P2).\n"},{"number":1268,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1296,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/6. Prime law/Reference-derived module design","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F6.%20Prime%20law%2FReference-derived%20module%20design","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"6899182686757e57f2365b17cec634dd7713ce820f957e0608dae4c6869b4a48","start_line":1269,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1269,"text":"### Reference-derived module design\n"},{"number":1270,"text":"\n"},{"number":1271,"text":"When a realisation is being derived from an existing design line, released\n"},{"number":1272,"text":"tenant or reference implementation, design-method completion does not rest\n"},{"number":1273,"text":"on code comparison alone (P6, P4b). The required derivation\n"},{"number":1274,"text":"evidence is: (1) constitutional WHAT; (2) reference design; (3) target\n"},{"number":1275,"text":"Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping; (4) target design mapping; (5)\n"},{"number":1276,"text":"target module boundary assets; (6) implementation. The rule exists to stop\n"},{"number":1277,"text":"code-first ports from importing reference drift, delivery quirks, helper\n"},{"number":1278,"text":"sprawl or accidental authority paths into the new realisation without a\n"},{"number":1279,"text":"later audit trail.\n"},{"number":1280,"text":"\n"},{"number":1281,"text":"The minimum lawful design assets for a reference-derived module boundary\n"},{"number":1282,"text":"are: the named reference design surfaces being used as source material;\n"},{"number":1283,"text":"the accepted target Ontology, including the disposition of reference\n"},{"number":1284,"text":"entities, functions, lifecycle, authority, effects and projections; the\n"},{"number":1285,"text":"target design surfaces that replace or bind those source surfaces; an\n"},{"number":1286,"text":"explicit mapping that says what is preserved, reshaped, deferred or\n"},{"number":1287,"text":"demoted to delivery binding in the target line; and the target module\n"},{"number":1288,"text":"boundary assets required by this profile, including the Ontology-derived\n"},{"number":1289,"text":"IACS and the three-view design asset (§7) (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":1290,"text":"\n"},{"number":1291,"text":"The design question is not \"how do I port these files?\" but \"what is the\n"},{"number":1292,"text":"target module boundary, and how does the new realisation derive it from\n"},{"number":1293,"text":"the reference design without inheriting incidental implementation drift?\"\n"},{"number":1294,"text":"If a target realisation cannot show that derivation chain, it is not yet\n"},{"number":1295,"text":"design-method complete under this profile (P6).\n"},{"number":1296,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1321,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"1ad62e11d9177e06f626e2c58b166840536d59264afd34ed66e71cb168e70e4c","start_line":1297,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1297,"text":"## 7. Ontology and three-view design gate\n"},{"number":1298,"text":"\n"},{"number":1299,"text":"Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary carries\n"},{"number":1300,"text":"one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset\n"},{"number":1301,"text":"before the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure (P6, P1). When\n"},{"number":1302,"text":"`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, design evidence, implementation and\n"},{"number":1303,"text":"tests may develop together before that gate; otherwise the affected\n"},{"number":1304,"text":"unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation is\n"},{"number":1305,"text":"accepted before retained implementation establishes it. Unchanged\n"},{"number":1306,"text":"boundaries cite their accepted basis; local realisation work with no\n"},{"number":1307,"text":"material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate this gate (P2).\n"},{"number":1308,"text":"\n"},{"number":1309,"text":"The asset contains all three views: a Mermaid `classDiagram` domain model;\n"},{"number":1310,"text":"a Mermaid `sequenceDiagram` execution model; and a Mermaid\n"},{"number":1311,"text":"`stateDiagram-v2` lifecycle model. A project may ratify another text-native\n"},{"number":1312,"text":"diagram format only when it preserves the same three distinct views and the\n"},{"number":1313,"text":"same cross-view checks. One broad flowchart does not substitute for the\n"},{"number":1314,"text":"three models. The three views may be sections of one existing design\n"},{"number":1315,"text":"surface and may share one acceptance decision; this rule does not require\n"},{"number":1316,"text":"three files, three tickets, three reviews or three approval ceremonies\n"},{"number":1317,"text":"(P2). The views are not decorative and are not peer truth surfaces: they\n"},{"number":1318,"text":"are fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology, and together\n"},{"number":1319,"text":"the sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle\n"},{"number":1320,"text":"and axiom conformance (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1321,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1338,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Ontology evidence","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FOntology%20evidence","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"1622bae2eb5cba701957504cc495dbaf3ccd9748b9cfe9ecb85068d03a2135d1","start_line":1322,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1322,"text":"### Ontology evidence\n"},{"number":1323,"text":"\n"},{"number":1324,"text":"The design asset cites one accepted Ontology for the active boundary and\n"},{"number":1325,"text":"includes or references its (P6): entity and\n"},{"number":1326,"text":"relationship inventory; invariant and cardinality law; entity-lifecycle\n"},{"number":1327,"text":"completeness matrix; authority matrix; atomic-function and\n"},{"number":1328,"text":"higher-order-function derivation matrix; governing composition and effect\n"},{"number":1329,"text":"algebra where applicable; whole-family Prime contraction, including every\n"},{"number":1330,"text":"accepted atom's admitted domain and realisation-projection mapping; and\n"},{"number":1331,"text":"explicit deferred, excluded and unresolved functionality.\n"},{"number":1332,"text":"\n"},{"number":1333,"text":"The Ontology may be a boundary-bounded slice of a wider accepted product\n"},{"number":1334,"text":"Ontology. The slice cites its parent and preserves parent identity,\n"},{"number":1335,"text":"relationship, lifecycle, authority and function law. Copying selected rows\n"},{"number":1336,"text":"into a new local model without that derivation creates another truth\n"},{"number":1337,"text":"surface (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":1338,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1410,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Invariant reconstruction sufficiency (UP-018)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FInvariant%20reconstruction%20sufficiency%20%28UP-018%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"202228e15bfe1a2b9cd47e2070c94a10ae1e2bfaf3b76e95f475a8342d61eb8e","start_line":1339,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1339,"text":"### Invariant reconstruction sufficiency (UP-018)\n"},{"number":1340,"text":"\n"},{"number":1341,"text":"The evidence above is not a documentation deliverable. It is the durable\n"},{"number":1342,"text":"reasoning state a bounded actor needs, because the actor selecting a local\n"},{"number":1343,"text":"action generally does not hold the reasoning that produced the governing\n"},{"number":1344,"text":"frames. Dialogue, commentary, prior-agent memory and implementation\n"},{"number":1345,"text":"folklore are not that state (P0, P4b). The general\n"},{"number":1346,"text":"reconstruction rule is [ACTIVATION §1 Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake); this\n"},{"number":1347,"text":"clause states what design evidence supplies to it.\n"},{"number":1348,"text":"\n"},{"number":1349,"text":"Given an accepted material-frame basis, as determined by the material\n"},{"number":1350,"text":"semantic boundary definition (§5), and a proposed bounded action, the\n"},{"number":1351,"text":"selected method basis together with the accepted design is sufficient to\n"},{"number":1352,"text":"recover every governing relation in the action's causally closed affected\n"},{"number":1353,"text":"set, and to decide whether the action preserves, changes, duplicates or\n"},{"number":1354,"text":"violates each of those relations. The two inputs are distinct and neither\n"},{"number":1355,"text":"substitutes for the other: the selected method describes which relations\n"},{"number":1356,"text":"are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies\n"},{"number":1357,"text":"the concrete invariant values. A design that restates method decision law\n"},{"number":1358,"text":"to satisfy this rule reproduces the local-method duplication this law\n"},{"number":1359,"text":"exists to remove (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1360,"text":"\n"},{"number":1361,"text":"| Decision | The action, against a governing relation | Core value |\n"},{"number":1362,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":1363,"text":"| preserves | leaves the relation intact and operates inside it | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":1364,"text":"| changes | alters the relation itself, and therefore re-enters at that relation before acceptance | `invalid_basis` |\n"},{"number":1365,"text":"| duplicates | establishes an equivalent path that is explicitly disposed as a constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":1366,"text":"| violates | contradicts the relation, or establishes an equivalent path that is left undisposed | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":1367,"text":"\n"},{"number":1368,"text":"The boundary between changes and violates is the locus of acceptance, not\n"},{"number":1369,"text":"the size of the delta: an otherwise lawful change accepted inside the\n"},{"number":1370,"text":"acting frame rather than at the relation it changes is a violation. The\n"},{"number":1371,"text":"boundary between duplicates and violates is disposition, not equivalence:\n"},{"number":1372,"text":"an equivalent path is lawful when disposed and a defect when not (P4b,\n"},{"number":1373,"text":"P6). Sufficiency is bound to a declared action and its affected set; it is\n"},{"number":1374,"text":"not a claim over an unbounded space of possible future changes, and the\n"},{"number":1375,"text":"performance of any particular reviewer is not evidence either way (P0).\n"},{"number":1376,"text":"\n"},{"number":1377,"text":"The four decisions are a refinement of the core result algebra\n"},{"number":1378,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer what the\n"},{"number":1379,"text":"action does to one governing relation, and each maps to exactly one core\n"},{"number":1380,"text":"value for the predicate \"the action is admissible in the acting frame on\n"},{"number":1381,"text":"the current governing basis\"; the value travels with that predicate and\n"},{"number":1382,"text":"with the decision, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6). `preserves` and a\n"},{"number":1383,"text":"disposed `duplicates` leave the relation as accepted. For `changes`, the\n"},{"number":1384,"text":"relation itself must change at its own locus before the action can be\n"},{"number":1385,"text":"accepted, so the current governing basis cannot support accepting it in\n"},{"number":1386,"text":"the acting frame, as for the disposition `re_enter` of\n"},{"number":1387,"text":"[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#disposition). For `violates`, the\n"},{"number":1388,"text":"contradiction or the undisposed equivalent path is the counterexample. An\n"},{"number":1389,"text":"evaluation that reaches none of the four decisions returns the core value\n"},{"number":1390,"text":"its cause selects, `indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot\n"},{"number":1391,"text":"decide, naming what would decide (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results); where the\n"},{"number":1392,"text":"cause is that the selected method basis and the accepted design do not\n"},{"number":1393,"text":"suffice, the case falsifies this law, as stated below. Purpose and material relation: a lawful change is\n"},{"number":1394,"text":"never read as a violation or as an action the acting frame may accept, and\n"},{"number":1395,"text":"a violation is never read as a re-entry (P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":1396,"text":"\n"},{"number":1397,"text":"This obligation adds no artifact. It is satisfied through the Ontology\n"},{"number":1398,"text":"evidence, authority matrix, transformation-admission relation, frame\n"},{"number":1399,"text":"declaration, views and module mapping already required, and is a property\n"},{"number":1400,"text":"of that material rather than a separate package (P2). The law is false if,\n"},{"number":1401,"text":"for a declared bounded action, the accepted design does not expose a\n"},{"number":1402,"text":"governing relation in that action's causally closed affected set, or the\n"},{"number":1403,"text":"preserve, change, duplicate or violate decision cannot be reached from the\n"},{"number":1404,"text":"selected method basis and accepted design without conversation history,\n"},{"number":1405,"text":"commentary, prior-worker memory or implementation folklore. Where the\n"},{"number":1406,"text":"sufficiency of a boundary is tested, the test uses named cases with known\n"},{"number":1407,"text":"governing relations and expected decisions, evaluated with conversation\n"},{"number":1408,"text":"history, commentary, prior-worker memory and implementation folklore\n"},{"number":1409,"text":"withheld (P6; EVALUATION §3).\n"},{"number":1410,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1432,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Domain model","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FDomain%20model","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"26dcc8059ab5cac02e505bd0207f44373359fa493721fa9447dd6ec37919e36c","start_line":1411,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1411,"text":"### Domain model\n"},{"number":1412,"text":"\n"},{"number":1413,"text":"The `classDiagram` is the structural domain projection of the Ontology\n"},{"number":1414,"text":"(P1, P3). It shows, for the active boundary: domain\n"},{"number":1415,"text":"identities and cardinalities rather than helper-class decomposition;\n"},{"number":1416,"text":"entity ownership, invariants and lawful lifecycle relationships; atomic\n"},{"number":1417,"text":"function families and their entity inputs and outputs where they cross the\n"},{"number":1418,"text":"active boundary; higher-order composition relationships where they\n"},{"number":1419,"text":"determine boundary shape; IACS carriers and their Prime-atom projection\n"},{"number":1420,"text":"mappings; subordinate payloads; effect-edge-only payloads; downstream-only\n"},{"number":1421,"text":"projections; deferred families outside the active slice; authoritative\n"},{"number":1422,"text":"versus downstream role; public versus module-local visibility; and\n"},{"number":1423,"text":"composition, containment, association and real variant-family structure.\n"},{"number":1424,"text":"\n"},{"number":1425,"text":"The standard stereotype vocabulary is `<<prime-conformant>>`,\n"},{"number":1426,"text":"`<<subordinate>>`, `<<effect-edge>>`, `<<deferred>>`, `<<authoritative>>`\n"},{"number":1427,"text":"and `<<downstream>>`. The standard visibility vocabulary is `+` public or\n"},{"number":1428,"text":"exported and `-` module-local or private. The standard relationship\n"},{"number":1429,"text":"expectations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association\n"},{"number":1430,"text":"for downstream consumption, and inheritance only for real variant or\n"},{"number":1431,"text":"outcome families (P1).\n"},{"number":1432,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1449,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Sequence model","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FSequence%20model","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"b73b0f0974cd6f8eeb3a7294fa0d455ee281af0ad072ece04d6d52399af65627","start_line":1433,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1433,"text":"### Sequence model\n"},{"number":1434,"text":"\n"},{"number":1435,"text":"The `sequenceDiagram` is the behavioural projection of Ontology functions\n"},{"number":1436,"text":"and authority (P1, P6). It shows the supported\n"},{"number":1437,"text":"execution path from admitted input to result or truthful stop, and names\n"},{"number":1438,"text":"the owner and required authority of every decision, admission, execution,\n"},{"number":1439,"text":"projection and effect boundary. Where applicable it shows malformed input\n"},{"number":1440,"text":"or output, retry, recursion, fan-out and fan-in, nested workflow and human\n"},{"number":1441,"text":"escalation paths. Every participant exists in the domain model or is an\n"},{"number":1442,"text":"explicitly external actor. Every message binds to a declared carrier\n"},{"number":1443,"text":"transform, graph or computation constructor, interpreter action or\n"},{"number":1444,"text":"effect-handler call; a private loop, service method, plugin, shell or\n"},{"number":1445,"text":"script may not silently replace a declared workflow transition. Every\n"},{"number":1446,"text":"message also binds to an Ontology function and its admitted authority\n"},{"number":1447,"text":"role; actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorise a\n"},{"number":1448,"text":"message (P6).\n"},{"number":1449,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1460,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/State model","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FState%20model","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"ce25bcec5413bbbf7127c1fe6424e38dca3c46c17970772f4e32f4ebb08741a6","start_line":1450,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1450,"text":"### State model\n"},{"number":1451,"text":"\n"},{"number":1452,"text":"The `stateDiagram-v2` is the lifecycle projection of Ontology entities\n"},{"number":1453,"text":"(P3, P5). It shows the complete admitted lifecycle for\n"},{"number":1454,"text":"the active boundary, including refusal, blocked, continuation, retry,\n"},{"number":1455,"text":"escalation and terminal states that the boundary can produce. Every\n"},{"number":1456,"text":"transition binds to an Ontology function and names its owning authority,\n"},{"number":1457,"text":"admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act.\n"},{"number":1458,"text":"Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the\n"},{"number":1459,"text":"product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership (P6).\n"},{"number":1460,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1528,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Cross-view axiom evaluation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FCross-view%20axiom%20evaluation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"df9bcacae45024afe130273aeb68031eaf2c6f0111eef10b7186715acd6a1f88","start_line":1461,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1461,"text":"### Cross-view axiom evaluation\n"},{"number":1462,"text":"\n"},{"number":1463,"text":"The design pack evaluates every applicable product, graph, language,\n"},{"number":1464,"text":"runtime, handler and module axiom with one of `pass`, `fail` or\n"},{"number":1465,"text":"`not_applicable` with a reason (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1466,"text":"The minimum evaluation columns are:\n"},{"number":1467,"text":"\n"},{"number":1468,"text":"| Axiom | Ontology evidence | Authority | Domain evidence | Sequence evidence | State evidence | Native enforcement | Admission/compiler enforcement | Verdict | Gap owner |\n"},{"number":1469,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":1470,"text":"\n"},{"number":1471,"text":"The cross-view evaluation proves that: every element in each view derives\n"},{"number":1472,"text":"from the accepted Ontology; every discovered functionality row has a\n"},{"number":1473,"text":"derived, deferred, excluded or gap disposition; every sequence participant\n"},{"number":1474,"text":"and lifecycle carrier exists in the domain model; every sequence message\n"},{"number":1475,"text":"has a declared semantic or effect boundary; every lifecycle transition is\n"},{"number":1476,"text":"derivable from admitted truth; every function and transition has an\n"},{"number":1477,"text":"explicit authority path and composition does not widen that authority\n"},{"number":1478,"text":"implicitly; every public operation is a projection of an Ontology function\n"},{"number":1479,"text":"rather than an independently authored semantic peer; raw probabilistic\n"},{"number":1480,"text":"output cannot transition directly to accepted or closed; handlers and\n"},{"number":1481,"text":"plugins own interiors only when the runtime owns admission, events,\n"},{"number":1482,"text":"continuation and closure; native types enforce locally decidable\n"},{"number":1483,"text":"relations; and admission or semantic compilation owns global references,\n"},{"number":1484,"text":"completeness and realisation gaps (P1, P6, P5).\n"},{"number":1485,"text":"\n"},{"number":1486,"text":"For graph-native work, every batch, retry, recursion or nested workflow is\n"},{"number":1487,"text":"visible through the product's declared graph or compute algebra. A\n"},{"number":1488,"text":"relied-on `semantic_not_realized` constructor is a blocking gap; it may\n"},{"number":1489,"text":"not be replaced by imperative glue in a plugin, shell, service, script or\n"},{"number":1490,"text":"test harness (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":1491,"text":"\n"},{"number":1492,"text":"Axiom verdicts. The three verdicts are a refinement of the core result\n"},{"number":1493,"text":"algebra ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). They answer\n"},{"number":1494,"text":"what the design pack concludes about one axiom for the active boundary,\n"},{"number":1495,"text":"and each maps to exactly one core value for the predicate \"on the exact\n"},{"number":1496,"text":"Ontology and design basis, the boundary's design meets the axiom, or the\n"},{"number":1497,"text":"axiom does not apply to the boundary\"; the value travels with that\n"},{"number":1498,"text":"predicate and with the verdict, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6). This\n"},{"number":1499,"text":"profile declares that predicate as a disjunction that includes\n"},{"number":1500,"text":"non-application, the case that\n"},{"number":1501,"text":"[ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability), Exclusion and\n"},{"number":1502,"text":"the core, permits and bounds. That paragraph decides what follows for the\n"},{"number":1503,"text":"verdicts: `not_applicable` rests on a false applicability premise, an\n"},{"number":1504,"text":"unresolved premise supports no `not_applicable`, and the `satisfied` of a\n"},{"number":1505,"text":"`not_applicable` verdict counts toward this disjunction only, never toward\n"},{"number":1506,"text":"the predicate that the design meets the axiom:\n"},{"number":1507,"text":"\n"},{"number":1508,"text":"| Verdict | Ground | Core value |\n"},{"number":1509,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":1510,"text":"| `pass` | the cited Ontology, view and enforcement evidence establishes that the design meets the axiom | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":1511,"text":"| `not_applicable` | the axiom's applicability premise is false for the active boundary on basis-bound facts, and the reason names those facts and the authority whose scope declaration excludes the axiom ([ACTIVATION §1 Applicability](ACTIVATION.md#applicability)) | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":1512,"text":"| `fail` | the axiom applies, and the evidence names an element, message, transition, authority path or enforcement that violates it; that is the counterexample | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":1513,"text":"\n"},{"number":1514,"text":"The verdict, recorded with its value, keeps the distinction between not\n"},{"number":1515,"text":"applying and meeting the axiom (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Recording). An evaluated axiom that reaches none of the three\n"},{"number":1516,"text":"verdicts records in the Verdict column the core value its cause selects,\n"},{"number":1517,"text":"with what would decide it: `indeterminate` where the admissible evidence\n"},{"number":1518,"text":"cannot decide the predicate, as where the applicability premise is\n"},{"number":1519,"text":"unresolved and the design does not meet the axiom; `out_of_frame` where\n"},{"number":1520,"text":"the evaluation needs a relation or evaluator capability that the activated\n"},{"number":1521,"text":"frame does not declare; `invalid_basis` where the Ontology or design basis\n"},{"number":1522,"text":"cannot support it. An applicable axiom that the pack did not evaluate has\n"},{"number":1523,"text":"no result (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed). None of these is\n"},{"number":1524,"text":"`pass`. Purpose and material relation: a design gate that combines axiom verdicts\n"},{"number":1525,"text":"with other results reads them in the one core, so an excluded axiom is\n"},{"number":1526,"text":"never read as conforming or as failing, and an undecided or unevaluated\n"},{"number":1527,"text":"axiom is never read as a pass or a fail (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1528,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1600,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Gate and retrospective work","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FGate%20and%20retrospective%20work","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"6fc558b30ec4b68cd1f1491a7d9eaed1d17a09d2aea9972fa4b3695e870cac3f","start_line":1529,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1529,"text":"### Gate and retrospective work\n"},{"number":1530,"text":"\n"},{"number":1531,"text":"For a new or semantically changed boundary, the Ontology and design\n"},{"number":1532,"text":"verdict are both `accepted` before the affected implementation, public\n"},{"number":1533,"text":"contract or semantic carrier is promoted or the work claims design-method\n"},{"number":1534,"text":"closure. Any failed applicable axiom, missing functionality disposition,\n"},{"number":1535,"text":"unresolved authority path or blocking realisation gap keeps the verdict\n"},{"number":1536,"text":"non-accepted (P6).\n"},{"number":1537,"text":"\n"},{"number":1538,"text":"The Ontology verdict and the design verdict are each an acceptance\n"},{"number":1539,"text":"result: a decision that consumes the results of assessment, distinct from\n"},{"number":1540,"text":"them. The decision owner is the\n"},{"number":1541,"text":"design authority that accepts the Ontology (§5), and the verdict is its\n"},{"number":1542,"text":"disposition of the Ontology or of the design pack at the design gate,\n"},{"number":1543,"text":"under [ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition), which owns\n"},{"number":1544,"text":"the dispositions and their core values. `accepted` is the disposition\n"},{"number":1545,"text":"`accept`, which maps to `satisfied` for \"the candidate is accepted at its\n"},{"number":1546,"text":"declared boundary\", the candidate being the Ontology or the design pack\n"},{"number":1547,"text":"and the boundary the design gate. A verdict that is not `accepted` is one\n"},{"number":1548,"text":"of the other three dispositions, mapped there, or no disposition yet,\n"},{"number":1549,"text":"which is no acceptance result. The verdict consumes the pack's availability\n"},{"number":1550,"text":"and assessment results, among them the evaluation of decision\n"},{"number":1551,"text":"completeness, which is the design gate's acceptance criterion\n"},{"number":1552,"text":"([§5 Decision-complete symbolic design](#decision-complete-symbolic-design)),\n"},{"number":1553,"text":"the axiom verdicts and the cross-view proofs, and stays separate from both\n"},{"number":1554,"text":"(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, availability, assessment and acceptance): a matrix in which every applicable axiom is\n"},{"number":1555,"text":"`pass` is evidence for the design authority, never the verdict, and a\n"},{"number":1556,"text":"step that produced the pack establishes neither.
