An axiom whose result\n"},{"number":1557,"text":"is not `satisfied`, whether `fail` or a core value recorded directly, an\n"},{"number":1558,"text":"applicable axiom with no result, or an axiom with no result whose\n"},{"number":1559,"text":"applicability is not established false, keeps the verdict non-accepted\n"},{"number":1560,"text":"as a failed axiom does, because a combination with a non-satisfied\n"},{"number":1561,"text":"mandatory result or a gap is never `satisfied`\n"},{"number":1562,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results))\n"},{"number":1563,"text":"(P6, P5). Purpose and material relation: neither a passing matrix nor a produced design pack is\n"},{"number":1564,"text":"read as acceptance, and the design gate's acceptance combines with other\n"},{"number":1565,"text":"results in the one core (P6).\n"},{"number":1566,"text":"\n"},{"number":1567,"text":"For an unchanged `realization_refactor`, the gate is proportional: cite\n"},{"number":1568,"text":"the accepted Ontology and design basis, identify the touched projection\n"},{"number":1569,"text":"set, and prove that entities, relationships, lifecycle, authority,\n"},{"number":1570,"text":"functions, effects and public semantics have no delta. That proof reuses\n"},{"number":1571,"text":"the existing verdict; it does not create a new Ontology or acceptance\n"},{"number":1572,"text":"ceremony (P2; ACTIVATION §7).\n"},{"number":1573,"text":"\n"},{"number":1574,"text":"When `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, implementation may precede or\n"},{"number":1575,"text":"develop with design evidence and may be retained after reconciliation.\n"},{"number":1576,"text":"Until the design gate is accepted it is provisional evidence: it does not\n"},{"number":1577,"text":"author semantic truth, earn publication authority, or satisfy promotion or\n"},{"number":1578,"text":"closure. Otherwise only a disposable spike may cross the affected\n"},{"number":1579,"text":"unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before\n"},{"number":1580,"text":"design acceptance (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":1581,"text":"\n"},{"number":1582,"text":"Existing implementation placed under retrospective review may continue to\n"},{"number":1583,"text":"inform the affected design. Co-evolution remains lawful only while\n"},{"number":1584,"text":"`co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds; newly discovered material ambiguity,\n"},{"number":1585,"text":"contradiction or a materially non-equivalent network makes\n"},{"number":1586,"text":"`decision_complete(B)` false and activates the design gate for that\n"},{"number":1587,"text":"decision. Promotion and design-method closure remain blocked until the\n"},{"number":1588,"text":"required Ontology, three-view asset and axiom evaluation are accepted. The\n"},{"number":1589,"text":"design evaluates the code against prior authority; it does not rewrite the\n"},{"number":1590,"text":"Ontology or diagrams merely to rationalise an unlawful implementation\n"},{"number":1591,"text":"shape (P6).\n"},{"number":1592,"text":"\n"},{"number":1593,"text":"The asset stays boundary-bounded. It is a defect if it mixes an active\n"},{"number":1594,"text":"semantic boundary with unrelated bootstrap, test-harness, projection or\n"},{"number":1595,"text":"delivery shapes merely to look complete (P2). If the Ontology, any of the\n"},{"number":1596,"text":"three views, the cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict is\n"},{"number":1597,"text":"absent, the boundary is not design-method complete. Work may continue as\n"},{"number":1598,"text":"provisional co-evolution only when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds, but\n"},{"number":1599,"text":"the affected boundary may not be promoted, published or closed (P6).\n"},{"number":1600,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1694,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/7. Ontology and three-view design gate/Computational realisation projection (UP-019)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F7.%20Ontology%20and%20three-view%20design%20gate%2FComputational%20realisation%20projection%20%28UP-019%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"1599339528f9e4f63c4762af5975f90859f5079ea1a485eb2eda00450f7f67ab","start_line":1601,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1601,"text":"### Computational realisation projection (UP-019)\n"},{"number":1602,"text":"\n"},{"number":1603,"text":"The three views project domain structure, execution and lifecycle. They\n"},{"number":1604,"text":"deliberately show domain identities, so they do not reveal that two\n"},{"number":1605,"text":"domain-distinct components rest on the same data structures and\n"},{"number":1606,"text":"algorithms. Repeated machinery is therefore invisible to a domain-only\n"},{"number":1607,"text":"reading, and each occurrence looks correctly owned and correctly named\n"},{"number":1608,"text":"within its own entity (P1).\n"},{"number":1609,"text":"\n"},{"number":1610,"text":"Component role sets. Every material realisation component has an explicit\n"},{"number":1611,"text":"set of semantic and operational roles. Technology capability does not\n"},{"number":1612,"text":"confer authority (an instance of\n"},{"number":1613,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds), What\n"},{"number":1614,"text":"creates no authority). A component's declared role set is design authority;\n"},{"number":1615,"text":"where a role carries authority, composition and use preserve the\n"},{"number":1616,"text":"applicable authority relation under IDENTITY §6, which is supporting law\n"},{"number":1617,"text":"here rather than the owner of the role model (P6). A component may\n"},{"number":1618,"text":"lawfully hold several roles. Three cases are distinguished: behaviour\n"},{"number":1619,"text":"already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new\n"},{"number":1620,"text":"operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are\n"},{"number":1621,"text":"each design changes, and only those two require re-entry. Use of a\n"},{"number":1622,"text":"component outside its declared role set does not silently establish\n"},{"number":1623,"text":"identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth (P6,\n"},{"number":1624,"text":"P3).\n"},{"number":1625,"text":"\n"},{"number":1626,"text":"The projection. At a material semantic boundary, the design projects the\n"},{"number":1627,"text":"domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,\n"},{"number":1628,"text":"identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and\n"},{"number":1629,"text":"effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational\n"},{"number":1630,"text":"mappings. The cross-view evaluation extends to prove that the domain views\n"},{"number":1631,"text":"and this projection describe one system (P1). For a material\n"},{"number":1632,"text":"producer-to-consumer path, the projection identifies fact establishment,\n"},{"number":1633,"text":"consuming operations, applicable basis and invalidators, effect\n"},{"number":1634,"text":"boundaries, retained alternatives and accumulated work, using the validity\n"},{"number":1635,"text":"and reuse relation of ACTIVATION §4 (Complete enclosing-relation\n"},{"number":1636,"text":"admission) and §7; method and assurance operations are included where\n"},{"number":1637,"text":"material. Component-local success cannot establish the complete-path\n"},{"number":1638,"text":"claim, and different names do not establish different computational\n"},{"number":1639,"text":"responsibilities (P4b, P6; ASSURANCE §13 Computational whole-path\n"},{"number":1640,"text":"evaluation).\n"},{"number":1641,"text":"\n"},{"number":1642,"text":"Operational assumptions. Material algorithmic work declares the supported\n"},{"number":1643,"text":"input dimensions, workload and growth, and the operational assumptions\n"},{"number":1644,"text":"needed for the selected outcome; the separation of material startup, framework\n"},{"number":1645,"text":"processing, external computation, transport and assurance costs is\n"},{"number":1646,"text":"ACTIVATION §6. Bind\n"},{"number":1647,"text":"any acceptance limits and their owning authority before qualification;\n"},{"number":1648,"text":"limits and workloads are Product-owned, not universal method constants.\n"},{"number":1649,"text":"Challenge the assumptions on representative supported paths and material\n"},{"number":1650,"text":"growth. Observe work directly where elapsed time cannot locate it, without\n"},{"number":1651,"text":"repeating the operation merely to count it. Existing design and proof\n"},{"number":1652,"text":"surfaces carry these relations; no additional accounting system or fixed\n"},{"number":1653,"text":"algorithmic complexity is required (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1654,"text":"\n"},{"number":1655,"text":"The projection is subordinate. It reveals repeated implementation\n"},{"number":1656,"text":"structure; it cannot decide semantic identity, ownership or authority\n"},{"number":1657,"text":"(FOUNDATIONS §4 Shared machinery). The evaluation sequence (P1, P6):\n"},{"number":1658,"text":"\n"},{"number":1659,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1660,"text":"computational similarity\n"},{"number":1661,"text":"  -> commonisation candidate\n"},{"number":1662,"text":"  -> semantic and operational equivalence evaluation\n"},{"number":1663,"text":"  -> reuse, parameterised common relation, or justified separation\n"},{"number":1664,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1665,"text":"\n"},{"number":1666,"text":"Two components may share a map or an append-only sequence while differing\n"},{"number":1667,"text":"in identity and key law, ownership, ordering, admissible mutation,\n"},{"number":1668,"text":"consistency and concurrency, retention, failure semantics, access policy,\n"},{"number":1669,"text":"lifecycle or authority over truth. A materially non-equivalent law among\n"},{"number":1670,"text":"those dimensions requires separation. Other differences justify separation\n"},{"number":1671,"text":"only when evaluation shows that parameterisation or adaptation would\n"},{"number":1672,"text":"weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational\n"},{"number":1673,"text":"constraints. The existence of a difference does not by itself discharge\n"},{"number":1674,"text":"Prime contraction or recurrence review (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1675,"text":"\n"},{"number":1676,"text":"Disposition is two-part. Each material algorithmic obligation in `M(B)`\n"},{"number":1677,"text":"carries a semantic disposition (existing accepted relation, extension, or\n"},{"number":1678,"text":"new candidate relation) and a realisation disposition (consume, implement\n"},{"number":1679,"text":"locally, optimise, adapt, or deliberately duplicate under stated\n"},{"number":1680,"text":"non-semantic constraints). Isolation, substrate, performance, security and\n"},{"number":1681,"text":"dependency ownership are each lawful grounds for an independent\n"},{"number":1682,"text":"implementation. The invariant is not that equivalent code is never\n"},{"number":1683,"text":"rebuilt; it is that a local realisation does not present an existing\n"},{"number":1684,"text":"accepted semantic or authoritative relation as newly owned local truth\n"},{"number":1685,"text":"(P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":1686,"text":"\n"},{"number":1687,"text":"This law is false if any of the following holds (P6, P3): two domain-named\n"},{"number":1688,"text":"components implement materially equivalent abstract data types or\n"},{"number":1689,"text":"algorithms without a semantic disposition; a generic building block\n"},{"number":1690,"text":"becomes a new semantic authority; superficially similar operations are\n"},{"number":1691,"text":"commonised despite different identity, ordering, failure, ownership or\n"},{"number":1692,"text":"lifecycle law; or a local realisation presents an existing accepted\n"},{"number":1693,"text":"relation as newly owned local truth.\n"},{"number":1694,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1725,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/8. Theoretical framing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F8.%20Theoretical%20framing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"6391211e2074a2aacf139bbcd7421b2cc50a85f65db05ab0c1526a0a51c0ce34","start_line":1695,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1695,"text":"## 8. Theoretical framing\n"},{"number":1696,"text":"\n"},{"number":1697,"text":"This profile is operational and stands on its own. It does not require a\n"},{"number":1698,"text":"user to adopt the world-model domain or accept any empirical ontology\n"},{"number":1699,"text":"programme before using it (P1). The capitalised Ontology of §5\n"},{"number":1700,"text":"is the engineering Ontology of one designed boundary; it does not require\n"},{"number":1701,"text":"adoption of the Constraint-Emergence Ontology, a world-model theory, or\n"},{"number":1702,"text":"any other metaphysical or empirical claim.\n"},{"number":1703,"text":"\n"},{"number":1704,"text":"The world-model profile ([WORLD_MODEL](WORLD_MODEL.md)) does provide a useful theoretical\n"},{"number":1705,"text":"framing for why these rules are shaped this way. It treats a Markov object\n"},{"number":1706,"text":"as a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose\n"},{"number":1707,"text":"effective blanket separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is\n"},{"number":1708,"text":"load-bearing for context. Under that framing the engineering problem is\n"},{"number":1709,"text":"not \"how do I name more field groups?\" but \"what is the smallest lawful\n"},{"number":1710,"text":"boundary that preserves the thing's identity under variation?\" Read into\n"},{"number":1711,"text":"this profile carefully: the IACS is the software-design analogue of the\n"},{"number":1712,"text":"smallest identity-bearing cut; the Promotion Test asks whether a\n"},{"number":1713,"text":"subordinate payload has enough independent authority to count as its own\n"},{"number":1714,"text":"boundary rather than as evidence carried inside another one; Boundary\n"},{"number":1715,"text":"Inflation is the software-design form of mistaking many sensed fragments,\n"},{"number":1716,"text":"attributes or payload groupings for many real peer objects; and strong\n"},{"number":1717,"text":"typing at the semantic boundary prevents the identity-bearing cut from\n"},{"number":1718,"text":"remaining fuzzy, reconstructive or controller-owned (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":1719,"text":"\n"},{"number":1720,"text":"This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite. The rules\n"},{"number":1721,"text":"of this profile remain engineering law even where the Markov-object\n"},{"number":1722,"text":"construct is irrelevant, unavailable or still only candidate-class\n"},{"number":1723,"text":"(FOUNDATIONS §5). The framing sharpens the ask; it does not expand the\n"},{"number":1724,"text":"scope of the profile (P1).\n"},{"number":1725,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1766,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/9. Module taxonomy","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F9.%20Module%20taxonomy","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"9284b70e069564533dc92b707b20776c276915eff7bb7d00a494c042d1caf5e7","start_line":1726,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1726,"text":"## 9. Module taxonomy\n"},{"number":1727,"text":"\n"},{"number":1728,"text":"When this profile governs a realisation boundary, modules should be\n"},{"number":1729,"text":"classified by role (P0, P6). Recommended\n"},{"number":1730,"text":"roles are:\n"},{"number":1731,"text":"\n"},{"number":1732,"text":"- carrier module: defines typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts,\n"},{"number":1733,"text":"  transitions, records or envelopes;\n"},{"number":1734,"text":"- semantic kernel module: implements the main transforms over carriers\n"},{"number":1735,"text":"  without performing side effects;\n"},{"number":1736,"text":"- effect shell module: performs event emission, file publication, network\n"},{"number":1737,"text":"  calls, subprocess execution, persistence or operator delivery;\n"},{"number":1738,"text":"- projection module: derives read models or reports from authoritative\n"},{"number":1739,"text":"  source truth;\n"},{"number":1740,"text":"- binding or adapter module: converts between external boundaries and the\n"},{"number":1741,"text":"  project's internal carriers without inventing semantic law; and\n"},{"number":1742,"text":"- constructor or materialisation module: writes generated or built\n"},{"number":1743,"text":"  artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans.\n"},{"number":1744,"text":"\n"},{"number":1745,"text":"The point of the taxonomy is not naming ceremony. Modules are\n"},{"number":1746,"text":"realisation-level tools for bounding traversal reasoning: they give\n"},{"number":1747,"text":"reviewers, maintainers and future refactor work a stable cut for global\n"},{"number":1748,"text":"reasoning without letting semantic law smear across mixed authority\n"},{"number":1749,"text":"surfaces. A good module boundary improves the likelihood of correct\n"},{"number":1750,"text":"traversal because the computation and evaluation surface is better\n"},{"number":1751,"text":"constrained; this holds for any intermediate traversal under finite\n"},{"number":1752,"text":"context, attention and time (P0). Review can ask what the bounded unit\n"},{"number":1753,"text":"owns, what it consumes, what it emits and what proof is sufficient without\n"},{"number":1754,"text":"re-reading the whole system. The same constrained surface makes later\n"},{"number":1755,"text":"consolidation into reusable libraries easier: repeated module-local\n"},{"number":1756,"text":"computations are visible as recurrence candidates instead of disappearing\n"},{"number":1757,"text":"into broad orchestration code (P2; §10 Recurrence extraction).\n"},{"number":1758,"text":"\n"},{"number":1759,"text":"The design-to-module evidence route, the module-derived unit-test rule and\n"},{"number":1760,"text":"the module lifecycle confirmation rule are assurance law, stated in\n"},{"number":1761,"text":"[ASSURANCE §14](ASSURANCE.md#14-design-to-module-evidence-route),\n"},{"number":1762,"text":"[§15](ASSURANCE.md#15-module-derived-unit-tests) and\n"},{"number":1763,"text":"[§16](ASSURANCE.md#16-module-lifecycle-confirmation); for a boundary this\n"},{"number":1764,"text":"profile governs they read through the binding declared at the head of this\n"},{"number":1765,"text":"member (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":1766,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1773,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"7fdc11294923d182abebf501b530ccd584d976e56915c9009a42096d18332713","start_line":1767,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1767,"text":"## 10. Realisation rules\n"},{"number":1768,"text":"\n"},{"number":1769,"text":"Projects using this profile prefer one algebraic primitive plus\n"},{"number":1770,"text":"projections over several local decision systems, and prefer total\n"},{"number":1771,"text":"functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds (P2, P5,\n"},{"number":1772,"text":"P6).\n"},{"number":1773,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1785,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Immutable carriers","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FImmutable%20carriers","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"e9456d5aa0f9e56aa47a2f0f8ebb9f6f6366e35085cdb8e3ff04d6717bb68fb2","start_line":1774,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1774,"text":"### Immutable carriers\n"},{"number":1775,"text":"\n"},{"number":1776,"text":"Source truth should be carried in typed immutable values unless mutation\n"},{"number":1777,"text":"is materially necessary (P3, P4b). The\n"},{"number":1778,"text":"preferred shape: a constructor or parser produces a typed carrier;\n"},{"number":1779,"text":"transforms consume one carrier and return another carrier or a closed\n"},{"number":1780,"text":"result; projections read those carriers without mutating them. Mutable\n"},{"number":1781,"text":"carrier state requires explicit justification when it is\n"},{"number":1782,"text":"performance-critical, required by the host runtime or framework, or\n"},{"number":1783,"text":"modelling a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth.\n"},{"number":1784,"text":"Convenience is not sufficient justification.\n"},{"number":1785,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1804,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Totality","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FTotality","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"ffc13185e36c6fe7dfd16f390367635df2278ba2aca6b5608703a75839b3fc44","start_line":1786,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1786,"text":"### Totality\n"},{"number":1787,"text":"\n"},{"number":1788,"text":"Semantic functions should be total or as close to total as the language\n"},{"number":1789,"text":"and problem allow (P5). The rule applies P5\n"},{"number":1790,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §3](FOUNDATIONS.md#3-commitments)) to a semantic function,\n"},{"number":1791,"text":"which can meet an input outside its admitted domain. The method's own\n"},{"number":1792,"text":"results, with their non-success values, are the core result algebra of\n"},{"number":1793,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). The outcome values a\n"},{"number":1794,"text":"semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of\n"},{"number":1795,"text":"this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value\n"},{"number":1796,"text":"(P5, P1). Preferred: invalid input is rejected at the boundary; semantic\n"},{"number":1797,"text":"kernels consume admitted carriers only; failure is returned in a typed and\n"},{"number":1798,"text":"explicit form when practical. Projects using this profile should prefer\n"},{"number":1799,"text":"`Result`-like or closed outcome carriers, explicit validation stages, and\n"},{"number":1800,"text":"explicit \"unsupported\" or \"rejected\" outcomes. They should avoid partial\n"},{"number":1801,"text":"functions that assume hidden preconditions, semantic `.get(...)` fallback\n"},{"number":1802,"text":"chains, and controller code that reconstructs missing truth from defaults\n"},{"number":1803,"text":"(P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1804,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1817,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Effect edge","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FEffect%20edge","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"879dc3cfab7f5b446780855883e8612855a18616849a9089742575e9102b456b","start_line":1805,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1805,"text":"### Effect edge\n"},{"number":1806,"text":"\n"},{"number":1807,"text":"Effects should be explicit and isolated (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1808,"text":"Typical effect edges include file writes, network calls, subprocess\n"},{"number":1809,"text":"execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and\n"},{"number":1810,"text":"database mutation. Semantic kernels should not perform these effects while\n"},{"number":1811,"text":"also deciding the law. The preferred sequence: (1) admit or parse the\n"},{"number":1812,"text":"authoritative input; (2) transform it into a typed plan or outcome; (3)\n"},{"number":1813,"text":"apply effects at the edge using that plan or outcome; (4) publish\n"},{"number":1814,"text":"resulting events or projections downstream. If a function both decides the\n"},{"number":1815,"text":"semantic meaning and directly performs the write, the design should be\n"},{"number":1816,"text":"treated as suspect.\n"},{"number":1817,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1830,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/No semantic centre","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FNo%20semantic%20centre","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"01bf6df0f7b7e1ba2bcbf6251dbf10197a72f3fc8abb7496193c1ebfb4efaede","start_line":1818,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1818,"text":"### No semantic centre\n"},{"number":1819,"text":"\n"},{"number":1820,"text":"No controller, manager, service method, runtime loop or public wrapper\n"},{"number":1821,"text":"should be the hidden semantic centre of the system (P6, P1). That includes deciding meaning procedurally\n"},{"number":1822,"text":"in orchestration code, rebuilding truth from payload fragments,\n"},{"number":1823,"text":"rehydrating current law from legacy files or fallbacks, and flattening\n"},{"number":1824,"text":"typed meaning into ad hoc dictionary handling and `.get(...)` chains. A\n"},{"number":1825,"text":"module is acting as an unlawful semantic centre when reviewers have to\n"},{"number":1826,"text":"read it to discover what counts as closure, what identity means, what\n"},{"number":1827,"text":"failure means, what work is next, or what the current truth is. Those\n"},{"number":1828,"text":"meanings should already exist in carriers, contracts or explicit design\n"},{"number":1829,"text":"modules.\n"},{"number":1830,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1842,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Coupling","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FCoupling","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"864222870f607f0b6c07cebbb7127fe3187257fafcbabeec2adfc991d2c4f68d","start_line":1831,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1831,"text":"### Coupling\n"},{"number":1832,"text":"\n"},{"number":1833,"text":"Coupling should be reduced by dependency shape, not only by file count\n"},{"number":1834,"text":"(P6). The preferred dependency direction is\n"},{"number":1835,"text":"`carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections`, not\n"},{"number":1836,"text":"`controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections`.\n"},{"number":1837,"text":"Design is too coupled when many modules read and mutate the same object;\n"},{"number":1838,"text":"projections inspect implementation state to infer truth; a consumer can\n"},{"number":1839,"text":"silently rebuild source truth from raw artifacts; or tests pass only\n"},{"number":1840,"text":"because several modules still carry the same meaning. Reducing coupling\n"},{"number":1841,"text":"means reducing the number of places where meaning can be invented.\n"},{"number":1842,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1863,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Governance and strategy separation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FGovernance%20and%20strategy%20separation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"a3ce32574371181c09d7a145a0b91df46113bee9ac414a63c804c9cb9f17e5d3","start_line":1843,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1843,"text":"### Governance and strategy separation\n"},{"number":1844,"text":"\n"},{"number":1845,"text":"When a boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another\n"},{"number":1846,"text":"actor, executor, builder or substrate, it publishes governance truth, not\n"},{"number":1847,"text":"imperative strategy law, unless strategy ownership is explicitly part of\n"},{"number":1848,"text":"the boundary's ratified responsibility (P0 boundary commitment, P6). Lawful governance publication\n"},{"number":1849,"text":"includes current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure or unresolved\n"},{"number":1850,"text":"identities, route eligibility, the lawful edit or proof frontier, admitted\n"},{"number":1851,"text":"policy identity, and prior-turn or prior-run continuity. Unlawful strategy\n"},{"number":1852,"text":"drift includes imperative instructions about how the downstream actor\n"},{"number":1853,"text":"should repair or act; framework-owned preference rules masquerading as\n"},{"number":1854,"text":"observability; budgets, scores, counters or heuristic ratings that\n"},{"number":1855,"text":"recreate the governed actor's own judgment unless that assessment boundary\n"},{"number":1856,"text":"is explicitly owned; and prompt, report or read-model surfaces that become\n"},{"number":1857,"text":"hidden strategy doctrine. Governance surfaces describe the state, boundary\n"},{"number":1858,"text":"and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor\n"},{"number":1859,"text":"should do the work. A system meant to remain governance and observability\n"},{"number":1860,"text":"over another actor does not drift into replacement decision-engine\n"},{"number":1861,"text":"behaviour through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers\n"},{"number":1862,"text":"(FOUNDATIONS §3 P0 boundary commitment).\n"},{"number":1863,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1903,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Opportunistic optimisation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FOpportunistic%20optimisation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"d629c559160380617c27d4e82d5a3c816adefd7c592f212788459011ab587d53","start_line":1864,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1864,"text":"### Opportunistic optimisation\n"},{"number":1865,"text":"\n"},{"number":1866,"text":"When a realisation boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or\n"},{"number":1867,"text":"bounded implementation work, the area should be left better than it was\n"},{"number":1868,"text":"found (P2, P6). This does not\n"},{"number":1869,"text":"outrank constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence or\n"},{"number":1870,"text":"functional equivalence; it is subordinate to them. Opportunistic\n"},{"number":1871,"text":"optimisation is lawful only when it is boundary-local to the active design\n"},{"number":1872,"text":"or module surface; behaviour-preserving at the declared semantic boundary;\n"},{"number":1873,"text":"authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth;\n"},{"number":1874,"text":"visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads; and\n"},{"number":1875,"text":"effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence or\n"},{"number":1876,"text":"bootstrap doctrine.\n"},{"number":1877,"text":"\n"},{"number":1878,"text":"Examples of lawful opportunistic clean-up include removing parser re-entry\n"},{"number":1879,"text":"on locally assembled truth; consolidating duplicated module-local route\n"},{"number":1880,"text":"logic; replacing a poor local algorithm or repeated scan inside the active\n"},{"number":1881,"text":"boundary when semantic behaviour stays the same; and simplifying proof\n"},{"number":1882,"text":"fixtures or module-derived tests without changing their governing module\n"},{"number":1883,"text":"claims. Examples that are not opportunistic clean-up and therefore require\n"},{"number":1884,"text":"explicit design re-entry include repricing lookup, indexing, caching or\n"},{"number":1885,"text":"persistence strategy across module boundaries; changing public carriers,\n"},{"number":1886,"text":"visibility or ownership of truth; widening effect boundaries or runtime\n"},{"number":1887,"text":"observability doctrine; and introducing performance behaviour that changes\n"},{"number":1888,"text":"product expectations rather than only improving local realisation quality\n"},{"number":1889,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":1890,"text":"\n"},{"number":1891,"text":"A cross-boundary opportunity discovered during lawful clean-up is not\n"},{"number":1892,"text":"silently absorbed into the active boundary; it is repricing input. If the\n"},{"number":1893,"text":"owning authority admits follow-up implementation, that work enters\n"},{"number":1894,"text":"separately at the smallest lawful re-entry point (SPEC_METHOD §4). This\n"},{"number":1895,"text":"profile owns the scope-separation rule, not the work-tracking mechanism;\n"},{"number":1896,"text":"for ticketed work, TICKETS governs whether admitted follow-up is recorded\n"},{"number":1897,"text":"and how it affects ticket closure (P6). The test: if the improvement stays\n"},{"number":1898,"text":"inside the active boundary and preserves declared behaviour, it is lawful\n"},{"number":1899,"text":"clean-up; if it changes authority, public meaning or cross-boundary\n"},{"number":1900,"text":"realisation doctrine, it is a new design decision. Leaving an opened area\n"},{"number":1901,"text":"better than it was found is good realisation practice; using clean-up as\n"},{"number":1902,"text":"cover for unauthorised redesign is not (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1903,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1943,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Recurrence extraction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FRecurrence%20extraction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"ea09552beda24228c14261620f2198a1e406375159a912a9f6d5b21445cb2550","start_line":1904,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1904,"text":"### Recurrence extraction\n"},{"number":1905,"text":"\n"},{"number":1906,"text":"When the same realisation pattern appears across more than one processed\n"},{"number":1907,"text":"boundary, review treats that pattern as a commonisation candidate rather\n"},{"number":1908,"text":"than as another purely local clean-up (P2, P4a). Module boundaries make this review\n"},{"number":1909,"text":"possible: they constrain computation and evaluation enough that repeated\n"},{"number":1910,"text":"local shapes can be compared honestly and consolidated into libraries\n"},{"number":1911,"text":"without changing product truth. A recurrence candidate is usually not\n"},{"number":1912,"text":"product truth, authority-neutral, reused across two or more tickets or\n"},{"number":1913,"text":"module boundaries, and consumable through local adapters without changing\n"},{"number":1914,"text":"semantic ownership. Typical candidates include expectation derivation;\n"},{"number":1915,"text":"nested contract or policy carriers; proof-helper or fixture shaping;\n"},{"number":1916,"text":"effect-edge request or plan shaping; and constructor or materialisation\n"},{"number":1917,"text":"helpers that do not own semantic law.\n"},{"number":1918,"text":"\n"},{"number":1919,"text":"The rule of two, its third-rebuild threshold and the commonisation order\n"},{"number":1920,"text":"are owned by\n"},{"number":1921,"text":"[TICKETS §6 Recurring realisation and library declaration](TICKETS.md#recurring-realisation-and-library-declaration),\n"},{"number":1922,"text":"which applies them to every implementation migration ticket together with\n"},{"number":1923,"text":"the fields `library_usage`, `governing_library` and `library_rationale`.\n"},{"number":1924,"text":"This profile refines that rule for design review: a third local rebuild\n"},{"number":1925,"text":"is not design-method conformant unless the active boundary consumes an\n"},{"number":1926,"text":"existing reusable library or commonisation surface, extends that surface\n"},{"number":1927,"text":"before the local implementation lands, or review records an explicit\n"},{"number":1928,"text":"do-not-commonise decision and why the pattern is still boundary-specific\n"},{"number":1929,"text":"(P2). This section defines the design review obligation, not a rival\n"},{"number":1930,"text":"ticket rule or lifecycle (P6).\n"},{"number":1931,"text":"\n"},{"number":1932,"text":"Under the commonisation order that TICKETS §6 owns, if a reusable\n"},{"number":1933,"text":"pattern remains tenant-local and authority-neutral, it should be extracted into a reusable\n"},{"number":1934,"text":"library or common realisation surface rather than recreated inside each\n"},{"number":1935,"text":"module. If commonisation would change ownership, public carriers, module\n"},{"number":1936,"text":"boundaries or shared common law, it is no longer recurrence extraction; it\n"},{"number":1937,"text":"is a separate design decision and is treated that way (P6). Commonisation\n"},{"number":1938,"text":"closes only when the selected path consumes the accepted relation and the\n"},{"number":1939,"text":"superseded production responsibility is retired or satisfies the retention\n"},{"number":1940,"text":"relation of SPEC_METHOD §7 Closure criterion. Compare removed work and\n"},{"number":1941,"text":"maintained responsibilities across the path; shared names, fewer lines or\n"},{"number":1942,"text":"an unused common helper do not establish contraction (P2, P4b).\n"},{"number":1943,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":2029,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Post-ticket design review","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FPost-ticket%20design%20review","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"1ee8f2f84fe85dfb2aa936ee52d30292a74a269e56c6be1716daf22facf0251f","start_line":1944,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":1944,"text":"### Post-ticket design review\n"},{"number":1945,"text":"\n"},{"number":1946,"text":"When a ticket applies this profile to its boundary and claims that\n"},{"number":1947,"text":"boundary has been processed, the design-method closure claim should not rest on\n"},{"number":1948,"text":"implementation status alone (P6, P2). The processed boundary is checked\n"},{"number":1949,"text":"against its accepted design basis and exact closure claim before the\n"},{"number":1950,"text":"ticket claims closure under this profile. The check may be part of the\n"},{"number":1951,"text":"ticket's normal verification; it does not require a separate artifact,\n"},{"number":1952,"text":"review round or reviewer. TICKETS remains the authority for ticket status,\n"},{"number":1953,"text":"closure mechanics, reopening, dependency handling and follow-up ticket\n"},{"number":1954,"text":"recording; this rule states what the design check covers when this\n"},{"number":1955,"text":"profile governs the ticketed boundary.\n"},{"number":1956,"text":"\n"},{"number":1957,"text":"The check determines whether the boundary stayed lawful under the current\n"},{"number":1958,"text":"design and module assets; whether the exact claim includes every causally\n"},{"number":1959,"text":"applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained\n"},{"number":1960,"text":"predecessor claim; whether the exact closure claim leaves competing or\n"},{"number":1961,"text":"ambiguous authority on its acceptance path; whether implementation\n"},{"number":1962,"text":"established a material architectural decision with durable consequences\n"},{"number":1963,"text":"that forecloses an admitted Product outcome; and whether any discovered\n"},{"number":1964,"text":"issue falsifies the current claim or an applicable hard stop (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":1965,"text":"\n"},{"number":1966,"text":"The check reconstructs the complete selected function from governing\n"},{"number":1967,"text":"requirements through the accepted Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views,\n"},{"number":1968,"text":"target modules, implementation and module-owned proof; it does not begin\n"},{"number":1969,"text":"and end with the previous review findings. Exact hashes establish subject\n"},{"number":1970,"text":"identity; headings and artifact presence establish location; green tests\n"},{"number":1971,"text":"establish only the properties they actually assert. None supplies a\n"},{"number":1972,"text":"missing semantic relation or substitutes a weaker property for the\n"},{"number":1973,"text":"governed claim (P6; EVALUATION §1).\n"},{"number":1974,"text":"\n"},{"number":1975,"text":"The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared\n"},{"number":1976,"text":"claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction. The\n"},{"number":1977,"text":"unchanged-boundary rules of §5 and §7 permit reuse of a current accepted\n"},{"number":1978,"text":"Ontology, design verdict and sufficient reconstruction evidence as closed\n"},{"number":1979,"text":"results under [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse),\n"},{"number":1980,"text":"which owns reuse and its three invalidators: the check confirms their\n"},{"number":1981,"text":"exact scope, traces and applicability, and that none of those invalidators\n"},{"number":1982,"text":"has occurred. The invalidators those rules name are instances of\n"},{"number":1983,"text":"ACTIVATION §7's three, and no fourth exists: a reprice of a governing\n"},{"number":1984,"text":"source, which invalidates only the affected Ontology relations and\n"},{"number":1985,"text":"downstream projections until their impact is re-evaluated (§5), is a\n"},{"number":1986,"text":"changed basis for those relations and projections; a later candidate\n"},{"number":1987,"text":"that satisfies the applicability criteria and could materially alter the\n"},{"number":1988,"text":"lawful frontier (§7) is a material input change for the affected\n"},{"number":1989,"text":"selection evidence; new evidence or another material dimension that\n"},{"number":1990,"text":"defeats a dominance relation (§7) is a material input change for that\n"},{"number":1991,"text":"relation. A new role, conversation or review occurrence is not one of\n"},{"number":1992,"text":"them, so it does not itself require re-authoring that evidence or\n"},{"number":1993,"text":"recreating the three views. Missing, stale or ambiguous coverage is not a\n"},{"number":1994,"text":"no-delta proof. A material changed relation or a new counterexample is an\n"},{"number":1995,"text":"instance of that section's material input change: it requires affected\n"},{"number":1996,"text":"reconstruction and the applicable design gate, conserving supported\n"},{"number":1997,"text":"unaffected relations. This reuse does not weaken §7's complete Ontology\n"},{"number":1998,"text":"and three-view coverage for a new or materially changed boundary (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1999,"text":"\n"},{"number":2000,"text":"The required consequence: an issue that falsifies the current claim or an\n"},{"number":2001,"text":"applicable hard stop blocks the design-method closure claim, because that\n"},{"number":2002,"text":"claim is then `falsified`, which never becomes `satisfied`\n"},{"number":2003,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)), and a hard stop is not\n"},{"number":2004,"text":"waived ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). Whether\n"},{"number":2005,"text":"a finding also blocks the boundary's current promotion is decided by\n"},{"number":2006,"text":"[EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion).\n"},{"number":2007,"text":"The check's determinations above are this profile's domain triggers for\n"},{"number":2008,"text":"that section's four conditions: a discovered falsifying issue for the\n"},{"number":2009,"text":"first; competing or ambiguous authority on the acceptance path for the\n"},{"number":2010,"text":"second; a boundary that is not lawful under the current design and module\n"},{"number":2011,"text":"assets, or a claim that omits a causally applicable requirement, accepted design\n"},{"number":2012,"text":"relation or retained predecessor claim, for the third; and the durable\n"},{"number":2013,"text":"architectural foreclosure for the fourth. Applied to this check: ticket or\n"},{"number":2014,"text":"review wording cannot narrow applicable active authority away;\n"},{"number":2015,"text":"boundary-local clean-up or commonisation is absorbed only when required to\n"},{"number":2016,"text":"make the current claim true, preserve singular authority, satisfy accepted\n"},{"number":2017,"text":"design, or avoid the durable architectural foreclosure above; other\n"},{"number":2018,"text":"clean-up, recurrence, generality and cross-boundary opportunities are\n"},{"number":2019,"text":"observations outside the exact claim, which EVALUATION §5 returns as\n"},{"number":2020,"text":"repricing inputs that do not automatically widen the subject, block its\n"},{"number":2021,"text":"bounded claim or require a follow-up ticket; and any repricing admitted by\n"},{"number":2022,"text":"the owning authority enters through the smallest lawful re-entry point\n"},{"number":2023,"text":"(SPEC_METHOD §4) (P6, P2). The rule keeps design closure truthful without turning discovery\n"},{"number":2024,"text":"into automatic scope expansion: current defects and hard stops remain\n"},{"number":2025,"text":"blocking, useful observations may survive as repricing input, and\n"},{"number":2026,"text":"unclaimed future capability and optional clean-up do not become implicit\n"},{"number":2027,"text":"work. No processed ticket that applies this profile should claim\n"},{"number":2028,"text":"design-method closure until this bounded design check is complete.\n"},{"number":2029,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":2041,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/10. Realisation rules/Interface bleed prohibition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md#DESIGN_MODULE%2F10.%20Realisation%20rules%2FInterface%20bleed%20prohibition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","sha256":"06291e415d10489fbc0b415a55e5089ec47e420ab9a02e8024a4444c5835df9d","start_line":2030,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/DESIGN_MODULE.md","lines":[{"number":2030,"text":"### Interface bleed prohibition\n"},{"number":2031,"text":"\n"},{"number":2032,"text":"No interface should bleed semantic authority into another interface family\n"},{"number":2033,"text":"(P6). Interface bleed exists when one\n"},{"number":2034,"text":"interface reconstructs another interface's source truth; projection logic\n"},{"number":2035,"text":"becomes closure logic; report or prompt logic becomes admission logic;\n"},{"number":2036,"text":"public wrappers decide kernel semantics; or adapters invent meaning instead\n"},{"number":2037,"text":"of translating boundaries. The required shape: each interface family has\n"},{"number":2038,"text":"one authoritative source truth; downstream interfaces consume that truth;\n"},{"number":2039,"text":"crossing an interface boundary does not create a new semantic centre. This profile adds no adopter. The adopting\n"},{"number":2386,"text":"Product's authority may record its adoption by citing the profile in ADRs\n"},{"number":2387,"text":"or design surfaces; naming it in the project's agent entry surface (such\n"},{"number":2388,"text":"as `AGENTS.md`) as the preferred realisation discipline; using it as\n"},{"number":2389,"text":"review criteria for implementation-migration tickets; and classifying\n"},{"number":2390,"text":"implementation modules by the taxonomy of §9 (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":2391,"text":"\n"},{"number":2392,"text":"When the profile is adopted, the project applies it consistently across the\n"},{"number":2393,"text":"named boundary: Ontology and architecture derivation; design modules;\n"},{"number":2394,"text":"runtime or execution kernels; prompt assembly and reporting paths;\n"},{"number":2395,"text":"constructors and materialisers; and projection and query surfaces. For\n"},{"number":2396,"text":"migrations involving carrier closure, schema closure or governance\n"},{"number":2397,"text":"boundaries, projects should make the boundary closure evaluators (§3)\n"},{"number":2398,"text":"explicit in the governing ADR or ticket rather than leaving them implicit\n"},{"number":2399,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":2400,"text":"\n"},{"number":2401,"text":"Every new or materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares or\n"},{"number":2402,"text":"cites its accepted Ontology before claiming design-method completion. The\n"},{"number":2403,"text":"Ontology evidence includes entity lifecycle, authority, function\n"},{"number":2404,"text":"derivation, whole-family Prime, each accepted atom's admitted domain,\n"},{"number":2405,"text":"atom-to-realisation projection mappings and projection traceability, at\n"},{"number":2406,"text":"the granularity applicable to the material change (P6, P2). When the\n"},{"number":2407,"text":"material change includes schema or typed carrier work, the project derives\n"},{"number":2408,"text":"and reconciles the IACS from that Ontology before claiming design-method\n"},{"number":2409,"text":"completion. When the new or materially changed boundary is derived from an\n"},{"number":2410,"text":"existing realisation, the project also publishes the reference-to-target\n"},{"number":2411,"text":"derivation asset and the Ontology-derived three-view design asset before\n"},{"number":2412,"text":"claiming design-method completion for the changed boundary. When the new or\n"},{"number":2413,"text":"materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also\n"},{"number":2414,"text":"publishes a module-derived unit test lane (ASSURANCE §15) before claiming\n"},{"number":2415,"text":"closure for that change (P6).\n"},{"number":2416,"text":"\n"},{"number":2417,"text":"Partial adoption is allowed, but the adopted boundary and adopted rule\n"},{"number":2418,"text":"family should be named explicitly. Partial adoption may narrow scope; it is\n"},{"number":2419,"text":"not used to claim design-method completion while skipping the evidence\n"},{"number":2420,"text":"needed to audit, refactor or reconstruct the realised boundary (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":2421,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":2455,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/12. So SPEC_METHOD answers what is\n"},{"number":2432,"text":"lawful process; RELEASE what is a lawful release, Product, install,\n"},{"number":2433,"text":"exact-cut acceptance and selector-promotion decision; the graph-execution\n"},{"number":2434,"text":"profile what is lawful graph-native product shape; this profile what is\n"},{"number":2435,"text":"the preferred implementation design discipline when you want\n"},{"number":2436,"text":"Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, no interface bleed, and explicit\n"},{"number":2437,"text":"authority and effect management; and the UX profile the additional\n"},{"number":2438,"text":"discipline that applies when a module realises a UI surface.\n"},{"number":2439,"text":"\n"},{"number":2440,"text":"For products governed by the graph-execution profile, that profile decides\n"},{"number":2441,"text":"whether the operative unit is an outcome traversal, graph function, GTL\n"},{"number":2442,"text":"module or ABG runtime boundary; this profile then governs the\n"},{"number":2443,"text":"deterministic module structure that realises, evaluates, adapts or\n"},{"number":2444,"text":"projects inside that boundary (§2). When that boundary includes a UX\n"},{"number":2445,"text":"surface, the UX profile adds the render-purity, reducer-purity,\n"},{"number":2446,"text":"effect-membrane and AssetSurface-binding rules required for strong\n"},{"number":2447,"text":"functional consistency between front end and back end (P6).\n"},{"number":2448,"text":"\n"},{"number":2449,"text":"The module lifecycle confirmation rule (ASSURANCE §16) detects whether the\n"},{"number":2450,"text":"realisation has enough lifecycle signal to be safely built and reviewed.\n"},{"number":2451,"text":"It does not decide release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector\n"},{"number":2452,"text":"promotion, install policy or operational rollout; those remain governed by\n"},{"number":2453,"text":"RELEASE and project-owned release, deployment or operational surfaces\n"},{"number":2454,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":2455,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":2469,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/12. Their standing as\n"},{"number":2463,"text":"defaults and the identity law of their override, its preservation\n"},{"number":2464,"text":"conditions and its publication surface are\n"},{"number":2465,"text":"[IDENTITY §7](IDENTITY.md#7-default-formats-and-overrides).\n"},{"number":2466,"text":"\n"},{"number":2467,"text":"The helper's F_D eligibility is the common §5 contract referenced in §2; an\n"},{"number":2468,"text":"identity default grants neither that eligibility nor additional writes.\n"},{"number":2469,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":2479,"heading":"DESIGN_MODULE/12. Claims\n"},{"number":12,"text":"\n"},{"number":13,"text":"A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the\n"},{"number":14,"text":"governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker\n"},{"number":15,"text":"property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.\n"},{"number":16,"text":"Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax,\n"},{"number":17,"text":"compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a\n"},{"number":18,"text":"semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because\n"},{"number":19,"text":"the weaker property is easier to measure (P6).\n"},{"number":20,"text":"\n"},{"number":21,"text":"Where a claim about a construction concerns its recursive or repeated\n"},{"number":22,"text":"work, it is one of the four kinds the construction relation keeps apart,\n"},{"number":23,"text":"preservation, progress, termination and outcome satisfaction\n"},{"number":24,"text":"([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation)), and states which.\n"},{"number":25,"text":"Its witness is an assertion whose predicate is the full obligation, a\n"},{"number":26,"text":"necessary condition of it or part of a sufficient conjunction, and the\n"},{"number":27,"text":"claim states which. Its expected result has assertion provenance and its\n"},{"number":28,"text":"execution has execution provenance, as\n"},{"number":29,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)\n"},{"number":30,"text":"and [Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)\n"},{"number":31,"text":"define them; a passing check of a necessary condition establishes that\n"},{"number":32,"text":"condition and no more (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":33,"text":"\n"},{"number":34,"text":"Boundary congruence. A checker, validator, harness, reviewer or other\n"},{"number":35,"text":"assurance surface supporting promotion or closure binds the exact claimed\n"},{"number":36,"text":"subject and its authoritative composition relation. Evidence over one file\n"},{"number":37,"text":"or carrier proves only that boundary; it cannot establish a multi-file or\n"},{"number":38,"text":"carrier-set claim. Cross-carrier satisfaction and conflict are decided at\n"},{"number":39,"text":"the declared composite boundary (P3, P6). A claim of mechanical enforcement\n"},{"number":40,"text":"names an executable or reproducible predicate and a witness reachable\n"},{"number":41,"text":"through the declared ordinary assurance path; a planned or\n"},{"number":42,"text":"specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification,\n"},{"number":43,"text":"and until both the predicate and such a witness are observed the claim\n"},{"number":44,"text":"remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property (P6).\n"},{"number":45,"text":"\n"},{"number":46,"text":"A claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated\n"},{"number":47,"text":"evidence. Generalising a local defect or observation needs a declared\n"},{"number":48,"text":"inference relation, the relevant comparable population, explicit\n"},{"number":49,"text":"counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence\n"},{"number":50,"text":"invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is\n"},{"number":51,"text":"superseded, withdrawn or requalified (P6). The quantifier rule and the\n"},{"number":52,"text":"boundary rule are false if assurance observes a weaker or different\n"},{"number":53,"text":"subject, if per-carrier evidence closes an unevaluated composite claim, if\n"},{"number":54,"text":"mechanical enforcement lacks its predicate or a reachable witness, if\n"},{"number":55,"text":"planned evidence is reported as observed verification, if a verdict outruns\n"},{"number":56,"text":"its evaluated population or declared inference relation, or if dependent\n"},{"number":57,"text":"verdicts survive material counterevidence without requalification.\n"},{"number":58,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":140,"heading":"EVALUATION/1.
