Algebra/Preservation through construction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FPreservation%20through%20construction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"f9a6ed4025ceff985d99c3dd22907c3e2155c82c0e11e6c9fdb3d35906bb5460","start_line":1110,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1110,"text":"### Preservation through construction\n"},{"number":1111,"text":"\n"},{"number":1112,"text":"A construction binds its starting state A and required outcome Z under\n"},{"number":1113,"text":"[ACTIVATION §1 Construction relation](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation);\n"},{"number":1114,"text":"the governing basis bound at its intake and the material assumptions are\n"},{"number":1115,"text":"together written Γ here. The\n"},{"number":1116,"text":"predicate for Z includes required effects and trace properties where\n"},{"number":1117,"text":"these matter.\n"},{"number":1118,"text":"\n"},{"number":1119,"text":"For a sequence of transformations, let `X_i` be the state or trace domain\n"},{"number":1120,"text":"at boundary i, `F_i ⊆ X_i × X_(i+1)` the declared transition relation, and\n"},{"number":1121,"text":"`P_i` the property to retain or establish there. A claimed preservation\n"},{"number":1122,"text":"step has the form:\n"},{"number":1123,"text":"\n"},{"number":1124,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1125,"text":"For all x, x':  P_i(x) and F_i(x, x')  implies  P_(i+1)(x').\n"},{"number":1126,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1127,"text":"\n"},{"number":1128,"text":"The relation accounts for the outcomes, effects and assumptions material\n"},{"number":1129,"text":"to the claim. A relation covering successful completion alone supplies no\n"},{"number":1130,"text":"claim about refusal, failure, interruption or unknown effects; those\n"},{"number":1131,"text":"cases follow Results above and the result, authority and recovery\n"},{"number":1132,"text":"contracts of ACTIVATION §3 and §5. The real execution's conformance to\n"},{"number":1133,"text":"the relation is a separate obligation (P4a, P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1134,"text":"\n"},{"number":1135,"text":"An end-to-end argument establishes the initial condition, each step's\n"},{"number":1136,"text":"applicable premises, compatibility at each composition boundary, and the\n"},{"number":1137,"text":"connection from the final property to Z. The preceding postcondition\n"},{"number":1138,"text":"must establish the next precondition, or the missing condition must be\n"},{"number":1139,"text":"acquired and justified. Concurrency, alternative branches and external effects\n"},{"number":1140,"text":"require their applicable composition law; a sequential drawing does not\n"},{"number":1141,"text":"establish one. Local success alone establishes neither composition\n"},{"number":1142,"text":"compatibility nor Z. Preservation is distinct from progress, termination\n"},{"number":1143,"text":"and the availability of a suitable next step (P4a, P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1144,"text":"\n"},{"number":1145,"text":"Exact transformations preserve the declared meaning. Approximate\n"},{"number":1146,"text":"transformations state their adequacy relation and an established bound\n"},{"number":1147,"text":"for the complete composition; local tolerances cannot be assumed to add or\n"},{"number":1148,"text":"to remain unchanged. [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement),\n"},{"number":1149,"text":"Exact and approximate steps, owns the per-step law and applies this\n"},{"number":1150,"text":"obligation to refinement steps. A\n"},{"number":1151,"text":"change to the governing outcome or meaning follows its owner and the\n"},{"number":1152,"text":"successor rules of SPEC_METHOD §4 and RELEASE §9 (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1153,"text":"\n"},{"number":1154,"text":"The algorithmic account states the required operation, the informational\n"},{"number":1155,"text":"account the meaning and distinctions retained, and the computational\n"},{"number":1156,"text":"binding how work and observations are realised\n"},{"number":1157,"text":"([§2 Accounts of a construction](#accounts-of-a-construction)). A claim\n"},{"number":1158,"text":"across these accounts identifies its maps and preservation obligations;\n"},{"number":1159,"text":"execution by a person, a machine or a mixed arrangement does not\n"},{"number":1160,"text":"discharge them by itself. A commuting diagram, functor or equivalence\n"},{"number":1161,"text":"claim requires the categorical demonstration above (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1162,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1270,"heading":"FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Assertions and observation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FAssertions%20and%20observation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"d06088be839d28531eb7bfc2cd55657f4118c465200dc089cea8c9a96ab3e7a4","start_line":1163,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1163,"text":"### Assertions and observation\n"},{"number":1164,"text":"\n"},{"number":1165,"text":"For a selected source obligation r, let `Q_r = interpret(r, Γ, Ω)` be its\n"},{"number":1166,"text":"required predicate over the declared domain Ω of cases. The interpretation\n"},{"number":1167,"text":"retains the obligation's scope, conditions, exceptions and permitted\n"},{"number":1168,"text":"alternatives. A source identifier or digest authenticates the selected\n"},{"number":1169,"text":"text; it does not prove the interpretation faithful (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":1170,"text":"\n"},{"number":1171,"text":"An assertion targets a predicate `q_t` and states whether that predicate\n"},{"number":1172,"text":"is the full obligation or a narrower claim. The directions differ:\n"},{"number":1173,"text":"\n"},{"number":1174,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1175,"text":"Q_r implies q_t                   : q_t is a necessary condition of Q_r.\n"},{"number":1176,"text":"q_t implies Q_r                   : establishing q_t is sufficient for Q_r.\n"},{"number":1177,"text":"(q_1 and ... and q_n) implies Q_r : the stated conjunction is sufficient.\n"},{"number":1178,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1179,"text":"\n"},{"number":1180,"text":"These implications are conditional on Γ and Ω. Passing a check of a\n"},{"number":1181,"text":"necessary condition does not establish the full obligation. A conjunction\n"},{"number":1182,"text":"requires its own coverage and compatibility argument; a collection of\n"},{"number":1183,"text":"passing tests does not supply it by its count (P1, P6, P5).\n"},{"number":1184,"text":"\n"},{"number":1185,"text":"Let `π: Ω → O` describe the observations available to a checker and\n"},{"number":1186,"text":"`T ⊆ O × R` its admitted evaluation relation, where R is the core result\n"},{"number":1187,"text":"algebra of Results above. A deterministic checker is a functional special\n"},{"number":1188,"text":"case. A human or probabilistic checker can admit different conclusions on\n"},{"number":1189,"text":"the same observations; a universal soundness claim covers all admitted\n"},{"number":1190,"text":"conclusions, not a favourable selected run. `indeterminate` is the core\n"},{"number":1191,"text":"judgment whose admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate (Results).\n"},{"number":1192,"text":"It is distinct from an evaluation that was not performed, and from work\n"},{"number":1193,"text":"or coverage that remains unresolved, which is a state of the work\n"},{"number":1194,"text":"([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),\n"},{"number":1195,"text":"[§5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) and not a judgment value.\n"},{"number":1196,"text":"Writing `sat` and `fal` for the satisfied and falsified judgments about\n"},{"number":1197,"text":"`q_t`, not new execution states:\n"},{"number":1198,"text":"\n"},{"number":1199,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1200,"text":"For every s in Ω:\n"},{"number":1201,"text":"  (π(s), sat) in T  implies  q_t(s).\n"},{"number":1202,"text":"  (π(s), fal) in T  implies  not q_t(s).\n"},{"number":1203,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1204,"text":"\n"},{"number":1205,"text":"The candidate identifies what supports each claimed direction and where\n"},{"number":1206,"text":"it is unresolved. A relation admitting both a sound satisfied judgment\n"},{"number":1207,"text":"and an indeterminate judgment need not always decide the case. A\n"},{"number":1208,"text":"restricted deterministic model retains its scope, and an actual checker\n"},{"number":1209,"text":"requires its own conformance account. An observed test pass remains an\n"},{"number":1210,"text":"observation while the oracle's fidelity is unestablished; it does not\n"},{"number":1211,"text":"become established satisfaction of the source obligation, and a reported\n"},{"number":1212,"text":"failure is treated the same way. The observation binding itself needs\n"},{"number":1213,"text":"support: an idealised π does not establish that the instrument, actor or\n"},{"number":1214,"text":"execution acquired the required facts correctly. A probabilistic claim\n"},{"number":1215,"text":"uses its declared distribution over outcomes under Quantified assurance\n"},{"number":1216,"text":"below; the relation alone supplies no probabilities (P6, P5, P1).\n"},{"number":1217,"text":"\n"},{"number":1218,"text":"Observation sufficiency. A checker that always decides `q_t` correctly\n"},{"number":1219,"text":"from π alone requires:\n"},{"number":1220,"text":"\n"},{"number":1221,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1222,"text":"For all s, s' in Ω:\n"},{"number":1223,"text":"  π(s) = π(s')  implies  q_t(s) = q_t(s').\n"},{"number":1224,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1225,"text":"\n"},{"number":1226,"text":"If two admissible cases have the same observation but opposite truth\n"},{"number":1227,"text":"values, that observation cannot support a sound complete decision between\n"},{"number":1228,"text":"them; further evidence, a justified narrower scope or an indeterminate\n"},{"number":1229,"text":"judgment is required. In a classical set model this condition permits a\n"},{"number":1230,"text":"predicate on the image of π; it establishes neither an executable decision\n"},{"number":1231,"text":"procedure nor its cost. Unknown effects and unavailable observations\n"},{"number":1232,"text":"retain their distinctions from falsehood and from an evaluation that was\n"},{"number":1233,"text":"not performed (Results) (P3, P1, P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1234,"text":"\n"},{"number":1235,"text":"Where a representation is claimed sufficient for subsequent decisions,\n"},{"number":1236,"text":"identify the consumer-required observations and readouts and material\n"},{"number":1237,"text":"applicability conditions, directly or by reference to the consuming contract.\n"},{"number":1238,"text":"Identify input and policy scope and horizon where the claim depends on them.\n"},{"number":1239,"text":"Retain the standing, obligations, currentness and invalidation, causal\n"},{"number":1240,"text":"producer and authority distinctions those consumers require. Two cases with\n"},{"number":1241,"text":"the same representation but incompatible required decisions under those\n"},{"number":1242,"text":"fixed conditions falsify the sufficiency claim. This requires no anticipation\n"},{"number":1243,"text":"of all future uses (P1, P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1244,"text":"\n"},{"number":1245,"text":"When a chosen functional account claims decision preservation, define its\n"},{"number":1246,"text":"functions and domain: s is a state, u a permitted input under the fixed\n"},{"number":1247,"text":"conditions Γ, alpha maps states to representations, delta(s,u) is the\n"},{"number":1248,"text":"consumer's decision, and delta_hat is that decision on representations.\n"},{"number":1249,"text":"Demonstrate `delta(s,u) = delta_hat(alpha(s),u)` on the declared domain\n"},{"number":1250,"text":"(equivalently factor delta through alpha with u held fixed). When it\n"},{"number":1251,"text":"claims transition preservation, also demonstrate\n"},{"number":1252,"text":"`alpha(T(s,u)) ≈ T_hat(alpha(s),u)`, where T and T_hat are the state and\n"},{"number":1253,"text":"representation transitions and ≈ is the declared adequacy relation, and\n"},{"number":1254,"text":"demonstrate the declared readout preservation on\n"},{"number":1255,"text":"that domain and horizon. Other frames preserve their consumer-required\n"},{"number":1256,"text":"relational distinctions under the owning contracts; these equations impose\n"},{"number":1257,"text":"no universal functional model or executable decision procedure. Mandatory\n"},{"number":1258,"text":"authority and hold distinctions remain exact where their contracts require\n"},{"number":1259,"text":"exactness. Approximation needs explicit latitude and a justified horizon\n"},{"number":1260,"text":"bound; a one-step bound alone supplies no multi-step guarantee (P1, P4a, P6).\n"},{"number":1261,"text":"\n"},{"number":1262,"text":"The [one-assessment example](examples/DETERMINISTIC_CONTRACTS.md#continuation-sensitive-sufficiency)\n"},{"number":1263,"text":"separates an unperformed assessment from a closed indeterminate assessment.\n"},{"number":1264,"text":"Its four-state representation retains every modeled state distinction under\n"},{"number":1265,"text":"fixed conditions Γ. It is a sufficiency witness with no state aggregation,\n"},{"number":1266,"text":"not a proof of compression, minimal context or general task selection. A\n"},{"number":1267,"text":"smallest or cheapest sufficient-material claim needs its own objective,\n"},{"number":1268,"text":"scope and evidence; representation size and total operating cost are\n"},{"number":1269,"text":"different quantities (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1270,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1325,"heading":"FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Parallel derivation and mutual assurance","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FParallel%20derivation%20and%20mutual%20assurance","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"554d00b0a31862bfe603a62b53521ff921a4fd925a6b4708039f1c810bf63892","start_line":1271,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1271,"text":"### Parallel derivation and mutual assurance\n"},{"number":1272,"text":"\n"},{"number":1273,"text":"Construction and assurance can follow different paths from a common\n"},{"number":1274,"text":"obligation. For `requirement → refinement → realisation`, assertions\n"},{"number":1275,"text":"derived from the requirement check its applicable conditions in the\n"},{"number":1276,"text":"realisation; assertions derived from the refinement check its more\n"},{"number":1277,"text":"detailed obligations there. Acceptance tests and build-level tests can\n"},{"number":1278,"text":"instantiate these paths\n"},{"number":1279,"text":"([ASSURANCE §14](ASSURANCE.md#14-design-to-module-evidence-route)); the\n"},{"number":1280,"text":"roles identify the selected sources and subject in this example and\n"},{"number":1281,"text":"prescribe no stage names or test classes (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1282,"text":"\n"},{"number":1283,"text":"An expected result or acceptance predicate has assertion provenance: the\n"},{"number":1284,"text":"owning obligation, its interpretation, assumptions, derivation and shared\n"},{"number":1285,"text":"dependencies, which give it meaning. An execution has execution\n"},{"number":1286,"text":"provenance: the actual checker, exact subject, applicable environment,\n"},{"number":1287,"text":"inputs, observations and result. Both are needed for the claims they\n"},{"number":1288,"text":"support; execution records alone cannot establish that the expected\n"},{"number":1289,"text":"answer follows from the requirement. Authentication of a returned\n"},{"number":1290,"text":"assessment, which binds a result to its producer, subject, basis and\n"},{"number":1291,"text":"evidence ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)), is a\n"},{"number":1292,"text":"third thing and establishes neither provenance (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":1293,"text":"\n"},{"number":1294,"text":"An implementation-derived test can be useful for regression or a stated\n"},{"number":1295,"text":"local property. Repeating the implementation's decision supplies no\n"},{"number":1296,"text":"independent justification of its fidelity to an upstream obligation. A\n"},{"number":1297,"text":"shorter assertion path can be easier to inspect and execute than\n"},{"number":1298,"text":"construction; that is a supported design claim for the selected path, not\n"},{"number":1299,"text":"a guarantee of correctness, coverage or independence. Valid distinct\n"},{"number":1300,"text":"implementations can produce different outputs within the same acceptable\n"},{"number":1301,"text":"relation; equality of outputs is not always the oracle (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1302,"text":"\n"},{"number":1303,"text":"Mutual assurance compares independently justified constructions or\n"},{"number":1304,"text":"assertions within their stated scope. Agreement is compatible with both\n"},{"number":1305,"text":"being correct and with a shared error; disagreement requires diagnosis\n"},{"number":1306,"text":"([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation))\n"},{"number":1307,"text":"and does not identify the faulty party by itself. Assurance accounts for\n"},{"number":1308,"text":"shared specifications, interpretations, tools, fixtures, observations,\n"},{"number":1309,"text":"copied material and other material failure causes. Different actors,\n"},{"number":1310,"text":"model families or codebases do not establish statistical independence.\n"},{"number":1311,"text":"Porting retains authorship and common dependencies\n"},{"number":1312,"text":"([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)). Repeating\n"},{"number":1313,"text":"evidence does not create a new independent observation. Agreement with\n"},{"number":1314,"text":"an incorrect common model cannot validate that model against the desired\n"},{"number":1315,"text":"real-world outcome; validation of the governing expectations uses its\n"},{"number":1316,"text":"declared purpose and external observations through their owners, and\n"},{"number":1317,"text":"proposed corrections preserve counterexamples and follow the applicable\n"},{"number":1318,"text":"change authority ([SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#4-change-management))\n"},{"number":1319,"text":"(P4a, P6, P1).\n"},{"number":1320,"text":"\n"},{"number":1321,"text":"These relationships are recoverable from the existing sources, bindings\n"},{"number":1322,"text":"and evidence carriers. Shared derivations can be recorded once and applied\n"},{"number":1323,"text":"to a declared family. No new per-test document, parallel ledger, fixed\n"},{"number":1324,"text":"number of reviewers or prescribed provenance format is required (P6).\n"},{"number":1325,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1377,"heading":"FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Quantified assurance","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FQuantified%20assurance","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"9666dc3e83bbd769efe823a3c7657c55db8f444bc5944bc2260bd1194263229b","start_line":1326,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1326,"text":"### Quantified assurance\n"},{"number":1327,"text":"\n"},{"number":1328,"text":"Risk model. The actor exercising the admitted work authority selects the required\n"},{"number":1329,"text":"assurance for the stated risk, obligations and resource limits. That\n"},{"number":1330,"text":"selection identifies material failure consequences, coverage and\n"},{"number":1331,"text":"uncertainty, and the conditions for action or acceptance. Additional\n"},{"number":1332,"text":"evidence can strengthen a claim only within its applicability and\n"},{"number":1333,"text":"dependence account; neither a test count nor an assumed preference for more checks\n"},{"number":1334,"text":"substitutes for that account (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":1335,"text":"\n"},{"number":1336,"text":"Where quantified assurance is claimed, its model states the population or\n"},{"number":1337,"text":"uncertainty being modelled, prior information, likelihoods, shared causes\n"},{"number":1338,"text":"and calibration limits. For a specified violation event V and evidence\n"},{"number":1339,"text":"event E:\n"},{"number":1340,"text":"\n"},{"number":1341,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1342,"text":"P(V | E, Γ) =\n"},{"number":1343,"text":"  P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ)\n"},{"number":1344,"text":"  / [P(E | V, Γ) P(V | Γ) + P(E | not V, Γ) P(not V | Γ)].\n"},{"number":1345,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1346,"text":"\n"},{"number":1347,"text":"The denominator must be nonzero. E can include agreement, disagreement or other\n"},{"number":1348,"text":"observations; its likelihood under both faulty and non-faulty conditions\n"},{"number":1349,"text":"matters. The formula supplies no missing likelihood or prior, and a\n"},{"number":1350,"text":"numerical posterior is no stronger than its model and evidence.\n"},{"number":1351,"text":"\n"},{"number":1352,"text":"Let `M_i` mean that check i misses V under the specified evaluation\n"},{"number":1353,"text":"conditions. The joint miss probability factors exactly by conditional\n"},{"number":1354,"text":"probabilities:\n"},{"number":1355,"text":"\n"},{"number":1356,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1357,"text":"P(M_1 and ... and M_n | V, Γ)\n"},{"number":1358,"text":"  = product over i of P(M_i | V, Γ, M_1, ..., M_(i-1)).\n"},{"number":1359,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1360,"text":"\n"},{"number":1361,"text":"Conditional terms require defined conditioning events; zero-probability\n"},{"number":1362,"text":"prefixes are handled without inventing a conditional value. Replacing\n"},{"number":1363,"text":"those terms with `P(M_i | V, Γ)` requires conditional independence under\n"},{"number":1364,"text":"the declared model. One minus the joint miss probability is the chance of\n"},{"number":1365,"text":"at least one detection under those same conditions; it is not the\n"},{"number":1366,"text":"probability that the whole product is correct. Agreement does not\n"},{"number":1367,"text":"necessarily increase confidence when shared causes or new information\n"},{"number":1368,"text":"change the model (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":1369,"text":"\n"},{"number":1370,"text":"Calibration from sampled cases or injected defects supports only its\n"},{"number":1371,"text":"justified relationship to operational failures. Unsupported numeric\n"},{"number":1372,"text":"confidence remains unresolved; qualitative evidence and stated limits\n"},{"number":1373,"text":"remain usable within the governing policy. No universal probability\n"},{"number":1374,"text":"threshold is imposed and no probability estimate is required for every\n"},{"number":1375,"text":"test. Required safety, authority and acceptance conditions cannot be\n"},{"number":1376,"text":"waived by a cheaper assurance plan (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1377,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1462,"heading":"FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Change impact and evidence reuse","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FChange%20impact%20and%20evidence%20reuse","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"e989bf4b8c0dd996e5545f18db94f8ba275d14485697c0b046429746ed3bfbc6","start_line":1378,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1378,"text":"### Change impact and evidence reuse\n"},{"number":1379,"text":"\n"},{"number":1380,"text":"Assertion justification and evidence validity are related but distinct\n"},{"number":1381,"text":"dependency relations. The former explains why a check expresses an\n"},{"number":1382,"text":"obligation. The latter identifies what can affect the check's behaviour,\n"},{"number":1383,"text":"conclusion or applicability: implementation, shared libraries, data,\n"},{"number":1384,"text":"instruments, environments and governing assumptions. A\n"},{"number":1385,"text":"requirements-to-test link alone is not a complete impact model (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1386,"text":"\n"},{"number":1387,"text":"Let Δ be a change to material facts or dependencies, including a newly\n"},{"number":1388,"text":"discovered invalid assumption. Let `I(Δ)`, the impact cover, conservatively cover the changed\n"},{"number":1389,"text":"facts and their affected dependents. For each check t, let `D*(t)` cover\n"},{"number":1390,"text":"the transitive dependencies material to its assertion, execution and use\n"},{"number":1391,"text":"of evidence. A candidate selection is:\n"},{"number":1392,"text":"\n"},{"number":1393,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1394,"text":"S_Δ = { t : D*(t) intersects I(Δ) }.\n"},{"number":1395,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1396,"text":"\n"},{"number":1397,"text":"The representation of these dependencies is the tenant's choice; no\n"},{"number":1398,"text":"exhaustive graph database is required. Excluding a check requires\n"},{"number":1399,"text":"supported coverage of its material dependencies and a reason the change\n"},{"number":1400,"text":"cannot invalidate the intended reused claim; an absent edge is not\n"},{"number":1401,"text":"evidence of non-influence. Unknown impact widens reassessment or leaves\n"},{"number":1402,"text":"the dependent assurance unresolved. New obligations or cases create\n"},{"number":1403,"text":"assessment work even when no existing check covers them. A mandatory\n"},{"number":1404,"text":"gate, an assessment that the governing policy requires irrespective of\n"},{"number":1405,"text":"selection ([RELEASE §8](RELEASE.md#8-acceptance)), remains applicable\n"},{"number":1406,"text":"(P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1407,"text":"\n"},{"number":1408,"text":"For a new subject and basis, let `E_old` be the existing evidence records,\n"},{"number":1409,"text":"`E_reassessed` the evidence newly produced by reassessment, and `E_new`\n"},{"number":1410,"text":"the resulting account. Reassessment includes the checks selected in\n"},{"number":1411,"text":"`S_Δ`, the assessment of new obligations and the applicable mandatory\n"},{"number":1412,"text":"gates. Selection alone produces no execution evidence; failed and\n"},{"number":1413,"text":"indeterminate results retain their standing:\n"},{"number":1414,"text":"\n"},{"number":1415,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1416,"text":"E_new = retain_applicable(E_old, new_subject, new_basis) union E_reassessed.\n"},{"number":1417,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1418,"text":"\n"},{"number":1419,"text":"Retention establishes the material validity conditions on the new\n"},{"number":1420,"text":"subject: the claim and its scope still apply, its assertion and\n"},{"number":1421,"text":"observation basis remain justified, and the affected dependencies are\n"},{"number":1422,"text":"unchanged or covered by an established preservation relation. The\n"},{"number":1423,"text":"original evidence keeps its original subject; a new applicability\n"},{"number":1424,"text":"relation permits its use. A changed hash alone establishes neither\n"},{"number":1425,"text":"invalidity nor equivalence. A corrected run is not an unchanged independent\n"},{"number":1426,"text":"test of the correction: the corrected subject carries its own evidence.\n"},{"number":1427,"text":"Known failures, unresolved coverage and their\n"},{"number":1428,"text":"citations remain visible until a supported repair, a reassessment or an\n"},{"number":1429,"text":"authorised change of obligation disposes of them (P3, P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":1430,"text":"\n"},{"number":1431,"text":"If a governing requirement changes, dependent expectations may need\n"},{"number":1432,"text":"authorised revision as well as new execution. A correction in a\n"},{"number":1433,"text":"refinement revisits the affected obligations and their links to both the\n"},{"number":1434,"text":"requirement and the realisation. A correction in the realisation\n"},{"number":1435,"text":"reassesses the affected implementation and integration under the\n"},{"number":1436,"text":"still-applicable obligations. These are semantic dependency boundaries,\n"},{"number":1437,"text":"not file or directory boundaries. Recovery reacquires current reality and\n"},{"number":1438,"text":"invalidates affected claims; it need not erase valid work or rerun every\n"},{"number":1439,"text":"check ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)) (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1440,"text":"\n"},{"number":1441,"text":"The governing assurance can be established from applicable retained\n"},{"number":1442,"text":"evidence together with new evidence; the completeness of that account is\n"},{"number":1443,"text":"distinct from the freshness of every execution. Selection considers\n"},{"number":1444,"text":"impact-analysis, acquisition, execution and assessment costs together,\n"},{"number":1445,"text":"with anticipated costs distinguished from measurements\n"},{"number":1446,"text":"([ACTIVATION §6](ACTIVATION.md#6-cost-and-proportionality)). The\n"},{"number":1447,"text":"required assurance, risk policy and mandatory gates constrain that\n"},{"number":1448,"text":"optimisation; a cheap selection that leaves a required obligation\n"},{"number":1449,"text":"uncovered is insufficient. Broad or\n"},{"number":1450,"text":"uncertain impact, a change to the selection model, an applicable release\n"},{"number":1451,"text":"rule or evidence that selection missed a dependency can justify wider\n"},{"number":1452,"text":"testing; full-suite execution remains available and may itself have\n"},{"number":1453,"text":"coverage gaps. No universal full-suite cadence follows, and no\n"},{"number":1454,"text":"optimisation removes a separately required gate. Failures enter diagnosis\n"},{"number":1455,"text":"and an authorised response\n"},{"number":1456,"text":"([ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation));\n"},{"number":1457,"text":"the next selected action may acquire evidence before any repair is\n"},{"number":1458,"text":"justified. [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse)\n"},{"number":1459,"text":"applies this relation to closed results and handoffs; its three\n"},{"number":1460,"text":"invalidators are kinds of change Δ, and a closed result is affected when\n"},{"number":1461,"text":"its `D*(t)` meets `I(Δ)` (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1462,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1499,"heading":"FOUNDATIONS/4. Algebra/Formal representation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F4.%20Algebra%2FFormal%20representation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"ee781e1bc6aff83d8076d1acb5f713935e36ce959d635e3cd4642910bce2913d","start_line":1463,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1463,"text":"### Formal representation\n"},{"number":1464,"text":"\n"},{"number":1465,"text":"An a_c interpretation of these assurance relations represents their\n"},{"number":1466,"text":"material obligations and dependency relationships. Its fidelity and the\n"},{"number":1467,"text":"acquired views that project it follow\n"},{"number":1468,"text":"[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §6](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#6-interpretation-and-models)\n"},{"number":1469,"text":"and [Constraint surfaces](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#constraint-surfaces).\n"},{"number":1470,"text":"It distinguishes five kinds of support for a statement: a\n"},{"number":1471,"text":"stated formula, a discharged mathematical argument, mechanically checked\n"},{"number":1472,"text":"structure, an externally assessed predicate, and evidence from execution.\n"},{"number":1473,"text":"An external predicate retains the source, scope and evidence required to\n"},{"number":1474,"text":"establish it; an arbitrary truth label does not discharge the obligation.\n"},{"number":1475,"text":"No particular proof assistant, probability library or execution engine is\n"},{"number":1476,"text":"selected (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1477,"text":"\n"},{"number":1478,"text":"Assessment of these assurance relations demonstrates the applicable\n"},{"number":1479,"text":"positive, negative and unresolved cases in [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md),\n"},{"number":1480,"text":"including weak assertions, insufficient observations, shared error, and change selection\n"},{"number":1481,"text":"that either retains valid evidence or invalidates affected evidence.\n"},{"number":1482,"text":"Mathematical proof, exhaustive checks of a finite model, sampled tests and\n"},{"number":1483,"text":"observed use retain their distinct scopes. Finite examples do not prove\n"},{"number":1484,"text":"the universal implications above. An unproved universal claim can remain\n"},{"number":1485,"text":"unresolved while bounded construction and assurance proceed where their\n"},{"number":1486,"text":"governing conditions permit them (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1487,"text":"\n"},{"number":1488,"text":"Assessment of these owners and their consumers follows\n"},{"number":1489,"text":"[EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations) and\n"},{"number":1490,"text":"[§7](EVALUATION.md#7-qualification-of-frames-and-of-the-method).\n"},{"number":1491,"text":"Source semantics, formal fidelity and actual use retain their separate\n"},{"number":1492,"text":"evidence within the applicable conformance and qualification criteria;\n"},{"number":1493,"text":"these obligations do not make each test a theorem-proving exercise (P6).\n"},{"number":1494,"text":"\n"},{"number":1495,"text":"Purpose and material relation of the assurance relations: they connect\n"},{"number":1496,"text":"construction results to the obligations they support, expose shared\n"},{"number":1497,"text":"errors, and direct reassessment to affected claims while retaining\n"},{"number":1498,"text":"evidence whose applicability is established (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":1499,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1506,"heading":"FOUNDATIONS/5. Hypotheses","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md#FOUNDATIONS%2F5.%20Hypotheses","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","sha256":"9ed39575457f5c1d6345b2c8540d82c6830cf66b2ce0a75b077d3ed1eab2a70b","start_line":1500,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","lines":[{"number":1500,"text":"## 5. Hypotheses\n"},{"number":1501,"text":"\n"},{"number":1502,"text":"Not law; carried for falsification: categorical equivalence of 𝒜 and ℐ under\n"},{"number":1503,"text":"some reformulation; universal algorithmic capture of meaning; the statistical\n"},{"number":1504,"text":"Markov boundary (candidate status under\n"},{"number":1505,"text":"[WORLD_MODEL §4](WORLD_MODEL.md#epistemic-status));\n"},{"number":1506,"text":"traversal composition laws of any runtime.\n"}]},{"end_line":9,"heading":"GLOSSARY","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/GLOSSARY.md#GLOSSARY","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/GLOSSARY.md","sha256":"4fefd86952744fdc94ce3ac65d8abf098bdd4a67e30d0d2edb5dd5200e64fec6","start_line":1,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/GLOSSARY.md","lines":[{"number":1,"text":"# GLOSSARY\n"},{"number":2,"text":"\n"},{"number":3,"text":"Guide. A non-deciding locator index from indexed spellings to the clauses\n"},{"number":4,"text":"of this corpus that declare their bounded contexts and own their concepts.\n"},{"number":5,"text":"It realises the glossary that\n"},{"number":6,"text":"[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#5-bounded-context-semantic-resolution)\n"},{"number":7,"text":"names and adds nothing to that law. Every clause names the principle that\n"},{"number":8,"text":"requires it (P0 to P6, FOUNDATIONS §3).\n"},{"number":9,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":36,"heading":"GLOSSARY/1. Index contract","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/GLOSSARY.md#GLOSSARY%2F1.%20Index%20contract","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/GLOSSARY.md","sha256":"7a742b9d0e6a890bc0757ed591768314a1a1c8958fd939854971a43bd6dd7698","start_line":10,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/GLOSSARY.md","lines":[{"number":10,"text":"## 1. Index contract\n"},{"number":11,"text":"\n"},{"number":12,"text":"This member contains no semantic definition. It declares no bounded\n"},{"number":13,"text":"context, concept, import, translation, equivalence, disambiguation or\n"},{"number":14,"text":"authority. It is a non-deciding index into the clauses that own those\n"},{"number":15,"text":"meanings in the selected complete STDO basis (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":16,"text":"\n"},{"number":17,"text":"Each row records an indexed spelling, the bounded-context identity\n"},{"number":18,"text":"declared by the cited owning clause, and the exact owning concept clause.\n"},{"number":19,"text":"§17 uses a second row form for a label that several clauses use: the\n"},{"number":20,"text":"label, a locator naming where that use occurs, and the owning clause. The\n"},{"number":21,"text":"locator only says where to look; it defines nothing and declares no\n"},{"number":22,"text":"context, which the owning clause supplies;\n"},{"number":23,"text":"§2 states how a row records a concept that a context holds by import, and\n"},{"number":24,"text":"a concept whose member declares no bounded context for it.\n"},{"number":25,"text":"The owning clause together with the selected basis identifies the candidate meaning;\n"},{"number":26,"text":"the occurrence being resolved still supplies its own governed scope (P1,\n"},{"number":27,"text":"P3). A row whose context or owning clause does not resolve is invalid, and\n"},{"number":28,"text":"this index cannot repair it (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":29,"text":"\n"},{"number":30,"text":"Repeated spellings in different rows are intentional. Locator law\n"},{"number":38,"text":"\n"},{"number":39,"text":"Every locus is an owning clause within this corpus (P6, P3). Each\n"},{"number":40,"text":"section names the clause that declares its context. A row's owning concept\n"},{"number":41,"text":"clause is the section that defines the concept. Where that section's\n"},{"number":42,"text":"member declares the row's context, the clause declares the row's\n"},{"number":43,"text":"bounded-context identity and owns the concept, in its own text or through\n"},{"number":44,"text":"the context-ownership statement of its own member (P6, P1). Where a\n"},{"number":45,"text":"context holds a concept that another member defines, by an import\n"},{"number":46,"text":"declaration or by an owner relation that the context's declaring member\n"},{"number":47,"text":"states\n"},{"number":48,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members)),\n"},{"number":49,"text":"the row cites the defining section as owning concept clause and names the\n"},{"number":50,"text":"declaration or owner relation in its relation clause (P1, P3). Otherwise\n"},{"number":51,"text":"the relation clause, where given, points to a clause that relates the\n"},{"number":52,"text":"concept to another member or context; the index states no relation itself\n"},{"number":53,"text":"(P1, P6).\n"},{"number":54,"text":"\n"},{"number":55,"text":"A concept defined outside every bounded context its member declares has\n"},{"number":56,"text":"that member as its source context\n"},{"number":57,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members)).\n"},{"number":58,"text":"§16 indexes those concepts with the member in place of a bounded-context\n"},{"number":59,"text":"identity. Such a row declares no context, and a context holds one of those\n"},{"number":60,"text":"concepts only by its own import (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":61,"text":"\n"},{"number":62,"text":"A term without such an owning clause is not a valid row under §1, and\n"},{"number":63,"text":"this index carries no such row (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":64,"text":"\n"},{"number":65,"text":"Index watch. A derived surface or projected frame that relies on this\n"},{"number":66,"text":"index to locate meaning watches it through the index's path and digest,\n"},{"number":67,"text":"recorded separately from the deciding sources it was derived from. Locator\n"},{"number":68,"text":"drift in this index then makes that surface or frame stale\n"},{"number":69,"text":"([PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#11-one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary),\n"},{"number":70,"text":"staleness binding), and the watch does not make this index an owner of\n"},{"number":71,"text":"meaning (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":72,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":82,"heading":"GLOSSARY/3. A boundary claim names its\n"},{"number":150,"text":"object, the evidence that supports it and the basis it holds on, and it\n"},{"number":151,"text":"holds only as far as that evidence goes (P3, P6). A claim that an\n"},{"number":152,"text":"object's observed boundary state is sufficient for a task is a material\n"},{"number":153,"text":"sufficiency claim of\n"},{"number":154,"text":"[RF-003](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-003-material-sufficiency), bounded by\n"},{"number":155,"text":"that task: it is not completeness, and it does not establish that the\n"},{"number":156,"text":"boundary screens the object's interior from everything outside it. That\n"},{"number":157,"text":"stronger claim, a statistical Markov boundary, is a hypothesis\n"},{"number":158,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §5](FOUNDATIONS.md#5-hypotheses)); no work relies on it as\n"},{"number":159,"text":"established, and a profile that uses such a construct states its\n"},{"number":160,"text":"epistemic status (P5). Purpose and material relation: this law was\n"},{"number":161,"text":"decided only in the optional world-model profile, so a Product that does\n"},{"number":162,"text":"not adopt that profile had no rule for boundary claims, and the common\n"},{"number":163,"text":"single ownership requirement, item 8, requires generic law to be\n"},{"number":164,"text":"available without an optional profile; [WORLD_MODEL §4](WORLD_MODEL.md#4-the-markov-object-construct)\n"},{"number":165,"text":"refines it.\n"},{"number":166,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":180,"heading":"IDENTITY/3. Readable and opaque identity\n"},{"number":168,"text":"\n"},{"number":169,"text":"Identity may be opaque, such as a GUID or UUID; human-readable, such as\n"},{"number":170,"text":"`REQ-F-CAPABILITY-001`; or hybrid, where one component is readable and\n"},{"number":171,"text":"another is opaque. Authority identity and conservation (STDO-UP-004)\n"},{"number":225,"text":"\n"},{"number":226,"text":"Authority is an identity-bearing semantic relation, not a display label,\n"},{"number":227,"text":"capability string, actor identity or reachable code path. What such a realisation publishes, and for which surfaces, is\n"},{"number":266,"text":"realisation law outside this member\n"},{"number":267,"text":"([DESIGN_MODULE §12](DESIGN_MODULE.md#identity-defaults-from-a-bound-runtime-realisation)).\n"},{"number":268,"text":"\n"},{"number":269,"text":"Derived domains may override identity format and structure for their own\n"},{"number":270,"text":"kinds. An override is lawful only if it preserves (P3):\n"},{"number":271,"text":"\n"},{"number":272,"text":"- scoped uniqueness;\n"},{"number":273,"text":"- explicit kind distinction;\n"},{"number":274,"text":"- deterministic parsing or reading;\n"},{"number":275,"text":"- non-aliasing between family and member identities; and\n"},{"number":276,"text":"- stable downstream traceability.\n"},{"number":277,"text":"\n"},{"number":278,"text":"Overrides are published in domain authority. They do not exist only as\n"},{"number":279,"text":"ad hoc regex assumptions hidden in implementation code (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":280,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":309,"heading":"IDENTITY/7. and\n"},{"number":292,"text":"- the distinction between grouping identities and concrete executable or\n"},{"number":293,"text":"  traceable identities.\n"},{"number":294,"text":"\n"},{"number":295,"text":"Suitable publication surfaces include (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":296,"text":"\n"},{"number":297,"text":"- the product definition (conventionally `PRODUCT.md`) for the active\n"},{"number":298,"text":"  identity kinds and their governed role;\n"},{"number":299,"text":"- requirement surfaces for obligations around identity stability or\n"},{"number":300,"text":"  uniqueness;\n"},{"number":301,"text":"- design or ADR surfaces for parsing, serialisation or normalisation\n"},{"number":302,"text":"  rules; and\n"},{"number":303,"text":"- a dedicated identity registry surface, such as a project's own\n"},{"number":304,"text":"  `IDENTITY.md`, when the domain has enough complexity to justify one.\n"},{"number":305,"text":"\n"},{"number":306,"text":"The important rule is that identity overrides are visible in domain\n"},{"number":307,"text":"authority, auditable, and recoverable without reverse-engineering regexes\n"},{"number":308,"text":"from implementation code (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":309,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":328,"heading":"IDENTITY/8. Parsing\n"},{"number":311,"text":"\n"},{"number":312,"text":"Regex extraction from prose is not a complete identity model. At most,\n"},{"number":313,"text":"regex may be a provisional extractor over a surface whose identity law is\n"},{"number":314,"text":"already defined elsewhere (P3, P1). Therefore:\n"},{"number":315,"text":"\n"},{"number":316,"text":"- a parser distinguishes concrete identity kinds from grouping labels;\n"},{"number":317,"text":"- family markers, display aliases and prose headings are not promoted\n"},{"number":318,"text":"  into executable or traceable object identities unless the governing\n"},{"number":319,"text":"  identity law says they are first-class identities of their own kind;\n"},{"number":320,"text":"  and\n"},{"number":321,"text":"- acceptance criteria, test cases and similar subordinate identities are\n"},{"number":322,"text":"  not collapsed into requirement identity merely because their readable\n"},{"number":323,"text":"  form is derived from a requirement token.\n"},{"number":324,"text":"\n"},{"number":325,"text":"If a domain needs family identities, it should publish them explicitly as\n"},{"number":326,"text":"`requirement_family` identities rather than rely on string-shape\n"},{"number":327,"text":"accidents (P3).\n"},{"number":328,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":347,"heading":"IDENTITY/9. Release version boundary\n"},{"number":330,"text":"\n"},{"number":331,"text":"Release version is not the same thing as object identity (P3). Under the release law\n"},{"number":332,"text":"([RELEASE §1 and §2](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities), with\n"},{"number":333,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §6](SPEC_METHOD.md#6-lineage-and-release)):\n"},{"number":334,"text":"\n"},{"number":335,"text":"- an immutable release cut is the only exact operative release\n"},{"number":336,"text":"  identifier;\n"},{"number":337,"text":"- an RC-profile mutable version-line selector only names the highest-ordinal\n"},{"number":338,"text":"  published immutable cut on its line (FOUNDATIONS §2); a stable profile\n"},{"number":339,"text":"  discovers its immutable tag directly under RELEASE §2;\n"},{"number":340,"text":"- release version is a release-process fact; and\n"},{"number":341,"text":"- release version is not the live constitutional identity of every\n"},{"number":342,"text":"  object in the project.\n"},{"number":343,"text":"\n"},{"number":344,"text":"So the method distinguishes object identity, release identity,\n"},{"number":345,"text":"publication or revision coordinates, and mutable discovery selectors.\n"},{"number":346,"text":"These may relate, but they are not interchangeable (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":347,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":364,"heading":"IDENTITY/10. Minimum questions\n"},{"number":349,"text":"\n"},{"number":350,"text":"When defining or auditing an identity surface, ask (P3, P6):\n"},{"number":351,"text":"\n"},{"number":352,"text":"1. What authority owns this identity?\n"},{"number":353,"text":"2. What kind of thing does this identity denote?\n"},{"number":354,"text":"3. What scope makes it unique?\n"},{"number":355,"text":"4. Is the identity stable enough for the governed lifecycle?\n"},{"number":356,"text":"5. Is the readable form only convenience, or is it being over-trusted?\n"},{"number":357,"text":"6. Can a parser distinguish families, members, aliases and revisions\n"},{"number":358,"text":"   without ambiguity?\n"},{"number":359,"text":"7. Is this an engine or runtime identity, a domain semantic identity, or\n"},{"number":360,"text":"   a release identity?\n"},{"number":361,"text":"\n"},{"number":362,"text":"If those questions cannot be answered, the identity surface is\n"},{"number":363,"text":"under-defined (P3).\n"},{"number":364,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":366,"heading":"IDENTITY/11. Consequence for implementations\n"},{"number":392,"text":"\n"},{"number":393,"text":"Implementations should prefer typed identity readers, explicit\n"},{"number":394,"text":"identity-kind distinctions, and source-of-authority parsing contracts.\n"},{"number":395,"text":"They should avoid broad regex mining as the real identity model, silent\n"},{"number":396,"text":"coercion between family identities and concrete identities, and leaking\n"},{"number":397,"text":"engine identity grammar into domain semantics (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":398,"text":"\n"},{"number":399,"text":"If a project currently relies on those patterns, the first lawful repair\n"},{"number":400,"text":"is to contain the immediate bug. The enduring repair is to publish\n"},{"number":401,"text":"explicit identity law and move implementations onto it (P3, P0).\n"}]},{"end_line":24,"heading":"ODD","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ODD.md","sha256":"0f37f6950ece2b8aef9a2dfb499c2ac292f3d0e2e11c245da66e096739a4254f","start_line":1,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ODD.md","lines":[{"number":1,"text":"# ODD\n"},{"number":2,"text":"\n"},{"number":3,"text":"Tier 3. The Outcome-Driven Development profile: graph-native product\n"},{"number":4,"text":"authoring over a declared asset graph. It imports the families that\n"},{"number":5,"text":"[§1 Foundation to law](#foundation-to-law) lists by reference under\n"},{"number":6,"text":"[PROFILES §1](PROFILES.md#1-the-boundary) and restates none of them. Inside\n"},{"number":7,"text":"its bounded context it uses its own terms freely: graph, node, asset,\n"},{"number":8,"text":"vector, edge, graph function, traversal, worksite, ledger, event log, GTL,\n"},{"number":9,"text":"ABG, F_P and F_H (P0, P1). `F_D` is the exact-edition common import below.\n"},{"number":10,"text":"\n"},{"number":11,"text":"Two definitions are used here and owned elsewhere. The a_c traversal record\n"},{"number":12,"text":"and the functor kinds are\n"},{"number":13,"text":"[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds);\n"},{"number":14,"text":"the core result algebra is [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results).\n"},{"number":15,"text":"This profile's graph traversal and its F_P and F_H shorthands are its\n"},{"number":16,"text":"own concepts and are not those records by spelling. Its F_D use imports\n"},{"number":17,"text":"the common kind through [§5](#probabilistic-compute), without inheriting\n"},{"number":18,"text":"any operation authority. The Executive, Worker\n"},{"number":19,"text":"and Reviewer of [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) are roles, and roles\n"},{"number":20,"text":"are relations over steps in which no role name confers an operation\n"},{"number":21,"text":"([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)); the actor, the\n"},{"number":22,"text":"executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are different\n"},{"number":23,"text":"coordinates (AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5) (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":24,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":76,"heading":"ODD/1. Position\n"},{"number":26,"text":"\n"},{"number":27,"text":"This profile makes one instruction precise: `using ODD, build this\n"},{"number":28,"text":"product`. The instruction should mean something stronger than writing\n"},{"number":29,"text":"product documents, sketching a graph or adding a few helper scripts (P0,\n"},{"number":30,"text":"P2). It means:\n"},{"number":31,"text":"\n"},{"number":32,"text":"- build the product as a GTL/ABG domain product;\n"},{"number":33,"text":"- define typed domain assets and nodes;\n"},{"number":34,"text":"- publish named graph functions as the constructive carrier;\n"},{"number":35,"text":"- bind them into a GTL module;\n"},{"number":36,"text":"- let ABG own traversal governance, runtime facts and provenance;\n"},{"number":37,"text":"- let ABG own continuation and re-entry after each publish boundary;\n"},{"number":38,"text":"- keep product commands and services as cooperative bounded-step\n"},{"number":39,"text":"  subsystems that publish assets or evidence and return control to ABG;\n"},{"number":40,"text":"- expose visible current state as a projection over constructive history.\n"},{"number":41,"text":"\n"},{"number":42,"text":"ODD is a programming paradigm, not only a documentation preference. Its form\n"},{"number":43,"text":"is `product = typed asset/domain model + GTL-defined graph functions + ABG\n"},{"number":44,"text":"traversal-control runtime + governed projection/query surfaces`. A product\n"},{"number":45,"text":"whose constructive carrier stays hidden in imperative loops, local service\n"},{"number":46,"text":"logic or product-specific orchestration scripts is not yet built with this\n"},{"number":47,"text":"profile (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":48,"text":"\n"},{"number":49,"text":"ODD, GTL and ABG name normative capability roles and a construction\n"},{"number":50,"text":"algebra, not a required repository, package, vendor or concrete\n"},{"number":51,"text":"implementation. ODD, Outcome-Driven Development, names the graph-native\n"},{"number":52,"text":"product-authoring profile. GTL, Graph Transformation Language, names the\n"},{"number":53,"text":"role of the typed declarative graph language. ABG names the role of the\n"},{"number":54,"text":"singular traversal-governance and runtime-truth authority (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":55,"text":"\n"},{"number":56,"text":"This profile owns those concepts in the graph-native bounded context\n"},{"number":57,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:graph-native-odd` under the selected complete\n"},{"number":58,"text":"STDO basis. The context covers the ODD product shape, the GTL language\n"},{"number":59,"text":"role, the ABG method role, graph assets, vectors, functions, traversals and\n"},{"number":60,"text":"the graph and runtime worker and evaluator shorthands defined here. It does\n"},{"number":61,"text":"not absorb a consuming Product's domain semantics, nor a concrete runtime's\n"},{"number":62,"text":"carriers that happen to share a spelling (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":63,"text":"\n"},{"number":64,"text":"A consumer binds the roles to concrete conforming realisations in its own\n"},{"number":65,"text":"Product, requirements, design and immutable dependency identity. A\n"},{"number":66,"text":"consumer, a reference realisation or a historical product may prove or\n"},{"number":67,"text":"falsify conformance; none of them supplies method authority (P6).\n"},{"number":68,"text":"\n"},{"number":69,"text":"The profile has two core jobs: to describe the product as a declared asset\n"},{"number":70,"text":"graph in graph-native terms, and to ensure that automation never outruns a\n"},{"number":71,"text":"lawful manual traversal of the same graph. Method role\n"},{"number":202,"text":"\n"},{"number":203,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD](SPEC_METHOD.md) is the general constitutional method: the\n"},{"number":204,"text":"baseline for goals, intent, product, requirements, design and lawful\n"},{"number":205,"text":"re-entry. This profile is the graph-native ODD product-authoring method\n"},{"number":206,"text":"whose primary constructive carrier is GTL-defined graph functions. It holds\n"},{"number":207,"text":"two kinds of law: constitutional law for graph-native traversal governance\n"},{"number":208,"text":"(assets, vectors, traversal, graph functions), and product-authoring law\n"},{"number":209,"text":"for building an ODD product correctly over that substrate (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":210,"text":"\n"},{"number":211,"text":"The profile does not replace a product-specific domain method such as the\n"},{"number":212,"text":"world-model profile (WORLD_MODEL, tier 3). Where a product is both ODD and\n"},{"number":213,"text":"world-model-driven, this profile governs graph-native structure and ODD\n"},{"number":214,"text":"product shape and the world-model profile governs world-model semantics,\n"},{"number":215,"text":"publication and composition law. The two compose (P1, P4a).\n"},{"number":216,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":240,"heading":"ODD/3. Method composition\n"},{"number":218,"text":"\n"},{"number":219,"text":"This profile alone does not suffice for domain-correct product work. It\n"},{"number":220,"text":"gives the structural law for how a graph-native ODD product should be\n"},{"number":221,"text":"built. It does not give the product's domain semantics, its current intent\n"},{"number":222,"text":"and product-definition line, its local capability and constraint\n"},{"number":223,"text":"requirements, or its currently ratified design surfaces (P1, P2).\n"},{"number":224,"text":"\n"},{"number":225,"text":"The composition rule: this profile says how to build the product as a\n"},{"number":226,"text":"graph-native ODD product; domain methods say what semantic law the product\n"},{"number":227,"text":"must honour; the local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design say\n"},{"number":228,"text":"what the currently ratified local line is. For a graph-native\n"},{"number":229,"text":"software-development ODD product, this profile provides the substrate and\n"},{"number":230,"text":"structural law and the product's local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,\n"},{"number":231,"text":"requirements, design records and GTL surfaces provide the local line. For\n"},{"number":232,"text":"a world-model product, this profile provides the substrate and structural\n"},{"number":233,"text":"law, the world-model profile provides the semantic law, and the product's\n"},{"number":234,"text":"local `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, requirements and design provide the local\n"},{"number":235,"text":"line (P1, P2).\n"},{"number":236,"text":"\n"},{"number":237,"text":"An agent that reads only this profile should understand the paradigm.\n"},{"number":238,"text":"To build one concrete product correctly it must then read the\n"},{"number":239,"text":"product-specific method and the local authority surfaces (P1, P2).\n"},{"number":240,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":272,"heading":"ODD/4. Method library classes\n"},{"number":242,"text":"\n"},{"number":243,"text":"The method library has two roles: mutable source authors a future release,\n"},{"number":244,"text":"and consumers select one complete immutable release. The source library in\n"},{"number":245,"text":"the methodology's source repository is the authoring library for the next\n"},{"number":246,"text":"method cut; mutable source governs no consumer before publication and\n"},{"number":247,"text":"explicit selection. The shared versioned STDO store holds each installed\n"},{"number":248,"text":"distribution of one selected immutable release cut. A product definition\n"},{"number":249,"text":"addresses that distribution by an exact logical release URI and\n"},{"number":250,"text":"installed-manifest digest, independent of the machine-local store path; a\n"},{"number":251,"text":"project-local copy is optional and is not the default (P6, P3;\n"},{"number":252,"text":"[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#4-shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager)).\n"},{"number":253,"text":"\n"},{"number":254,"text":"The selected immutable cut is consumer authority. Installed bytes must\n"},{"number":255,"text":"match that cut; mutable source and the moving version-line selector cannot\n"},{"number":256,"text":"silently repair, replace or outrank it. A mismatch is an adoption defect,\n"},{"number":257,"text":"resolved by selecting and installing one complete released cut and not\n"},{"number":258,"text":"by mixing source and installed members. When an installed distribution\n"},{"number":259,"text":"disagrees with its selected immutable release, the selected release wins\n"},{"number":260,"text":"and the installation must be repaired. Mutable source authors a future\n"},{"number":261,"text":"cut; it does not govern the installed consumer (P6, P3;\n"},{"number":262,"text":"[RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption)).\n"},{"number":263,"text":"\n"},{"number":264,"text":"Both the authoring library and an installed distribution contain three\n"},{"number":265,"text":"classes of document. Method members are the constitutional method\n"},{"number":266,"text":"surfaces, the members that [README](README.md#documents) names as method\n"},{"number":267,"text":"members: the tier 1 and tier 2 standards and, when a\n"},{"number":268,"text":"project selects them, the tier 3 profiles. Guides (`*_GUIDE.md`) are operational guides and application standards\n"},{"number":269,"text":"that refine application of the method. Templates (`*_TEMPLATE.md`) are\n"},{"number":270,"text":"reusable starter forms and examples and are convenience artifacts only.\n"},{"number":271,"text":"Only method members are constitutional method surfaces (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":272,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":277,"heading":"ODD/5. In one software-development ODD product the nodes include\n"},{"number":282,"text":"`intent`, `product`, `requirements`, `design`, `module_decomp`, `code`,\n"},{"number":283,"text":"`uat_testcases`, `integration_tests`, `bootloader` and build targets. Graph model/Probabilistic compute","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ODD.md#ODD%2F5.%20Graph%20model%2FProbabilistic%20compute","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ODD.md","sha256":"943df32e76b20ff7b0b6131d75b5bca2fc30deab48f89102c704123cb4e49e76","start_line":294,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/ODD.md","lines":[{"number":294,"text":"### Probabilistic compute\n"},{"number":295,"text":"\n"},{"number":296,"text":"Probabilistic compute in this profile is bounded constructive work over\n"},{"number":297,"text":"one declared vector or edge traversal, where the graph or runtime does not\n"},{"number":298,"text":"fully determine the worker's internal solution path. One vector or edge\n"},{"number":299,"text":"traversal is the bounded unit of probabilistic compute (P0).\n"},{"number":300,"text":"\n"},{"number":301,"text":"Binding of the bounded step. FOUNDATIONS P0 lets a\n"},{"number":302,"text":"profile bind the bounded step to its own traversal unit and names\n"},{"number":303,"text":"[PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this profile,\n"},{"number":304,"text":"as the keeper of that binding. Direction: from the step of\n"},{"number":305,"text":"FOUNDATIONS P0 to one declared ODD vector or edge traversal. Preserved\n"},{"number":306,"text":"meaning: the step's selected context fits the actor's envelope, the\n"},{"number":307,"text":"actor's internal path within the step is its own, and the traversal is\n"},{"number":308,"text":"the admissible external space. Narrowed scope: one declared vector or edge\n"},{"number":309,"text":"traversal of a published graph. Invalidation: a change to FOUNDATIONS P0,\n"},{"number":310,"text":"to the vector's declaration or to the selected basis invalidates the\n"},{"number":311,"text":"binding until it is evaluated again (P0, P1).\n"},{"number":312,"text":"\n"},{"number":313,"text":"The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required\n"},{"number":314,"text":"upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role\n"},{"number":315,"text":"or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance\n"},{"number":316,"text":"obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion\n"},{"number":317,"text":"states. ABG may govern, invoke, observe and classify the traversal; it\n"},{"number":318,"text":"does not own the worker's hidden constructive path. Whatever the traversal\n"},{"number":319,"text":"boundary does not constrain remains worker-internal HOW: hidden LLM\n"},{"number":320,"text":"reasoning, heuristic search, domain implementation strategy, tool-local\n"},{"number":321,"text":"execution detail and product-specific business choice (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":322,"text":"\n"},{"number":323,"text":"The classifications of work inside one traversal bind two profile\n"},{"number":324,"text":"specialisations and one common import. Equal spelling alone establishes\n"},{"number":325,"text":"none of those relations (P1, P3):\n"},{"number":326,"text":"\n"},{"number":327,"text":"- `F_P` (`urn:stdo:concept:graph-native-odd:f-p`) is the shorthand for the\n"},{"number":328,"text":"  bounded probabilistic worker turn. A\n"},{"number":389,"text":"graph function may realise one outer vector directly, refine one outer\n"},{"number":390,"text":"vector into a small inner workflow, or act as a reusable higher-order\n"},{"number":391,"text":"library function. The outer vector remains the constitutional contract;\n"},{"number":392,"text":"the graph function is the constructive realisation of that contract (P4a,\n"},{"number":393,"text":"P0).\n"},{"number":394,"text":"\n"},{"number":395,"text":"Binding of refinement.\n"},{"number":396,"text":"[ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement) generalises the\n"},{"number":397,"text":"refinement of one outer vector into an inner workflow to any realisation,\n"},{"number":398,"text":"lets a refinement carry an earlier output to a later step only through a\n"},{"number":399,"text":"declared adapter or specialised contract whose declared domain names it,\n"},{"number":400,"text":"and names [PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution), which indexes this\n"},{"number":401,"text":"profile, as the keeper of the ODD binding. Direction: from the typed refinement of ACTIVATION §4 to a graph\n"},{"number":406,"text":"function that refines one outer vector, with the §11.8 environment as its\n"},{"number":407,"text":"specialised contract. Narrowed scope: one published outer\n"},{"number":411,"text":"vector and its declared inner workflow, whose retained functions should\n"},{"number":412,"text":"declare `environment.requires`, `environment.provides` and\n"},{"number":413,"text":"`environment.carries` (§11.8); a later function's declared domain is its\n"},{"number":414,"text":"`environment.requires`, which may require any typed binding available in\n"},{"number":415,"text":"the cumulative carried environment, not only the immediately previous\n"},{"number":416,"text":"output. Self-host boundary\n"},{"number":463,"text":"\n"},{"number":464,"text":"Self-hosting is lawful only while the installed product in use stays\n"},{"number":465,"text":"distinct from the product under development. The distinction is between the installed\n"},{"number":468,"text":"released builder and the in-development product being built, the same\n"},{"number":469,"text":"boundary one compiler release keeps when it builds the next (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":470,"text":"\n"},{"number":471,"text":"The framework must preserve distinct territories, authority surfaces,\n"},{"number":472,"text":"runtime state, and project-owned specification and build-tenant surfaces. If\n"},{"number":473,"text":"automation, runtime resolution or qualification silently merges those\n"},{"number":474,"text":"surfaces, the framework violates this profile (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":475,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":501,"heading":"ODD/8. Responsibility layers and local binding\n"},{"number":477,"text":"\n"},{"number":478,"text":"This profile governs structural responsibility layers and their required\n"},{"number":479,"text":"publication shape. It does not freeze one product's local asset names as\n"},{"number":480,"text":"universal ODD doctrine. A responsibility layer expresses one capability\n"},{"number":481,"text":"class; the product binds that capability to its own local domain\n"},{"number":482,"text":"semantics; the GTL carrier publishes the lawful transitions for that bound\n"},{"number":483,"text":"capability (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":484,"text":"\n"},{"number":485,"text":"Capability classes may include bootstrap or intake, design,\n"},{"number":486,"text":"implementation, qualification, release, operational transition and\n"},{"number":487,"text":"retrofit. They are responsibility-layer ideas, not mandatory universal\n"},{"number":488,"text":"instance names (P1).\n"},{"number":489,"text":"\n"},{"number":490,"text":"In one concrete product each active layer should bind explicitly to local\n"},{"number":491,"text":"typed assets or typed nodes, public graph-function carriers, the required\n"},{"number":492,"text":"carried environment, proof or closure surfaces, and projection or query\n"},{"number":493,"text":"surfaces. An audit should therefore distinguish clearly between shared\n"},{"number":494,"text":"ODD structural law and local product semantic bindings (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":495,"text":"\n"},{"number":496,"text":"A product that copies another product's local asset names without\n"},{"number":497,"text":"semantic need is not reusing the method; that is accidental doctrine\n"},{"number":498,"text":"transfer. A product that declares a capability in prose but does not bind\n"},{"number":499,"text":"it into typed assets, graph functions and proof lanes has under-built that\n"},{"number":500,"text":"capability (P1, P2).\n"},{"number":501,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":548,"heading":"ODD/9. Method governance and audit\n"},{"number":503,"text":"\n"},{"number":504,"text":"Products governed under this profile should be audited against it as the\n"},{"number":505,"text":"shared constitutional surface. The audit should ask at minimum (P6):\n"},{"number":506,"text":"\n"},{"number":507,"text":"- which responsibility layer or capability class is being implemented;\n"},{"number":508,"text":"- which local typed assets or nodes bind that capability into the product;\n"},{"number":509,"text":"- which public graph functions carry the constructive transition;\n"},{"number":510,"text":"- which proof or closure lane justifies the capability;\n"},{"number":511,"text":"- which projected or query state is exposed without replacing ABG runtime\n"},{"number":512,"text":"  truth;\n"},{"number":513,"text":"- whether any product command, service or query surface is trying to\n"},{"number":514,"text":"  replace ABG continuation with tenant-local orchestration;\n"},{"number":515,"text":"- whether the execution-authority audit (§11.5B) proves that traversal\n"},{"number":516,"text":"  loops, actor invocation, process supervision, retry and continuation,\n"},{"number":517,"text":"  runtime events and closure folds remain owned by ABG.\n"},{"number":518,"text":"\n"},{"number":519,"text":"Approved shared-pattern work must update this profile when it changes or\n"},{"number":520,"text":"clarifies the reusable structural law; product-local work may stay local\n"},{"number":521,"text":"when it changes no shared structural law. Grey work must not be silently\n"},{"number":522,"text":"absorbed into the line (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":523,"text":"\n"},{"number":524,"text":"An implementation or design move that the current profile does not\n"},{"number":525,"text":"clearly cover must be evaluated against this profile and resolved as one\n"},{"number":526,"text":"of: compliant with the current profile; non-compliant with it; or valid\n"},{"number":527,"text":"and worth incorporating into it. If the result is incorporation, the\n"},{"number":528,"text":"implementation is not fully approved until this profile is updated. If the\n"},{"number":529,"text":"result is non-compliance, the implementation should be repriced, repaired\n"},{"number":530,"text":"or rejected, not normalised by repetition (P6).\n"},{"number":531,"text":"\n"},{"number":532,"text":"Mapping of the audit outcome to the core result algebra. Purpose: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) states\n"},{"number":533,"text":"the outcome of every evaluation in the core. Material relation: a design,\n"},{"number":534,"text":"ticket or proof that consumes the audit reads incorporation as neither\n"},{"number":535,"text":"compliance nor failure. Each outcome maps for the predicate \"the move\n"},{"number":536,"text":"complies with the current profile\" (P5, P6):\n"},{"number":537,"text":"\n"},{"number":538,"text":"| Outcome | Core value | Ground |\n"},{"number":539,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":540,"text":"| compliant | satisfied | the move meets the law of the current profile |\n"},{"number":541,"text":"| non-compliant | falsified | the law of this profile that the move violates is the counterexample |\n"},{"number":542,"text":"| valid and worth incorporating | out_of_frame | the current profile does not declare the law the move needs; the outcome names that law, this profile as its owner and the update it requires, which is the reconfiguration pressure of out_of_frame ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or indeterminate) |\n"},{"number":543,"text":"\n"},{"number":544,"text":"In practice no shared structural pattern becomes approved by usage; no\n"},{"number":545,"text":"grey pattern becomes constitutional by drift; reusable structural law is\n"},{"number":546,"text":"ratified in this profile; and local product law is ratified in the\n"},{"number":547,"text":"product's own authority surfaces (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":548,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":585,"heading":"ODD/10. What an ODD product is\n"},{"number":550,"text":"\n"},{"number":551,"text":"An ODD product is a configured GTL/ABG domain product whose constructive\n"},{"number":552,"text":"work is carried by published graph functions over typed domain assets. Its\n"},{"number":553,"text":"stable application boundary is (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":554,"text":"\n"},{"number":555,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":556,"text":"App\n"},{"number":557,"text":"= Bootstrap Surface\n"},{"number":558,"text":"+ Initialization Surface\n"},{"number":559,"text":"+ Domain Configuration\n"},{"number":560,"text":"+ Typed Domain Assets / Nodes\n"},{"number":561,"text":"+ GTL Function Catalog\n"},{"number":562,"text":"+ GTL Module\n"},{"number":563,"text":"+ Policy Hook Bindings\n"},{"number":564,"text":"+ ABG Runtime\n"},{"number":565,"text":"+ Projection / Query Surface\n"},{"number":566,"text":"+ Proof Surface\n"},{"number":567,"text":"```\n"},{"number":568,"text":"\n"},{"number":569,"text":"The ownership split is read strictly. The two topology subsections below\n"},{"number":570,"text":"name the default topology of a software-development ODD product in this\n"},{"number":571,"text":"ecosystem; the product's `stdo_<label>.json` definition under\n"},{"number":572,"text":"[PRODUCT_DEFINITION](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md) binds the actual locations. At\n"},{"number":573,"text":"the universal layer this profile commits to the authority split (one WHAT\n"},{"number":574,"text":"surface, one HOW relation, runtime owned by ABG, product owning domain\n"},{"number":575,"text":"meaning) and not to directory names; existing projects and other ODD\n"},{"number":576,"text":"product types may use another layout that keeps the split (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":577,"text":"\n"},{"number":578,"text":"The product definition's `reference_frame_bases` bindings carry the\n"},{"number":579,"text":"evaluation-frame meaning of [REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md).
