Scenario rule\n"},{"number":1625,"text":"\n"},{"number":1626,"text":"Scenarios are graph-native proving surfaces, not only test\n"},{"number":1627,"text":"documentation. A scenario bundle should make clear which feature or\n"},{"number":1628,"text":"use-case boundary is exercised; which assets are expected to exist before\n"},{"number":1629,"text":"the scenario starts; which vectors are expected to be traversed; which\n"},{"number":1630,"text":"significant paths are expected to be exercised; and what evidence closes\n"},{"number":1631,"text":"the scenario (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1632,"text":"\n"},{"number":1633,"text":"The best proving paths come from declared scenarios and use cases,\n"},{"number":1634,"text":"because they pressure both feature intent and design decisions. That makes\n"},{"number":1635,"text":"them the best source for selecting the significant code and control paths\n"},{"number":1636,"text":"the system must exercise (P2).\n"},{"number":1637,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1648,"heading":"ODD/13. Installed-dev rule\n"},{"number":1639,"text":"\n"},{"number":1640,"text":"Where the product has an installable development form, decisive proof\n"},{"number":1641,"text":"runs against that installed development form in an isolated environment.\n"},{"number":1642,"text":"For a graph-native ODD product the proving lane should exercise install,\n"},{"number":1643,"text":"project bootstrap, graph traversal, evidence collection and\n"},{"number":1644,"text":"target-relative closure. Direct source checks stay useful and do not\n"},{"number":1645,"text":"replace installed-dev proof (P6, P3). This rule is the profile's binding of\n"},{"number":1646,"text":"[ASSURANCE §5 Installed dev proof](ASSURANCE.md#5-installed-dev-proof), which\n"},{"number":1647,"text":"owns it.\n"},{"number":1648,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1659,"heading":"ODD/14. Dogfooding rule\n"},{"number":1650,"text":"\n"},{"number":1651,"text":"The product should be developed through the same graph-native method it\n"},{"number":1652,"text":"claims to provide. Where the product provides ODD framework behaviour, it\n"},{"number":1653,"text":"must build that behaviour through ODD graph functions and must not merely\n"},{"number":1654,"text":"publish ODD-shaped artifacts after imperative execution has already\n"},{"number":1655,"text":"decided the work. The project should therefore increasingly describe and\n"},{"number":1656,"text":"build itself through explicit assets, explicit vectors, explicit graph\n"},{"number":1657,"text":"functions, explicit scenario bundles and explicit target-relative closure.\n"},{"number":1658,"text":"The method is stronger when the product can walk itself (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":1659,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1668,"heading":"ODD/15. Failure pattern\n"},{"number":1670,"text":"\n"},{"number":1671,"text":"This profile is violated when any of these holds (P6):\n"},{"number":1672,"text":"\n"},{"number":1673,"text":"1. a claimed product step has no corresponding node or vector;\n"},{"number":1674,"text":"2. a graph function exists with no clear outer contract;\n"},{"number":1675,"text":"3. automation performs work that cannot be described as a manual\n"},{"number":1676,"text":"   traversal;\n"},{"number":1677,"text":"4. the installed product depends on authoring-carrier knowledge that a\n"},{"number":1678,"text":"   clean target project should not contain;\n"},{"number":1679,"text":"5. scenarios cannot name the significant paths they intend to prove;\n"},{"number":1680,"text":"6. the project claims closure without target-relative evidence;\n"},{"number":1681,"text":"7. \"last-output feeds next-input\" wiring bypasses the cumulative\n"},{"number":1682,"text":"   environment law;\n"},{"number":1683,"text":"8. zoomed and unzoomed views disagree about whether a carrier is closed;\n"},{"number":1684,"text":"9. imperative service code owns an operative transition that has no\n"},{"number":1685,"text":"   published graph-function outcome contract;\n"},{"number":1686,"text":"10. framework behaviour is implemented as workspace orchestration first\n"},{"number":1687,"text":"    and described with GTL vocabulary only later;\n"},{"number":1688,"text":"11. imperative code decides closure, continuation, semantic target\n"},{"number":1689,"text":"    movement or lineage truth outside declared graph-function, ABG runtime\n"},{"number":1690,"text":"    or product-owned carrier truth;\n"},{"number":1691,"text":"12. a GTL/ABG product or plugin carries hidden execution authority for\n"},{"number":1692,"text":"    traversal loops, actor invocation, process supervision, retry,\n"},{"number":1693,"text":"    continuation, runtime events, projection or closure folds;\n"},{"number":1694,"text":"13. yield or lawful iteration is flattened into retry, block, timeout, a\n"},{"number":1695,"text":"    local waiting state or a hidden CLI loop instead of being represented\n"},{"number":1696,"text":"    as a replay-visible closure disposition;\n"},{"number":1697,"text":"14. a public query, gaps view, postflight string, service method or\n"},{"number":1698,"text":"    installed operator summary can decide next work outside the\n"},{"number":1699,"text":"    constructive evaluation loop;\n"},{"number":1700,"text":"15. a constitutional process cannot be followed end to end by an agentic\n"},{"number":1701,"text":"    coder from the declared authority, or a produced constitutional\n"},{"number":1702,"text":"    artifact is accepted without passing deterministic admission\n"},{"number":1703,"text":"    (§11.7A).\n"},{"number":1704,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1739,"heading":"ODD/17. Invocation rule\n"},{"number":1706,"text":"\n"},{"number":1707,"text":"When an agent or designer is told `using ODD, build this product`, the\n"},{"number":1708,"text":"expected sequence is (P2, P0):\n"},{"number":1709,"text":"\n"},{"number":1710,"text":"1. read SPEC_METHOD and keep the constitutional chain intact;\n"},{"number":1711,"text":"2. read the product-specific method if one exists;\n"},{"number":1712,"text":"3. read the local product authority surfaces: `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,\n"},{"number":1713,"text":"   the relevant requirement families and the active design surfaces;\n"},{"number":1714,"text":"4. identify the product's semantic chain from source to published outcome;\n"},{"number":1715,"text":"5. identify the domain-specific typed assets or nodes;\n"},{"number":1716,"text":"6. identify the public graph-function carriers;\n"},{"number":1717,"text":"7. define the machine-readable function catalogue;\n"},{"number":1718,"text":"8. define or update the GTL module, including the outer callable carriers\n"},{"number":1719,"text":"   and the live traversal boundaries;\n"},{"number":1720,"text":"9. define how coarse carriers, refined inner carriers and executable proof\n"},{"number":1721,"text":"   lanes close together without scale contradiction;\n"},{"number":1722,"text":"10. complete the execution-authority audit for the affected runtime,\n"},{"number":1723,"text":"    plugin, worker, event, projection, assurance, closure or continuation\n"},{"number":1724,"text":"    surfaces;\n"},{"number":1725,"text":"11. define the constructive evaluation loop from intent lineage and model\n"},{"number":1726,"text":"    synthesis through observation, target binding, lawful action\n"},{"number":1727,"text":"    selection, admitted evidence, fulfilment ledger, closure decision and\n"},{"number":1728,"text":"    next-action projection;\n"},{"number":1729,"text":"12. define the closure decision vocabulary, including `yield` as lawful\n"},{"number":1730,"text":"    iteration and not retry, block, timeout or a local waiting state;\n"},{"number":1731,"text":"13. define the projection and query lane as a projection over admitted\n"},{"number":1732,"text":"    constructive history, including the structural coherence rule between\n"},{"number":1733,"text":"    the read model and its source carrier;\n"},{"number":1734,"text":"14. only then implement code, policy and transport surfaces.\n"},{"number":1735,"text":"\n"},{"number":1736,"text":"The instruction does not mean starting from imperative scripts and adding\n"},{"number":1737,"text":"GTL words later, treating graph functions as documentation wrappers, or\n"},{"number":1738,"text":"letting service code become the hidden real carrier (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":1739,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1743,"heading":"ODD/18. Ramp-up checklist\n"},{"number":1778,"text":"\n"},{"number":1779,"text":"An LLM ramping into an ODD product should quickly answer (P0, P2):\n"},{"number":1780,"text":"\n"},{"number":1781,"text":"1. Canonical compression\n"},{"number":1808,"text":"\n"},{"number":1809,"text":"This profile is the graph-native product-authoring method for building\n"},{"number":1810,"text":"GTL/ABG domain products. It requires typed domain assets, named graph\n"},{"number":1811,"text":"functions, a published function catalogue, a GTL module as the operative\n"},{"number":1812,"text":"carrier, ABG-owned execution authority, one constructive evaluation loop\n"},{"number":1813,"text":"from observation to the next lawful action, projection and query surfaces\n"},{"number":1814,"text":"that expose current state as a projection over constructive history, and\n"},{"number":1815,"text":"automation that stays explainable as a lawful manual traversal of the same\n"},{"number":1816,"text":"graph. Operative framework behaviour must be built outcome-first: outcome\n"},{"number":1817,"text":"traversals first, declarative GTL/ABG carrier structure second, minimal\n"},{"number":1818,"text":"imperative adapter code last. Yield is the lawful iteration boundary, not\n"},{"number":1819,"text":"retry, block, timeout or a hidden local loop. Agentic development conforms\n"},{"number":1820,"text":"by following the constitutional process from a minimal declared authority\n"},{"number":1821,"text":"packet, with produced artifacts passing deterministic admission: the\n"},{"number":1822,"text":"agentic walkthrough proves the process can be followed, and admission\n"},{"number":1823,"text":"proves each act conforms (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":1824,"text":"\n"},{"number":1825,"text":"This section is a compression of this member, a derived surface in the\n"},{"number":1826,"text":"sense of [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),\n"},{"number":1827,"text":"Acquisition. Its sources are §1, §2, §11.1 to §11.5D, §11.7 and §11.7A of\n"},{"number":1828,"text":"this member at the same digest, and it owns no determination. Where it and\n"},{"number":1829,"text":"a source section differ, the source section decides\n"},{"number":1830,"text":"([ACTIVATION §2 Staleness of derived surfaces](ACTIVATION.md#staleness-of-derived-surfaces))\n"},{"number":1831,"text":"(P1, P6).\n"}]},{"end_line":16,"heading":"POSTING_GUIDE","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/POSTING_GUIDE.md#POSTING_GUIDE","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/POSTING_GUIDE.md","sha256":"cc0a00e2ce4a5de4c78ee27bd0d5d88321273bdd45195ca6abd49371dd5b18b6","start_line":1,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/POSTING_GUIDE.md","lines":[{"number":1,"text":"# POSTING_GUIDE\n"},{"number":2,"text":"\n"},{"number":3,"text":"Guide. Overlay and layout independence\n"},{"number":35,"text":"\n"},{"number":36,"text":"This member owns the product-definition-routing bounded context,\n"},{"number":37,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:product-definition-routing`, under the selected\n"},{"number":38,"text":"complete STDO basis, and defines that context's overlay, definition,\n"},{"number":39,"text":"discovery, locator and composition concepts. It is not Product\n"},{"number":54,"text":"identity. It identifies one continuing WHAT definition, not one immutable\n"},{"number":58,"text":"released Product (P3).\n"},{"number":59,"text":"\n"},{"number":60,"text":"The definition identity may stay stable while that source line authors\n"},{"number":61,"text":"successive Product releases. A fork, a\n"},{"number":63,"text":"replacement or an independently governed WHAT definition receives another\n"},{"number":64,"text":"`product.definition_id`; changing a released Product does not repurpose\n"},{"number":65,"text":"the definition identity as release identity (P3; SPEC_METHOD §6).\n"},{"number":66,"text":"\n"},{"number":67,"text":"Product-definition, immutable Product, bounded-context and build-tenant\n"},{"number":68,"text":"identity URIs are identity carriers, not self-authorising strings. and\n"},{"number":172,"text":"- `$schema` and `kind`: the schema locator and the\n"},{"number":173,"text":"  `stdo.product-definition` discriminator.\n"},{"number":174,"text":"\n"},{"number":175,"text":"The overlay owns this locator and relation map; Constitutional-set sufficiency\n"},{"number":188,"text":"\n"},{"number":189,"text":"A Constitutional Set is the complete set of governing documents selected\n"},{"number":190,"text":"for a product, not a prescribed number of files. Collectively the selected\n"},{"number":191,"text":"set makes five things recoverable for the governed scope (P2, P1):\n"},{"number":192,"text":"\n"},{"number":193,"text":"- axioms: irreducible starting truths, invariants and refusal conditions;\n"},{"number":194,"text":"- ontology: the kinds of things treated as real and their material\n"},{"number":195,"text":"  identities, relations, boundaries and lifecycle;\n"},{"number":196,"text":"- epistemology: how claims become knowable or acceptable, including\n"},{"number":197,"text":"  admissible evidence, observation, uncertainty, falsification and\n"},{"number":198,"text":"  decision authority;\n"},{"number":199,"text":"- taxonomy: the classifications and kind distinctions that prevent\n"},{"number":200,"text":"  category collapse; and\n"},{"number":201,"text":"- semantics: the governed meaning of terms, relations, states, operations\n"},{"number":202,"text":"  and outcomes.\n"},{"number":203,"text":"\n"},{"number":204,"text":"These are sufficiency dimensions of the complete set, not filename classes,\n"},{"number":205,"text":"required folders or a one-document-per-dimension partition. One document\n"},{"number":206,"text":"may cover several dimensions and one dimension may be distributed across\n"},{"number":207,"text":"several owning documents (P2).\n"},{"number":208,"text":"\n"},{"number":209,"text":"`constitution.stdo.basis` locates the complete selected STDO constitutional\n"},{"number":210,"text":"set; `constitution.additional_authorities` locates every additional\n"},{"number":211,"text":"constitutional set or source. The STDO basis identifies one complete\n"},{"number":212,"text":"immutable release cut and its exact installed-release manifest, never a\n"},{"number":213,"text":"hand-selected subset. Each `constitution.entrypoints[]` member names the\n"},{"number":214,"text":"basis against which its URI resolves. Entry points are derived navigation\n"},{"number":215,"text":"and can neither narrow nor replace a complete selected constitution (P3,\n"},{"number":216,"text":"P6).\n"},{"number":217,"text":"\n"},{"number":218,"text":"This rule promotes no concrete design ontology into constitutional WHAT.\n"},{"number":219,"text":"Product-level ontology that fixes Product meaning belongs in, or is cited\n"},{"number":220,"text":"by, the bound WHAT. An accepted design ontology of a realisation boundary\n"},{"number":221,"text":"(the design profile's) stays semantic-design authority for that boundary,\n"},{"number":222,"text":"derives from constitutional WHAT and the applicable domain methods, and\n"},{"number":223,"text":"cannot invent missing Product meaning (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":224,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":351,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F4.%20Shared%20installed%20release%20basis%20and%20toolchain%20manager","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"926acce5ff1a9d7a161729654554499905f6a60bc1d268ed03194069a798a7d5","start_line":225,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":225,"text":"## 4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager\n"},{"number":226,"text":"\n"},{"number":227,"text":"Within the product-definition-routing context an Installed Release Basis\n"},{"number":228,"text":"is the pair (P3):\n"},{"number":229,"text":"\n"},{"number":230,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":231,"text":"(immutable stdo://releases/<cut>/ URI, installed-manifest SHA-256)\n"},{"number":232,"text":"```\n"},{"number":233,"text":"\n"},{"number":234,"text":"The URI identifies one immutable annotated release cut. The digest identifies\n"},{"number":235,"text":"the deterministic installed-release manifest, which binds the cut's tag\n"},{"number":236,"text":"object, commit, repository tree, standards subtree, exact standards\n"},{"number":237,"text":"inventory, member bytes and admitted auxiliary payloads. The manifest shape\n"},{"number":238,"text":"is owned by `schemas/installed-release-manifest.schema.json`. The manifest\n"},{"number":239,"text":"is transport and integrity evidence, not a replacement constitution (P6).\n"},{"number":240,"text":"\n"},{"number":241,"text":"An Adoption Plan is the read-only, deterministic acceptance object that\n"},{"number":242,"text":"binds one current Product Definition's identity and bytes to its current\n"},{"number":243,"text":"basis and to one resolved immutable target's cut, annotated tag object,\n"},{"number":244,"text":"commit, tree and installed-manifest digest. Its SHA-256 is the\n"},{"number":245,"text":"operator-presentable acceptance token. Possession of the token alone grants\n"},{"number":246,"text":"no authority; a mismatch proves that the presented subject is no longer the\n"},{"number":247,"text":"subject being mutated (P6, P3). A Fleet Adoption Plan binds an authorised\n"},{"number":248,"text":"fleet root and the complete ordered set of per-definition plan digests\n"},{"number":249,"text":"under the same law.\n"},{"number":250,"text":"\n"},{"number":251,"text":"Plan hashing covers the acceptance object only: local installation status\n"},{"number":252,"text":"and machine-local install paths are excluded. The canonical bytes are UTF-8\n"},{"number":253,"text":"JSON with recursively sorted object keys, two-space indentation, LF line\n"},{"number":254,"text":"endings and one final LF. Fleet order is deterministic discovery-path\n"},{"number":255,"text":"order. These rules make a presented digest independently reproducible\n"},{"number":256,"text":"rather than an opaque session token (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":257,"text":"\n"},{"number":258,"text":"The STDO Toolchain Manager is the bounded executable realisation that (P2,\n"},{"number":259,"text":"P3):\n"},{"number":260,"text":"\n"},{"number":261,"text":"- installs each immutable cut once in a shared, versioned release store;\n"},{"number":262,"text":"- resolves logical `stdo://releases/...` URIs to verified installed bytes;\n"},{"number":263,"text":"- inventories and verifies complete installed distributions;\n"},{"number":264,"text":"- synchronises the exact basis already selected by a Product Definition;\n"},{"number":265,"text":"- emits an exact digest-bound adoption plan from a release-profile discovery\n"},{"number":266,"text":"  route and performs adoption only when that plan is explicitly\n"},{"number":267,"text":"  accepted;\n"},{"number":268,"text":"- manages the stable marker-bounded bootstrap in declared agent files; and\n"},{"number":269,"text":"- applies those operations to an explicitly discovered fleet of Product\n"},{"number":270,"text":"  Definitions.\n"},{"number":271,"text":"\n"},{"number":272,"text":"The store may live at any machine-local path. Its registry maps logical\n"},{"number":273,"text":"release URIs to installed paths and manifest digests and owns neither\n"},{"number":274,"text":"Product selection nor method meaning. A consumer repository therefore needs\n"},{"number":275,"text":"no project-local standards copy and no prescribed folder structure, and\n"},{"number":276,"text":"several Product Definitions on one machine may select different installed\n"},{"number":277,"text":"cuts concurrently (P3, P6). Every manager-owned component from the\n"},{"number":278,"text":"configured store root downward is a physical directory or regular file of\n"},{"number":279,"text":"its declared type; a symlink, junction, reparse point, device, socket or\n"},{"number":280,"text":"other redirection or special entry fails closed. Verification inventories\n"},{"number":281,"text":"every filesystem entry type, directories included, rejects any entry not\n"},{"number":282,"text":"derived from the manifest's exact file paths, and never follows an\n"},{"number":283,"text":"unmanifested alias (P5, P3).\n"},{"number":284,"text":"\n"},{"number":285,"text":"`constitution.stdo.source.repository` identifies the transport source.\n"},{"number":286,"text":"`constitution.stdo.selector` is a `stdo://channels/<version>` discovery\n"},{"number":287,"text":"route whose profile semantics are owned by [RELEASE §4](RELEASE.md#4-selector-and-consumer-adoption).\n"},{"number":288,"text":"An RC line resolves its mutable selector; a stable line resolves its exact\n"},{"number":289,"text":"immutable cut without a second selector. Neither discovery nor the transport\n"},{"number":290,"text":"source is operative authority.\n"},{"number":291,"text":"`constitution.stdo.basis.uri` and `constitution.stdo.basis.manifest_sha256`\n"},{"number":292,"text":"are the sole authored STDO selection for that Product Definition (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":293,"text":"\n"},{"number":294,"text":"The manager observes these command boundaries (P6, P5):\n"},{"number":295,"text":"\n"},{"number":296,"text":"- `install` admits one explicitly named immutable release cut without changing\n"},{"number":297,"text":"  any Product Definition;\n"},{"number":298,"text":"- `sync` installs and verifies only the exact basis already selected by\n"},{"number":299,"text":"  the Product Definition and never consults its mutable selector;\n"},{"number":300,"text":"- `adopt --dry-run` resolves the selected release profile and immutable cut, and\n"},{"number":301,"text":"  presents the target cut, tag object, commit, tree, manifest digest,\n"},{"number":302,"text":"  current Product-Definition byte digest and a deterministic\n"},{"number":303,"text":"  adoption-plan digest, without mutation;\n"},{"number":304,"text":"- mutating `adopt` requires that exact prior plan digest as explicit\n"},{"number":305,"text":"  acceptance, re-derives it before installation, installs only the bound\n"},{"number":306,"text":"  target, rechecks the Product Definition bytes, and atomically changes\n"},{"number":307,"text":"  only its basis and its basis-relative schema locator; any drift refuses\n"},{"number":308,"text":"  mutation;\n"},{"number":309,"text":"- `status`, `verify`, `list`, `manifest` and `resolve` are read-only with\n"},{"number":310,"text":"  respect to Product Definitions; and\n"},{"number":311,"text":"- fleet adoption emits, and requires explicit acceptance of, one aggregate\n"},{"number":312,"text":"  plan digest over every per-definition plan; all fleet writes require\n"},{"number":313,"text":"  explicit whole-selection authorisation and infer no composition or\n"},{"number":314,"text":"  inheritance from directory nesting.\n"},{"number":315,"text":"\n"},{"number":316,"text":"Missing cuts, moved immutable tags, tag-to-commit mismatch, manifest-digest\n"},{"number":317,"text":"mismatch, missing, extra or changed installed members, ambiguous Product\n"},{"number":318,"text":"Definition discovery, unaccepted or stale adoption plans, URI escape,\n"},{"number":319,"text":"physical store redirection, undeclared filesystem entry types and malformed\n"},{"number":320,"text":"bootstrap markers fail closed (P5). Every `stdo:` schema locator is parsed\n"},{"number":321,"text":"before schema loading under URI scheme case-insensitivity and names the\n"},{"number":322,"text":"same immutable cut as `constitution.stdo.basis`; spelling variation cannot\n"},{"number":323,"text":"cross that basis. No cache, registry entry, source checkout, version alias,\n"},{"number":324,"text":"schema or agent file may silently replace the basis selected in the\n"},{"number":325,"text":"Product Definition (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":326,"text":"\n"},{"number":327,"text":"`constitution.agent_bootstrap` embeds no other constitution. It names one\n"},{"number":328,"text":"basis-qualified bootstrap entrypoint and the local instruction files (such\n"},{"number":329,"text":"as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` targets) whose small discovery block the\n"},{"number":330,"text":"manager owns between explicit markers. Each target is a portable relative\n"},{"number":331,"text":"path resolved against `product.source_project`; absolute paths, parent\n"},{"number":332,"text":"traversal, redirected path components and escape from that boundary fail\n"},{"number":333,"text":"closed. A fleet additionally confines every resolved source project to its\n"},{"number":334,"text":"explicitly authorised fleet root and preflights every target before the\n"},{"number":335,"text":"first write. Exactly one correctly ordered marker span may be replaced;\n"},{"number":336,"text":"the bytes before and after it, trailing whitespace included, stay\n"},{"number":337,"text":"project-owned and byte-identical, and appending a new span preserves all\n"},{"number":338,"text":"existing bytes as an exact prefix. The bootstrap routes agents to the\n"},{"number":339,"text":"applicable Product Definition, the exact installed basis and the owning\n"},{"number":340,"text":"sources; it can neither restate nor override them (P6, P3, P5).\n"},{"number":341,"text":"\n"},{"number":342,"text":"Recursive fleet discovery prunes these exact directory names as\n"},{"number":343,"text":"version-control, dependency, generated, cache or managed-store internals:\n"},{"number":344,"text":"`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.bzr`, `.venv`, `venv`, `node_modules`, `vendor`,\n"},{"number":345,"text":"`site-packages`, `build`, `dist`, `out`, `target`, `.gradle`, `.tox`,\n"},{"number":346,"text":"`.nox`, `.cache`, `.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.pytest_cache`,\n"},{"number":347,"text":"`__pycache__`, `.genesis` and `.stdo`. A discovered Product Definition may\n"},{"number":348,"text":"not itself be a symlink. These exclusions are discovery law, not evidence\n"},{"number":349,"text":"that an excluded tree lacks another independently governed Product (P5,\n"},{"number":350,"text":"P6).\n"},{"number":351,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":478,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/4. Shared installed release basis and toolchain manager/Explicit complete consumer update","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F4.%20Shared%20installed%20release%20basis%20and%20toolchain%20manager%2FExplicit%20complete%20consumer%20update","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"c63f3b832c046b3ac884985d4d338c539048dbc5bb61a7560e3fc89fb06f4905","start_line":352,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":352,"text":"### Explicit complete consumer update\n"},{"number":353,"text":"\n"},{"number":354,"text":"A Complete Consumer Update Plan binds one explicitly selected Product\n"},{"number":355,"text":"Definition and the complete companion population of one exact upstream\n"},{"number":356,"text":"release-matched cohort to the consumer bindings selected by the\n"},{"number":357,"text":"invocation's owner. The Product Definition continues to own composition;\n"},{"number":358,"text":"the upstream cohort and each Product's release record own release and\n"},{"number":359,"text":"member identity. An invocation selection and its derived plan and result\n"},{"number":360,"text":"are operation evidence, not another persistent dependency declaration,\n"},{"number":361,"text":"registry or lock. The caller selects every native route and derived context\n"},{"number":362,"text":"for the claimed update scope; directory proximity or an empty discovery\n"},{"number":363,"text":"result cannot supply that selection, and an empty derived-context\n"},{"number":364,"text":"population means the owner selected none, not that the manager established\n"},{"number":365,"text":"the absence of semantic context (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":366,"text":"\n"},{"number":367,"text":"The separate `cohort-update` operation presents the whole plan without\n"},{"number":368,"text":"consumer effects. Unlike the basis-only Adoption Plan above, its acceptance\n"},{"number":369,"text":"object also binds the physical effect destinations and binding preimages,\n"},{"number":370,"text":"the exact selected cohort bytes, the companion annotated tags, commits,\n"},{"number":371,"text":"subtrees and inventories, the replacement dependency locators, the native\n"},{"number":372,"text":"routes and the declared derived-source observations. It uses the same\n"},{"number":373,"text":"canonical JSON hashing rule. Already-installed status supplies no\n"},{"number":374,"text":"additional authority and does not change the digest. Mutation requires\n"},{"number":375,"text":"explicit acceptance of this exact plan and re-derives it; possession of its\n"},{"number":376,"text":"digest alone grants no operation authority. The `adopt`, `sync` and fleet\n"},{"number":377,"text":"contracts above keep their narrower boundaries (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":378,"text":"\n"},{"number":379,"text":"The complete operation verifies the selected cohort's dependency closure\n"},{"number":380,"text":"and each exact companion's definition, release record and admitted members\n"},{"number":381,"text":"before relying on them. It stages absent immutable installs, verifies\n"},{"number":382,"text":"existing installs without repairing them in place, and preflights every\n"},{"number":383,"text":"consumer target. Only the selected basis and schema, the existing\n"},{"number":384,"text":"composition locators and contracts, and the selected native and install\n"},{"number":385,"text":"links may change; historical installs and unrelated consumer content stay\n"},{"number":386,"text":"available and unchanged. It creates no consumer-local checker and changes\n"},{"number":387,"text":"no Product meaning or local semantic map (P3, P6, P2).\n"},{"number":388,"text":"\n"},{"number":389,"text":"For each selected derived context, missing, ambiguous, changed or\n"},{"number":390,"text":"unavailable program, map or source evidence holds the complete update\n"},{"number":391,"text":"before any consumer effect. The source owner performs any semantic re-entry\n"},{"number":392,"text":"that is needed; the manager cannot mechanically relabel an older map as\n"},{"number":393,"text":"current. Exact source freshness is integrity evidence, not semantic\n"},{"number":394,"text":"conformance and not an independent semantic verdict (P1, P6). After\n"},{"number":395,"text":"immutable staging the manager rechecks the consumer preimages and the\n"},{"number":396,"text":"source evidence. It reports completion only after verifying every selected\n"},{"number":397,"text":"resulting binding and companion. Refusal before consumer effects retains\n"},{"number":398,"text":"the prior state; a caught application failure restores the affected\n"},{"number":399,"text":"consumer preimages and does not report completion; newly staged immutable\n"},{"number":400,"text":"installs may stay unused. The operation requires an exclusive consumer\n"},{"number":401,"text":"write scope during application. It claims no crash-atomic transaction\n"},{"number":402,"text":"across independent filesystem paths: abrupt process or host loss, or\n"},{"number":403,"text":"unavailable rollback storage, requires recovery from the presented\n"},{"number":404,"text":"preimages before the complete relation can be claimed (P5, P4b).\n"},{"number":405,"text":"\n"},{"number":406,"text":"Outcomes as results. The outcomes of the manager's operations in §4,\n"},{"number":407,"text":"its refusals, its reported completion and the recovery that\n"},{"number":408,"text":"loss requires, are stated in the core result algebra of\n"},{"number":409,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) through the refinements\n"},{"number":410,"text":"of [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition), each\n"},{"number":411,"text":"for its own predicate; the cause of an outcome selects its value, and the\n"},{"number":412,"text":"mapping adds no core value (P5, P6):\n"},{"number":413,"text":"\n"},{"number":414,"text":"- Effect. An operation that writes, such as `install`, `sync`, a mutating\n"},{"number":415,"text":"  `adopt`, fleet adoption or the complete consumer update, has an\n"},{"number":416,"text":"  intended external effect, recorded under\n"},{"number":417,"text":"  [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) for the predicate \"the\n"},{"number":418,"text":"  intended effect occurred\". Reported completion is `completed`\n"},{"number":419,"text":"  (`satisfied`) only where evidence about the subject establishes the\n"},{"number":420,"text":"  effect in full, as the complete update's verification of every\n"},{"number":421,"text":"  selected resulting binding and companion does. The cause selects the\n"},{"number":422,"text":"  other values. A refusal before any effect, with the retained prior\n"},{"number":423,"text":"  state as the evidence about the subject, is `not_effected`\n"},{"number":424,"text":"  (`falsified`), and the effect has ended. A caught application failure\n"},{"number":425,"text":"  is also `not_effected` (`falsified`): the failure observed on the\n"},{"number":426,"text":"  subject establishes that the complete update is not attained, and the\n"},{"number":427,"text":"  operation applies no later part of it, so no later completion of this\n"},{"number":428,"text":"  effect can attain it. Whether its restored preimages are verified\n"},{"number":429,"text":"  decides only whether the effect's end is established, never the value:\n"},{"number":430,"text":"  verified, the effect has ended; a restoration not verified, or rollback\n"},{"number":431,"text":"  storage unavailable after the failure, leaves the end not established,\n"},{"number":432,"text":"  recorded beside the value as a residual naming the verification that\n"},{"number":433,"text":"  would establish it. Newly staged immutable installs left unused are\n"},{"number":434,"text":"  named with the value as the part that did occur. Abrupt process or\n"},{"number":435,"text":"  host loss, where no caught failure establishes that the update fell\n"},{"number":436,"text":"  short, is `completion_unknown` (`indeterminate`), never `completed` or\n"},{"number":437,"text":"  `not_effected`. `completion_unknown`, and `not_effected` with its end\n"},{"number":438,"text":"  not established, are effects of uncertain completion under\n"},{"number":439,"text":"  [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects): recovery from the\n"},{"number":440,"text":"  presented preimages reconciles them, as\n"},{"number":441,"text":"  [ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart) states, before\n"},{"number":442,"text":"  any repetition or claim of the complete relation.\n"},{"number":443,"text":"- Refusal. A refusal also answers whether the operation may apply its\n"},{"number":444,"text":"  effect on the exact subject and basis it binds. Found before the\n"},{"number":445,"text":"  operation begins, it is an outcome of\n"},{"number":446,"text":"  [ACTIVATION §3 Admission and activation](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation),\n"},{"number":447,"text":"  for \"the step is lawfully admitted and activated on the exact subject\n"},{"number":448,"text":"  and basis\"; found after it has begun, as by the recheck after immutable\n"},{"number":449,"text":"  staging, it is a value of\n"},{"number":450,"text":"  [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability),\n"},{"number":451,"text":"  for \"a candidate is available\". A missing explicit acceptance of the\n"},{"number":452,"text":"  exact plan, or missing whole-selection authorisation of a fleet write,\n"},{"number":453,"text":"  is missing operation authority: `admission_refused(authority)`\n"},{"number":454,"text":"  (`out_of_frame`), naming the acceptance or authorisation needed and\n"},{"number":455,"text":"  its owner. Every other refusal has a basis cause: drift of the Product\n"},{"number":456,"text":"  Definition bytes or of a consumer preimage; a stale plan; each other\n"},{"number":457,"text":"  condition of the fail-closed list above, ambiguous discovery included\n"},{"number":458,"text":"  because it leaves no exact subject; a path, locator or marker span that\n"},{"number":459,"text":"  escapes or breaks its boundary; and missing, ambiguous, changed or\n"},{"number":460,"text":"  unavailable derived-context evidence, which holds the complete update.\n"},{"number":461,"text":"  It is `admission_refused(basis)` before the operation begins and\n"},{"number":462,"text":"  `re_entry_requested(basis)` after, `invalid_basis` in both, and names\n"},{"number":463,"text":"  the basis coordinate that fails and, for derived-context evidence, the\n"},{"number":464,"text":"  source owner whose re-entry repairs it.\n"},{"number":465,"text":"- Command without an intended effect. A command without an intended\n"},{"number":466,"text":"  external effect, such as `verify` or `adopt --dry-run`, has no value\n"},{"number":467,"text":"  under Effects, and its refusal maps by cause as above. A condition it\n"},{"number":468,"text":"  reports about the subject it evaluates, such as a member that `verify`\n"},{"number":469,"text":"  finds missing, extra or changed, is a counterexample to that command's\n"},{"number":470,"text":"  own predicate, `falsified`, not a refusal.\n"},{"number":471,"text":"\n"},{"number":472,"text":"Purpose and material relation: a consumer that combines the manager's\n"},{"number":473,"text":"outcomes with other results cannot read a refused or failed operation as\n"},{"number":474,"text":"completed, an operation whose value is `completion_unknown` as either\n"},{"number":475,"text":"completed or not effected, a caught failure whose restoration is not\n"},{"number":476,"text":"verified as undecided when the update is known to have fallen short, or\n"},{"number":477,"text":"a refusal for missing acceptance as one for a defective basis (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":478,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":601,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/5. Bounded-context semantic resolution","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F5.%20Bounded-context%20semantic%20resolution","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"f0d8379c7f1eee99b44f6c86c5120d62ad1ad04cea12be8504f46f0230ebeff4","start_line":479,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":479,"text":"## 5. Bounded-context semantic resolution\n"},{"number":480,"text":"\n"},{"number":481,"text":"This member owns this law in the semantic-resolution bounded context,\n"},{"number":482,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:semantic-resolution`, under the selected complete\n"},{"number":483,"text":"STDO basis. A glossary may index this identity and does not participate in\n"},{"number":484,"text":"its declaration (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":485,"text":"\n"},{"number":486,"text":"A term is a lexical label used in an occurrence, not a context-free concept\n"},{"number":487,"text":"identity. A bounded context is an explicitly identified semantic scope in\n"},{"number":488,"text":"which a governed vocabulary, concept set and relation set are jointly\n"},{"number":489,"text":"interpretable under named authority. A concept reference is an exact,\n"},{"number":490,"text":"resolvable reference to a meaning owned by an authority under a selected\n"},{"number":491,"text":"basis; the reference locates that meaning and mints neither the meaning nor\n"},{"number":492,"text":"its authority (P1, P3, P6).\n"},{"number":493,"text":"\n"},{"number":494,"text":"A bounded context exists only when an owning authority declares its stable\n"},{"number":495,"text":"identity, owner, selected basis and governed semantic scope. A consuming\n"},{"number":496,"text":"member may define a concept inside that context only through an explicit\n"},{"number":497,"text":"owner relation. A filename, heading, index row, glossary section, schema\n"},{"number":498,"text":"value or bare URI cannot constitute the context (P6).\n"},{"number":499,"text":"\n"},{"number":500,"text":"Every material term occurrence resolves under this semantic address (P1):\n"},{"number":501,"text":"\n"},{"number":502,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":503,"text":"(term, bounded-context identity, owning authority, selected basis, governed scope)\n"},{"number":504,"text":"```\n"},{"number":505,"text":"\n"},{"number":506,"text":"Equal spelling, capitalisation, shape, file location, directory nesting,\n"},{"number":507,"text":"actor or implementation does not establish equal meaning, concept identity,\n"},{"number":508,"text":"equivalence, inheritance or authority; different spelling does not prove\n"},{"number":509,"text":"different meaning. Those relations follow only from the applicable semantic\n"},{"number":510,"text":"address or from an explicit authorised relation (P1, P3). This applies the\n"},{"number":511,"text":"Representation row of [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) to\n"},{"number":512,"text":"terms; the list names the representations a term takes in this member.\n"},{"number":513,"text":"\n"},{"number":514,"text":"Resolution proceeds in this order (P1, P5):\n"},{"number":515,"text":"\n"},{"number":516,"text":"1. identify the occurrence's governed scope and nearest explicit\n"},{"number":517,"text":"   bounded-context declaration;\n"},{"number":518,"text":"2. identify the exact selected basis and the authorities applicable to\n"},{"number":519,"text":"   that context and scope;\n"},{"number":520,"text":"3. collect the context-local definitions and the explicitly imported\n"},{"number":521,"text":"   concept references admitted by those authorities and that basis;\n"},{"number":522,"text":"4. apply every applicable owner-authorised override or disambiguation; and\n"},{"number":523,"text":"5. admit the occurrence only when exactly one concept remains.\n"},{"number":524,"text":"\n"},{"number":525,"text":"A document, section, schema field, operation or other owning surface may\n"},{"number":526,"text":"declare a context for all subordinate occurrences, so uniquely resolved\n"},{"number":527,"text":"prose need not repeat a qualifier on every term. A repository, directory,\n"},{"number":528,"text":"filename, heading, glossary match, prompt, actor or nearby definition does\n"},{"number":529,"text":"not declare a bounded context by accident (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":530,"text":"\n"},{"number":531,"text":"Zero applicable concepts is unresolved meaning; more than one is ambiguous\n"},{"number":532,"text":"meaning. Both fail closed at a material boundary: an agent, design, schema,\n"},{"number":533,"text":"implementation, test, translation or reviewer must not select one by\n"},{"number":534,"text":"familiarity, frequency, recency, nominal match or a context-free glossary\n"},{"number":535,"text":"fallback (P5, P1). For an evaluation that depends on such an occurrence,\n"},{"number":536,"text":"the definition, import or disambiguation that would select one concept is\n"},{"number":537,"text":"a material relation its frame does not declare: the evaluation returns\n"},{"number":538,"text":"`out_of_frame` and names that relation and its owner, or returns\n"},{"number":539,"text":"`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence also cannot decide the\n"},{"number":540,"text":"claim and so gives that ground too, and in either case names the ground,\n"},{"number":541,"text":"as [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Out of frame or\n"},{"number":542,"text":"indeterminate, states (P5, P1).\n"},{"number":543,"text":"\n"},{"number":544,"text":"The glossary (the [GLOSSARY](GLOSSARY.md) member) is a non-deciding locator index. Each\n"},{"number":545,"text":"record points to an exact source clause that declares the bounded context\n"},{"number":546,"text":"and owns the indexed concept. The glossary defines neither and cannot\n"},{"number":547,"text":"repair a missing declaration. An indexed concept applies only when the\n"},{"number":548,"text":"semantic address selects its owning clause or the target context explicitly\n"},{"number":549,"text":"imports it; appearance in the glossary creates no shared default (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":550,"text":"\n"},{"number":551,"text":"A cross-context relation is explicit and owner-authorised. Its carrier\n"},{"number":552,"text":"states (P1, P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":553,"text":"\n"},{"number":554,"text":"- the exact source and target concept references and bounded-context\n"},{"number":555,"text":"  identities;\n"},{"number":556,"text":"- whether the relation imports unchanged meaning, disambiguates a use,\n"},{"number":557,"text":"  translates directionally (a specialisation included) or establishes the\n"},{"number":558,"text":"  stronger equivalence claim;\n"},{"number":559,"text":"- its direction and any lawful inverse where material;\n"},{"number":560,"text":"- the preserved meaning, changed meaning, loss and refusal conditions;\n"},{"number":561,"text":"- the source and target semantic owners, without transferring either\n"},{"number":562,"text":"  authority;\n"},{"number":563,"text":"- the selected source and target bases, the governed scope and\n"},{"number":564,"text":"  provenance; and\n"},{"number":565,"text":"- its lifecycle and invalidation conditions.\n"},{"number":566,"text":"\n"},{"number":567,"text":"The four relation kinds refine the rule of\n"},{"number":568,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members),\n"},{"number":569,"text":"which owns what an import is, its direction, its loss and its lack of\n"},{"number":570,"text":"authority, and states that a use that changes, narrows or loses the source\n"},{"number":571,"text":"meaning is not an import. That rule is stated for members. Here it\n"},{"number":572,"text":"applies between any two bounded contexts, with the context an owning\n"},{"number":573,"text":"authority declares as source or target. A carrier's concept references,\n"},{"number":574,"text":"bounded-context identities, direction and loss are the contents of an\n"},{"number":575,"text":"import declaration under that rule; its semantic owners are authorities,\n"},{"number":576,"text":"distinct from the owning clause to which a concept reference resolves.\n"},{"number":577,"text":"Each kind reads in the owner's terms once (P1, P6):\n"},{"number":578,"text":"\n"},{"number":579,"text":"| Kind | In the terms of FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members |\n"},{"number":580,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":581,"text":"| Semantic Import | an import, applied for its declared target scope; its unchanged meaning, direction, loss and lack of authority are those FOUNDATIONS §2 states |\n"},{"number":582,"text":"| Semantic Translation | not an import, because it declares how meaning changes in one direction; its carrier states the coordinates an import declaration states (the concept, its owner, the source and target contexts and the direction) and declares the changed meaning and the loss. A specialisation (below) is a translation |\n"},{"number":583,"text":"| Semantic Equivalence | not an import: each concept keeps its own owner and context, and neither adopts the other's meaning. It requires the governing authorities to establish the claimed equality; neither identical spelling nor two opposing translations proves it automatically |\n"},{"number":584,"text":"| Semantic Disambiguation | not an import: it selects one meaning for one scope and does not make competing concepts equal. Where the selected concept is owned in another bounded context, it enters that scope only by the import, translation or equivalence its carrier declares (§6) |\n"},{"number":585,"text":"\n"},{"number":586,"text":"No relation widens its source or target authority; for an import,\n"},{"number":587,"text":"FOUNDATIONS §2 states this, and for the other three kinds this section\n"},{"number":588,"text":"does (P1, P6). These four kinds are related to the typed relations that\n"},{"number":589,"text":"AC-012, AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4, names. The reading of each kind in the\n"},{"number":590,"text":"owner's terms is stated here. Purpose and material relation: an\n"},{"number":591,"text":"import has one definition, so a translation, equivalence or\n"},{"number":592,"text":"disambiguation cannot pass as an import that adopts meaning unchanged\n"},{"number":593,"text":"(P1, P6).\n"},{"number":594,"text":"\n"},{"number":595,"text":"A specialisation is a directional translation whose target preserves the\n"},{"number":596,"text":"declared source meaning while narrowing its admissible instances or adding\n"},{"number":597,"text":"target-context constraints. It identifies the exact target concept, the\n"},{"number":598,"text":"preserved and narrowed meaning, the excluded source instances, and the\n"},{"number":599,"text":"absence or law of any inverse. Calling a term a specialisation without\n"},{"number":600,"text":"those coordinates establishes nothing (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":601,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":636,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/6. Local constitutional binding","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F6.%20Local%20constitutional%20binding","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"170d72603455117a840d6597abef618a46006c1430098c0ef972f0ecdc50d65a","start_line":602,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":602,"text":"## 6. Local constitutional binding\n"},{"number":603,"text":"\n"},{"number":604,"text":"A local axiom, override or disambiguation gains no authority from its file\n"},{"number":605,"text":"category or from being listed in the overlay. Every local entry names (P6):\n"},{"number":606,"text":"\n"},{"number":607,"text":"- the URI carrying the local decision;\n"},{"number":608,"text":"- the existing Product, requirement, accepted-design or other lawful\n"},{"number":609,"text":"  authority that owns it;\n"},{"number":610,"text":"- the clause or ambiguity it overrides or resolves, where applicable; and\n"},{"number":611,"text":"- the exact scope to which it applies.\n"},{"number":612,"text":"\n"},{"number":613,"text":"Each `local_constitution.disambiguations` binding additionally names (P1,\n"},{"number":614,"text":"P3):\n"},{"number":615,"text":"\n"},{"number":616,"text":"- `term`: the exact lexical label being resolved;\n"},{"number":617,"text":"- `context`: the bounded-context identity in which the resolution applies;\n"},{"number":618,"text":"- `disambiguates`: the complete material candidate concept or clause\n"},{"number":619,"text":"  references;\n"},{"number":620,"text":"- `resolves_to`: the exact selected concept reference, which is one member\n"},{"number":621,"text":"  of `disambiguates`;\n"},{"number":622,"text":"- `basis`: every selected semantic basis needed to interpret the\n"},{"number":623,"text":"  candidates and the resolution; and\n"},{"number":624,"text":"- `uri`, `authority` and `applies_to`: the owning resolution carrier, the\n"},{"number":625,"text":"  lawful authority and the exact governed scope.\n"},{"number":626,"text":"\n"},{"number":627,"text":"The referenced `uri` owns the resolution. When the candidates cross bounded\n"},{"number":628,"text":"contexts, that carrier also declares the complete import, translation or\n"},{"number":629,"text":"equivalence relation §5 requires. The overlay metadata makes the relation\n"},{"number":630,"text":"discoverable and checkable; it neither restates the source-owned meanings\n"},{"number":631,"text":"nor mints the decision (P6).\n"},{"number":632,"text":"\n"},{"number":633,"text":"An empty local array explicitly declares that no local entry of that kind\n"},{"number":634,"text":"is bound for the product. Omission is not an equivalent declaration (P6,\n"},{"number":635,"text":"P4b).\n"},{"number":636,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":731,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/7. Collective reference-frame basis","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F7.%20Collective%20reference-frame%20basis","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"cf57606beafcaa89a099ab75bcea86f673407dc4d0f2435d4d054ffa2e4ce37d","start_line":637,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":637,"text":"## 7. Collective reference-frame basis\n"},{"number":638,"text":"\n"},{"number":639,"text":"A Project Reference-Frame Basis is the Product-owned accepted declaration\n"},{"number":640,"text":"of the shared frame set through which finite actors collectively engage one\n"},{"number":641,"text":"governed Product scope or outcome (P0, P6). It binds:\n"},{"number":642,"text":"\n"},{"number":643,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":644,"text":"Project Reference-Frame Basis\n"},{"number":645,"text":"  = exact reference-frame law and optional profile basis\n"},{"number":646,"text":"  + admitting authorities and governed scopes\n"},{"number":647,"text":"  + frame declarations and evaluation inventory\n"},{"number":648,"text":"  + actor-binding rules and capability envelopes\n"},{"number":649,"text":"  + semantic, evaluation, operation and decision grants\n"},{"number":650,"text":"  + result, conjunction, translation and coverage relations\n"},{"number":651,"text":"  + lifecycle activation triggers and invalidation law\n"},{"number":652,"text":"```\n"},{"number":653,"text":"\n"},{"number":654,"text":"[REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md) supplies frame principles only, and\n"},{"number":655,"text":"its §4 the shape of a frame-set declaration; a profile member (the\n"},{"number":656,"text":"Executive baseline, tier 3) supplies one optional profile only. Neither\n"},{"number":657,"text":"selects, adopts or owns a Product binding. The adopting Product's existing\n"},{"number":658,"text":"authority owns the concrete declaration and every grant it contains (P6).\n"},{"number":659,"text":"\n"},{"number":660,"text":"`reference_frame_bases` is the non-empty locator set for the accepted\n"},{"number":661,"text":"frame bases through which finite actors collectively engage the governed\n"},{"number":662,"text":"Product and its work. Each entry names (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":663,"text":"\n"},{"number":664,"text":"- the URI carrying one accepted frame-basis declaration;\n"},{"number":665,"text":"- every existing Goals, Product, requirement, accepted-design or other\n"},{"number":666,"text":"  lawful authority that admits the declaration; and\n"},{"number":667,"text":"- the exact Product, bounded context, build tenant, outcome or other\n"},{"number":668,"text":"  governed scope to which it applies.\n"},{"number":669,"text":"\n"},{"number":670,"text":"The referenced declaration owns the selected frame set, the method or\n"},{"number":671,"text":"profile basis, the governed outcome, the actor-binding rules, the\n"},{"number":672,"text":"capability envelopes, the grant requirements, the triggers, the coverage,\n"},{"number":673,"text":"the result relations and the invalidation law. It may adopt an available\n"},{"number":674,"text":"profile or define a project configuration. The JSON entry locates that\n"},{"number":675,"text":"declaration and its authority relation; it does not contain the binding,\n"},{"number":676,"text":"adopt the profile, restate the frames or create frame-set authority (P6).\n"},{"number":677,"text":"\n"},{"number":678,"text":"Profile availability, Product adoption and execution-scoped activation are\n"},{"number":679,"text":"three distinct relations. Inclusion in a selected method cut makes a\n"},{"number":680,"text":"profile available; only Product authority may adopt it; only an exact\n"},{"number":681,"text":"authorised work instruction may activate one bound frame for an actor and\n"},{"number":682,"text":"subject (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":683,"text":"\n"},{"number":684,"text":"The collective basis and an actor activation are distinct. An Agent Frame\n"},{"number":685,"text":"Activation is the execution-scoped binding of one agent to an applicable\n"},{"number":686,"text":"frame declaration or active configuration, an exact evaluation, subject,\n"},{"number":687,"text":"basis, evidence boundary and capability envelope; what the agent receives\n"},{"number":688,"text":"is the activation packet of REFERENCE_FRAME §11, and the step it performs\n"},{"number":689,"text":"is ACTIVATION §1. The Product Definition records the durable shared basis;\n"},{"number":690,"text":"a ticket or other authorised work instruction carries the activation\n"},{"number":691,"text":"packet. An Agent Frame Activation does not mutate the overlay, and the overlay\n"},{"number":692,"text":"registers no agents, assigns no permanent frames and persists no temporary\n"},{"number":693,"text":"active frame configuration (P3, P0).\n"},{"number":694,"text":"\n"},{"number":695,"text":"Frames and actors keep separate identities. Several agents may activate\n"},{"number":696,"text":"overlapping subsets of one frame set; one agent may activate different\n"},{"number":697,"text":"frames over time. Neither an actor name nor a broad frame grants semantic,\n"},{"number":698,"text":"operation, review, acceptance or disposition authority beyond the cited\n"},{"number":699,"text":"owners and the exact activation (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":700,"text":"\n"},{"number":701,"text":"The Project Reference-Frame Basis also records the Product-role map when\n"},{"number":702,"text":"the governed outcome crosses a chain of Products. The map keeps mutable\n"},{"number":703,"text":"source projects, Product Definitions, candidate checkpoints, release cuts,\n"},{"number":704,"text":"released Products, installs, artifacts and dependent Products as distinct\n"},{"number":705,"text":"identities (SPEC_METHOD §6), and records each development product as a\n"},{"number":706,"text":"role binding over its exact underlying install identity. Every directed\n"},{"number":707,"text":"Product-composition edge names its source and target roles, governing\n"},{"number":708,"text":"authority and contracts, lifecycle, evidence boundary, refusal and\n"},{"number":709,"text":"invalidation conditions. Common actors, repositories, files,\n"},{"number":710,"text":"implementations, outputs or tool access create no composition or identity\n"},{"number":711,"text":"relation (P3, P6). The recursive capability, authority and context bindings\n"},{"number":712,"text":"of [§9](#9-recursive-discovery-and-explicit-composition) apply equally to\n"},{"number":713,"text":"peer Products and enclosing/constituent outcomes; the Product-role map\n"},{"number":714,"text":"retains those separate uses rather than flattening their grants.\n"},{"number":715,"text":"\n"},{"number":716,"text":"An accepted Project Reference-Frame Basis may be expressed entirely as\n"},{"number":717,"text":"source-linked prose. The starter at\n"},{"number":718,"text":"`templates/PROJECT_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASIS_TEMPLATE.md` projects this binding\n"},{"number":719,"text":"law into one copyable shape. The template is not authority, and no schema,\n"},{"number":720,"text":"axiomatic representation, prompt framework or runtime frame engine is\n"},{"number":721,"text":"needed to use the method. An adopting Product replaces every placeholder\n"},{"number":722,"text":"with its own exact identities, owners, scopes, sources, grants, results and\n"},{"number":723,"text":"invalidation conditions, then admits that completed declaration under\n"},{"number":724,"text":"existing authority (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":725,"text":"\n"},{"number":726,"text":"A Product, domain or runtime carrier also named `Frame` is not included by\n"},{"number":727,"text":"nominal match. It stays governed by its bound WHAT and HOW and may be the\n"},{"number":728,"text":"subject or a coordinate of an evaluation frame. It enters the collective\n"},{"number":729,"text":"frame set only through an explicit frame declaration with the required\n"},{"number":730,"text":"evaluation and authority relations (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":731,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":776,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/8. WHAT, HOW and work carriers","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F8.%20WHAT%2C%20HOW%20and%20work%20carriers","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"afaf9294f0bad01a8bd8cb6b14be94943781707af06b6a863893272ac1fc7f1e","start_line":732,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":732,"text":"## 8. WHAT, HOW and work carriers\n"},{"number":733,"text":"\n"},{"number":734,"text":"This member owns the build-tenancy bounded context,\n"},{"number":735,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy`, under the selected complete STDO\n"},{"number":736,"text":"basis. These concepts of the context are owned in other members, each by\n"},{"number":737,"text":"an explicit owner relation (§5) (P1, P3):\n"},{"number":738,"text":"\n"},{"number":739,"text":"- the build tenant, the relation by which one constitutional product WHAT\n"},{"number":740,"text":"  is realised by one or more independent project-owned HOW tenants, and\n"},{"number":741,"text":"  each tenant's build-tenant binding:\n"},{"number":742,"text":"  [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding), its terms and\n"},{"number":743,"text":"  rule 1;\n"},{"number":744,"text":"- the multi-build-tenant work-item relation:\n"},{"number":745,"text":"  [TICKETS §4](TICKETS.md#multi-build-tenant-independence).\n"},{"number":746,"text":"\n"},{"number":747,"text":"In this context build tenancy is that one-or-more relation; one tenant is\n"},{"number":748,"text":"its singleton case, and multi-build-tenancy begins when the same WHAT has\n"},{"number":749,"text":"more than one independent realisation (P3, P2).\n"},{"number":750,"text":"\n"},{"number":751,"text":"`what.intent`, `what.product` and `what.specification` locate the current\n"},{"number":752,"text":"constitutional WHAT. Intent and Product each have one canonical entrypoint;\n"},{"number":753,"text":"specification may cite more than one requirement or specification surface\n"},{"number":754,"text":"(P3).\n"},{"number":755,"text":"\n"},{"number":756,"text":"The Tenant Registry is the canonical `how.build_tenants` collection for the\n"},{"number":757,"text":"product's independent HOW realisations. Each entry has stable identity and\n"},{"number":758,"text":"locates its root, design and implementation surfaces; the tenant's\n"},{"number":759,"text":"binding, which those surfaces declare, is governed by SPEC_METHOD §11.\n"},{"number":760,"text":"The Common Build-Tenant Surface is the realisation law bound by `how.common` and\n"},{"number":761,"text":"explicitly adopted across more than one tenant. A separate\n"},{"number":762,"text":"`TENANT_REGISTRY.md` may remain as a human-readable companion or generated\n"},{"number":763,"text":"projection and cannot become a second tenant-identity or location\n"},{"number":764,"text":"authority (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":765,"text":"\n"},{"number":766,"text":"`ticketing.goals` locates the current work-wave carrier.\n"},{"number":767,"text":"`ticketing.tickets` locates the durable ticket root and the minimum\n"},{"number":768,"text":"backlog, active and completed lanes. `ticketing.comments` locates the\n"},{"number":769,"text":"commentary root. `ticketing.sprints` optionally locates bounded\n"},{"number":770,"text":"execution-batch manifests. These bindings may resolve to directories,\n"},{"number":771,"text":"repository resources, tracker collections, API endpoints or product-scoped\n"},{"number":772,"text":"queries. Goals own the bounded work wave, ticket state stays ticket\n"},{"number":773,"text":"authority, and comments stay non-authoritative commentary (P6, P3). Which\n"},{"number":774,"text":"carrier a given work item takes is SPEC_METHOD §4 and the [TICKETS](TICKETS.md) member;\n"},{"number":775,"text":"this section binds where each carrier kind lives.\n"},{"number":776,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":842,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"32e993046270630d5a30e7a8a30969b0411b0b8c8d9506105c44bc7b83bc32ed","start_line":777,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":777,"text":"## 9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition\n"},{"number":778,"text":"\n"},{"number":779,"text":"Tools discover `stdo_*.json` recursively within the selected workspace\n"},{"number":780,"text":"boundary: definitions at the workspace root and definitions at arbitrarily\n"},{"number":781,"text":"deep nested project roots (P3).\n"},{"number":782,"text":"\n"},{"number":783,"text":"For a requested Product scope exactly one applicable definition is\n"},{"number":784,"text":"selected; zero or several unresolved definitions fail closed, and a\n"},{"number":785,"text":"symlinked definition is refused (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":786,"text":"\n"},{"number":787,"text":"Directory nesting creates no implicit inheritance, ownership, composition\n"},{"number":788,"text":"or constitutional override. Parent and child definitions stay independent\n"},{"number":789,"text":"until `composition` explicitly relates them. Each composition entry records\n"},{"number":790,"text":"(P6, P3):\n"},{"number":791,"text":"\n"},{"number":792,"text":"- `product_definition`: the current locator for the target definition;\n"},{"number":793,"text":"- `target_definition_id`: the stable identity expected from the target's\n"},{"number":794,"text":"  `product.definition_id`;\n"},{"number":795,"text":"- `relation`: the authority defining the directed composition kind, the\n"},{"number":796,"text":"  source and target roles, owner, scope, lifecycle and invalidation\n"},{"number":797,"text":"  conditions; and\n"},{"number":798,"text":"- `contracts`: one or more exact interface, capability, identity,\n"},{"number":799,"text":"  lifecycle, data, evidence or other governing contract references\n"},{"number":800,"text":"  consumed by that relation.\n"},{"number":801,"text":"\n"},{"number":802,"text":"Resolution verifies both the locator and the expected identity. Moving a\n"},{"number":803,"text":"definition requires a locator update and does not change its identity.\n"},{"number":804,"text":"Replacing the content at the same locator with another definition identity\n"},{"number":805,"text":"fails closed. When an edge binds exact immutable Product or release\n"},{"number":806,"text":"versions, the cited relation and contracts also carry and verify those\n"},{"number":807,"text":"identities; the mutable definition identity cannot substitute for them\n"},{"number":808,"text":"(P3, P5).\n"},{"number":809,"text":"\n"},{"number":810,"text":"A conforming discovered set satisfies all of the following (P3, P6, P1):\n"},{"number":811,"text":"\n"},{"number":812,"text":"- every definition validates against its selected released schema;\n"},{"number":813,"text":"- every required URI and fragment resolves under the declared workspace\n"},{"number":814,"text":"  and resolver boundary;\n"},{"number":815,"text":"- every `product.definition_id` is unique;\n"},{"number":816,"text":"- every build-tenant identity is unique within its overlay;\n"},{"number":817,"text":"- every governed scope has a resolvable applicable reference-frame basis,\n"},{"number":818,"text":"  and overlapping basis bindings are reconciled by their cited authority;\n"},{"number":819,"text":"- every local disambiguation binds one exact term, target context,\n"},{"number":820,"text":"  complete material candidate set, selected concept, authority, basis and\n"},{"number":821,"text":"  scope; `resolves_to` is a member of `disambiguates`; and its referenced\n"},{"number":822,"text":"  resolution carrier is congruent with those bindings;\n"},{"number":823,"text":"- every material cross-context term seam resolves through an explicit\n"},{"number":824,"text":"  import, disambiguation, translation or equivalence relation rather than\n"},{"number":825,"text":"  nominal match;\n"},{"number":826,"text":"- every composition target resolves to another product definition whose\n"},{"number":827,"text":"  `product.definition_id` equals `target_definition_id`, and every\n"},{"number":828,"text":"  relation and non-empty contract set resolves; and\n"},{"number":829,"text":"- no two carriers claim authority for the same Product, tenant, ticket\n"},{"number":830,"text":"  state or constitutional relation.\n"},{"number":831,"text":"\n"},{"number":832,"text":"Portable Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema validation establishes structural shape.\n"},{"number":833,"text":"The schema's `uri` and `uri-reference` formats are annotations unless the\n"},{"number":834,"text":"declared validator implements format assertion. Conformance therefore\n"},{"number":835,"text":"performs an explicit RFC 3986 URI and URI-reference syntax check with an\n"},{"number":836,"text":"assertion-capable validator, followed separately by resolution, fragment\n"},{"number":837,"text":"existence, selected-release identity, uniqueness across files,\n"},{"number":838,"text":"constitutional sufficiency, semantic-resolution and cross-context-relation\n"},{"number":839,"text":"completeness, and authority-congruence checks. The structural subset and\n"},{"number":840,"text":"the semantic subset of these checks are distinct claims (EVALUATION §2;\n"},{"number":841,"text":"P1, P6).\n"},{"number":842,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":856,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. They define no second\n"},{"number":847,"text":"admission or result algebra. A Product may consume, coordinate or assess\n"},{"number":848,"text":"another Product through its declared relation; these roles are neither a closed\n"},{"number":849,"text":"nor disjoint kind taxonomy, and none confers authority (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":850,"text":"\n"},{"number":851,"text":"[The contract template](templates/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION_CONTRACT_TEMPLATE.md)\n"},{"number":852,"text":"projects these coordinates; [the recursive example](examples/PRODUCT_COMPOSITION.md)\n"},{"number":853,"text":"works them through a shared leaf and an independently enterable composite.\n"},{"number":854,"text":"[CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md#product-composition-discriminators) names their\n"},{"number":855,"text":"positive and adverse discriminators. Alternative\n"},{"number":860,"text":"realizations of that WHAT are build tenants. A decomposition into Products names\n"},{"number":861,"text":"which distinct outcomes and authorities each constituent owns, and which outer\n"},{"number":862,"text":"outcome the composition owns.\n"},{"number":863,"text":"\n"},{"number":864,"text":"Under the identity and ownership laws (P3, P6), within a declared decomposition scope, a leaf has no further constituent Product\n"},{"number":865,"text":"boundary exposed by that decomposition. It may contain modules and declared\n"},{"number":866,"text":"external dependencies. A composite relates two or more constituent capabilities\n"},{"number":867,"text":"or an outer capability to its constituent capability; its own capability may in\n"},{"number":868,"text":"turn be consumed as a constituent. The same definition, contract and authority\n"},{"number":869,"text":"laws apply at every depth. Shared constituents keep one identity and their\n"},{"number":870,"text":"separately bound uses; a hierarchy view may show several references to one leaf.\n"},{"number":871,"text":"\n"},{"number":872,"text":"Decomposition, capability/data dependency, inspection permission, authority and\n"},{"number":873,"text":"work prerequisites are distinct relations. A directory tree establishes none of\n"},{"number":874,"text":"them. A named composition view states its root, participating identities,\n"},{"number":875,"text":"selected boundaries and relation kinds rather than treating all reachable edges\n"},{"number":876,"text":"as one hierarchy.\n"},{"number":877,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":894,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Recursive discovery and explicit composition/PC-02 — Independent entry and the integrated outcome","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F9.%20Recursive%20discovery%20and%20explicit%20composition%2FPC-02%20%E2%80%94%20Independent%20entry%20and%20the%20integrated%20outcome","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"525d68562c67b3037df86c494b877b9accf26286464a4624650e4063fc967e76","start_line":878,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":878,"text":"### PC-02 — Independent entry and the integrated outcome\n"},{"number":879,"text":"\n"},{"number":880,"text":"A Product offered as a standalone constituent must be enterable through its own\n"},{"number":881,"text":"Product Definition and a Product-authorized applicable frame basis, with the\n"},{"number":882,"text":"dependency closure and capabilities its contract declares. Entry must not require\n"},{"number":883,"text":"an enclosing composition's activation unless that enclosing capability is itself\n"},{"number":884,"text":"an explicit prerequisite. Such a prerequisite is disclosed as a limit on the\n"},{"number":885,"text":"standalone claim. Shared or externally located frame documents are permitted\n"},{"number":886,"text":"where adoption, scope and availability are established; file ownership alone is\n"},{"number":887,"text":"not the deciding test.\n"},{"number":888,"text":"\n"},{"number":889,"text":"Standalone does not imply dependency-free, separately deployable or able to\n"},{"number":890,"text":"supply every host itself. The claim names which construction, evaluation or use\n"},{"number":891,"text":"can be performed independently and its required inputs. The composition owner\n"},{"number":892,"text":"separately establishes interface compatibility, material joins and its complete\n"},{"number":893,"text":"outcome. Successful constituent checks do not establish that outer predicate.\n"},{"number":894,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":916,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Source and target Product identities and roles; the consumed capability,\n"},{"number":901,"text":"   outcome, purpose, selected basis and currentness policy.\n"},{"number":902,"text":"2. The existing owners and grants for each material operation: acquisition,\n"},{"number":903,"text":"   disclosure, use, execution, mutation, assessment and disposition. A kind or\n"},{"number":904,"text":"   role label records no grant by itself.\n"},{"number":905,"text":"3. Admissible inputs and exports; material assumptions, effects, failures,\n"},{"number":906,"text":"   obligations and evidence; restrictions on implementation material and derived\n"},{"number":907,"text":"   information where applicable.\n"},{"number":908,"text":"4. The acting principals or binding rule, task/phase scope, permitted delegation,\n"},{"number":909,"text":"   return consumer, stop/refusal conditions and revocation/invalidation route.\n"},{"number":910,"text":"\n"},{"number":911,"text":"These coordinates may be supplied by source-linked prose. The relation locates\n"},{"number":912,"text":"and constrains lawfully granted authority; it cannot manufacture the target's\n"},{"number":913,"text":"permission or the source's admission. Missing material authority or an unresolved\n"},{"number":914,"text":"conflict withholds the dependent action. The execution-scoped activation remains\n"},{"number":915,"text":"the place where a particular actor, input, effect and return are bound.\n"},{"number":916,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":938,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9.
