Neither\n"},{"number":920,"text":"A → B plus B → C nor two routes to a shared leaf imply a union of their grants.\n"},{"number":921,"text":"Each onward acquisition, disclosure or delegated effect needs authority for that\n"},{"number":922,"text":"actor, purpose and path, including any permitted onward use of returned material.\n"},{"number":923,"text":"Existing delegation may authorize a chain explicitly; its scope cannot expand\n"},{"number":924,"text":"silently at a recursive step.\n"},{"number":925,"text":"\n"},{"number":926,"text":"A provider may encapsulate internal dependencies behind an adequate contract.\n"},{"number":927,"text":"Consumers need not flatten every implementation dependency into a direct edge.\n"},{"number":928,"text":"Where an outer claim materially relies on a far-side contract, assumption,\n"},{"number":929,"text":"evidence item or acquisition, that reliance and its applicable authority must be\n"},{"number":930,"text":"preserved through the boundary. Unknown impact is not evidence of encapsulation.\n"},{"number":931,"text":"\n"},{"number":932,"text":"Durable Product consumption and bounded authorized inspection are different\n"},{"number":933,"text":"relations. A Reviewer or diagnostic Worker may inspect a larger causal cone under\n"},{"number":934,"text":"an explicit access grant without thereby adopting those internals as a runtime\n"},{"number":935,"text":"dependency or gaining a write grant. If findings become a continuing construction\n"},{"number":936,"text":"constraint or dependency, their producer, applicability and governing relation\n"},{"number":937,"text":"must be retained.\n"},{"number":938,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":963,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. Permission covers the source information and permitted derivations,\n"},{"number":943,"text":"not only paths or filenames. The boundary identifies eligible source classes,\n"},{"number":944,"text":"exports and tool outputs, material provenance, intended use, later acquisitions\n"},{"number":945,"text":"and the effect of prior exposure. An allowed file location or a fresh summary\n"},{"number":946,"text":"does not sanitize prohibited information.\n"},{"number":947,"text":"\n"},{"number":948,"text":"A target owner may authorize an export, but clean-room eligibility additionally\n"},{"number":949,"text":"requires that the engagement's information policy admits that export and its\n"},{"number":950,"text":"provenance. The actual delivered/acquired material must be recorded to the extent\n"},{"number":951,"text":"required by the claim. An uncertain or prohibited exposure follows the declared\n"},{"number":952,"text":"hold/re-entry rule; it cannot be repaired by deleting its receipt or relabeling\n"},{"number":953,"text":"the same actor fresh. Prior actor knowledge and external acquisition channels are\n"},{"number":954,"text":"part of the declared limits.\n"},{"number":955,"text":"\n"},{"number":956,"text":"Adequacy retains the distinctions required for the task's decisions and\n"},{"number":957,"text":"continuations, including unresolved obligations, result standing, currentness and\n"},{"number":958,"text":"authority. If the permitted material is insufficient, acquire an authorized\n"},{"number":959,"text":"extension, narrow the task with the owner, use a suitable actor or return the\n"},{"number":960,"text":"unresolved outcome. Permission is not evidence of sufficiency, and a budget is\n"},{"number":961,"text":"not permission to omit a deciding condition. This applies [FOUNDATIONS Observation sufficiency](FOUNDATIONS.md#assurance-relations)\n"},{"number":962,"text":"and its scoped preservation law; it supplies no general optimal context selector (P1, P2, P6).\n"},{"number":963,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":979,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/9. A cycle of current prerequisite claims requires an executable resolution:\n"},{"number":969,"text":"for example an admitted prior revision, explicit seed, staged contract or bounded\n"},{"number":970,"text":"iteration with its continuation/stop conditions. Naming a lead alone does not\n"},{"number":971,"text":"supply a missing prerequisite or establish convergence.\n"},{"number":972,"text":"\n"},{"number":973,"text":"Replacing a constituent or refining it into further Products preserves the\n"},{"number":974,"text":"consumer's material contract: meaning, preconditions, effects, failures,\n"},{"number":975,"text":"authority, lifecycle, evidence and subsequent obligations. A semantic change\n"},{"number":976,"text":"requires an authorized successor relation and affected reassessment. The [ACTIVATION refinement contract](ACTIVATION.md#refinement) governs this\n"},{"number":977,"text":"preservation. Matching signatures, labels or a sample output is insufficient (P4a, P6). Git is one\n"},{"number":985,"text":"possible carrier, not a mandatory identity system.\n"},{"number":986,"text":"\n"},{"number":987,"text":"Changes and new counterexamples propagate through material assertion, execution\n"},{"number":988,"text":"and evidence-use dependencies under [FOUNDATIONS Change impact and evidence reuse](FOUNDATIONS.md#change-impact-and-evidence-reuse). Historical\n"},{"number":989,"text":"evidence remains about its original subject. Semantic-resolution conformance cases\n"},{"number":997,"text":"\n"},{"number":998,"text":"Conformance covers both uniquely resolved use and material collision. At\n"},{"number":999,"text":"minimum it establishes these cases under an exact selected basis (P1, P6):\n"},{"number":1000,"text":"\n"},{"number":1001,"text":"| Term | Candidate contexts | Required result without an explicit cross-context relation |\n"},{"number":1002,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":1003,"text":"| `Frame` | the reference-frame-evaluation context (REFERENCE_FRAME §1) and a consumer-owned runtime carrier | remain distinct; nominal match cannot enrol the runtime carrier as an evaluation frame |\n"},{"number":1004,"text":"| `Owner` | a generic specialist evaluation family and a semantic or decision authority owner | remain distinct; the evaluation family acquires no owner authority |\n"},{"number":1005,"text":"| `Product` | an immutable released Product and a mutable Product Definition | remain distinct and select only through the occurrence's declared context |\n"},{"number":1006,"text":"| `Tenant` | an STDO build realisation and hosted, customer, account, runtime or data tenancy | remain distinct; build tenancy supplies no default for the other contexts |\n"},{"number":1007,"text":"| `User` | a Product role, human person, identity principal, account, actor, operator or data subject | unresolved until downstream authority defines or explicitly relates the applicable meanings |\n"},{"number":1008,"text":"\n"},{"number":1009,"text":"A positive local case declares one context and resolves exactly one\n"},{"number":1010,"text":"concept. A positive cross-context case supplies the complete authorised\n"},{"number":1011,"text":"relation. Negative cases cover zero candidates, multiple candidates after\n"},{"number":1012,"text":"disambiguation, a selected concept outside the candidate set, a\n"},{"number":1013,"text":"context-free glossary fallback, incomplete relation coordinates, authority\n"},{"number":1014,"text":"or basis mismatch, undeclared loss and invalidated relations. Correct\n"},{"number":1015,"text":"downstream behaviour produced through a guessed meaning does not pass\n"},{"number":1016,"text":"semantic conformance (P6, P1). [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md) may index\n"},{"number":1017,"text":"these cases; it does not redefine them.\n"},{"number":1018,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1076,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/11. One constitutional surface and version boundary\n"},{"number":1020,"text":"\n"},{"number":1021,"text":"STDO-SURFACE-001. The shared methodology is modular in authorship and\n"},{"number":1022,"text":"singular in authority. Each law has one owning member; other members\n"},{"number":1023,"text":"consume it by reference. The members become operative only as one complete\n"},{"number":1024,"text":"released version of the method (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":1025,"text":"\n"},{"number":1026,"text":"A released cut identifies its exact member set, member digests, review\n"},{"number":1027,"text":"basis, human acceptance and immutable identity. Compressions, templates,\n"},{"number":1028,"text":"comments, candidate work, installed copies and mutable source are derived,\n"},{"number":1029,"text":"evidential or authoring surfaces. They cannot become a selectable partial\n"},{"number":1030,"text":"constitution and cannot reinterpret the owning members (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1031,"text":"\n"},{"number":1032,"text":"Within their declared scope, derived instructions preserve the owning\n"},{"number":1033,"text":"clauses' applicability, obligations, permissions, exclusions, decision\n"},{"number":1034,"text":"owners and invalidators. A projected prohibition cannot lose its condition\n"},{"number":1035,"text":"or its lawful alternative, even when every source digest is correct. A\n"},{"number":1036,"text":"summary, bootstrap or index cannot require a stricter or weaker relation by\n"},{"number":1037,"text":"compression. Its references are resolvable within the declared actor's\n"},{"number":1038,"text":"access; otherwise the required meaning is supplied directly (P4b, P1;\n"},{"number":1039,"text":"FOUNDATIONS §4, reference versus body).\n"},{"number":1040,"text":"\n"},{"number":1041,"text":"Staleness binding. What a derived surface is, when it is stale, and\n"},{"number":1042,"text":"what an actor uses in its place are\n"},{"number":1043,"text":"[ACTIVATION §2 Staleness of derived surfaces](ACTIVATION.md#staleness-of-derived-surfaces);\n"},{"number":1044,"text":"which questions a derived surface decides on its own is ACTIVATION §2,\n"},{"number":1045,"text":"Standalone scope. This member refines that law for the derived surfaces\n"},{"number":1046,"text":"a released cut or an installation carries, among them compressions,\n"},{"number":1047,"text":"templates, bootstraps, indexes and projected frames. Each carries the\n"},{"number":1048,"text":"path and digest of each deciding source it was derived from, and of each\n"},{"number":1049,"text":"index it watches (GLOSSARY §2). A change to any of those digests is the\n"},{"number":1050,"text":"source change that makes it stale under that law, and it must be\n"},{"number":1051,"text":"regenerated or explicitly re-accepted before an installation treats it\n"},{"number":1052,"text":"as current. What a matching digest establishes is stated above\n"},{"number":1053,"text":"(EVALUATION §7). The raw owning members of the same\n"},{"number":1054,"text":"selected cut remain the deciding authority: a question that a stale or\n"},{"number":1055,"text":"insufficient carrier cannot decide is decided from them, as ACTIVATION\n"},{"number":1056,"text":"§2 states (P3, P5, P6).\n"},{"number":1057,"text":"\n"},{"number":1058,"text":"The method owns normative construction algebra, authority relations,\n"},{"number":1059,"text":"abstract state and transition laws, admissibility conditions, necessary\n"},{"number":1060,"text":"causal order and evidence invariants. Consumers own concrete Product\n"},{"number":1061,"text":"realisation: instantiated types and schemas, files, tools, runtime and\n"},{"number":1062,"text":"orchestration machinery, tests and executable conformance implementation.\n"},{"number":1063,"text":"A concrete form is method law only when the method explicitly accepts it\n"},{"number":1064,"text":"as an interoperability boundary, as §1 does for the definition schema and\n"},{"number":1065,"text":"template (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1066,"text":"\n"},{"number":1067,"text":"A shared-method amendment cannot create an executable tool, workflow\n"},{"number":1068,"text":"engine, runtime, assurance system or consumer realisation as STDO Product\n"},{"number":1069,"text":"scope without separate explicit human authorisation. An agent recording a\n"},{"number":1070,"text":"ruling cannot widen its subject, implication, authority or change class\n"},{"number":1071,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":1072,"text":"\n"},{"number":1073,"text":"Only a released method version is publication authority. Mutable method\n"},{"number":1074,"text":"source may author a future cut; it must not silently govern a consumer\n"},{"number":1075,"text":"(P6, P3).\n"},{"number":1076,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1224,"heading":"PRODUCT_DEFINITION/12. Bootstrap","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#PRODUCT_DEFINITION%2F12.%20Bootstrap","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","sha256":"2cb7ea2f0854f35d930bf604550acf46a167906d85b2c5576f84532e12902f85","start_line":1077,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md","lines":[{"number":1077,"text":"## 12. Bootstrap\n"},{"number":1078,"text":"\n"},{"number":1079,"text":"Every product defined under this method begins from\n"},{"number":1080,"text":"`templates/PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json`, copied to the product's\n"},{"number":1081,"text":"definition root as `stdo_default.json` for a singleton default project or\n"},{"number":1082,"text":"as `stdo_<label>.json` for a named product definition. An existing project\n"},{"number":1083,"text":"fills the URI bindings over its current layout; adoption requires no\n"},{"number":1084,"text":"moving, renaming or duplicating of existing authority or realisation\n"},{"number":1085,"text":"surfaces (P2, P3).\n"},{"number":1086,"text":"\n"},{"number":1087,"text":"The default scaffold binds:\n"},{"number":1088,"text":"\n"},{"number":1089,"text":"- a shared versioned STDO store, addressed through the exact\n"},{"number":1090,"text":"  `constitution.stdo.basis`, as the installed distribution of the selected\n"},{"number":1091,"text":"  process constitution;\n"},{"number":1092,"text":"- `specification/GOALS.md` as current work-wave orientation;\n"},{"number":1093,"text":"- `specification/INTENT.md` as domain direction;\n"},{"number":1094,"text":"- `specification/PRODUCT.md` as the current product-definition surface;\n"},{"number":1095,"text":"- `specification/requirements/` as the live requirement surface;\n"},{"number":1096,"text":"- `build_tenants/` as the root for shared and tenant-local realisation\n"},{"number":1097,"text":"  surfaces; and\n"},{"number":1098,"text":"- `.ai-workspace/` as the sprint, ticket and comment carrier root.\n"},{"number":1099,"text":"\n"},{"number":1100,"text":"These are template defaults, not universal path law; the definition's URI\n"},{"number":1101,"text":"bindings select the actual project carriers (P2).\n"},{"number":1102,"text":"\n"},{"number":1103,"text":"The authority split is (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":1104,"text":"\n"},{"number":1105,"text":"- mutable methodology authoring lives in the method's own source workspace\n"},{"number":1106,"text":"  (the standards of its source project) and governs only a future\n"},{"number":1107,"text":"  candidate cut;\n"},{"number":1108,"text":"- released methodology authority is the exact immutable STDO version\n"},{"number":1109,"text":"  selected by the consumer;\n"},{"number":1110,"text":"- installed methodology distribution lives in the toolchain manager's\n"},{"number":1111,"text":"  shared versioned store by default and matches the basis URI and manifest\n"},{"number":1112,"text":"  digest;\n"},{"number":1113,"text":"- project-owned constitutional surfaces live at the definition's `what`\n"},{"number":1114,"text":"  bindings; and\n"},{"number":1115,"text":"- project-owned realisation and work surfaces live at its `how` and\n"},{"number":1116,"text":"  `ticketing` bindings.\n"},{"number":1117,"text":"\n"},{"number":1118,"text":"A project creates no competing local methodology root, such as a default\n"},{"number":1119,"text":"`specification/standards/`, and binds no mutable or partial method source\n"},{"number":1120,"text":"as if it were the selected immutable release (P6).\n"},{"number":1121,"text":"\n"},{"number":1122,"text":"Method authority is singular: the selected immutable STDO release\n"},{"number":1123,"text":"authority, projected into the installed distribution located by the\n"},{"number":1124,"text":"overlay; and the project constitutional authority at the definition's\n"},{"number":1125,"text":"bound WHAT surfaces (P6). When editing or repricing methodology, the\n"},{"number":1126,"text":"mutable source path is authoring authority for the candidate being\n"},{"number":1127,"text":"constructed; it is not operative consumer law before release and explicit\n"},{"number":1128,"text":"selection (P3, P6). When operating inside a governed workspace, the\n"},{"number":1129,"text":"resolved installed basis is the operative distribution of the selected\n"},{"number":1130,"text":"immutable release until the consumer explicitly adopts another cut. A\n"},{"number":1131,"text":"project-local exact copy stays lawful when explicitly bound and verified;\n"},{"number":1132,"text":"it is not the default, and file proximity cannot select it (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":1133,"text":"\n"},{"number":1134,"text":"The corresponding default folder shape is:\n"},{"number":1135,"text":"\n"},{"number":1136,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1137,"text":"stdo_default.json\n"},{"number":1138,"text":"\n"},{"number":1139,"text":"specification/\n"},{"number":1140,"text":"├── GOALS.md\n"},{"number":1141,"text":"├── INTENT.md\n"},{"number":1142,"text":"├── PRODUCT.md\n"},{"number":1143,"text":"└── requirements/\n"},{"number":1144,"text":"    └── *.md\n"},{"number":1145,"text":"\n"},{"number":1146,"text":"build_tenants/\n"},{"number":1147,"text":"├── common/\n"},{"number":1148,"text":"└── default/\n"},{"number":1149,"text":"\n"},{"number":1150,"text":".ai-workspace/\n"},{"number":1151,"text":"├── sprints/\n"},{"number":1152,"text":"├── tickets/\n"},{"number":1153,"text":"│   ├── backlog/\n"},{"number":1154,"text":"│   ├── active/\n"},{"number":1155,"text":"│   └── completed/\n"},{"number":1156,"text":"└── comments/\n"},{"number":1157,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1158,"text":"\n"},{"number":1159,"text":"This is a starter topology, not a conformance requirement. A monorepo may\n"},{"number":1160,"text":"place several `stdo_<label>.json` definitions at one root and bind each to\n"},{"number":1161,"text":"a different WHAT. A hierarchical repository may place one or more\n"},{"number":1162,"text":"definitions at any nested project root. Recursive discovery (§9) finds both\n"},{"number":1163,"text":"shapes; explicit composition, never directory nesting, relates their\n"},{"number":1164,"text":"products (P3, P2).\n"},{"number":1165,"text":"\n"},{"number":1166,"text":"A project need not start with a complete `requirements/` tree on day zero.\n"},{"number":1167,"text":"Requirements may be sourced from any legitimate constitutional input\n"},{"number":1168,"text":"regardless of its path, including `GOALS.md`, `INTENT.md`, `PRODUCT.md`,\n"},{"number":1169,"text":"existing requirement documents, imported standards or policy material,\n"},{"number":1170,"text":"prior project versions, and migration or repricing source material. Most\n"},{"number":1171,"text":"projects begin by deriving `INTENT.md` from `GOALS.md`, then `PRODUCT.md`\n"},{"number":1172,"text":"from `INTENT.md`, then the first requirement surface from the product\n"},{"number":1173,"text":"definition; that is the usual starting point, not the only lawful source\n"},{"number":1174,"text":"(P2).\n"},{"number":1175,"text":"\n"},{"number":1176,"text":"The bootstrap sequence is (P3, P6, P2):\n"},{"number":1177,"text":"\n"},{"number":1178,"text":"1. Install the STDO toolchain manager once, resolve the applicable release-profile\n"},{"number":1179,"text":"   discovery route (§4), and explicitly select one immutable release cut.\n"},{"number":1180,"text":"2. Install that complete cut in the shared release store and retain its\n"},{"number":1181,"text":"   deterministic installed-manifest digest.\n"},{"number":1182,"text":"3. Copy `PRODUCT_DEFINITION_TEMPLATE.json` from that exact cut to the\n"},{"number":1183,"text":"   product definition root as `stdo_default.json` or `stdo_<label>.json`.\n"},{"number":1184,"text":"4. Assign the stable `product.definition_id` for the mutable WHAT\n"},{"number":1185,"text":"   definition line, its source-project locator and its bounded-context\n"},{"number":1186,"text":"   declaration; keep it distinct from every immutable Product and release\n"},{"number":1187,"text":"   identity.\n"},{"number":1188,"text":"5. Bind `constitution.stdo.source`, its non-operative selector, the exact\n"},{"number":1189,"text":"   basis URI and manifest digest, every additional constitutional\n"},{"number":1190,"text":"   authority and the relevant basis-qualified entrypoints; confirm that\n"},{"number":1191,"text":"   the set collectively defines axioms, ontology, epistemology, taxonomy\n"},{"number":1192,"text":"   and semantics for the governed scope (§3).\n"},{"number":1193,"text":"6. Bind the agent bootstrap entrypoint and portable targets relative to\n"},{"number":1194,"text":"   the resolved `product.source_project`, then let the manager preflight\n"},{"number":1195,"text":"   every target and install or refresh only their marker-bounded\n"},{"number":1196,"text":"   discovery blocks.\n"},{"number":1197,"text":"7. Bind, or explicitly empty, the local axiom, override and\n"},{"number":1198,"text":"   disambiguation collections (§6).\n"},{"number":1199,"text":"8. Bind at least one accepted collective reference-frame basis, its\n"},{"number":1200,"text":"   admitting authorities and its exact governed scope (§7).\n"},{"number":1201,"text":"9. Write or confirm the current Goals carrier, run the goals to intent to\n"},{"number":1202,"text":"   product steps, and bind the resulting Intent and Product entrypoints.\n"},{"number":1203,"text":"10. Gather, derive, classify and bind the live specification or\n"},{"number":1204,"text":"    requirement surfaces without creating a co-equal rival.\n"},{"number":1205,"text":"11. Bind at least one build tenant, including its root, design and\n"},{"number":1206,"text":"    implementation surfaces, and bind any shared realisation law (§8).\n"},{"number":1207,"text":"12. Bind the Goals carrier, the ticket lanes, the comments root and the\n"},{"number":1208,"text":"    optional sprint root.\n"},{"number":1209,"text":"13. Bind every known product-composition edge explicitly, including its\n"},{"number":1210,"text":"    target definition identity, relation authority and non-empty contract\n"},{"number":1211,"text":"    set (§9). Bind the standalone/composed outcome, material recursive\n"},{"number":1212,"text":"    reliance and each actor's information boundary under PC-01–PC-07;\n"},{"number":1213,"text":"    separate authorized inspection from durable consumption.\n"},{"number":1214,"text":"14. Validate the JSON shape, assert URI and URI-reference syntax,\n"},{"number":1215,"text":"    synchronise and verify the exact installed basis, then resolve every\n"},{"number":1216,"text":"    URI and perform the cross-definition identity, composition,\n"},{"number":1217,"text":"    constitutional-sufficiency and authority-congruence checks. Mechanical\n"},{"number":1218,"text":"    resolution alone establishes neither the grants nor context adequacy\n"},{"number":1219,"text":"    of an admitted activation; unresolved material conditions remain open.\n"},{"number":1220,"text":"\n"},{"number":1221,"text":"Once a bound requirement set is the live constitutional surface, no rival\n"},{"number":1222,"text":"monolithic requirements document should remain co-equal authority with it. This\n"},{"number":1223,"text":"keeps requirement truth structurally clear, derivable and non-monolithic\n"},{"number":1224,"text":"without prescribing its folder (P6, P2).\n"}]},{"end_line":8,"heading":"PROFILES","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md#PROFILES","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md","sha256":"d6a2b07822f7150af5d5bf48b15352dd77cb4d782fe68f5590f433e3eebc2269","start_line":1,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md","lines":[{"number":1,"text":"# PROFILES\n"},{"number":2,"text":"\n"},{"number":3,"text":"Tier 3. Owns the boundary between the core and the profiles, the\n"},{"number":4,"text":"declared-binding rule and the import rule that every profile applies\n"},{"number":5,"text":"(§1), and indexes the profiles (§2 to §6). A profile is a domain or\n"},{"number":6,"text":"operational specialisation of the method; the members of tiers 1 and 2\n"},{"number":7,"text":"are the core.\n"},{"number":8,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":52,"heading":"PROFILES/1. The boundary","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md#PROFILES%2F1.%20The%20boundary","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md","sha256":"ab1d51958b9f86a9c32fa3b62e35fabf971f4172c2bc92fa70251d2f50742587","start_line":9,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md","lines":[{"number":9,"text":"## 1. The boundary\n"},{"number":10,"text":"\n"},{"number":11,"text":"The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor. Terms owned outside\n"},{"number":12,"text":"the core, by a profile or a realisation, never enter tier 1 or 2: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event\n"},{"number":13,"text":"log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, and the design\n"},{"number":14,"text":"profile's IACS and Prime. The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,\n"},{"number":15,"text":"F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and\n"},{"number":16,"text":"\"module\" is a generic term under [ASSURANCE](ASSURANCE.md); neither is\n"},{"number":17,"text":"restricted here. A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of these;\n"},{"number":18,"text":"the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved\n"},{"number":19,"text":"meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. In this member \"binding\" means\n"},{"number":20,"text":"that declared binding of a core mechanism; a Product's adoption binding is\n"},{"number":21,"text":"[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)'s,\n"},{"number":22,"text":"and a carrier binding to a typed contract is [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding)'s;\n"},{"number":23,"text":"the three are not interchanged (P0 boundary, P1). Concrete applications\n"},{"number":24,"text":"of the declared-binding rule are ODD's exact-edition F_D import and\n"},{"number":25,"text":"specialisations of F_P and F_H, which\n"},{"number":26,"text":"[ODD §5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute) owns in the\n"},{"number":27,"text":"graph-native context.\n"},{"number":28,"text":"\n"},{"number":29,"text":"Import rule. A profile imports the generic families of tiers 1 and 2 that\n"},{"number":30,"text":"its rules rest on, and owns only its own bindings: the terms and choices\n"},{"number":31,"text":"it adds for its domain or operation, among them the declared bindings\n"},{"number":32,"text":"above (P1, P6). It imports each concept it uses from a member of tiers 1\n"},{"number":33,"text":"and 2 under\n"},{"number":34,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members),\n"},{"number":35,"text":"which states what an import is, and restates none of that member's rules.\n"},{"number":36,"text":"Its family table, in the format of\n"},{"number":37,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),\n"},{"number":38,"text":"names each imported family by its ID and the section that holds its table,\n"},{"number":39,"text":"in the premise column; the profile's rules rest on that family's\n"},{"number":40,"text":"consequences, with the standing FOUNDATIONS §3 gives them, and the\n"},{"number":41,"text":"family's rules and choices keep their owners. A profile that refines\n"},{"number":42,"text":"another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile\n"},{"number":43,"text":"keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":44,"text":"Purpose and material relation:\n"},{"number":45,"text":"each profile table cites the families it rests on without restating them,\n"},{"number":46,"text":"so no generic rule gains a second owner in a profile and no choice a\n"},{"number":47,"text":"profile adds is presented as following from the foundations (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":48,"text":"\n"},{"number":49,"text":"A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test\n"},{"number":50,"text":"subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by\n"},{"number":51,"text":"precedent.\n"},{"number":52,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":69,"heading":"PROFILES/2. Graph execution","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md#PROFILES%2F2.%20Graph%20execution","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md","sha256":"f0c8fc4ddfda905f3ec50ffd687703fdac4e371cfbf2340216f099a2a4e450ef","start_line":53,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/PROFILES.md","lines":[{"number":53,"text":"## 2. The frame as the engagement unit\n"},{"number":14,"text":"\n"},{"number":15,"text":"An actor, human or computational, has finite context, attention, time and\n"},{"number":16,"text":"capability. A workspace may hold more material truth, history, topology,\n"},{"number":17,"text":"authority and evidence than one actor can evaluate at once. This member\n"},{"number":18,"text":"makes that limit explicit (P0):\n"},{"number":19,"text":"\n"},{"number":20,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":21,"text":"declared evaluation family\n"},{"number":22,"text":"  + exact workspace and topology basis\n"},{"number":23,"text":"  + finite material relations and coordinates\n"},{"number":24,"text":"  + applicable invariants and authorities\n"},{"number":25,"text":"  + admissible evidence and exclusions\n"},{"number":26,"text":"  + actor capability envelope\n"},{"number":27,"text":"  = activated reference frame\n"},{"number":28,"text":"  -> one closed result in the core algebra of FOUNDATIONS §4 Results\n"},{"number":29,"text":"```\n"},{"number":30,"text":"\n"},{"number":31,"text":"A project engages a body of work through a declared frame set (P6, P2):\n"},{"number":32,"text":"\n"},{"number":33,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":34,"text":"workspace and governed outcome\n"},{"number":35,"text":"  + accumulated practice and historical failures\n"},{"number":36,"text":"  + available actor capabilities\n"},{"number":37,"text":"  + human judgment\n"},{"number":38,"text":"  -> declared frame set\n"},{"number":39,"text":"  -> bounded evaluations\n"},{"number":40,"text":"  -> conjunction or translation where required\n"},{"number":41,"text":"  -> coverage ledger and residual uncertainty\n"},{"number":42,"text":"  -> empirical frame-set revision\n"},{"number":43,"text":"```\n"},{"number":44,"text":"\n"},{"number":45,"text":"The reference frame is the atomic engagement unit: the unit that is\n"},{"number":46,"text":"activated and evaluated as one bounded context. Frame-set selection,\n"},{"number":47,"text":"activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are\n"},{"number":48,"text":"separate functions over it (§5). A frame supports a bounded evaluation\n"},{"number":49,"text":"without first containing a universal theory of its possible relationships.\n"},{"number":50,"text":"\"Atomic\" is said at engagement altitude only. It does not assert that every\n"},{"number":51,"text":"relation inside the frame is one irreducible semantic atom; a frame may\n"},{"number":52,"text":"carry several semantic atoms and several owner relations without merging\n"},{"number":53,"text":"their meaning or authority (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":54,"text":"\n"},{"number":55,"text":"Scope. This member governs how finite actors construct and use bounded\n"},{"number":56,"text":"reasoning or execution contexts over a changing body of work. It applies to\n"},{"number":57,"text":"human work, agentic work, deterministic evaluation, probabilistic\n"},{"number":58,"text":"construction, assurance and mixed work wherever the governing product or\n"},{"number":59,"text":"method permits them. It is engagement law only: it defines no application\n"},{"number":60,"text":"profile, role mapping, product-owned frame-basis binding, domain product,\n"},{"number":61,"text":"specification taxonomy, design ontology, runtime, workflow, adoption\n"},{"number":62,"text":"relation or assurance implementation. Other members and products may import or\n"},{"number":63,"text":"specialise its relations under their own authority, and that external\n"},{"number":64,"text":"relation neither enters nor amends this member (P2: an obligation stops\n"},{"number":65,"text":"where its purpose stops). This member owns the reference-frame-evaluation\n"},{"number":66,"text":"bounded context, `urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation`,\n"},{"number":67,"text":"under its exact publication basis. This member owns only its frame\n"},{"number":68,"text":"declaration, activation, evaluation, basis, relation, result, coverage,\n"},{"number":69,"text":"revision and qualification concepts. The context also holds the concepts\n"},{"number":70,"text":"imported below, each kept by its owner. A same-spelled profile, product,\n"},{"number":71,"text":"role or runtime carrier is not imported by proximity or nominal match (P3,\n"},{"number":72,"text":"P1).\n"},{"number":73,"text":"\n"},{"number":74,"text":"Substrate. A reference frame may be represented in prose, structured data,\n"},{"number":75,"text":"a prompt, a design asset, a typed carrier, a runtime context or any other\n"},{"number":76,"text":"form its consumer selects. No class, aggregate, actor, controller, service,\n"},{"number":77,"text":"registry, graph or frame engine is required (P2; RF-016).\n"},{"number":78,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":119,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/1. It covers this member; the\n"},{"number":127,"text":"context construction of\n"},{"number":128,"text":"[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope);\n"},{"number":129,"text":"and the frame objects, authority kinds, disjointness and independence and\n"},{"number":130,"text":"frame tuple of [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects). A rule in\n"},{"number":131,"text":"another member is marked \"outside this member\" in the third column; the\n"},{"number":132,"text":"table owns none of the rules it names. Its instance premises are: (a) a\n"},{"number":133,"text":"workspace holds more material than one actor's capability envelope (its\n"},{"number":134,"text":"competence, context capacity, tools and access) can evaluate at once; (b)\n"},{"number":135,"text":"the evaluations to be made are declared questions about a governed\n"},{"number":136,"text":"outcome; (c) several frames and actors may bear on one workspace, and their\n"},{"number":137,"text":"material may overlap; (d) the workspace, its topology and the actors'\n"},{"number":138,"text":"capabilities change between activations; (e) an actor may read both owning\n"},{"number":139,"text":"sources and surfaces derived from them by copying, projection or\n"},{"number":140,"text":"compression. They are conditions of the work this family governs, not\n"},{"number":141,"text":"commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone. Two of P0's\n"},{"number":142,"text":"premises are cited by name: its actor-change premise, that the actor of one\n"},{"number":143,"text":"step need not be the actor of the next and may re-acquire declared sources\n"},{"number":144,"text":"but not private memory; and its open-world premise, that the world is open.\n"},{"number":145,"text":"The standing of the consequences below is stated in\n"},{"number":146,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).\n"},{"number":147,"text":"\n"},{"number":148,"text":"| Premises, with standing | Consequence that follows | Rule in this member that states it | Added domain or policy choice, and its owner | Pillar |\n"},{"number":149,"text":"|---|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":150,"text":"| P0 (recovered); instance premise a | By P0 an actor's attention is finite, and by (a) the workspace exceeds it, so no finite actor is presumed to hold the complete workspace in active attention. The unit of engagement is one activated reference frame, activated and evaluated as one bounded context; frame-set selection, activation, evaluation, conjunction, translation, coverage and revision are separate functions over it | [§1](#1-the-frame-as-the-engagement-unit), the two compressions and the engagement unit; [§2](#2-core-claims) claim 1; [§12](#12-violations) item 1 | none | 7 |\n"},{"number":151,"text":"| P1 (independent), P3 (independent), P2 (independent); instance premise c | By P1 and P3 meaning and authority stay with their owners however material is grouped, and by P2 frames are chosen for the evaluation, so a frame is atomic at engagement altitude only: it may carry several semantic atoms and owner relations without merging their meaning or authority, and one semantic atom may take part in several frames. A frame set is not contracted to a disjoint minimum because its material variables overlap | [§1](#1-the-frame-as-the-engagement-unit), \"Atomic\"; [Engagement atom and semantic atom](#engagement-atom-and-semantic-atom) | a semantic-contraction law for a domain's atoms: the adopting method that supplies it, such as the design profile's [Prime law](DESIGN_MODULE.md#6-prime-law) | 6, 7 |\n"},{"number":152,"text":"| P2 (independent), P3 (independent), P1 (independent) | By P2 each member governs only the question it owns, and by P1 and P3 a specialisation keeps its own meaning and owner, so this member's law stops at engagement: it defines no application profile, role mapping, product-owned frame-basis binding, domain product, runtime, workflow or assurance implementation. A member or product that specialises its relations does so under its own authority, and that relation neither enters nor amends this member; a same-spelled carrier enters the context by no proximity or nominal match | [§1](#1-the-frame-as-the-engagement-unit), Scope | the bounded-context identity `urn:stdo:bounded-context:reference-frame-evaluation`: this member; each specialisation: the profile or product that declares it | 1, 7 |\n"},{"number":153,"text":"| P1 (independent), P3 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P1 and P3 a concept means what its owner defines on its basis, and by P6 using it grants nothing, so a concept used here that another member defines keeps that owner and that meaning. It enters by a reference-only import, which grants no semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority; a refinement this member states names its owner and maps back to the core | [Imports into this context](#imports-into-this-context) | which concepts are imported, and from which member: this member's declaration; the import rule: [FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members), traced in family F12 | 2, 7 |\n"},{"number":154,"text":"| P0 (recovered), P1 (independent), P2 (independent), P3 (independent), P6 (independent) | By P0 an actor engages only a finite specification, and by P1 and P3 a carrier is a representation of it, not the relation, so a reference frame is a finite specification of the attention, coordinates, authority, evidence and result relations one evaluation family requires. It specifies a relation, not a required schema or runtime carrier; a prompt, context packet or program is a projection of an activated frame, not the frame. A frame is bound only when every material coordinate resolves to an exact source, subject, basis, authority, evidence route, actor envelope, result relation and invalidation condition, and representation cannot create, widen or replace that binding | [FOUNDATIONS §2 The frame tuple](FOUNDATIONS.md#the-frame-tuple) and [Frame objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects), Workspace, Material-relation manifold, Reference frame and Active frame configuration, outside this member | the twelve components ⟨Q, B, M, C, I, A, E, X, R, J, K, D⟩: FOUNDATIONS §2 The frame tuple | 6, 7 |\n"},{"number":155,"text":"| P2 (independent), P1 (independent); instance premise b | By P2 a frame exists for an evaluation, and by P1 wording carries no meaning of its own, so a frame's sufficiency can be tested only against the evaluation family it declares, so every frame declares one; a module, file, service, role, persona, prompt or lens with no declared evaluation relation is not a frame. Similar wording does not show that two evaluations share a family: an evaluation is within a frame's family only when the question it decides is one that family states at the frame's declared coordinates, whatever the frame's name or its membership in the set | [RF-001](#rf-001-evaluation-relativity); [FOUNDATIONS §2 Frame objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects), Evaluation, Evaluation family and Role, persona, abstraction, component, outside this member; [Diagnostic order](#diagnostic-order), question 1; [§12](#12-violations) item 2 | each frame's evaluation family: the frame's declaration, made under the frame-set authority (§4) | 7 |\n"},{"number":156,"text":"| P0 (recovered, with its actor-change premise), P2 (independent), P6 (independent); instance premise a | By P0 and its actor-change premise an attention surface must fit and be reconstructable by the actor that uses it, so an activated frame's attention surface is finite and fits the selected actor's declared envelope; a frame that needs undeclared ambient memory, conversation history or an effectively global workspace context is not reconstructable for that actor. Where the envelope declares a context capacity, the selected context's size is measured before the actor reads it, over a stated boundary, and recorded with the capacity and the comparison; context outside the boundary is recorded as not measured. The measurement applies there and only there, is no budget and no universal gate, and shows fit and nothing else | [RF-002](#rf-002-finite-attention); [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) step 3, the size measurement, outside this member; [§12](#12-violations) item 10 | the capacity and its unit, bytes or tokens: the actor's declared envelope; the measured boundary, and time, spend and other resource limits: the selected execution binding ([SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding)) | 7, 8 |\n"},{"number":157,"text":"| P2 (independent), P0 (recovered, with its open-world premise), P5 (derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise); instance premise a | By P2 and P5 a result is sound only if every relation that can change it is present, and by P0's open-world premise relations not held are not thereby absent, so every known relation whose lawful change can alter the result, the validity of the basis, the sufficiency of evidence, operation authority or decision authority appears in the frame or enters through a declared authoritative input, and omitting one makes the frame insufficient; the law does not require proof that no undiscovered material relation exists. The context starts as the material closure of the intake's seed set (the subject, outcome and affected relations it names) under that relation family, and a closure that is not finite and unique on the exact basis stops the step and is not guessed | [RF-003](#rf-003-material-sufficiency); [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) step 1, outside this member | the closure law: [AC-010](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-010-material-closure); the stop's outcome, `closure_unresolved`: [ACTIVATION §3 Admission and activation](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation) | 6, 7 |\n"},{"number":158,"text":"| P2 (independent) | By P2 attention is spent only on what bears on the evaluation, so relations that cannot affect the declared evaluation stay outside active attention unless they are needed to establish that irrelevance; adjacent material, or the presence of the corpus, is no reason to load or read it. The closure is projected to the selected context with its boundary recorded | [RF-004](#rf-004-irrelevance-exclusion); [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) step 2 and Acquisition, outside this member | the seams the boundary records (excluded, external, unresolved, translated, invalidation-sensitive): ACTIVATION §2 step 2, applying [AC-011](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-011-projection) | 7 |\n"},{"number":159,"text":"| P3 (independent), P1 (independent) | By P3 a result binds its exact basis, and by P1 equal names or shapes do not establish equal meaning, so every result binds its exact subject, basis, coordinates and evidence scope. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis returns `invalid_basis` or requires reactivation; equal names, values, shapes, locations or apparent topology positions never substitute for declared coordinate equality | [RF-005](#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates); [FOUNDATIONS §2 Frame objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects), Coordinate, outside this member; [§12](#12-violations) item 7 | each frame's coordinate and equality law: its declaration (C of the frame tuple) | 2, 7 |\n"},{"number":160,"text":"| P6 (independent), P3 (independent); instance premise c | By P6 authority exists only through an admitted grant, and by P3 it binds its owner and scope, so a frame carries and applies admitted authority and never mints, widens, transfers or reconstructs it from actor identity, capability, evidence shape, implementation reachability or frame selection; declaring, selecting, activating or executing a frame, or naming a role, grants none. The kinds of authority may coincide in a lawful case and never collapse by default, and actor identity is not an authority. A read-only evaluation declares no operation authority; an effectful one inherits the exact operation grant from its existing owner. A proxy for human authority keeps its identity distinct from the human authority's | [RF-006](#rf-006-authority-conservation); [FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds) and [Frame objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects), Role, persona, abstraction, component, outside this member; [§2](#2-core-claims) claim 8; [§12](#12-violations) item 6 | the division into frame-set, semantic, evaluation, operation and decision authority, with actor identity apart, and frame-set authority as human authority: FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds; when a bounded proxy may act: [IDENTITY §6](IDENTITY.md#6-authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004) | 7, 9 |\n"},{"number":161,"text":"| P6 (independent) | By P6 meaning, evidence, application, operation and decision are separate authorities, so semantic law defines what the evaluation means, evidence supplies observations, the evaluator applies the declared relation, the existing operation owner supplies any operation grant, and decision authority disposes the result; a frame declaration keeps these roles distinguishable even when one actor performs several. The evaluator applies the frame's declared invariants, evidence rules and result algebra and records every assumption whose failure could change the result | [RF-007](#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation); [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) Evaluation, outside this member | none; [EVALUATION §2](EVALUATION.md#2-separation) applies this law to review (family F6) | 7, 9 |\n"},{"number":162,"text":"| P1 (independent), P3 (independent); instance premise c | By P1 shared material does not share meaning, and by P3 each frame binds its own basis, so frames may share entities, variables, evidence or coordinates; shared material establishes neither identical meaning nor identical basis, authority or result, and every cross-frame equality or translation an evaluation uses is declared where it is used | [RF-008](#rf-008-overlap-without-identity-collapse); [§12](#12-violations) item 7 | none | 2, 7 |\n"},{"number":163,"text":"| P3 (independent), P1 (independent), P6 (independent), P2 (independent); instance premise c | By P3 and P1 a relation holds only where it is declared, and by P6 and P2 each structure answers its own question, so parent and child relations among frames apply only where declared. Functional decomposition, communication, authority precedence, frame configuration, subject topology and evaluation dependency are distinct relation structures, which a consumer may align where the governed subject warrants it and never silently treats as one hierarchy; an exchange of information grants no authority and establishes neither a decomposition nor an evaluation dependency. No frame relation is the default topology, and a project declares only the relations its evaluations and coverage claims need | [RF-009](#rf-009-no-assumed-hierarchy); [§7](#7-frame-relations); [§12](#12-violations) item 3 | the ten named frame relations: this member (§7); which relations a project declares, and where it aligns relation structures: that project, for its governed subject | 4, 7 |\n"},{"number":164,"text":"| P6 (independent), P1 (independent); instance premise c | By P6 and P1 each kind of independence is a different relation, so frame disjointness (structural), evaluation independence (procedural) and assurance independence (claim-relative) are three relations: disjoint frames need not be independently evaluated, independently activated evaluations need not be disjoint, and the unqualified word \"independent\" establishes none of them. Separately activated evaluations may overlap in subject, manifold or evidence, and neither consumes nor influences the other's unclosed working result | [FOUNDATIONS §2 Disjointness and independence](FOUNDATIONS.md#disjointness-and-independence), outside this member; [Independently activated co-evaluation](#independently-activated-co-evaluation) | the conditions a verdict needs to count as independent assurance: the governing assurance law ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment), family F6) | 7, 9 |\n"},{"number":165,"text":"| P4a (independent), P6 (independent), P2 (independent) | By P4a composition is needed only where parts combine through declared relations, and by P2 nothing is composed that the evaluation does not need, so using several frames does not require composing their internal manifolds. Composition law is required only when the evaluation combines their internal variables, transports evidence or values across them, or treats their operations as one material execution relation. Independently activated evaluations may instead return closed results to one declared conjunction or decision rule. A material composition is introduced only when the evaluation requires it, and declares its shared invariants, effect or decision order where material, closure, failure and the conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority | [RF-010](#rf-010-composition-on-demand); [§6](#6-frames-in-conjunction), Result conjunction and Material composition; [§12](#12-violations) items 4 and 5 | each material composition: the owning application; the conjunction: [FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) (family F3); the choices its declared rule leaves open: the member or profile that applies the conjunction, in its declared rule | 3, 4, 7 |\n"},{"number":166,"text":"| P1 (independent), P4b (derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable); instance premise c | By P1 a value carried across frames keeps its meaning only through a declared relation, and by P4b what is lost must travel with it, so where one frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another, the translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions; a loss inside the accepted loss travels with the value as a residual | [Evidence or coordinate translation](#evidence-or-coordinate-translation); [§5](#5-method-functions), the outcomes of `translate` | the accepted loss and the refusal conditions of each translation: its declarer | 3, 6, 7 |\n"},{"number":167,"text":"| P3 (independent), P4b (derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable); instance premise d | By P3 a result binds coordinates that a topology change can alter, and by P4b a stale result persists until re-evaluated, so an activated frame declares the topology changes capable of invalidating its coordinates or its materiality judgment, and a detected material topology mutation causes reevaluation, frame revision or recharting before a previous result is reused. A material revision of a frame produces a new revision coordinate and states which prior activations, results and coverage claims need reevaluation; every result bound to the prior revision is reopened until a recorded re-check finds it independent of the change or it is re-evaluated, and silence keeps no result closed. A revision that changes no declaration of the frame needs no new coordinate, and an unchanged declaration is no ground for keeping a result closed: whether a closed result stays valid is decided by the reuse rule of ACTIVATION §7 | [RF-011](#rf-011-topology-mutation-and-recharting); [Revision actions](#revision-actions); [FOUNDATIONS §2 Frame objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects), Topology, outside this member; [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), the reuse rule, outside this member; [§12](#12-violations) item 11 | each frame's invalidation and rechart conditions: its declaration (J of the frame tuple); the revision actions listed: this member (§10) | 2, 7 |\n"},{"number":168,"text":"| P0 (recovered, with its actor-change premise), P6 (independent), P2 (independent), P3 (independent) | By P0's actor-change premise a frame must work for a fresh actor, and by P6 and P3 that actor receives only declared, bound inputs, so a fresh competent actor inside the declared envelope can reconstruct the activated evaluation from the frame declaration, the exact subject, the basis and the admissible inputs, without undocumented conversational or historical context. An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the workspace from ambient context; it may own its internal reasoning where the governing method permits, returns through the declared result relation, and hidden reasoning substitutes for no required evidence, provenance or authority. Every field of the binding resolves through stable identities and source references, for which paths, line numbers, counts, summaries and matching labels do not substitute | [RF-013](#rf-013-reconstructable-activation); [§11](#11-the-activation-packet); [Minimal activation binding](#minimal-activation-binding) | the packet's minimum contents and the binding's fields: this member; the carrier: its consumer (RF-016) | 7, 9 |\n"},{"number":169,"text":"| P0 (recovered), P5 (derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise), P6 (independent); instance premise a | By P0 an actor's envelope is finite, and by P5 a step cannot report success on what it did not hold, so frame adequacy includes actor usability. When the material manifold exceeds an actor's envelope, the lawful responses are another actor, a refined frame or outer contract, sequenced activations, a lawful compression or `out_of_frame`; silently omitting material relations to fit is never one of them, and a frame never silently grows beyond the selected actor's envelope. Actor capability may justify a different frame size or activation sequence, and can neither waive an invariant nor widen authority | [RF-014](#rf-014-capability-fit); [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) step 3, the responses when the context does not fit, outside this member; [FOUNDATIONS §2 Frame objects](FOUNDATIONS.md#frame-objects), Capability envelope, outside this member; [§11](#11-the-activation-packet), frame size; [§12](#12-violations) item 10 | the selection among these responses: human authority, directly or in advance through the grant; which responses a step selects within its grant (refinement, sequencing, compression) and which re-enter the owner of the grant or envelope (another actor, a larger envelope): ACTIVATION §2 step 3 | 7, 8 |\n"},{"number":170,"text":"| P2 (independent), P0 (recovered), P6 (independent) | By P2 a compression serves the evaluation, and by P0 it must fit the envelope, so a compression preserves the material distinctions and failure detections the evaluation family requires while fitting the envelope; it need not be a unique smallest frame. Intentional overlap is kept where it supplies independently activated evaluation, different capability fit, different evidence altitude or useful fault detection, and frames are merged only when the merged frame preserves evaluation meaning, authority, capability fit and proportional reasoning cost. Whether a compression preserved what the evaluation needs is a claim: the compressing step records the compression and its preservation argument | [RF-017](#rf-017-proportional-compression); [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope) step 3, compression, outside this member; [§12](#12-violations) item 13 | whether that claim is assessed independently: the promotion it serves ([EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment)) | 6, 7 |\n"},{"number":171,"text":"| P0 (recovered, with its open-world premise), P4b (derived from P0 and P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable), P6 (independent) | By P0's open-world premise unknown relations exist, and by P4b and P6 an absence of a counterexample is not evidence, so coverage and evaluation results keep known uncertainty explicit: unresolved relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of completeness. Without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate, a finite frame set cannot establish, by inspecting its own inventory, that no material evaluation is undiscovered; coverage therefore stays falsifiable and states an explicit residual boundary | [RF-015](#rf-015-residual-uncertainty); [§9](#9-completeness-boundary) | a closed-domain completeness predicate, where one is used: the owner of that domain, who establishes it independently | 7, 9 |\n"},{"number":172,"text":"| P2 (independent), P0 (recovered) | By P2 the method requires only what the outcome needs, and by P0 an actor needs the relations, not a carrier, so this member requires the declared relations and the observable outcomes, and no frame runtime, universal carrier, registry, controller, prompt format, repository layout, collaboration topology, worker count or software framework. A frame and the method functions may be realised in any conforming form, and the signatures describe relations, not callable interfaces; the minimal declarations are the least content that declares a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result, in any carrier | [RF-016](#rf-016-implementation-neutrality); [§1](#1-the-frame-as-the-engagement-unit), Substrate; [§5](#5-method-functions), the signatures; [§13](#13-minimal-declarations); [§12](#12-violations) item 14 | the carrier: its consumer; the fields of the three minimal declarations: this member, with the out_of_frame residual field carrying what [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) requires | 7, 8 |\n"},{"number":173,"text":"| P6 (independent), P2 (independent); instance premise b | By P6 human authority may declare what it owns, and by P2 and (b) a declaration serves the outcome from known evidence, so human authority may declare a project frame set from accumulated practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the outcome's risk and knowledge of the available actors, without reconstructing it from the workspace bottom up. The declaration records the governed workspace and outcome, the evaluation inventory, the frames and their envelopes, intentional overlaps, dependencies or translations, the authorities, exclusions and residual uncertainty, and the conditions for revision. Frame-set contraction asks a different\n"},{"number":456,"text":"question: whether two frame declarations support the same evaluation\n"},{"number":457,"text":"relation without material difference in evidence, authority, capability\n"},{"number":458,"text":"fit, evaluation or assurance independence, or failure detection. Frame-set declaration\n"},{"number":463,"text":"\n"},{"number":464,"text":"Human authority may declare an initial project frame set from accumulated\n"},{"number":465,"text":"development practice, known failure modes, domain expertise, the governed\n"},{"number":466,"text":"outcome's risk and knowledge of the available agents and other actors. The\n"},{"number":467,"text":"declaration need not reconstruct the set from the workspace bottom up (P6,\n"},{"number":468,"text":"P2). It records:\n"},{"number":469,"text":"\n"},{"number":470,"text":"- the governed workspace and outcome;\n"},{"number":471,"text":"- the known evaluation inventory;\n"},{"number":472,"text":"- the selected frames and their capability envelopes;\n"},{"number":473,"text":"- intentional overlaps and separately activated checks;\n"},{"number":474,"text":"- known frame dependencies or translations;\n"},{"number":475,"text":"- semantic, evaluation, operation where material, decision and acceptance\n"},{"number":476,"text":"  authority;\n"},{"number":477,"text":"- known exclusions and residual uncertainty; and\n"},{"number":478,"text":"- the conditions for revision.\n"},{"number":479,"text":"\n"},{"number":480,"text":"Human selection is a lawful source of method structure. It proves neither\n"},{"number":481,"text":"that the selected set is complete nor that the frames hold authority over\n"},{"number":482,"text":"the subject relations they inspect (P6; RF-006, RF-015).\n"},{"number":483,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":512,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/4. For the known\n"},{"number":487,"text":"material evaluations E(W, G) of workspace W and governed outcome G, a\n"},{"number":488,"text":"selected frame set S meets the baseline coverage constraint when, for every\n"},{"number":489,"text":"evaluation e in E(W, G), there is a frame F in S and an available actor a\n"},{"number":490,"text":"inside F's capability envelope K_F such that F with a is capable of e (P2,\n"},{"number":491,"text":"P0). Selection also weighs actor context and\n"},{"number":492,"text":"competence; evaluation risk and consequence; acquisition and reasoning\n"},{"number":493,"text":"cost; evidence availability; useful independently activated overlap;\n"},{"number":494,"text":"translation and reconciliation cost; historical blind spots; and\n"},{"number":495,"text":"reversibility when the set proves inadequate. No optimisation algorithm is\n"},{"number":496,"text":"prescribed. Human authority may accept a non-minimal set where its added\n"},{"number":497,"text":"cost buys material risk reduction or better actor fit (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":498,"text":"\n"},{"number":499,"text":"These considerations create no universal resource ledger, benchmark,\n"},{"number":500,"text":"budget or measurement gate: cost is selected, not universal, under\n"},{"number":501,"text":"[ACTIVATION §6](ACTIVATION.md#6-cost-and-proportionality), which owns\n"},{"number":502,"text":"resource limits, and these four are its instances in frame selection. In\n"},{"number":503,"text":"frame selection a resource control applies only through an explicitly\n"},{"number":504,"text":"selected frame and its owning applicability and work scope; ACTIVATION §6\n"},{"number":505,"text":"is that selection where a cost claim is the governed question. The test\n"},{"number":506,"text":"that an activated frame's context fits the selected actor is RF-002's,\n"},{"number":507,"text":"distinct from the actor context that selection weighs, and\n"},{"number":508,"text":"[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)\n"},{"number":509,"text":"owns its measurement and when the measurement applies. Frame selection\n"},{"number":510,"text":"cannot waive another applicable semantic, authority, evidence or\n"},{"number":511,"text":"independence constraint (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":512,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":596,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/5. Method functions","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md#REFERENCE_FRAME%2F5.%20Method%20functions","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md","sha256":"15a806416fe59148b7c514193eb913d324b85d59407f6f164d5b7866c6218e34","start_line":513,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md","lines":[{"number":513,"text":"## 5. Method functions\n"},{"number":514,"text":"\n"},{"number":515,"text":"The frame and the functions over it remain distinct. An application may\n"},{"number":516,"text":"realise the following relations in any conforming form; the signatures\n"},{"number":517,"text":"describe relations, not callable software interfaces (P2; RF-016):\n"},{"number":518,"text":"\n"},{"number":519,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":520,"text":"declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities)\n"},{"number":521,"text":"  -> frame_set\n"},{"number":522,"text":"\n"},{"number":523,"text":"activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor)\n"},{"number":524,"text":"  -> activated_frame | activation_refusal\n"},{"number":525,"text":"\n"},{"number":526,"text":"evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence)\n"},{"number":527,"text":"  -> result + evidence + residuals\n"},{"number":528,"text":"\n"},{"number":529,"text":"conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results)\n"},{"number":530,"text":"  -> decision | conflict | indeterminate\n"},{"number":531,"text":"\n"},{"number":532,"text":"translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping)\n"},{"number":533,"text":"  -> translated_value | declared_loss | refusal\n"},{"number":534,"text":"\n"},{"number":535,"text":"audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set)\n"},{"number":536,"text":"  -> coverage_ledger\n"},{"number":537,"text":"\n"},{"number":538,"text":"revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change)\n"},{"number":539,"text":"  -> proposed_frame_set_delta\n"},{"number":540,"text":"```\n"},{"number":541,"text":"\n"},{"number":542,"text":"`declare` is §4; `activate` and `evaluate` are ACTIVATION §1 and §2;\n"},{"number":543,"text":"`evaluate` returns its result under RF-012, and the closed result is\n"},{"number":544,"text":"returned and reused under ACTIVATION §7; `conjoin` and `translate` are §6;\n"},{"number":545,"text":"`audit_coverage` is §8, which maps the statuses of its ledger to the core;\n"},{"number":546,"text":"`revise` is §10. EVALUATION §7 qualifies each.\n"},{"number":547,"text":"\n"},{"number":548,"text":"The outcomes of `activate`, `conjoin` and `translate` form a refinement of\n"},{"number":549,"text":"the core algebra, stated under the refinement rule of\n"},{"number":550,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): each outcome below maps\n"},{"number":551,"text":"to exactly one core value for the predicate its function names, the value\n"},{"number":552,"text":"travels with that predicate and with the outcome, whose meaning stays here,\n"},{"number":553,"text":"and an outcome named in the signatures above that would map to more than\n"},{"number":554,"text":"one core value according to its cause carries the cause in its name, as in\n"},{"number":555,"text":"`activation_refusal(basis)` (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: a consumer that combines these\n"},{"number":556,"text":"outcomes with other results reads them in the one core, so a refusal, a\n"},{"number":557,"text":"conflict or a loss outside the accepted loss is neither mistaken for\n"},{"number":558,"text":"success nor merged with an evaluation that was not performed.\n"},{"number":559,"text":"\n"},{"number":560,"text":"| Function and predicate | Outcome | Cause | Core value |\n"},{"number":561,"text":"|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":562,"text":"| `activate`: the frame is activated for this evaluation, subject, basis and actor | `activated_frame` | the frame declaration is bound to the exact evaluation, subject, basis and actor | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":563,"text":"| | `activation_refusal(capability)` | the frame declares a capability the evaluation needs, and the selected actor's declared envelope lacks it; the refusal names that capability and its owner where the subject gives one | `out_of_frame` |\n"},{"number":564,"text":"| | `activation_refusal(authority)` | the activation needs semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority that is not admitted to it; the refusal names that authority's owner | `out_of_frame` |\n"},{"number":565,"text":"| | `activation_refusal(basis)` | the subject or basis is stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched (RF-005), a topology mismatch included: the subject's topology is not the topology basis the frame declares (RF-011) | `invalid_basis` |\n"},{"number":566,"text":"| `conjoin`: the composite predicate holds under the declared decision rule | `decision(holds)` | the conjunction of FOUNDATIONS §4 reports `satisfied` | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":567,"text":"| | `decision(fails)` | the conjunction reports `falsified`, and no mandatory result for the same claim is `satisfied` | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":568,"text":"| | `conflict` | the conjunction reports `falsified` while mandatory results for the same claim disagree, one `satisfied` and another `falsified`; the counterexample survives the join, and the disagreement stays unresolved for the decision authority | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":569,"text":"| | `indeterminate` | the conjunction reports `indeterminate` | `indeterminate` |\n"},{"number":570,"text":"| `translate`: the value or evidence enters the target frame as the declared translation states | `translated_value` | the value or evidence is carried into the target coordinates with its declared meaning | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":571,"text":"| | `declared_loss` | the value or evidence is carried with a loss inside the declared accepted loss; the loss travels with it as a residual (P4b) | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":572,"text":"| | `refusal(condition)` | a refusal condition the translation declares holds, a loss outside the accepted loss included; or the value or evidence fails identity or equality under the translation's declared equality law | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":573,"text":"| | `refusal(authority)` | an authority mismatch the translation does not declare: the value or evidence carries semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority whose relation to the target frame's authority the translation states neither as preserved nor as a refusal condition; the refusal names that authority's owner | `out_of_frame` |\n"},{"number":574,"text":"| | `refusal(basis)` | the source value or evidence binds a stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis or coordinate (RF-005) | `invalid_basis` |\n"},{"number":575,"text":"\n"},{"number":576,"text":"Where no frame the actor can use declares a material relation or\n"},{"number":577,"text":"capability the evaluation needs, `activate` returns `out_of_frame` itself\n"},{"number":578,"text":"([ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),\n"},{"number":579,"text":"Activation). Where the conjunction reports `out_of_frame` or\n"},{"number":580,"text":"`invalid_basis`, `conjoin` returns that value; the signatures name no\n"},{"number":581,"text":"outcome for either case, and a basis mismatch is this returned\n"},{"number":582,"text":"`invalid_basis`, as EVALUATION §7 names it for `conjoin`. Under a\n"},{"number":583,"text":"declared veto or deferral, `conjoin` returns the outcome above whose cause\n"},{"number":584,"text":"holds for the value the conjunction reports\n"},{"number":585,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)), or that value\n"},{"number":586,"text":"itself where it is `out_of_frame` or `invalid_basis`. A planned\n"},{"number":587,"text":"assessment without a closed result, and required coverage that no planned\n"},{"number":588,"text":"assessment addresses, are no outcome of `conjoin`:\n"},{"number":589,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results) records them\n"},{"number":590,"text":"beside the reported value, and they map to no core value. The outcomes of\n"},{"number":591,"text":"`activate` answer whether a frame was activated, never the\n"},{"number":592,"text":"evaluation's claim: a refused activation performs no evaluation.\n"},{"number":593,"text":"`decision(holds)` assesses the composite predicate and is not its\n"},{"number":594,"text":"acceptance, which is a separate result\n"},{"number":595,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)).\n"},{"number":596,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":601,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/6. Frame relations\n"},{"number":645,"text":"\n"},{"number":646,"text":"Frames may relate as:\n"},{"number":647,"text":"\n"},{"number":648,"text":"- disjoint: no material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency\n"},{"number":649,"text":"  is shared for the declared evaluations;\n"},{"number":650,"text":"- overlapping: some material variables, evidence or entities are shared;\n"},{"number":651,"text":"- complementary: distinct evaluations jointly inform one decision;\n"},{"number":652,"text":"- alternative: different frames can evaluate the same claim under declared\n"},{"number":653,"text":"  capability or evidence conditions;\n"},{"number":654,"text":"- refinement: one frame resolves a material distinction left aggregated in\n"},{"number":655,"text":"  another;\n"},{"number":656,"text":"- restriction: one frame evaluates a lawful subset of another frame's\n"},{"number":657,"text":"  domain;\n"},{"number":658,"text":"- translated: values or evidence move through a declared coordinate map;\n"},{"number":659,"text":"- temporally successive: a later frame evaluates a changed basis;\n"},{"number":660,"text":"- composed: several frame relations form one governed evaluation or\n"},{"number":661,"text":"  action; or\n"},{"number":662,"text":"- governing and subordinate: one frame inherits declared constraints from\n"},{"number":663,"text":"  another where a real authority or decomposition relation exists.\n"},{"number":664,"text":"\n"},{"number":665,"text":"No relation is the default universal frame topology.
