otherwise none |\n"},{"number":722,"text":"| decision authority | the owner of the disposition |\n"},{"number":723,"text":"| evidence | the required observations and their provenance |\n"},{"number":724,"text":"| dependencies | material frame or seam relations |\n"},{"number":725,"text":"| status | the coverage disposition |\n"},{"number":726,"text":"| residual | uncertainty, exclusion or re-entry condition |\n"},{"number":727,"text":"\n"},{"number":728,"text":"The baseline coverage statuses are `covered`, `separately_covered`,\n"},{"number":729,"text":"`conditionally_covered`, `conflicted`, `uncovered`, `unknown` and\n"},{"number":730,"text":"`excluded_by_authority`.\n"},{"number":731,"text":"\n"},{"number":732,"text":"The statuses form a refinement of the core, stated under the refinement\n"},{"number":733,"text":"rule of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). They answer\n"},{"number":734,"text":"whether a row's coverage obligation is met, for the predicate \"on the\n"},{"number":735,"text":"declared coverage tuple, a capable frame of S covers the evaluation with\n"},{"number":736,"text":"no unresolved conflict among the frames, results or authorities that\n"},{"number":737,"text":"cover it, or a governing authority the row cites excludes it\". Each status\n"},{"number":738,"text":"maps to exactly one core value, and the value travels with that predicate\n"},{"number":739,"text":"and with the status, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6):\n"},{"number":740,"text":"\n"},{"number":741,"text":"| Status | Cause | Core value |\n"},{"number":742,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":743,"text":"| `covered` | a capable frame of S evaluates it on the tuple, with no unresolved conflict among what covers it | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":744,"text":"| `separately_covered` | separately activated frames of S each evaluate it on the tuple, with no unresolved conflict among them (High-risk separately activated coverage) | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":745,"text":"| `excluded_by_authority` | the governing authority the row cites excludes the evaluation from the claim (Operational full coverage, item 7) | `satisfied` |\n"},{"number":746,"text":"| `conditionally_covered` | a capable frame of S covers it only under a condition the audit has not established; the residual names the condition and the evidence that would decide it | `indeterminate` |\n"},{"number":747,"text":"| `conflicted` | the frames, results or authorities that cover it conflict, and the conflict is unresolved; the conflict is the counterexample and stays unresolved for the decision authority (Operational full coverage, item 6) | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":748,"text":"| `uncovered` | no capable frame of S evaluates it, and no cited authority excludes it; that absence is the counterexample | `falsified` |\n"},{"number":749,"text":"| `unknown` | the admissible evidence cannot decide whether a capable frame of S covers it, as where the actor capability or the materiality is unknown | `indeterminate` |\n"},{"number":750,"text":"\n"},{"number":751,"text":"These values are results of `audit_coverage` for this predicate, never\n"},{"number":752,"text":"results of the covered evaluation itself. `satisfied` for an excluded row\n"},{"number":753,"text":"establishes that the obligation is met by the cited exclusion, never that\n"},{"number":754,"text":"the evaluation is covered or was performed; the status keeps that\n"},{"number":755,"text":"distinction (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Recording). In a conjunction over the\n"},{"number":756,"text":"governed claim, an evaluation whose row is `uncovered` is required\n"},{"number":757,"text":"coverage that no planned assessment addresses\n"},{"number":758,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)), never a\n"},{"number":759,"text":"`falsified` component. Where the coverage tuple itself is stale, advanced,\n"},{"number":760,"text":"ambiguous or mismatched, the audit returns `invalid_basis` (RF-005) and\n"},{"number":761,"text":"assigns no status. Purpose and material\n"},{"number":762,"text":"relation: a coverage claim combined with other results is read in the one\n"},{"number":763,"text":"core, so a conditional, conflicted, unknown or uncovered row is never read\n"},{"number":764,"text":"as covered, and a cited exclusion is never read as a failure (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":765,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":772,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/8. and\n"},{"number":814,"text":"8. uncovered and unknown residuals are explicit and compatible with the\n"},{"number":815,"text":"   claim.\n"},{"number":816,"text":"\n"},{"number":817,"text":"Operational full coverage is relative to its tuple. Completeness boundary\n"},{"number":821,"text":"\n"},{"number":822,"text":"Without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate,\n"},{"number":823,"text":"a finite frame set cannot establish the absence of every undiscovered\n"},{"number":824,"text":"material evaluation by inspecting its own declared inventory. A finite,\n"},{"number":825,"text":"formally closed domain may support exhaustive coverage relative to that\n"},{"number":826,"text":"domain and its completeness predicate; the result does not generalise\n"},{"number":827,"text":"beyond that boundary. Formal incompleteness results motivate this caution;\n"},{"number":828,"text":"they do not by themselves prove that a particular workspace or frame set is\n"},{"number":829,"text":"incomplete (P0 with the open-world premise; P6).\n"},{"number":830,"text":"\n"},{"number":831,"text":"Coverage therefore stays falsifiable and externally challengeable.\n"},{"number":832,"text":"Challenge sources include human knowledge outside the current frame set;\n"},{"number":833,"text":"independent review; historical failures and predecessor systems; mutation,\n"},{"number":834,"text":"adversarial and counterexample search; live operation and user behaviour;\n"},{"number":835,"text":"adjacent workspace or domain comparison; and changes in actor capability,\n"},{"number":836,"text":"law, dependencies or topology. The method requires an explicit residual\n"},{"number":837,"text":"boundary and never a claim of metaphysical or universal completeness\n"},{"number":838,"text":"(RF-015).\n"},{"number":839,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":841,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/10. Discovery and revision/Diagnostic order","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md#REFERENCE_FRAME%2F10.%20Discovery%20and%20revision%2FDiagnostic%20order","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md","sha256":"071c611a8562d120f20590cac634848e7d2191716308893b06560874b7b8c749","start_line":858,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME.md","lines":[{"number":858,"text":"### Diagnostic order\n"},{"number":859,"text":"\n"},{"number":860,"text":"Diagnosis asks, in this order (P2):\n"},{"number":861,"text":"\n"},{"number":862,"text":"1. Was the correct declared frame activated?\n"},{"number":863,"text":"2. Were the subject and basis exact?\n"},{"number":864,"text":"3. Was the actor inside the capability envelope?\n"},{"number":865,"text":"4. Was admissible evidence available?\n"},{"number":866,"text":"5. Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame?\n"},{"number":867,"text":"6. Is a required conjunction or translation missing?\n"},{"number":868,"text":"7. Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete?\n"},{"number":869,"text":"8. Is another frame required?\n"},{"number":870,"text":"\n"},{"number":871,"text":"Question 1 is answered by family inclusion, not by set membership. An\n"},{"number":872,"text":"evaluation is within a frame's family when the question it decides is one\n"},{"number":873,"text":"the frame's declared evaluation family states, at the frame's declared\n"},{"number":874,"text":"coordinates (RF-001). Membership of the frame in the frame set, the frame's\n"},{"number":875,"text":"name, a role label or similar wording of the question does not place an\n"},{"number":876,"text":"evaluation in the frame's family; an activation of a frame on an evaluation\n"},{"number":877,"text":"outside its family answers question 1 no, whatever the frame's standing in\n"},{"number":878,"text":"the set (P2, the evaluations determine the attention surface; P1, a name\n"},{"number":879,"text":"carries no meaning; the material relation drawn is evaluation-to-family\n"},{"number":880,"text":"inclusion).\n"},{"number":881,"text":"\n"},{"number":882,"text":"The order prevents every difficult evaluation from creating another frame.\n"},{"number":883,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":932,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/10. Every\n"},{"number":892,"text":"material revision changes frame identity or revision coordinates and states\n"},{"number":893,"text":"which prior activations, results and coverage claims require reevaluation\n"},{"number":894,"text":"(P3, P4b).\n"},{"number":895,"text":"\n"},{"number":896,"text":"Stated plainly: a material revision of a frame produces a new frame\n"},{"number":897,"text":"revision coordinate. Every prior closed result bound to the previous\n"},{"number":898,"text":"revision of a materially revised frame is bound to a mismatched coordinate\n"},{"number":899,"text":"(RF-005) and is invalidated for reuse until it is re-checked against the\n"},{"number":900,"text":"new revision (RF-011; ACTIVATION §7). The revision record lists those\n"},{"number":901,"text":"results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check\n"},{"number":902,"text":"that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation\n"},{"number":903,"text":"on the new revision. A material revision does not select which of the\n"},{"number":904,"text":"results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep\n"},{"number":905,"text":"a result closed (P3, P4b).\n"},{"number":906,"text":"\n"},{"number":907,"text":"Whether a revision needs a new frame revision coordinate turns on the\n"},{"number":908,"text":"frame's declarations; whether a result already closed stays valid is a\n"},{"number":909,"text":"separate question. A revision is material when it changes a frame\n"},{"number":910,"text":"declaration in a way that is material under\n"},{"number":911,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology). A revision that changes no\n"},{"number":912,"text":"declaration of the frame needs no new coordinate. That answer decides\n"},{"number":913,"text":"nothing about any result: an unchanged declaration is no ground for\n"},{"number":914,"text":"keeping a result closed. Whether a closed result stays valid is decided\n"},{"number":915,"text":"by the reuse rule of\n"},{"number":916,"text":"[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), with materiality\n"},{"number":917,"text":"as [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology) defines it, and that rule\n"},{"number":918,"text":"can reopen results although no declaration changed; results it reopens\n"},{"number":919,"text":"without a material revision are recorded as reopened in the work state\n"},{"number":920,"text":"([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart)). For example, a\n"},{"number":921,"text":"clarification that finds a recorded activation outside its frame's family,\n"},{"number":922,"text":"so that the result fails the exact applicability check of ACTIVATION §7\n"},{"number":923,"text":"([RF-001](#rf-001-evaluation-relativity);\n"},{"number":924,"text":"[Diagnostic order](#diagnostic-order) question 1), or newly acquired\n"},{"number":925,"text":"admissible evidence that is material to a closed result, a material\n"},{"number":926,"text":"input change under ACTIVATION §7, reopens that result\n"},{"number":927,"text":"and every coverage ledger row and coverage claim that consumed it, and\n"},{"number":928,"text":"preserves every demonstrably independent surviving result. A harmless\n"},{"number":929,"text":"explanatory clarification, which changes no material input and is no\n"},{"number":930,"text":"revising observation, invalidates no result by itself;\n"},{"number":931,"text":"reuse still requires the consumer's exact applicability check (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":932,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":959,"heading":"REFERENCE_FRAME/11. The activation packet\n"},{"number":934,"text":"\n"},{"number":935,"text":"An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame\n"},{"number":936,"text":"configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete\n"},{"number":937,"text":"workspace from ambient context (P0). The minimum\n"},{"number":938,"text":"activation packet contains:\n"},{"number":939,"text":"\n"},{"number":940,"text":"- frame identity and revision;\n"},{"number":941,"text":"- the evaluation and its result algebra;\n"},{"number":942,"text":"- the exact subject and basis;\n"},{"number":943,"text":"- the material relations and applicable invariants;\n"},{"number":944,"text":"- semantic, evaluation, operation where material, and decision authority;\n"},{"number":945,"text":"- admissible evidence and tools;\n"},{"number":946,"text":"- the capability and context envelope;\n"},{"number":947,"text":"- exclusions and prohibited assumptions;\n"},{"number":948,"text":"- declared frame dependencies or conjunction outputs; and\n"},{"number":949,"text":"- invalidation, stop and reconfiguration conditions.\n"},{"number":950,"text":"\n"},{"number":951,"text":"The actor may own its internal reasoning and search where the governing\n"},{"number":952,"text":"method permits. It returns through the declared result relation. Hidden\n"},{"number":953,"text":"internal reasoning is no substitute for required evidence, provenance or\n"},{"number":954,"text":"authority (P6). The RC suffix does not\n"},{"number":55,"text":"make a published release provisional or require a second final cut. The\n"},{"number":56,"text":"stable profile is an explicit naming and discovery choice, not stronger\n"},{"number":57,"text":"semantic qualification. Release identities\n"},{"number":145,"text":"\n"},{"number":146,"text":"The release-publication context distinguishes (P3):\n"},{"number":147,"text":"\n"},{"number":148,"text":"- Project Release Namespace: a stable repository-local key assigned by\n"},{"number":149,"text":"  the Product release authority to one independently released source\n"},{"number":150,"text":"  project;\n"},{"number":151,"text":"- Project Subtree: the exact repository-relative source-project root and\n"},{"number":152,"text":"  Git tree object selected for one cut;\n"},{"number":153,"text":"- Candidate Source: the candidate source of FOUNDATIONS §2, the mutable\n"},{"number":154,"text":"  source-project state constructing a possible successor;\n"},{"number":155,"text":"- RC Branch: a mutable project-qualified carrier for the current\n"},{"number":156,"text":"  candidate window;\n"},{"number":157,"text":"- Immutable Release Cut: an annotated project-qualified Git tag plus its\n"},{"number":158,"text":"  exact Product release subject (FOUNDATIONS §2), under the selected RC or\n"},{"number":159,"text":"  stable profile; publication, qualification and acceptance retain their\n"},{"number":160,"text":"  respective meanings; it realises the release cut;\n"},{"number":161,"text":"- Version-Line Selector: the mutable project-qualified tag alias naming\n"},{"number":162,"text":"  the highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut for that project and\n"},{"number":163,"text":"  version line; it realises the version-line selector of FOUNDATIONS §2;\n"},{"number":164,"text":"  and\n"},{"number":165,"text":"- Release Branch: an optional mutable project-qualified convenience\n"},{"number":166,"text":"  carrier aligned to the same latest-published commit as the selector.\n"},{"number":167,"text":"\n"},{"number":168,"text":"Equal version text does not collapse these identities. Branches and the\n"},{"number":169,"text":"version-line selector may move. An immutable release tag never moves (P3).\n"},{"number":170,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":205,"heading":"RELEASE/2. It matches\n"},{"number":174,"text":"`[a-z0-9]+(?:[-_][a-z0-9]+)*`, contains no slash, is unique within the\n"},{"number":175,"text":"release source, and remains stable for the continuing release line. It is\n"},{"number":176,"text":"assigned by the Product release authority. A directory name, display name,\n"},{"number":177,"text":"definition label, package name or matching version cannot infer or\n"},{"number":178,"text":"reassign it (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":179,"text":"\n"},{"number":180,"text":"A shared release source uses these exact ref shapes for an RC-profile\n"},{"number":181,"text":"publication (P3):\n"},{"number":182,"text":"\n"},{"number":183,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":184,"text":"RC branch:              refs/heads/rc/<project>/<version>\n"},{"number":185,"text":"immutable RC cut tag:   refs/tags/<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>\n"},{"number":186,"text":"version-line selector:  refs/tags/<project>/v<version>\n"},{"number":187,"text":"release branch:         refs/heads/release/<project>/<version>\n"},{"number":188,"text":"```\n"},{"number":189,"text":"\n"},{"number":190,"text":"The short Git tag names are therefore `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` and\n"},{"number":191,"text":"`<project>/v<version>`. A shared release source does not publish a future\n"},{"number":192,"text":"cut or selector under the unqualified `v<version>-rc.<n>` or `v<version>`\n"},{"number":193,"text":"refs (P3).\n"},{"number":194,"text":"\n"},{"number":195,"text":"A single-project release source may retain the unqualified ref profile\n"},{"number":196,"text":"only while it has exactly one independently released project and its\n"},{"number":197,"text":"release record declares that profile. Each numeric component is a\n"},{"number":210,"text":"nonnegative decimal integer, with no leading zero except the single digit\n"},{"number":211,"text":"`0`. The tag is annotated, targets a commit and contains exactly one\n"},{"number":212,"text":"standalone annotation line (P3):\n"},{"number":213,"text":"\n"},{"number":214,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":215,"text":"STDO-Release-Profile: stable-v1\n"},{"number":216,"text":"```\n"},{"number":217,"text":"\n"},{"number":218,"text":"Its exact release declaration names the same stable cut, declared payload,\n"},{"number":219,"text":"source selection and predecessor. The installed manifest records\n"},{"number":220,"text":"`release.profile = \"stable-v1\"` alongside the complete identity of\n"},{"number":221,"text":"[Project-subtree release identity](#project-subtree-release-identity).\n"},{"number":222,"text":"An RC manifest retains its prior shape; adding stable support must not\n"},{"number":223,"text":"change the canonical bytes of a historical release manifest (P3, P4b).\n"},{"number":224,"text":"\n"},{"number":225,"text":"The stable coordinate is available only on a fresh version line with no\n"},{"number":226,"text":"same-version RC tag in either the historical or project-qualified namespace\n"},{"number":227,"text":"and no historical unqualified bare-version tag. The stable tag itself is\n"},{"number":228,"text":"create-only. A same-line collision or a missing, duplicated or different\n"},{"number":229,"text":"profile marker refuses stable acquisition; bare spelling or annotation alone\n"},{"number":230,"text":"cannot turn an RC selector into an immutable cut (P3, P5).\n"},{"number":231,"text":"\n"},{"number":232,"text":"There is no separate version-line selector or RC branch for this profile.\n"},{"number":233,"text":"A channel `stdo://channels/<major>.<minor>.<patch>` may discover that exact\n"},{"number":234,"text":"immutable stable tag; its cut ordinal is absent (`null`), and resolution\n"},{"number":235,"text":"must verify the stable profile and complete identity. That channel route\n"},{"number":236,"text":"creates neither another tag nor mutable alias semantics. Consumer adoption\n"},{"number":237,"text":"still follows §4 (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":238,"text":"\n"},{"number":239,"text":"A published stable tag never moves. Any change to its qualifying bytes\n"},{"number":240,"text":"requires a new version and a new immutable cut, not an RC added to the\n"},{"number":241,"text":"already stable line. Historical RC lines keep their selector semantics,\n"},{"number":242,"text":"refs, objects, peels and URIs; this profile neither finalises nor renames\n"},{"number":243,"text":"them. An RC-labelled published release remains a proper release (P3, P4b).\n"},{"number":244,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":273,"heading":"RELEASE/2. Release identities/Project-subtree release identity","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F2.%20Release%20identities%2FProject-subtree%20release%20identity","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"f28866be30e87306bf8da20f8d94b1ddde636db0c39a96fe598529b97294bad3","start_line":245,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":245,"text":"### Project-subtree release identity\n"},{"number":246,"text":"\n"},{"number":247,"text":"In a shared release source, an immutable cut binds all of (P3):\n"},{"number":248,"text":"\n"},{"number":249,"text":"- the Project Release Namespace and owning Product authority;\n"},{"number":250,"text":"- the exact qualified Git ref and annotated tag object;\n"},{"number":251,"text":"- the peeled commit and repository-root tree;\n"},{"number":252,"text":"- the normalised repository-relative Project Subtree root at that commit;\n"},{"number":253,"text":"- the Git tree object at that exact Project Subtree root;\n"},{"number":254,"text":"- the declared Product member inventory and release-scoped claim bytes;\n"},{"number":255,"text":"  and\n"},{"number":256,"text":"- the predecessor and successor dispositions required by §9.\n"},{"number":257,"text":"\n"},{"number":258,"text":"The Project Subtree root is a locator inside the exact peeled commit, not\n"},{"number":259,"text":"Product identity. Its canonical spelling is the slash-separated Git path\n"},{"number":260,"text":"from the repository root, with no leading or trailing slash and no empty,\n"},{"number":261,"text":"`.` or `..` component; `.` alone denotes the repository root. Each\n"},{"number":262,"text":"non-root component names the exact tree entry bytes traversed at that\n"},{"number":263,"text":"commit. Moving a source project changes this locator and its cut identity\n"},{"number":264,"text":"without reassigning the Project Release Namespace. If the source project\n"},{"number":265,"text":"occupies the repository root, its project-subtree tree equals the\n"},{"number":266,"text":"repository-root tree (P3).\n"},{"number":267,"text":"\n"},{"number":268,"text":"A tag over a monorepo commit does not make sibling subtrees Product\n"},{"number":269,"text":"members. Unrelated sibling bytes remain carrier state outside the declared\n"},{"number":270,"text":"Product subject. Conversely, a member inventory or payload digest without\n"},{"number":271,"text":"the qualified ref, commit, Project Subtree root and Project Subtree tree is\n"},{"number":272,"text":"not a complete reacquirable release identity (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":273,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":298,"heading":"RELEASE/2. Release identities/Historical ref and public-URI conservation","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F2.%20Release%20identities%2FHistorical%20ref%20and%20public-URI%20conservation","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"1e3df791d7fb6f3ee842114e3a889c8405770bdd58b121a388a967699d88906c","start_line":274,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":274,"text":"### Historical ref and public-URI conservation\n"},{"number":275,"text":"\n"},{"number":276,"text":"Project qualification is prospective. Existing unqualified refs retain\n"},{"number":277,"text":"their names, objects, peels and public links. A historical tag object may\n"},{"number":278,"text":"remain reachable through an additional archival ref, but it is not\n"},{"number":279,"text":"recreated, re-annotated, moved or replaced. An immutable historical tag\n"},{"number":280,"text":"remains the same object regardless of which preserving ref reaches it\n"},{"number":281,"text":"(P3, P4b).\n"},{"number":282,"text":"\n"},{"number":283,"text":"Product-local cut names and public logical release URIs also remain\n"},{"number":284,"text":"unchanged. An RC logical STDO release remains\n"},{"number":285,"text":"`stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/`; a stable release uses\n"},{"number":286,"text":"`stdo://releases/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>/`. The project-qualified Git ref is\n"},{"number":287,"text":"transport identity and is not inserted into that URI. Resolution binds\n"},{"number":288,"text":"the public logical cut to its exact historical or project-qualified Git\n"},{"number":289,"text":"ref and fails closed if one project-local coordinate names different tag\n"},{"number":290,"text":"objects (P3, P5).\n"},{"number":291,"text":"\n"},{"number":292,"text":"When one version line spans the transition, latest means the greatest\n"},{"number":293,"text":"positive RC ordinal across that project's preserved historical cuts and\n"},{"number":294,"text":"its qualified future cuts. The first qualified publication creates the\n"},{"number":295,"text":"qualified selector. The historical unqualified selector is preserved at\n"},{"number":296,"text":"its existing object and ceases to be the current selector for the shared\n"},{"number":297,"text":"source; it is not force-moved to imitate the qualified namespace (P3).\n"},{"number":298,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":314,"heading":"RELEASE/3. Phases\n"},{"number":300,"text":"\n"},{"number":301,"text":"The release process has three phases (P0, P3, P6):\n"},{"number":302,"text":"\n"},{"number":303,"text":"1. mutable candidate construction;\n"},{"number":304,"text":"2. immutable publication under the selected profile, with RC selector\n"},{"number":305,"text":"   advancement only for an RC line; and\n"},{"number":306,"text":"3. exact-cut qualification, acceptance and explicit consumer adoption.\n"},{"number":307,"text":"\n"},{"number":308,"text":"An accepted RC needs no second final cut. RC publication immediately makes\n"},{"number":309,"text":"the new highest ordinal discoverable through its selector. Stable publication\n"},{"number":310,"text":"makes its one exact tag discoverable under the stable profile. Acceptance is\n"},{"number":311,"text":"a verdict over the exact immutable subject, not a second carrier. A change\n"},{"number":312,"text":"to qualifying bytes requires a higher RC on an applicable RC line or a new\n"},{"number":313,"text":"version after a stable cut (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":314,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":329,"heading":"RELEASE/3. Phases/Mutable candidate construction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FMutable%20candidate%20construction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"4e9daeb436bb684ef3f7b321e20f5cb9f3f2aaa58b22e6f078e6fdc9f3570724","start_line":315,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":315,"text":"### Mutable candidate construction\n"},{"number":316,"text":"\n"},{"number":317,"text":"During candidate construction (P0, P6):\n"},{"number":318,"text":"\n"},{"number":319,"text":"- bounded fixes are allowed after intake triage;\n"},{"number":320,"text":"- qualification and operator review may continue;\n"},{"number":321,"text":"- release notes may remain draft until publication;\n"},{"number":322,"text":"- the candidate branch may move; and\n"},{"number":323,"text":"- mutable source is explicitly non-operative for released consumers.\n"},{"number":324,"text":"\n"},{"number":325,"text":"The intended Product boundary, release-scoped claims, excluded\n"},{"number":326,"text":"source-project state and qualification basis become explicit before\n"},{"number":327,"text":"publication. A material scope change is repriced instead of being silently\n"},{"number":328,"text":"absorbed (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":329,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":360,"heading":"RELEASE/3. Phases/Immutable RC publication","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FImmutable%20RC%20publication","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"35653af8ad5ffddbefc4c174d5643ea92cf822672fb1dea88b5534880b80c7a1","start_line":330,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":330,"text":"### Immutable RC publication\n"},{"number":331,"text":"\n"},{"number":332,"text":"A published RC cut exists to provide one exact subject for review, replay\n"},{"number":333,"text":"and possible acceptance. To publish it, the project (P3, P5, P6):\n"},{"number":334,"text":"\n"},{"number":335,"text":"1. confirms the triaged scope and lawful constitutional re-entry;\n"},{"number":336,"text":"2. declares the exact Product release subject and release-scoped claim\n"},{"number":337,"text":"   set;\n"},{"number":338,"text":"3. reconciles the release note and other release-facing assets to that\n"},{"number":339,"text":"   subject;\n"},{"number":340,"text":"4. runs the proportionate pre-RC qualification and operator checks;\n"},{"number":341,"text":"5. commits the exact carrier;\n"},{"number":342,"text":"6. resolves and records the exact Project Release Namespace, Project\n"},{"number":343,"text":"   Subtree root and Project Subtree tree;\n"},{"number":344,"text":"7. creates one annotated immutable `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>` tag and\n"},{"number":345,"text":"   an annotated `<project>/v<version>` selector tag over that same commit\n"},{"number":346,"text":"   in a shared release source;\n"},{"number":347,"text":"8. atomically pushes the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector\n"},{"number":348,"text":"   and optional release branch where the transport supports it;\n"},{"number":349,"text":"9. verifies remotely that the immutable tag, selector and release branch\n"},{"number":350,"text":"   resolve to the highest published RC commit; and\n"},{"number":351,"text":"10. records enough ref, subtree, identity and inventory evidence to\n"},{"number":352,"text":"    reacquire the cut without trusting a mutable checkout.\n"},{"number":353,"text":"\n"},{"number":354,"text":"Each published RC tag is immutable. Further work increments `<n>` on the\n"},{"number":355,"text":"same version line when the intended line remains applicable. It does not\n"},{"number":356,"text":"require a minor-version increment merely because review found a bounded\n"},{"number":357,"text":"repair. A published higher RC without matching selector advancement is an\n"},{"number":358,"text":"invalid, fail-closed release state; it never authorises resolution of the\n"},{"number":359,"text":"older cut as the version-line latest (P3, P5).\n"},{"number":360,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":374,"heading":"RELEASE/3. Phases/Immutable stable publication","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FImmutable%20stable%20publication","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"a87c511d4f35f9889f99a8b4c26cad0e8dc014c3d0c9121c4a80c3bdb0f06e97","start_line":361,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":361,"text":"### Immutable stable publication\n"},{"number":362,"text":"\n"},{"number":363,"text":"Stable publication applies the same scope, source reconciliation, proportionate\n"},{"number":364,"text":"checks, exact carrier, subtree and inventory obligations as RC publication.\n"},{"number":365,"text":"It instead creates one stable-v1 annotated tag and any explicitly selected\n"},{"number":366,"text":"release branch, with no RC branch or separate selector. Before publication,\n"},{"number":367,"text":"verify the fresh-line conditions of [Stable cuts](#stable-cuts), bind remote\n"},{"number":368,"text":"absence for the immutable tag and bind every mutable destination's expected\n"},{"number":369,"text":"object. Publish the selected refs atomically where supported; a changed\n"},{"number":370,"text":"expectation stops publication for reconciliation. Read back the remote tag\n"},{"number":371,"text":"object, commit, subtree and declared assets. The release is publicly classified\n"},{"number":372,"text":"as a normal published release; release-host flags do not replace exact identity\n"},{"number":373,"text":"or qualification evidence (P3, P5, P6).\n"},{"number":374,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":398,"heading":"RELEASE/3. Phases/Exact-cut qualification","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FExact-cut%20qualification","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"69ecedd29f1850b08e8c1bf984d9f38246cefdf73d9a84bfeb98b546adda869f","start_line":375,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":375,"text":"### Exact-cut qualification\n"},{"number":376,"text":"\n"},{"number":377,"text":"Qualification binds (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":378,"text":"\n"},{"number":379,"text":"- the Project Release Namespace, qualified immutable release ref, annotated tag\n"},{"number":380,"text":"  object, peeled commit, repository tree, Project Subtree root and tree,\n"},{"number":381,"text":"  and declared Product member set;\n"},{"number":382,"text":"- the exact release-scoped claim bytes;\n"},{"number":383,"text":"- the governing Product and release basis;\n"},{"number":384,"text":"- each claimed property and its observation boundary;\n"},{"number":385,"text":"- evidence subjects, owner verdicts and unresolved gaps; and\n"},{"number":386,"text":"- the complete successor relation to the declared predecessor (§9).\n"},{"number":387,"text":"\n"},{"number":388,"text":"Evidence matches the claim. Source success does not prove packaged or\n"},{"number":389,"text":"installed behaviour; packaging equivalence does not prove semantic\n"},{"number":390,"text":"behaviour; artifact presence does not prove usability unless presence is\n"},{"number":391,"text":"the exact claim (P6, P1; EVALUATION §1 is the generic claim law).\n"},{"number":392,"text":"\n"},{"number":393,"text":"A cut is accepted only when the required exact-cut review and operator\n"},{"number":394,"text":"checks are complete and the human authority accepts that exact subject. If\n"},{"number":395,"text":"review requires a qualifying-byte change, the verdict stays on its original\n"},{"number":396,"text":"subject and the applicable successor rule is used. Acceptance does not move\n"},{"number":397,"text":"an immutable tag or create another final carrier (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":398,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":427,"heading":"RELEASE/3. Phases/Monotonic version-line advancement","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F3.%20Phases%2FMonotonic%20version-line%20advancement","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"c97d5e88f364681660063f546e92139a9523b142f64dfb3f980f250f8da0675e","start_line":399,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":399,"text":"### Monotonic version-line advancement\n"},{"number":400,"text":"\n"},{"number":401,"text":"On an RC-profile line, version-line advancement makes the newly published highest RC for one\n"},{"number":402,"text":"Project Release Namespace discoverable (P3, P5):\n"},{"number":403,"text":"\n"},{"number":404,"text":"1. identify the exact new immutable RC tag, ordinal and peeled commit;\n"},{"number":405,"text":"2. confirm that no higher RC ordinal already exists on that line;\n"},{"number":406,"text":"3. confirm the project-qualified selector is absent or currently resolves\n"},{"number":407,"text":"   to a lower RC ordinal on the same project line;\n"},{"number":408,"text":"4. atomically create or force-update the annotated `<project>/v<version>`\n"},{"number":409,"text":"   selector to the new highest RC commit;\n"},{"number":410,"text":"5. create or update `release/<project>/<version>` to the same commit when\n"},{"number":411,"text":"   that optional carrier is used;\n"},{"number":412,"text":"6. push the carrier, RC branch, immutable RC tag, selector and optional\n"},{"number":413,"text":"   release branch atomically where the transport supports it; and\n"},{"number":414,"text":"7. verify remotely that the selector peels to the highest RC commit and\n"},{"number":415,"text":"   that the matching immutable annotated RC tag exists.\n"},{"number":416,"text":"\n"},{"number":417,"text":"Advancement is refused when the target has no matching immutable annotated\n"},{"number":418,"text":"RC tag, any higher ordinal already exists, the selector would move to a\n"},{"number":419,"text":"lower RC, or the selector and release branch would not align to the same\n"},{"number":420,"text":"highest commit (P5).\n"},{"number":421,"text":"\n"},{"number":422,"text":"Forward movement is strictly monotonic by RC ordinal. A later defect is\n"},{"number":423,"text":"repaired through a higher immutable RC, not by moving an old RC tag or\n"},{"number":424,"text":"rolling the selector backward. The selector is therefore equivalent to\n"},{"number":425,"text":"`v<version>-rc.latest`, while every concrete RC tag remains addressable\n"},{"number":426,"text":"(P3).\n"},{"number":427,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":483,"heading":"RELEASE/4. Selector and consumer adoption","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F4.%20Selector%20and%20consumer%20adoption","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"7e6a65d35daf1f0cf5b9c633ddad6d5d0f10ce2e1fd55033235bb7c9d1ec5ee5","start_line":428,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":428,"text":"## 4. Selector and consumer adoption\n"},{"number":429,"text":"\n"},{"number":430,"text":"An RC-profile version-line selector answers only (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":431,"text":"\n"},{"number":432,"text":"> Which highest-ordinal published immutable RC cut currently exists on\n"},{"number":433,"text":"> this version line?\n"},{"number":434,"text":"\n"},{"number":435,"text":"It never answers:\n"},{"number":436,"text":"\n"},{"number":437,"text":"> Which exact STDO cut governs this consumer?\n"},{"number":438,"text":"\n"},{"number":439,"text":"A Product Definition may retain `stdo://channels/<version>` as its\n"},{"number":440,"text":"discovery selector, but its operative basis is the exact\n"},{"number":441,"text":"`stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<n>/` or stable\n"},{"number":442,"text":"`stdo://releases/v<major>.<minor>.<patch>/` URI and installed-manifest digest,\n"},{"number":443,"text":"the installed release basis of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4. Moving the Git\n"},{"number":444,"text":"version-line selector does not update any consumer. Adoption is a separate\n"},{"number":445,"text":"explicit Product-Definition transition that resolves, presents, installs,\n"},{"number":446,"text":"verifies and pins the selected immutable cut. RC resolution requires an\n"},{"number":447,"text":"annotated selector with a distinct peeled commit; absence of a peeled\n"},{"number":448,"text":"selector ref fails closed and cannot be interpreted as a lightweight\n"},{"number":449,"text":"selector whose tag object is its commit (P6, P3, P5).\n"},{"number":450,"text":"\n"},{"number":451,"text":"For an RC line, channel resolution enumerates the published RC tags for the selected\n"},{"number":452,"text":"Project Release Namespace, including preserved unqualified historical cuts\n"},{"number":453,"text":"during a namespace transition, selects the greatest positive ordinal,\n"},{"number":454,"text":"requires that cut and the current selector to be annotated tags peeling to\n"},{"number":455,"text":"the same commit, and fails closed when the selector lags or points\n"},{"number":456,"text":"elsewhere. Channel adoption also refuses a same-line target whose ordinal\n"},{"number":457,"text":"is below the Product Definition's current exact basis. A consumer that\n"},{"number":458,"text":"intentionally retains an older cut names that immutable RC URI and digest\n"},{"number":459,"text":"explicitly and uses exact-basis operations such as `sync`; it does not\n"},{"number":460,"text":"express that choice through the latest-version channel (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":461,"text":"\n"},{"number":462,"text":"For a stable line, channel resolution returns its verified stable-v1 cut\n"},{"number":463,"text":"without ordinal comparison or a separate selector. A legacy bare selector is\n"},{"number":464,"text":"never admitted as a stable exact basis; an ambiguous profile is refused. The\n"},{"number":465,"text":"same digest-bound adoption operation applies to either profile (P3, P5, P6).\n"},{"number":466,"text":"\n"},{"number":467,"text":"Presentation and mutation are separate invocations. The read-only plan,\n"},{"number":468,"text":"the Adoption Plan of PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4, binds the current Product\n"},{"number":469,"text":"Definition bytes and basis to the target immutable cut, annotated tag\n"},{"number":470,"text":"object, peeled commit, tree and installed-manifest digest, then emits a\n"},{"number":471,"text":"deterministic plan digest. Mutation requires that exact digest as the\n"},{"number":472,"text":"operator's acceptance and re-derives it before changing any Product\n"},{"number":473,"text":"Definition. Selector, target, manifest or definition drift invalidates the\n"},{"number":474,"text":"acceptance. A fleet uses the same law with one aggregate digest over all\n"},{"number":475,"text":"exact per-definition plans. Planning inside a mutating invocation is not\n"},{"number":476,"text":"external presentation and cannot authorise itself. The plan's hashing rule\n"},{"number":477,"text":"and the manager's command boundaries are PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4 (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":478,"text":"\n"},{"number":479,"text":"This split lets operators refer to `v<version>` for the latest published\n"},{"number":480,"text":"RC without repeatedly incrementing the version line, while every governed\n"},{"number":481,"text":"project retains reproducible exact-cut authority and changes only through\n"},{"number":482,"text":"explicit adoption (P2, P3, P6).\n"},{"number":483,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":509,"heading":"RELEASE/5. Naming","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md#RELEASE%2F5.%20Naming","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","sha256":"1524cad0dda8e13dfd592c84d132b08a991c9d8a23ec55a09902c874084c4953","start_line":484,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/RELEASE.md","lines":[{"number":484,"text":"## 5. Naming\n"},{"number":485,"text":"\n"},{"number":486,"text":"The shared-source RC-profile naming shape is (P3):\n"},{"number":487,"text":"\n"},{"number":488,"text":"- RC branch: `rc/<project>/<version>`;\n"},{"number":489,"text":"- immutable RC tag: `<project>/v<version>-rc.<n>`;\n"},{"number":490,"text":"- optional release branch: `release/<project>/<version>`; and\n"},{"number":491,"text":"- mutable version-line selector tag: `<project>/v<version>`.\n"},{"number":492,"text":"\n"},{"number":493,"text":"For example, on an RC line:\n"},{"number":494,"text":"\n"},{"number":495,"text":"- candidate branch: `rc/example/3.0.0`;\n"},{"number":496,"text":"- first immutable cut: `example/v3.0.0-rc.1`;\n"},{"number":497,"text":"- second immutable cut: `example/v3.0.0-rc.2`;\n"},{"number":498,"text":"- latest-release branch: `release/example/3.0.0`; and\n"},{"number":499,"text":"- latest-published selector: `example/v3.0.0`.\n"},{"number":500,"text":"\n"},{"number":501,"text":"A stable example is `example/v3.0.2`, with the stable-v1 marker and no\n"},{"number":502,"text":"separate selector. The published tag is immutable.\n"},{"number":503,"text":"\n"},{"number":504,"text":"The unqualified RC profile remains lawful only under the single-project and\n"},{"number":505,"text":"historical-conservation conditions of §2. Projects may choose another\n"},{"number":506,"text":"spelling only in a release source whose ref policy proves collision\n"},{"number":507,"text":"freedom and preserves the same project namespace, mutable carrier,\n"},{"number":508,"text":"immutable cut and mutable selector distinctions (P3).\n"},{"number":509,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":511,"heading":"RELEASE/6.
