Predecessor and\n"},{"number":1004,"text":"successor identities, changed inputs, surviving facts and affected J\n"},{"number":1005,"text":"dependencies are preserved; the wider frontier is recomputed where\n"},{"number":1006,"text":"independence is unproved (ACTIVATION §7).\n"},{"number":1007,"text":"[TICKETS §7](TICKETS.md#recorded-judgment-and-owner-ruling-continuity) owns\n"},{"number":1008,"text":"the existing carrier and the recorded J and O continuity rules.\n"},{"number":1009,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1040,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Consistency gate","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F4.%20Change%20management%2FConsistency%20gate","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"32e37858bd414b65f4db82db8280b20db1fe01d34886beb8292ca9747028bc08","start_line":1010,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1010,"text":"### Consistency gate\n"},{"number":1011,"text":"\n"},{"number":1012,"text":"No gate closes while the affected active surfaces are internally\n"},{"number":1013,"text":"inconsistent (P6, P4b). For the declared\n"},{"number":1014,"text":"change span the framework proves that the upstream surface remains\n"},{"number":1015,"text":"sufficient for the downstream surface, that downstream artifacts do not\n"},{"number":1016,"text":"contradict active upstream truth, and that tests and qualification prove\n"},{"number":1017,"text":"the active intended behaviour rather than stale precedent. If that proof is\n"},{"number":1018,"text":"missing the change remains open even if one local artifact already looks\n"},{"number":1019,"text":"correct.\n"},{"number":1020,"text":"\n"},{"number":1021,"text":"The gate closes only under the closure condition that\n"},{"number":1022,"text":"[TICKETS §7 Condition-based closure and reuse](TICKETS.md#condition-based-closure-and-reuse)\n"},{"number":1023,"text":"owns, applied here with the obligations declared for the change span as\n"},{"number":1024,"text":"its required coverage. A material counterexample\n"},{"number":1025,"text":"to a mandatory constraint, a required judgment or ruling without a closed\n"},{"number":1026,"text":"result, or an obligation that no evidence addresses keeps the gate from\n"},{"number":1027,"text":"closing, and each stays recorded by kind (P5, P6). Reuse of the gate's\n"},{"number":1028,"text":"evidence and results is\n"},{"number":1029,"text":"[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); TICKETS §7\n"},{"number":1030,"text":"records the work state on its carrier. A\n"},{"number":1031,"text":"review event, a passing aggregate, a completed artifact or a status change\n"},{"number":1032,"text":"cannot substitute for that conjunction (EVALUATION §5).\n"},{"number":1033,"text":"\n"},{"number":1034,"text":"When a code and test mismatch appears during ticketed work, implementation\n"},{"number":1035,"text":"behaviour is evidence but not authority. The mismatch is reconciled through\n"},{"number":1036,"text":"the admitted ticket, its intake triage, its lawful re-entry point and the\n"},{"number":1037,"text":"governing requirement, design, module, carrier or closure surface.\n"},{"number":1038,"text":"[TICKETS §7](TICKETS.md#test-case-authority) defines the ticket-local\n"},{"number":1039,"text":"test-case authority rule (ASSURANCE §3 states the test authority rule).\n"},{"number":1040,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1085,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Sprint execution boundary","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F4.%20Change%20management%2FSprint%20execution%20boundary","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"2e28773cb115d7039c1259ffdeb03d064cd4e6d623c1dddefa17de1f2c8fe9cd","start_line":1041,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1041,"text":"### Sprint execution boundary\n"},{"number":1042,"text":"\n"},{"number":1043,"text":"A sprint is a bounded execution-control surface, not a new layer in the\n"},{"number":1044,"text":"constitutional chain (P6, P2). It may\n"},{"number":1045,"text":"batch work, coordinate tickets or iteration entries, price proof cost and\n"},{"number":1046,"text":"force close review under existing goals, intent, product definition,\n"},{"number":1047,"text":"requirements and design authority; it does not create, supersede, weaken\n"},{"number":1048,"text":"or override that authority.\n"},{"number":1049,"text":"\n"},{"number":1050,"text":"A lawful sprint states at least: the goal or work wave it serves; the\n"},{"number":1051,"text":"upstream authority surfaces it depends on; the scope it admits; the\n"},{"number":1052,"text":"product, requirement, design, runtime, data-contract or governance\n"},{"number":1053,"text":"boundaries it excludes; the change classes it expects to contain; the\n"},{"number":1054,"text":"local proof or compliance debt, if any, that may be deferred during the\n"},{"number":1055,"text":"sprint; the closure trigger and closure law; and the paydown or repricing\n"},{"number":1056,"text":"path for debt discovered at close.\n"},{"number":1057,"text":"\n"},{"number":1058,"text":"Sprints exist because proof cost is not uniform. For some work, especially\n"},{"number":1059,"text":"projection-surface and user-interface iteration, proving every micro-change\n"},{"number":1060,"text":"before the next change can cost more than making the bounded change visible\n"},{"number":1061,"text":"and correcting it at close. That optimisation is lawful only when the\n"},{"number":1062,"text":"deferred cost remains local, visible, bounded and repayable. Deferred\n"},{"number":1063,"text":"compliance inside a sprint is escrow, not acceptance: it satisfies no\n"},{"number":1064,"text":"method, release or product closure until it is paid down, explicitly\n"},{"number":1065,"text":"accepted under the governing method, or repriced into the appropriate\n"},{"number":1066,"text":"upstream surface.\n"},{"number":1067,"text":"\n"},{"number":1068,"text":"A sprint may be recommended for close when its timebox expires, its\n"},{"number":1069,"text":"intended scope has been reached, accumulated changed surface area makes\n"},{"number":1070,"text":"continued iteration more expensive than review, review uncertainty makes\n"},{"number":1071,"text":"more work unsafe without reconciliation, or discovered gaps suggest the\n"},{"number":1072,"text":"sprint boundary is no longer the right container. Sprint close is a\n"},{"number":1073,"text":"forensic reconciliation event, not automatic approval: close review\n"},{"number":1074,"text":"compares the accumulated work and evidence against the governing\n"},{"number":1075,"text":"authority, classifies each gap, accepts compliant work, opens paydown work\n"},{"number":1076,"text":"for local debt, and escalates any authority drift through the lawful\n"},{"number":1077,"text":"change class. If a sprint discovers a goal, intent, product, requirement,\n"},{"number":1078,"text":"design, runtime, data-contract, governance or other product-truth change,\n"},{"number":1079,"text":"the sprint manifest does not authorise landing it; the work is split,\n"},{"number":1080,"text":"escalated, repriced or carried as explicit paydown.\n"},{"number":1081,"text":"[TICKETS §3](TICKETS.md#3-sprint-rules) defines the sprint mechanics,\n"},{"number":1082,"text":"including compliance escrow, and §4 the ticket mechanics; a profile may\n"},{"number":1083,"text":"define when sprint compliance escrow is an appropriate cost optimisation\n"},{"number":1084,"text":"for its domain (PROFILES).\n"},{"number":1085,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1097,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Carriers","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F4.%20Change%20management%2FCarriers","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"06e6d109f9964e8438e961bdaf8e0582aa223d6067c81184886958baf0f40b56","start_line":1086,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1086,"text":"### Carriers\n"},{"number":1087,"text":"\n"},{"number":1088,"text":"The carrier of a work item is selected for its required lifetime: a\n"},{"number":1089,"text":"durable ticket where the work needs identity across sessions; a\n"},{"number":1090,"text":"sprint-local entry where its only value is traceability inside a batch; a\n"},{"number":1091,"text":"run or return record where the work lives and dies with one activation.\n"},{"number":1092,"text":"The triage fields are required wherever substantive work begins; a ticket\n"},{"number":1093,"text":"per change is not (P2, P4b; [TICKETS §1](TICKETS.md#1-work-carriers) owns\n"},{"number":1094,"text":"the carrier model and\n"},{"number":1095,"text":"[TICKETS §5](TICKETS.md#carrier-selection) the selection of the smallest\n"},{"number":1096,"text":"lawful carrier).\n"},{"number":1097,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1171,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/4. Change management/Procedures","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F4.%20Change%20management%2FProcedures","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"30ada55cfb59e61472d2a5380ef9d6c1f07976adddd8075112ec9745a4a011ab","start_line":1098,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1098,"text":"### Procedures\n"},{"number":1099,"text":"\n"},{"number":1100,"text":"When any substantive intake arrives (P2, P4b): enter\n"},{"number":1101,"text":"[Universal intake triage](#universal-intake-triage), keeping classification\n"},{"number":1102,"text":"unresolved until the evidence supports a lawful class; determine the lawful\n"},{"number":1103,"text":"re-entry point into the constitutional chain when that class is established; identify the affected downstream span that must\n"},{"number":1104,"text":"remain consistent; only then treat the work as implementation, repricing or\n"},{"number":1105,"text":"release-bound change.\n"},{"number":1106,"text":"\n"},{"number":1107,"text":"When a feature is introduced or changed: update goals if the current\n"},{"number":1108,"text":"bounded work wave or overriding concerns have changed; update intent if the\n"},{"number":1109,"text":"purpose or scope has changed; update product if the current product\n"},{"number":1110,"text":"realisation, terms, boundaries or end-state shape have changed; update\n"},{"number":1111,"text":"requirements so the invariant truths are explicit as a decomposition of the\n"},{"number":1112,"text":"product definition, including any lifecycle obligations or named lifecycle\n"},{"number":1113,"text":"ambiguity gaps, and classify each new or changed requirement by category;\n"},{"number":1114,"text":"establish or update design so it owns the governing structural HOW, where\n"},{"number":1115,"text":"under the design profile its decision-completeness rule applies (design,\n"},{"number":1116,"text":"implementation and tests may co-evolve only when its co-evolution predicate\n"},{"number":1117,"text":"holds, otherwise the smallest causally closed affected design set is\n"},{"number":1118,"text":"accepted before retained implementation establishes an unresolved,\n"},{"number":1119,"text":"contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation;\n"},{"number":1120,"text":"[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md)), and\n"},{"number":1121,"text":"where that profile does not apply design, implementation and tests may\n"},{"number":1122,"text":"co-evolve when upstream truth leaves no unresolved material design\n"},{"number":1123,"text":"decision, and when such a decision remains the affected design is accepted\n"},{"number":1124,"text":"before retained implementation establishes it, ADRs being one valid design\n"},{"number":1125,"text":"form; write scenarios for capability claims that require operational proof\n"},{"number":1126,"text":"and define other evidence surfaces for non-capability requirements where\n"},{"number":1127,"text":"appropriate; prefer declarative expression of the problem and acceptance\n"},{"number":1128,"text":"surface before adding imperative mechanism; check the reconstruction\n"},{"number":1129,"text":"boundary, whether current goals support current intent, current intent the\n"},{"number":1130,"text":"current product, current product the intended requirements, current\n"},{"number":1131,"text":"requirements the intended design, and current design the intended\n"},{"number":1132,"text":"implementation; record any major ambiguity discovered at the active\n"},{"number":1133,"text":"boundary and govern it by declared risk appetite rather than silent\n"},{"number":1134,"text":"convenience; develop code under the selected design relation and reconcile\n"},{"number":1135,"text":"design, implementation and tests before promotion or closure; use events,\n"},{"number":1136,"text":"projection and delta to verify whether reality still satisfies the\n"},{"number":1137,"text":"requirements.\n"},{"number":1138,"text":"\n"},{"number":1139,"text":"When bootstrapping a project or repricing a requirement surface: resolve\n"},{"number":1140,"text":"the applicable product definition, verify its exact installed basis, load\n"},{"number":1141,"text":"its declared bootstrap entrypoint (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12), then load the\n"},{"number":1142,"text":"goals surface or the bound equivalent current work-wave carrier; perform\n"},{"number":1143,"text":"the goals-to-intent step and write or confirm the intent surface; perform\n"},{"number":1144,"text":"the intent-to-product step and write or confirm the product definition as\n"},{"number":1145,"text":"the current bridge; gather requirement source material from the relevant\n"},{"number":1146,"text":"constitutional inputs; perform the product-to-requirements step and write\n"},{"number":1147,"text":"the resulting live surface under the requirement surface; store\n"},{"number":1148,"text":"requirements as individual files or grouped families, whichever best\n"},{"number":1149,"text":"preserves clarity and avoids monolithic sprawl; make the requirement\n"},{"number":1150,"text":"surface the sole live requirement authority before proceeding to design and\n"},{"number":1151,"text":"code; prefer declarative structure over procedural workaround while shaping\n"},{"number":1152,"text":"the new surface; record any major ambiguity that remains at the current\n"},{"number":1153,"text":"boundary before downstream realisation proceeds; only after that surface\n"},{"number":1154,"text":"exists should downstream design and implementation be treated as\n"},{"number":1155,"text":"constitutionally grounded.\n"},{"number":1156,"text":"\n"},{"number":1157,"text":"When a real use case reveals a gap: enter\n"},{"number":1158,"text":"[Universal intake triage](#universal-intake-triage) first and keep the\n"},{"number":1159,"text":"classification unresolved until the evidence supports a lawful change class;\n"},{"number":1160,"text":"then write the scenario as the first\n"},{"number":1161,"text":"substantive project artifact for the gap so the pressure becomes concrete\n"},{"number":1162,"text":"and testable; run gap analysis to locate its cause under\n"},{"number":1163,"text":"[Universal intake triage](#universal-intake-triage), which keeps open what\n"},{"number":1164,"text":"the evidence cannot yet separate; then re-enter at the layer the selected\n"},{"number":1165,"text":"[change class](#change-classes) names and flow forward from it, writing new\n"},{"number":1166,"text":"goals or intent only where the work wave, direction or scope changes.\n"},{"number":1167,"text":"The intake source does not change this rule: a bug report, feature request,\n"},{"number":1168,"text":"failed test case, release blocker or operator observation still enters\n"},{"number":1169,"text":"through intake triage first, then follows the lawful change class selected\n"},{"number":1170,"text":"there.\n"},{"number":1171,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1239,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/5. Ambiguity governance and lifecycle","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F5.%20Ambiguity%20governance%20and%20lifecycle","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"a57045ddc644798bf7eeb532737e335e6324bc143da5bd62155fcce3f1e2b763","start_line":1172,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1172,"text":"## 5. Ambiguity governance and lifecycle\n"},{"number":1173,"text":"\n"},{"number":1174,"text":"This member owns the substrate-neutral ambiguity-governance bounded context\n"},{"number":1175,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:ambiguity-governance` under the selected complete\n"},{"number":1176,"text":"basis; a profile's runtime shorthands for its own frames stay in that\n"},{"number":1177,"text":"profile's context unless an explicit relation imports or translates them\n"},{"number":1178,"text":"(P3, P1).\n"},{"number":1179,"text":"\n"},{"number":1180,"text":"Spec-driven development is not only a derivation pipeline; it is a governed\n"},{"number":1181,"text":"disambiguation pipeline. The upstream chain progressively reduces\n"},{"number":1182,"text":"ambiguity: goals narrow active priority and work-wave focus; intent narrows\n"},{"number":1183,"text":"direction and scope; product narrows current realisation shape and terms;\n"},{"number":1184,"text":"requirements narrow constitutional obligation; build-tenant or stack\n"},{"number":1185,"text":"choice, a tenant's binding under §11, narrows the executable realisation\n"},{"number":1186,"text":"class; design narrows structural\n"},{"number":1187,"text":"interpretation; implementation narrows local realisation detail (P2).\n"},{"number":1188,"text":"\n"},{"number":1189,"text":"The narrowing is not uniform. Major ambiguity materially changes\n"},{"number":1190,"text":"architecture, stack, product boundary, execution or deployment\n"},{"number":1191,"text":"admissibility, public contract shape or other downstream realisation law;\n"},{"number":1192,"text":"micro ambiguity is a local implementation choice inside an already-governed\n"},{"number":1193,"text":"design boundary. Major ambiguity is always surfaced and governed; it may\n"},{"number":1194,"text":"not remain hidden inside informal operator judgment, ambient precedent or\n"},{"number":1195,"text":"silent model choice. At each major boundary the process detects and\n"},{"number":1196,"text":"records the major ambiguity that remains or is newly introduced; identifies\n"},{"number":1197,"text":"the affected invariant, asset or decision boundary; records the decision\n"},{"number":1198,"text":"taken if work proceeds; and records whether the ambiguity was resolved,\n"},{"number":1199,"text":"carried forward, escalated or blocked. Those outcomes are `resolved`,\n"},{"number":1200,"text":"`carried`, `escalated` and `blocked` of\n"},{"number":1201,"text":"[ACTIVATION §3 Ambiguity outcome](ACTIVATION.md#ambiguity-outcome), which\n"},{"number":1202,"text":"gives each its core value for the predicate \"the declared ambiguity is\n"},{"number":1203,"text":"resolved on the exact basis\". Only `resolved` is `satisfied`, so a later\n"},{"number":1204,"text":"boundary rests no dependent claim on an ambiguity that is carried,\n"},{"number":1205,"text":"escalated or blocked as if it were resolved. Ambiguity detection is\n"},{"number":1206,"text":"mandatory; blocking is policy (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":1207,"text":"\n"},{"number":1208,"text":"Lawful probabilistic processing\n"},{"number":1209,"text":"(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:lawful-probabilistic-processing`)\n"},{"number":1210,"text":"is bounded non-human processing permitted by declared policy to carry or\n"},{"number":1211,"text":"resolve declared ambiguity. Human adjudication\n"},{"number":1212,"text":"(`urn:stdo:concept:ambiguity-governance:human-adjudication`) is explicit\n"},{"number":1213,"text":"human judgment admitted by authority to resolve declared ambiguity where\n"},{"number":1214,"text":"policy or risk appetite requires it. That admission makes an operation\n"},{"number":1215,"text":"human adjudication. A person who relays, records or carries out a step\n"},{"number":1216,"text":"does not adjudicate by doing so, and a person who carries or decides a\n"},{"number":1217,"text":"declared ambiguity where policy permits it, without that admission, acts\n"},{"number":1218,"text":"under the policy and recording that govern lawful probabilistic\n"},{"number":1219,"text":"processing; who performs an operation does not decide its kind (§11, rule\n"},{"number":1220,"text":"2). The default governance model: ambiguity\n"},{"number":1221,"text":"may be carried or decided by lawful probabilistic processing when project\n"},{"number":1222,"text":"policy allows it; it may be escalated to explicit human adjudication when\n"},{"number":1223,"text":"project policy requires it; the threshold between those actions is\n"},{"number":1224,"text":"determined by declared risk appetite, not by silent convenience. Projects\n"},{"number":1225,"text":"may therefore choose different ambiguity-handling policies: a lower risk\n"},{"number":1226,"text":"appetite escalates more major ambiguity to explicit human judgment; a\n"},{"number":1227,"text":"higher one permits more bounded probabilistic decision-making. In either\n"},{"number":1228,"text":"case the ambiguity and the decision are recorded.\n"},{"number":1229,"text":"\n"},{"number":1230,"text":"The hard stops of [ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)\n"},{"number":1231,"text":"hold regardless of risk appetite. The method is therefore not \"eliminate\n"},{"number":1232,"text":"all ambiguity before work\"; it is \"make ambiguity visible, govern it\n"},{"number":1233,"text":"explicitly, and reduce it progressively until downstream realisation is\n"},{"number":1234,"text":"sufficiently constrained\".\n"},{"number":1235,"text":"\n"},{"number":1236,"text":"The operational lifecycle sufficiency rule (§2) is this governance applied\n"},{"number":1237,"text":"to lifecycle phases: an unanswered phase is a recorded gap, never a silent\n"},{"number":1238,"text":"absence.\n"},{"number":1239,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1280,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/6. Lineage and release","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F6.%20Lineage%20and%20release","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"29666f015676cde58829dd6f31061c750c1a2a2977ea32fa6d01470e4bda8904","start_line":1240,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1240,"text":"## 6. Lineage and release\n"},{"number":1241,"text":"\n"},{"number":1242,"text":"Software is recursive and compositional. A released product may build the\n"},{"number":1243,"text":"next released version of itself, a dependent product, or downstream project\n"},{"number":1244,"text":"artifacts. The roles are distinct objects with distinct identities,\n"},{"number":1245,"text":"substrate, development product, source project, release cut, product,\n"},{"number":1246,"text":"install, artifact and product definition, defined once in FOUNDATIONS §2\n"},{"number":1247,"text":"(product lineage objects) with their governing rules and the compiler\n"},{"number":1248,"text":"analogy; the product definition is the source project's present-tense\n"},{"number":1249,"text":"surface, not the released artifact and not the builder that happens to be\n"},{"number":1250,"text":"running the build (P3).\n"},{"number":1251,"text":"\n"},{"number":1252,"text":"The only exact operative release identifier is an immutable release-cut\n"},{"number":1253,"text":"tag under the selected [RELEASE profile](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities):\n"},{"number":1254,"text":"an RC cut or an explicit stable cut (P3). That cut is a\n"},{"number":1255,"text":"point-in-time release identity, a boundary over the feature set accepted\n"},{"number":1256,"text":"for that cut, and part of release metadata and release-process evaluation;\n"},{"number":1257,"text":"it is not part of the live project specification. On an RC line the mutable\n"},{"number":1258,"text":"`v<version>` tag is a discovery selector to the highest published ordinal; it is not an exact dependency, evidence or constitutional\n"},{"number":1259,"text":"basis and cannot silently change a consumer selection. How an active\n"},{"number":1260,"text":"constitutional surface uses version labels is the\n"},{"number":1261,"text":"[§2 Specification surface rule](#specification-surface-rule); shared\n"},{"number":1262,"text":"realisation surfaces should likewise describe current truth by role,\n"},{"number":1263,"text":"boundary and status rather than by release-line version labels. Release criteria, immutable\n"},{"number":1264,"text":"release-cut publication, selector advancement and the process for cutting a\n"},{"number":1265,"text":"release belong to [RELEASE §2 to §8](RELEASE.md#2-release-identities)\n"},{"number":1266,"text":".\n"},{"number":1267,"text":"\n"},{"number":1268,"text":"Successor baseline conservation is\n"},{"number":1269,"text":"[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)\n"},{"number":1270,"text":"(P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1271,"text":"\n"},{"number":1272,"text":"Layer and release separation holds\n"},{"number":1273,"text":"([AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §7](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-020-layer-and-release-separation)):\n"},{"number":1274,"text":"a calculus, its interpretation of a subject and its carrier encoding keep\n"},{"number":1275,"text":"independent content identities, judgments, supersession relations and\n"},{"number":1276,"text":"proof obligations, and none is automatically an independently released\n"},{"number":1277,"text":"product. One constitutional surface and its version boundary for a project\n"},{"number":1278,"text":"are\n"},{"number":1279,"text":"[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §11](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#11-one-constitutional-surface-and-version-boundary).\n"},{"number":1280,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1305,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/6. Lineage and release/Shared method adoption and propagation (STDO-UP-012)","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F6.%20Lineage%20and%20release%2FShared%20method%20adoption%20and%20propagation%20%28STDO-UP-012%29","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"73c04a92925bf1f678a071ccf01567f361add2462a362eb27307162c24cd14f1","start_line":1281,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1281,"text":"### Shared method adoption and propagation (STDO-UP-012)\n"},{"number":1282,"text":"\n"},{"number":1283,"text":"A reusable change to this method keeps one authority relation from the\n"},{"number":1284,"text":"evidence that prompts it to the consumer that realises it (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":1285,"text":"\n"},{"number":1286,"text":"```text\n"},{"number":1287,"text":"incident or review evidence\n"},{"number":1288,"text":"  -> shared-method intake\n"},{"number":1289,"text":"  -> one owning standard\n"},{"number":1290,"text":"  -> consistency and independent review\n"},{"number":1291,"text":"  -> human-authority acceptance\n"},{"number":1292,"text":"  -> one complete released STDO version\n"},{"number":1293,"text":"  -> explicit consumer selection\n"},{"number":1294,"text":"  -> consumer-owned realisation and evidence\n"},{"number":1295,"text":"```\n"},{"number":1296,"text":"\n"},{"number":1297,"text":"The chain states authority causality. It prescribes no intake workflow and\n"},{"number":1298,"text":"no artifact set (P2). An executable tool, runtime, carrier schema or\n"},{"number":1299,"text":"assurance implementation cannot enter the method merely because it\n"},{"number":1300,"text":"accompanies a method lesson; it requires its own Product authorisation\n"},{"number":1301,"text":"(P6). Other standards consume admitted law by reference (P3, P6), and a\n"},{"number":1302,"text":"consumer selects a complete released version rather than mixing members from different cuts (P3;\n"},{"number":1303,"text":"the release version boundary above,\n"},{"number":1304,"text":"[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §4](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#4-shared-installed-release-basis-and-toolchain-manager)).\n"},{"number":1305,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1307,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"cc5dae01b654a99ec1dd1076282b692a300c2f37209ef326fda79c5b76344a67","start_line":1306,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1306,"text":"## 7. Migration\n"},{"number":1307,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1329,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Core interface migration","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FCore%20interface%20migration","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"43a6d92837d528be3dfe475aed9b7653b5b291fac00f57618d03ebe2d542050a","start_line":1308,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1308,"text":"### Core interface migration\n"},{"number":1309,"text":"\n"},{"number":1310,"text":"Core interface changes are not ordinary local patches. Where a change\n"},{"number":1311,"text":"alters a load-bearing contract, carrier, resolver, provider, projection\n"},{"number":1312,"text":"law, closure law or other shared interface that multiple surfaces depend\n"},{"number":1313,"text":"on, the work is handled as a constitutional migration, not as incremental\n"},{"number":1314,"text":"patching (P3, P6). The governing rule:\n"},{"number":1315,"text":"change the authoritative core contract first; ban bridge code for that\n"},{"number":1316,"text":"contract family as an authoritative surface; audit every producer and every\n"},{"number":1317,"text":"consumer of the impacted interface; migrate each producer and consumer to\n"},{"number":1318,"text":"the new contract; chase every downstream effect until no superseded closure\n"},{"number":1319,"text":"law remains; run complete migration-closure proof only after the migration\n"},{"number":1320,"text":"wave is complete, bounded product-slice proof remaining governed by the\n"},{"number":1321,"text":"path-relative promotion rule below.\n"},{"number":1322,"text":"\n"},{"number":1323,"text":"The rule exists because partial interface migration creates recurring\n"},{"number":1324,"text":"drift: one producer writes the new contract while another still writes the\n"},{"number":1325,"text":"old; runtime reads one carrier while reporting or topology reads another;\n"},{"number":1326,"text":"compatibility aliases silently remain authoritative; projections become a\n"},{"number":1327,"text":"second truth surface; tests go green while the architecture remains split.\n"},{"number":1328,"text":"Declaring such a state complete is forbidden.\n"},{"number":1329,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1400,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Constitutional migration options","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FConstitutional%20migration%20options","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"462c07db9c6855f6e08e2bd597a4b892e388792df6d169e7d48afa2a6315c3ec","start_line":1330,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1330,"text":"### Constitutional migration options\n"},{"number":1331,"text":"\n"},{"number":1332,"text":"Core interface and major implementation replacement work has two lawful\n"},{"number":1333,"text":"constitutional strategies (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1334,"text":"Inside-out hard-break migration applies when the project remains on the\n"},{"number":1335,"text":"same implementation line and the authoritative source truth is being\n"},{"number":1336,"text":"replaced in place; the work proceeds from the source carrier outward\n"},{"number":1337,"text":"through a sequence of deliberate breaks and repairs. Fundamental\n"},{"number":1338,"text":"re-adoption migration applies when the rewrite is major and the project is\n"},{"number":1339,"text":"intentionally re-deriving itself on a materially different implementation\n"},{"number":1340,"text":"basis, such as a new runtime model, carrier model, type system, execution\n"},{"number":1341,"text":"substrate or realisation tree; the prior implementation is moved sideways\n"},{"number":1342,"text":"and treated as reference material, not live authority.\n"},{"number":1343,"text":"\n"},{"number":1344,"text":"Where bounded evolution and fundamental re-adoption are both lawful and\n"},{"number":1345,"text":"feasible, and a working predecessor can reach the admitted product outcome\n"},{"number":1346,"text":"without retaining competing or ambiguous authority, evolution on the\n"},{"number":1347,"text":"supported product path is the rebuttable selection presumption. This does\n"},{"number":1348,"text":"not require continuing an unsafe or constitutionally inadmissible\n"},{"number":1349,"text":"predecessor path; it conserves accepted predecessor semantics and product\n"},{"number":1350,"text":"feedback, and it does not require preserving an internal implementation or\n"},{"number":1351,"text":"public mechanism that product authority explicitly supersedes. When bounded\n"},{"number":1352,"text":"evolution includes a core-interface migration, it uses the inside-out\n"},{"number":1353,"text":"hard-break strategy; bounded evolution is a strategy-selection presumption,\n"},{"number":1354,"text":"not a third strategy.\n"},{"number":1355,"text":"\n"},{"number":1356,"text":"Fundamental re-adoption requires explicit selection by the human authority\n"},{"number":1357,"text":"owning the affected product boundary. The selection compares re-adoption\n"},{"number":1358,"text":"with bounded evolution across product value, feedback latency, authority\n"},{"number":1359,"text":"risk, reversibility, total cost and retained predecessor semantics, and\n"},{"number":1360,"text":"states a bounded abort or re-entry condition. Implementation scale or\n"},{"number":1361,"text":"architectural preference alone does not select re-adoption (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":1362,"text":"\n"},{"number":1363,"text":"Both strategies share these non-negotiable rules: no proxy interface\n"},{"number":1364,"text":"partial implementation stands in for the new contract in any acceptance\n"},{"number":1365,"text":"path; no bridge or fallback path remains silently authoritative; promotion\n"},{"number":1366,"text":"of an affected product outcome requires one unambiguous authoritative path\n"},{"number":1367,"text":"for that outcome; competing or ambiguous executable authority on the\n"},{"number":1368,"text":"promoted acceptance path blocks that outcome; residual material from the\n"},{"number":1369,"text":"superseded interface family outside the promoted path may be deferred only\n"},{"number":1370,"text":"when it is explicitly non-authoritative for the promoted outcome or governs\n"},{"number":1371,"text":"an explicitly specified, disjoint product or compatibility scope with\n"},{"number":1372,"text":"deterministic routing, cannot falsify current or retained product claims,\n"},{"number":1373,"text":"and retains a bounded migration, qualification or release disposition;\n"},{"number":1374,"text":"tests are leak detectors and proof surfaces, not the migration plan.\n"},{"number":1375,"text":"\n"},{"number":1376,"text":"For this rule the affected acceptance path is the full causal closure of\n"},{"number":1377,"text":"the outcome: every admitted entrypoint, producer, consumer, resolver,\n"},{"number":1378,"text":"fallback, shared state surface, event, projection and proof surface capable\n"},{"number":1379,"text":"of changing, interpreting or closing the outcome. Singular authority means\n"},{"number":1380,"text":"one governing authority across that closure, not one selected successful\n"},{"number":1381,"text":"trace. If the same request, fact, identity, state or projection is\n"},{"number":1382,"text":"admissible to old and new authority, authority is competing and promotion\n"},{"number":1383,"text":"blocks (P3).\n"},{"number":1384,"text":"\n"},{"number":1385,"text":"Product-slice promotion and complete migration closure are distinct claims.\n"},{"number":1386,"text":"An intermediate product outcome may be promoted while its enclosing\n"},{"number":1387,"text":"migration remains open only when the outcome's acceptance path has singular\n"},{"number":1388,"text":"authority and the residual implementation satisfies the deferment rule\n"},{"number":1389,"text":"above. That promotion neither closes the migration nor waives its final\n"},{"number":1390,"text":"retirement criteria. The slice's identity and acceptance criteria derive\n"},{"number":1391,"text":"from the product plus every causally applicable live requirement, accepted\n"},{"number":1392,"text":"design relation and retained predecessor claim; ticket or review wording\n"},{"number":1393,"text":"cannot narrow that authority away. Active migration status does not renew\n"},{"number":1394,"text":"an accepted slice's exhausted growth authority: work that only discharges\n"},{"number":1395,"text":"already admitted removal, demotion and migration-closure proof obligations\n"},{"number":1396,"text":"may continue within that existing bound without claiming further product\n"},{"number":1397,"text":"progress; further material producer or consumer growth requires another\n"},{"number":1398,"text":"still-live basis admitted under §3, and ticket activity alone is not that\n"},{"number":1399,"text":"basis.\n"},{"number":1400,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1409,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/What counts as a core interface","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FWhat%20counts%20as%20a%20core%20interface","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"d02f23cc14ad73379988b3eea2c23066ddd8ec38dfe89e94a608642df4d1e539","start_line":1401,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1401,"text":"### What counts as a core interface\n"},{"number":1402,"text":"\n"},{"number":1403,"text":"A core interface is any shared contract or carrier that materially governs\n"},{"number":1404,"text":"runtime closure, reporting or status truth, topology or frame progression,\n"},{"number":1405,"text":"proof or qualification outcome, event or projection semantics, identity or\n"},{"number":1406,"text":"binding resolution, or provider or resolver behaviour. If changing the\n"},{"number":1407,"text":"interface can alter how multiple surfaces decide what is true now, it is a\n"},{"number":1408,"text":"core interface change (P3).\n"},{"number":1409,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1423,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Required migration protocol","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FRequired%20migration%20protocol","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"5b5709d670c8464ef0259897337d86da53295748eac720351ed1876e479a514c","start_line":1410,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1410,"text":"### Required migration protocol\n"},{"number":1411,"text":"\n"},{"number":1412,"text":"Every core interface migration explicitly declares: the exact affected\n"},{"number":1413,"text":"migration scope; every explicitly excluded or disjoint product or\n"},{"number":1414,"text":"compatibility scope and its deterministic routing relation; the new\n"},{"number":1415,"text":"authoritative contract; the superseded contract or surface; the\n"},{"number":1416,"text":"authoritative closure law for the new contract; the full set of producers\n"},{"number":1417,"text":"of the old and new contract; the full set of consumers of the old and new\n"},{"number":1418,"text":"contract; and every projection, report, status surface and proof surface\n"},{"number":1419,"text":"that derives from it. Every old path is then classified as `remove`,\n"},{"number":1420,"text":"`replace`, `re-authorize` or `temporary scaffolding`. Temporary scaffolding\n"},{"number":1421,"text":"is lawful only if it is explicitly non-authoritative and scheduled for\n"},{"number":1422,"text":"removal before closure (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":1423,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1436,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Bridge prohibition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FBridge%20prohibition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"03e255a9bf3fab0c67bc42183fdf76048826ff37c19a371322f81cbd69be2762","start_line":1424,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1424,"text":"### Bridge prohibition\n"},{"number":1425,"text":"\n"},{"number":1426,"text":"For a core interface migration: no compatibility alias remains\n"},{"number":1427,"text":"authoritative; no fallback identity law remains as silent runtime\n"},{"number":1428,"text":"behaviour; no bridge path participates in acceptance as if it were the new\n"},{"number":1429,"text":"contract; no old reader or writer remains authoritative for the promoted\n"},{"number":1430,"text":"outcome once the new contract governs that outcome; no proxy or partial\n"},{"number":1431,"text":"implementation of the new interface stands between old and new truth as if\n"},{"number":1432,"text":"it were completion. The only lawful exception is an explicit compatibility\n"},{"number":1433,"text":"feature retained as part of the live product, whose compatibility path is\n"},{"number":1434,"text":"intentionally specified, explicitly bounded, and clearly identified as\n"},{"number":1435,"text":"compatibility rather than current native truth (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1436,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1447,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Projection discipline","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FProjection%20discipline","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"a9de0d6f4d16bc87ac2ae590bfd7f51d611d00277451825db9757750032882ba","start_line":1437,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1437,"text":"### Projection discipline\n"},{"number":1438,"text":"\n"},{"number":1439,"text":"Projections, reports, status views and topology views may reflect the\n"},{"number":1440,"text":"authoritative carrier; they do not become a second closure surface (P6,\n"},{"number":1441,"text":"P1). If runtime, reporting, topology and proof\n"},{"number":1442,"text":"can disagree about closure because they consume different carriers or\n"},{"number":1443,"text":"different closure laws, the migration is incomplete; if a projection can\n"},{"number":1444,"text":"independently close while the authoritative carrier is still open, the\n"},{"number":1445,"text":"migration is incomplete; if the authoritative carrier can close while a\n"},{"number":1446,"text":"projection still depends on an older law, the migration is incomplete.\n"},{"number":1447,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1464,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Inside-out first sequencing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FInside-out%20first%20sequencing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"b607c894cfcb64cd238359fed5805d5c33ec9c34665cd978529967b046791b62","start_line":1448,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1448,"text":"### Inside-out first sequencing\n"},{"number":1449,"text":"\n"},{"number":1450,"text":"Inside-out hard-break migrations proceed from the new authoritative source\n"},{"number":1451,"text":"carrier outward (P4b, P6). The full\n"},{"number":1452,"text":"best-guess interface family is discovered before proof is used as closure\n"},{"number":1453,"text":"evidence, including producers, consumers, projections, prompts, reports,\n"},{"number":1454,"text":"wrappers, replay paths, ingest paths, bootstrap paths and proof surfaces.\n"},{"number":1455,"text":"Authoritative producer and source-carrier work comes before downstream\n"},{"number":1456,"text":"consumer, projection, prompt, dossier, report or review-surface hardening.\n"},{"number":1457,"text":"Downstream exploration may exist only as isolated non-authoritative work\n"},{"number":1458,"text":"and does not land in public runtime, projection, prompt, report or proof\n"},{"number":1459,"text":"entry points until the source carrier is published and admitted. A\n"},{"number":1460,"text":"downstream projection ticket does not close while the source-carrier\n"},{"number":1461,"text":"ticket it depends on is still open. Dependency direction reflects this\n"},{"number":1462,"text":"order explicitly so the ticket set exposes the migration wave from source\n"},{"number":1463,"text":"truth to downstream read models.\n"},{"number":1464,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1484,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Hard-break discipline","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FHard-break%20discipline","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"befd78c873f4b3baa03b2cf31daeb607ac587a11b64837386ca88dd009d223bf","start_line":1465,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1465,"text":"### Hard-break discipline\n"},{"number":1466,"text":"\n"},{"number":1467,"text":"Inside-out migration is a hard-break sequence over one interface family.\n"},{"number":1468,"text":"The migration wave is the ordered set of those breaks; it is not a separate\n"},{"number":1469,"text":"mode that permits competing or ambiguous dual truth over the same request,\n"},{"number":1470,"text":"fact, identity, state or projection. Explicitly specified, deterministically\n"},{"number":1471,"text":"routed, non-overlapping product or compatibility scopes may coexist while\n"},{"number":1472,"text":"the enclosing migration remains open (P3).\n"},{"number":1473,"text":"\n"},{"number":1474,"text":"For each break: publish or admit the new deepest authoritative source\n"},{"number":1475,"text":"carrier; deliberately sever one old authoritative seam; keep that seam\n"},{"number":1476,"text":"broken; repair outward from source truth to consumers, then projections,\n"},{"number":1477,"text":"then prompts and reports, then proof surfaces; run negative proof that the\n"},{"number":1478,"text":"severed seam is rejected rather than merely unused. During the sequence,\n"},{"number":1479,"text":"tests may discover missed interfaces but do not replace the required\n"},{"number":1480,"text":"interface inventory; newly discovered affected interfaces remain part of\n"},{"number":1481,"text":"the same migration wave unless the work is explicitly repriced upward;\n"},{"number":1482,"text":"re-enabling the old seam through wrappers, fallbacks, projections or prompt\n"},{"number":1483,"text":"paths is a migration defect.\n"},{"number":1484,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1496,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Proof-last rule","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FProof-last%20rule","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"eb78e2ed06aa7f552a6991972e58488d9d48d85339d12ade23534ee8078bc1b7","start_line":1485,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1485,"text":"### Proof-last rule\n"},{"number":1486,"text":"\n"},{"number":1487,"text":"Complete migration-closure proof is not valid while producers and\n"},{"number":1488,"text":"consumers are split across old and new contracts. Bounded product-slice\n"},{"number":1489,"text":"proof may establish only the exact intermediate outcome permitted by the\n"},{"number":1490,"text":"path-relative promotion rule; it cannot establish migration closure (P6). Tests that pass only\n"},{"number":1491,"text":"because bridge-state semantics remain alive do not count as closure proof;\n"},{"number":1492,"text":"green local tests do not overrule a split architecture; migration-closure\n"},{"number":1493,"text":"proof belongs after migration, not during a partially migrated state;\n"},{"number":1494,"text":"per-break proof shows the severed old seam is rejected or fails closed\n"},{"number":1495,"text":"before downstream hardening can count as progress.\n"},{"number":1496,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1523,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Closure criterion","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FClosure%20criterion","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"b79f1e5a4f7026f9791bc7c9e24056b8791250c57e97dd497c5ec57637f4065b","start_line":1497,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1497,"text":"### Closure criterion\n"},{"number":1498,"text":"\n"},{"number":1499,"text":"A core interface migration is complete across its declared affected scope\n"},{"number":1500,"text":"only when every authoritative producer writes the new contract; every\n"},{"number":1501,"text":"authoritative consumer reads the new contract; superseded authoritative\n"},{"number":1502,"text":"paths are retired unless justified for a distinct supported responsibility\n"},{"number":1503,"text":"under the retention relation below; projections are downstream of the same\n"},{"number":1504,"text":"authoritative truth rather than competing truth surfaces; runtime,\n"},{"number":1505,"text":"reporting, topology and proof share one closure law; and no temporary\n"},{"number":1506,"text":"scaffolding remains in the acceptance path. Until those conditions hold the\n"},{"number":1507,"text":"work remains an active migration wave, not a completed refactor (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":1508,"text":"\n"},{"number":1509,"text":"Retention bears the burden. Each retained superseded mechanism identifies a\n"},{"number":1510,"text":"current supported obligation, owner, purpose, execution scope and material\n"},{"number":1511,"text":"cost. Temporary compatibility or comparison work has an expiry or removal\n"},{"number":1512,"text":"trigger; existing tests, an oracle label or nominal demotion do not justify\n"},{"number":1513,"text":"duplicate production responsibility. A required cold reconstruction route\n"},{"number":1514,"text":"or independent test oracle may serve an enduring distinct obligation\n"},{"number":1515,"text":"without an invented expiry. Where an obligation survives replacement, its\n"},{"number":1516,"text":"surviving owner is identified; where it has no governing basis, no\n"},{"number":1517,"text":"replacement guard is required. Retirement inside a closed affected cone\n"},{"number":1518,"text":"does not await unrelated whole-product closure (P2).\n"},{"number":1519,"text":"\n"},{"number":1520,"text":"An accepted intermediate product slice within the wave names the slice it\n"},{"number":1521,"text":"closes and keeps the enclosing migration visibly open; it does not project\n"},{"number":1522,"text":"slice acceptance as migration, qualification or release closure.\n"},{"number":1523,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1595,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Fundamental migration","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FFundamental%20migration","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"34fcc7320b1a1e90f6056b5e309b1f25b8087694fd76b8c4442924a35078c8c8","start_line":1524,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1524,"text":"### Fundamental migration\n"},{"number":1525,"text":"\n"},{"number":1526,"text":"A fundamental migration is a constitutional reset, not an in-place\n"},{"number":1527,"text":"refactor. It applies when a project intentionally abandons a prior\n"},{"number":1528,"text":"constitutional shape and re-derives itself on a new branch, version line or\n"},{"number":1529,"text":"methodology basis (P3, P6). In that case:\n"},{"number":1530,"text":"inherited constitutional documents from the prior line become migration\n"},{"number":1531,"text":"source material, not live authority in the new line; it is lawful to zero\n"},{"number":1532,"text":"inherited constitutional surfaces on the migration line and rebuild them\n"},{"number":1533,"text":"from first principles; nothing carries forward by default, and every\n"},{"number":1534,"text":"retained statement, requirement, design choice or guide rule must be\n"},{"number":1535,"text":"explicitly re-adopted; every carry-forward is intentional and should land in the\n"},{"number":1536,"text":"correct layer, goals, intent, product, requirements, design, guide or template; old\n"},{"number":1537,"text":"design and code may be used as reference implementations but do not govern\n"},{"number":1538,"text":"the new constitutional surface unless explicitly re-derived and re-adopted;\n"},{"number":1539,"text":"absence from the new constitutional surface means not yet adopted and\n"},{"number":1540,"text":"carries no automatic authority from the prior line; the prior\n"},{"number":1541,"text":"implementation may be moved sideways as a reference line, and that sideways\n"},{"number":1542,"text":"line has no live implementation authority in the new line; every inherited\n"},{"number":1543,"text":"module, interface, carrier, projection and proof surface is explicitly\n"},{"number":1544,"text":"classified before reuse.\n"},{"number":1545,"text":"\n"},{"number":1546,"text":"The required implementation classifications are `carry_across` (the module\n"},{"number":1547,"text":"remains materially the same and is intentionally re-adopted into the new\n"},{"number":1548,"text":"line), `redundant` (no longer needed in the new line) and `rewrite`\n"},{"number":1549,"text":"(still needed but rebuilt under the new requirements and design).\n"},{"number":1550,"text":"Unclassified inherited implementation is a defect. The purpose is to\n"},{"number":1551,"text":"prevent accidental law from leaking through migration by mere inheritance:\n"},{"number":1552,"text":"fundamental migration is controlled adoption, not passive preservation.\n"},{"number":1553,"text":"\n"},{"number":1554,"text":"Performing a fundamental migration: declare the migration line and treat\n"},{"number":1555,"text":"the prior line as source material; establish fresh constitutional surfaces\n"},{"number":1556,"text":"for method, goals, intent, product, requirements and design; move the\n"},{"number":1557,"text":"prior implementation sideways if needed so it cannot continue as ambient\n"},{"number":1558,"text":"live authority; classify inherited constitutional material as adopted,\n"},{"number":1559,"text":"superseded, deferred or orphaned; classify inherited implementation\n"},{"number":1560,"text":"material as `carry_across`, `redundant` or `rewrite`; copy forward only\n"},{"number":1561,"text":"what is intentionally retained; re-derive downstream design and code from\n"},{"number":1562,"text":"the new constitutional surfaces, not from ambient precedent. In a\n"},{"number":1563,"text":"fundamental migration `carry_across` does not mean automatic copy-forward\n"},{"number":1564,"text":"but explicit re-adoption under the new line; direct runtime, projection,\n"},{"number":1565,"text":"prompt, proof or review dependence on the sideways implementation line is\n"},{"number":1566,"text":"bridge debt; proxy interfaces that partially imitate the target line while\n"},{"number":1567,"text":"still depending on the sideways line are not lawful closure. This is a\n"},{"number":1568,"text":"lawful form of supersession, not a violation of live surface immutability\n"},{"number":1569,"text":"(§2), because the new line creates a new constitutional surface rather than\n"},{"number":1570,"text":"silently mutating the old one.\n"},{"number":1571,"text":"\n"},{"number":1572,"text":"The four classes of inherited constitutional material record the\n"},{"number":1573,"text":"adoption decision the new line takes on each inherited statement. For an\n"},{"number":1574,"text":"inherited requirement, the legacy classifications of\n"},{"number":1575,"text":"[§2 Requirement categories and classification](#requirement-categories-and-classification)\n"},{"number":1576,"text":"record a different thing: the standing of a requirement that is in the\n"},{"number":1577,"text":"live surface. The two relate as follows, and are not one classification:\n"},{"number":1578,"text":"- an adopted requirement enters the live surface as Active, or as Deferred\n"},{"number":1579,"text":"  when it is adopted as an explicitly not-yet-operative obligation;\n"},{"number":1580,"text":"- a requirement whose adoption is deferred is not in the live surface: it\n"},{"number":1581,"text":"  has no legacy classification and no authority until it is adopted,\n"},{"number":1582,"text":"  because absence from the new surface means \"not yet adopted\";\n"},{"number":1583,"text":"- a superseded or orphaned inherited requirement takes Superseded or\n"},{"number":1584,"text":"  Orphaned, with that table's meanings.\n"},{"number":1585,"text":"\n"},{"number":1586,"text":"For other inherited\n"},{"number":1587,"text":"constitutional material the classes keep their names and the steps\n"},{"number":1588,"text":"above. They are declared states of the new line's surfaces and, as §2\n"},{"number":1589,"text":"states, none of them is or supplies the\n"},{"number":1590,"text":"[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)\n"},{"number":1591,"text":"disposition of a predecessor claim (P3, P6). Purpose and material\n"},{"number":1592,"text":"relation: an inherited requirement in a migration falls under both this\n"},{"number":1593,"text":"step and the legacy classification rule, and stating how the two records\n"},{"number":1594,"text":"relate leaves no two records of one standing to reconcile (P3).\n"},{"number":1595,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1620,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/7. Migration/Transformation wave","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F7.%20Migration%2FTransformation%20wave","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"7d6691abf3c14b34ba8fc21d5c6ddc32eb9cd18295d52d4c143c519f8d4d41f6","start_line":1596,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1596,"text":"### Transformation wave\n"},{"number":1597,"text":"\n"},{"number":1598,"text":"Refactor and migration should be understood as a transformation wave over\n"},{"number":1599,"text":"mutable\n"},{"number":1600,"text":"implementation surfaces (P3, P6). While\n"},{"number":1601,"text":"the wave is in flight: temporary mixed-state implementation may exist only\n"},{"number":1602,"text":"below the current break boundary and only as explicitly non-authoritative\n"},{"number":1603,"text":"plumbing; transitional adapters or scaffolds may exist only when they are\n"},{"number":1604,"text":"named, bounded and outside the acceptance path; refactor state may still\n"},{"number":1605,"text":"carry traces of the prior operative model, never as competing or ambiguous\n"},{"number":1606,"text":"dual authority over the same request, fact, identity, state or projection.\n"},{"number":1607,"text":"Explicitly specified, deterministically routed, non-overlapping product or\n"},{"number":1608,"text":"compatibility scopes are not competing authority under this rule; they may\n"},{"number":1609,"text":"coexist while the enclosing migration remains visibly open.\n"},{"number":1610,"text":"\n"},{"number":1611,"text":"When the wave lands across its declared affected scope: only the new\n"},{"number":1612,"text":"current operative surface remains live for that scope; prior operative\n"},{"number":1613,"text":"paths for that scope are erased from the live product; the path taken to\n"},{"number":1614,"text":"get there survives only in version control, event history and superseded\n"},{"number":1615,"text":"records; mixed old and new operative models are not a stable end state. The\n"},{"number":1616,"text":"only lawful exception is an explicit compatibility feature, which is named\n"},{"number":1617,"text":"as current product behaviour, justified in the specification, bounded in\n"},{"number":1618,"text":"scope and tested as an intentional feature. Otherwise the correct action is\n"},{"number":1619,"text":"deletion, not passive preservation.\n"},{"number":1620,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1689,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/8. Bounded execution in this method","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F8.%20Bounded%20execution%20in%20this%20method","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"e85805240b6ccb39748e84780def9db8f081e100e4fe25cca59fe554d6f55857","start_line":1621,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1621,"text":"## 8. Bounded execution in this method\n"},{"number":1622,"text":"\n"},{"number":1623,"text":"Construction delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker is governed as\n"},{"number":1624,"text":"the step of ACTIVATION: the execution relation from accepted governing\n"},{"number":1625,"text":"basis through bounded affected relation set, selected computational\n"},{"number":1626,"text":"relations, delegated execution and decision authority, construction and\n"},{"number":1627,"text":"self-review, independent live-surface assessment where required, one of\n"},{"number":1628,"text":"accept, local repair, re-enter or reject, the exact accepted checkpoint,\n"},{"number":1629,"text":"and the next already-authorised bounded action (ACTIVATION §1, §3, §5 and\n"},{"number":1630,"text":"§7). The\n"},{"number":1631,"text":"construction relation that the step serves, from the bound current state\n"},{"number":1632,"text":"to the destination through a selected strategy, feedback and the distinct\n"},{"number":1633,"text":"claims of preservation, progress and completion, is\n"},{"number":1634,"text":"[ACTIVATION §1 Construction relation](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation);\n"},{"number":1635,"text":"this member applies it to delivery and correction (§4) and states no\n"},{"number":1636,"text":"second relation (P6). The\n"},{"number":1637,"text":"step states its results in the core of\n"},{"number":1638,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) through the refinements\n"},{"number":1639,"text":"of [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition): that a\n"},{"number":1640,"text":"candidate is available, how each assessment of it came out, and the\n"},{"number":1641,"text":"decision owner's disposition (`accept`, `local_repair`, `re_enter` or\n"},{"number":1642,"text":"`reject`) are separate results, so a candidate that is available or\n"},{"number":1643,"text":"assessed is not thereby accepted (P6). The selected computational relations\n"},{"number":1644,"text":"are drawn from the computational calculus of the tenant doing the work;\n"},{"number":1645,"text":"the actors, tools and processes that carry out the step belong to that\n"},{"number":1646,"text":"tenant's execution environment, and the step's time, spend and other\n"},{"number":1647,"text":"resource limits are those of its execution binding (§11). The\n"},{"number":1648,"text":"declared work boundary of a probabilistic unit is FOUNDATIONS §2 (work\n"},{"number":1649,"text":"boundary) and §3 (P0); the complete enclosing-relation admission of a\n"},{"number":1650,"text":"material transition and its standing structural qualification are\n"},{"number":1651,"text":"ACTIVATION §4; proportionality is ACTIVATION §6. This member binds the\n"},{"number":1652,"text":"generic terms to its own: the selected outcome of a step is the product\n"},{"number":1653,"text":"outcome, prerequisite or experiment of §3; the owning relations are the\n"},{"number":1654,"text":"chain's layers; the re-entry conditions are the change classes of §4.\n"},{"number":1655,"text":"\n"},{"number":1656,"text":"Delivery priority applies the proportionality relation to the current\n"},{"number":1657,"text":"product outcome, likelihood, impact, reversibility, dependency and the cost\n"},{"number":1658,"text":"of delayed product feedback. Probability informs lawful priority; it does\n"},{"number":1659,"text":"not waive authority, integrity, safety, retained release claims or another\n"},{"number":1660,"text":"hard stop. A probability stated for priority is a quantified claim under\n"},{"number":1661,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Quantified assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#quantified-assurance);\n"},{"number":1662,"text":"unsupported numeric confidence stays unresolved (P6). The default priority is work that exposes or advances the\n"},{"number":1663,"text":"smallest supported product path and its highest-value likely failures.\n"},{"number":1664,"text":"Defensive or prerequisite work that displaces that path identifies the\n"},{"number":1665,"text":"affected claim, evidence basis, bounded effort, return condition and\n"},{"number":1666,"text":"expected product consequence. This is a priority relation, not a fixed\n"},{"number":1667,"text":"global execution sequence or a scheduling runtime (P2, P0).\n"},{"number":1668,"text":"\n"},{"number":1669,"text":"Which frames carry construction, assessment and disposition, and which\n"},{"number":1670,"text":"consumer receives a step's return, is set by the configuration that\n"},{"number":1671,"text":"[ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration) derives from the\n"},{"number":1672,"text":"task's operations, dependencies, actor capabilities and required\n"},{"number":1673,"text":"assurance; this member adds no role inventory, coordinator or sequence. A\n"},{"number":1674,"text":"step's return goes to the consumer the configuration declares. Where the\n"},{"number":1675,"text":"configuration has a coordinator, the coordinator decides as\n"},{"number":1676,"text":"[ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), Coordination\n"},{"number":1677,"text":"across tasks, states, within its decision grant, and selects the next\n"},{"number":1678,"text":"authorised action. The executive configuration, with its Executive,\n"},{"number":1679,"text":"Worker and Reviewer frames, is one such configuration; the executive\n"},{"number":1680,"text":"baseline profile owns it, and it governs where it is selected\n"},{"number":1681,"text":"([EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md)) (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":1682,"text":"\n"},{"number":1683,"text":"Delivery is sequenced around the smallest real path from a supported entry\n"},{"number":1684,"text":"to a material outcome, established early and widened by increments chosen\n"},{"number":1685,"text":"for consequential uncertainty, interface reach and failure impact; a\n"},{"number":1686,"text":"passing path establishes only the relations it exercised. This is a\n"},{"number":1687,"text":"sequencing heuristic for any realisation, not law; the baseline's\n"},{"number":1688,"text":"steel-thread delivery governs its profile unchanged (P2).\n"},{"number":1689,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1706,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/9. Evidence","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F9.%20Evidence","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"77116f51e4323d35393442413868f8c17bf83a9ccfe0af1f22bcfe04d31f77f5","start_line":1690,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1690,"text":"## 9. Evidence\n"},{"number":1691,"text":"\n"},{"number":1692,"text":"The rules that govern how constitutional claims are proved in practice are\n"},{"number":1693,"text":"tier-1 law: proof target identity and adequacy (EVALUATION §1); semantic,\n"},{"number":1694,"text":"evidence and projection separation (EVALUATION §2); assurance-boundary\n"},{"number":1695,"text":"congruence and method qualification (EVALUATION §1, §3, §6 and §7).\n"},{"number":1696,"text":"Verification layers, the testing strategy taxonomy with fixture and proof\n"},{"number":1697,"text":"portability, test authority, scenario bundles, installed development proof\n"},{"number":1698,"text":"and significant path coverage are ASSURANCE §1 to §6 (P6).\n"},{"number":1699,"text":"\n"},{"number":1700,"text":"For a realisation claim, the evidence that the closure condition of\n"},{"number":1701,"text":"[TICKETS §7 Condition-based closure and reuse](TICKETS.md#condition-based-closure-and-reuse)\n"},{"number":1702,"text":"requires includes an authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof\n"},{"number":1703,"text":"where drift is plausible, and a present-tense statement of the residual\n"},{"number":1704,"text":"open pressure; this section adds no second closure condition (P6, P4b,\n"},{"number":1705,"text":"P5).\n"},{"number":1706,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1754,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/10. Design records","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F10.%20Design%20records","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"ff8c0d24ed41fab3388b55debf7259be8c4ec0c500aeda570692bb6856534dfe","start_line":1707,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1707,"text":"## 10. Design records\n"},{"number":1708,"text":"\n"},{"number":1709,"text":"Each ADR explicitly includes `Status:` (`active`, `superseded` or\n"},{"number":1710,"text":"`retired`); `Implements:` (the requirement identifiers the ADR makes true);\n"},{"number":1711,"text":"`Derives from:` (the intent identifier or strategy document that motivated\n"},{"number":1712,"text":"the decision); `Supersedes:` (the prior ADR or doctrine it replaces);\n"},{"number":1713,"text":"`Superseded by:` (the successor ADR when its status is superseded); and\n"},{"number":1714,"text":"`Retained special case:` (when earlier behaviour is intentionally retained\n"},{"number":1715,"text":"as a special case of the current surface) (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":1716,"text":"ADRs are written per decision boundary, not per requirement file; the\n"},{"number":1717,"text":"boundary is the question \"what design choice makes these acceptance\n"},{"number":1718,"text":"criteria true\". If a requirement names an operational mechanism, the ADR\n"},{"number":1719,"text":"names that mechanism too. If a requirement expands the event taxonomy, the\n"},{"number":1720,"text":"event-contract ADR is repriced immediately; event semantics do not drift\n"},{"number":1721,"text":"into a second constitution.\n"},{"number":1722,"text":"\n"},{"number":1723,"text":"ADRs are append-only history. When a later ADR supersedes one, the earlier\n"},{"number":1724,"text":"ADR stays in place with `Status: superseded` and `Superseded by:` naming\n"},{"number":1725,"text":"its successor; a superseded ADR is deleted only when it is explicitly\n"},{"number":1726,"text":"retired. When the scope of a shared or cross-tenant ADR narrows during\n"},{"number":1727,"text":"implementation to one tenant, the ADR moves to that tenant's design\n"},{"number":1728,"text":"surface and the move is recorded in the supersession chain (P4b, P3). This\n"},{"number":1729,"text":"section owns ADR lifecycle and location; templates project its rules.\n"},{"number":1730,"text":"\n"},{"number":1731,"text":"ADRs are stored at the design surface that owns the decision; an `adrs/`\n"},{"number":1732,"text":"subdirectory is the default scaffold, not a mandatory location (P3). Tenant-local build-tenant ADRs go to the\n"},{"number":1733,"text":"applicable tenant design surface bound by the product definition, by\n"},{"number":1734,"text":"default `build_tenants/<tenant-path>/design/adrs/`; shared or cross-tenant\n"},{"number":1735,"text":"ADRs to the applicable common surface, by default\n"},{"number":1736,"text":"`build_tenants/common/design/adrs/`; non-tenanted or project-local ADRs to\n"},{"number":1737,"text":"`<governing-design-surface>/adrs/`.
