In the default scaffold `<tenant-path>`\n"},{"number":1738,"text":"is one or more path segments beneath `build_tenants/`; both\n"},{"number":1739,"text":"capability-oriented `<product-family>/<realization-variant>` paths and\n"},{"number":1740,"text":"single-label `<realization-variant>` paths are lawful, the former is the\n"},{"number":1741,"text":"recommended default, existing or alternative layouts remain conformant and\n"},{"number":1742,"text":"need no migration, and in every layout the product's tenant registry entry\n"},{"number":1743,"text":"records the tenant identity and locations used (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §1).\n"},{"number":1744,"text":"The governing design surface is the closest design surface whose authority\n"},{"number":1745,"text":"owns the decision. ADRs are not placed in comments, generated views,\n"},{"number":1746,"text":"runtime archives or requirement folders. The filename convention is\n"},{"number":1747,"text":"`ADR-<local-id>-short-slug.md`, the local identifier unique within the\n"},{"number":1748,"text":"owning `adrs/` directory; numeric identifiers such as `ADR-001-...` are the\n"},{"number":1749,"text":"default, and namespace-prefixed identifiers such as `ADR-GM-005-...` are\n"},{"number":1750,"text":"allowed when the owning design surface already uses them. A `REGISTRY.md`\n"},{"number":1751,"text":"index alongside the ADR files is recommended for tooling and review and is\n"},{"number":1752,"text":"not required: the constitutional source remains each ADR file, and a\n"},{"number":1753,"text":"registry is a read model that may drift unless tooling maintains it.\n"},{"number":1754,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1954,"heading":"SPEC_METHOD/11. Build-tenant binding","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#SPEC_METHOD%2F11.%20Build-tenant%20binding","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","sha256":"17e4ef8cdac1e42945563e4982ac5cf79cfae71d9ae296a9716134b1fd299151","start_line":1755,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md","lines":[{"number":1755,"text":"## 11. Build-tenant binding\n"},{"number":1756,"text":"\n"},{"number":1757,"text":"This section owns the relation between a product's WHAT and the build\n"},{"number":1758,"text":"tenants that realise it: what a tenant binds, what stays fixed while it\n"},{"number":1759,"text":"chooses, and what its evidence shows. It applies to every product built\n"},{"number":1760,"text":"with this method (P2, P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1761,"text":"\n"},{"number":1762,"text":"Terms used in this section:\n"},{"number":1763,"text":"\n"},{"number":1764,"text":"- A build tenant is one independent, project-owned HOW realisation of a\n"},{"number":1765,"text":"  product's WHAT. The build-tenancy context of\n"},{"number":1766,"text":"  [PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#8-what-how-and-work-carriers)\n"},{"number":1767,"text":"  names it, and the product definition's tenant registry locates each one.\n"},{"number":1768,"text":"- The requirements calculus of a product is the set of obligations its\n"},{"number":1769,"text":"  WHAT states, the outcomes it permits, and its rules for refining and\n"},{"number":1770,"text":"  composing the work that realises it.\n"},{"number":1771,"text":"- A computational calculus is a declared set of executable operations,\n"},{"number":1772,"text":"  with the laws by which they compose, the transformations they permit,\n"},{"number":1773,"text":"  and their effects and resource behaviour, as far as these are material\n"},{"number":1774,"text":"  to the obligations.\n"},{"number":1775,"text":"- An execution environment is the concrete means that performs those\n"},{"number":1776,"text":"  operations: a technology stack; a human process, made of people, roles,\n"},{"number":1777,"text":"  documents, communication channels and decision procedures; or a\n"},{"number":1778,"text":"  combination of the two.\n"},{"number":1779,"text":"- A tenant's build-tenant binding has two parts: its calculus binding,\n"},{"number":1780,"text":"  from the requirements calculus to its computational calculus, and its\n"},{"number":1781,"text":"  execution binding, from that computational calculus to its execution\n"},{"number":1782,"text":"  environment. A tenant's registry entry locates the tenant; it is not the\n"},{"number":1783,"text":"  binding.\n"},{"number":1784,"text":"- A generic procedure is a method procedure whose scope is independent of\n"},{"number":1785,"text":"  the selected execution environment. It and its projections preserve the\n"},{"number":1786,"text":"  bindings Rule 2 permits: code, an event stream or reconstruction from a\n"},{"number":1787,"text":"  complete history is required only where the governing obligations or\n"},{"number":1788,"text":"  the selected execution binding require it, and an adequate human\n"},{"number":1789,"text":"  process using current records and direct observation is a permitted\n"},{"number":1790,"text":"  execution binding of a generic procedure that requires none of them\n"},{"number":1791,"text":"  (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1792,"text":"- Author identity and actor identity are as\n"},{"number":1793,"text":"  [EVALUATION §3](EVALUATION.md#3-independent-assessment) defines them:\n"},{"number":1794,"text":"  authorship is one condition of an assessment's independence there, and\n"},{"number":1795,"text":"  an actor's identity is not an authority.\n"},{"number":1796,"text":"  Operation kind is what an operation does, such as construct, assess,\n"},{"number":1797,"text":"  relay, record, measure or decide, together with the authority that kind\n"},{"number":1798,"text":"  of operation requires.\n"},{"number":1799,"text":"\n"},{"number":1800,"text":"The common deterministic functor kind is a separate coordinate owned by\n"},{"number":1801,"text":"[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds).\n"},{"number":1802,"text":"A binding that claims F_D establishes the common kind's total-domain contract.\n"},{"number":1803,"text":"It retains the operation's subject, evidence and effect permissions. Human,\n"},{"number":1804,"text":"machine and mixed bindings preserve these same distinctions; no runtime,\n"},{"number":1805,"text":"event log or annotation carrier follows from the classification.\n"},{"number":1806,"text":"\n"},{"number":1807,"text":"Rules:\n"},{"number":1808,"text":"\n"},{"number":1809,"text":"1. Realisations of one WHAT. One WHAT is realised by one or more\n"},{"number":1810,"text":"   independent build tenants, whatever the physical layout. The WHAT is\n"},{"number":1811,"text":"   constitutional and each tenant's realisation is HOW; a tenant-local\n"},{"number":1812,"text":"   realisation stays derivative until its governing truth is ratified in\n"},{"number":1813,"text":"   specification (§2). Each tenant binds the product's requirements\n"},{"number":1814,"text":"   calculus to a declared computational calculus and binds that calculus\n"},{"number":1815,"text":"   to a concrete execution environment. Both bindings are that tenant's\n"},{"number":1816,"text":"   design and realisation: they are declared in its existing design and\n"},{"number":1817,"text":"   realisation surfaces, chosen under the Design rule (§2) and recorded as\n"},{"number":1818,"text":"   design decisions (§10), and the method requires no further carrier. The\n"},{"number":1819,"text":"   tenant owns its binding, its realisation and their evidence; the WHAT\n"},{"number":1820,"text":"   keeps its meaning (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1821,"text":"2. Selection. The execution environment may be a technology stack, a\n"},{"number":1822,"text":"   human process or a combination. Its selection stays within the\n"},{"number":1823,"text":"   requirements calculus, including every human decision that calculus\n"},{"number":1824,"text":"   requires: no choice of environment removes a required human decision or\n"},{"number":1825,"text":"   a required independent assessment. Author identity, actor identity and\n"},{"number":1826,"text":"   operation kind stay distinct, and none determines another. Who authored\n"},{"number":1827,"text":"   a tenant does not select its environment; one actor may perform\n"},{"number":1828,"text":"   operations of several kinds, each under its own grant; and an actor's\n"},{"number":1829,"text":"   identity neither decides the kind of an operation nor grants authority\n"},{"number":1830,"text":"   for it. A person performing an operation does not by that make it human\n"},{"number":1831,"text":"   adjudication: §5 states the admission that makes an operation human\n"},{"number":1832,"text":"   adjudication and how a person who decides under policy without it is\n"},{"number":1833,"text":"   governed. The same holds for every decision the requirements reserve to\n"},{"number":1834,"text":"   a human: the person the governing authority admits for it takes it, and\n"},{"number":1835,"text":"   a person's part elsewhere in the process does not (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":1836,"text":"3. Material content. For the obligations it serves, the binding\n"},{"number":1837,"text":"   identifies:\n"},{"number":1838,"text":"   - the operations, each with its inputs, outputs, effects and outcome\n"},{"number":1839,"text":"     values; each outcome value maps to exactly one core value under\n"},{"number":1840,"text":"     [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), and an intended\n"},{"number":1841,"text":"     external effect, one of uncertain completion included, is recorded as\n"},{"number":1842,"text":"     [ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects) states;\n"},{"number":1843,"text":"   - the composition laws, and the transformations the calculus permits;\n"},{"number":1844,"text":"   - the resource measures;\n"},{"number":1845,"text":"   - the operational assumptions on which conformance depends, among them\n"},{"number":1846,"text":"     those about actors, tools, availability and failure.\n"},{"number":1847,"text":"\n"},{"number":1848,"text":"   Human effort, elapsed time, communication and machine resources are\n"},{"number":1849,"text":"   measured where a selected obligation needs them. Each measure states its\n"},{"number":1850,"text":"   unit and its boundary: what is counted, and where measurement starts and\n"},{"number":1851,"text":"   stops. A resource claim without its unit or its boundary supports no\n"},{"number":1852,"text":"   conformance claim. The size of a selected context is measured as\n"},{"number":1853,"text":"   [ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)\n"},{"number":1854,"text":"   step 3 measures it, against the capacity the binding declares for the\n"},{"number":1855,"text":"   actor. The law for declaring, measuring and honouring resource limits\n"},{"number":1856,"text":"   is [ACTIVATION §6 Resource limits](ACTIVATION.md#resource-limits), and\n"},{"number":1857,"text":"   this rule binds it: the values of a step's time, spend and other\n"},{"number":1858,"text":"   resource limits, and the units and boundaries the environment can\n"},{"number":1859,"text":"   measure, are those of the execution binding, stated before the\n"},{"number":1860,"text":"   activation they limit. Where a configuration states its resource limits\n"},{"number":1861,"text":"   and its assumptions about failure\n"},{"number":1862,"text":"   ([ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration)), it takes\n"},{"number":1863,"text":"   them from this binding (P0, P2, P5).\n"},{"number":1864,"text":"4. Conformance evidence. The obligations of the requirements calculus\n"},{"number":1865,"text":"   decide fitness; the kind of executor alone neither accepts nor rejects a\n"},{"number":1866,"text":"   realisation. Evidence establishes how the bound realisation satisfies\n"},{"number":1867,"text":"   the required meaning and constraints, including the applicable\n"},{"number":1868,"text":"   authority, independence, failure and recovery conditions. Conformance is\n"},{"number":1869,"text":"   judged under\n"},{"number":1870,"text":"   [EVALUATION §6](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations), and two\n"},{"number":1871,"text":"   conforming tenants need not behave identically outside the contract.\n"},{"number":1872,"text":"   Each assessment returns a core value for its predicate, and the tenant's\n"},{"number":1873,"text":"   conformance is their\n"},{"number":1874,"text":"   [conjunction](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results), with the\n"},{"number":1875,"text":"   obligations of the requirements calculus as its required coverage. A\n"},{"number":1876,"text":"   convenient stack never weakens an obligation. An execution plan that\n"},{"number":1877,"text":"   merges two required independent assessments, or substitutes an\n"},{"number":1878,"text":"   automated result for a required human decision, is a counterexample to\n"},{"number":1879,"text":"   the obligation it weakens, so the binding's conformance for that\n"},{"number":1880,"text":"   obligation is `falsified`; in any run under such a plan the lost\n"},{"number":1881,"text":"   assessment or decision has no applicable closed result. Matching\n"},{"number":1882,"text":"   outputs, lower cost or a faster run do not discharge the lost\n"},{"number":1883,"text":"   independence or authority. A claim that a binding preserves categorical\n"},{"number":1884,"text":"   structure is a further claim: it meets the Formal fragment of\n"},{"number":1885,"text":"   [FOUNDATIONS §4](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra) and stays distinct from\n"},{"number":1886,"text":"   conformance on the equivalence ladder of EVALUATION §6 (P6, P1, P4b).\n"},{"number":1887,"text":"5. Reuse. A computational calculus may be reused across tenants and\n"},{"number":1888,"text":"   execution environments wherever each binding satisfies its laws, and\n"},{"number":1889,"text":"   each binding shows that it does. A different language, tool, team or\n"},{"number":1890,"text":"   person does not by itself require a different calculus: replacing the\n"},{"number":1891,"text":"   executor of an operation while the calculus's laws hold changes the\n"},{"number":1892,"text":"   execution binding, not the calculus (P1, P4a).\n"},{"number":1893,"text":"6. Representation. A representation of the requirements calculus or of a\n"},{"number":1894,"text":"   binding in a_c, the axiomatic calculus of\n"},{"number":1895,"text":"   [AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md), prescribes no executor and\n"},{"number":1896,"text":"   does not establish execution conformance by structural validation alone\n"},{"number":1897,"text":"   ([AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)).\n"},{"number":1898,"text":"   An a_c model of a human process that passes structural validation\n"},{"number":1899,"text":"   neither selects an automated executor nor shows that the process meets\n"},{"number":1900,"text":"   its requirements; execution conformance needs its own evidence under\n"},{"number":1901,"text":"   rule 4 (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":1902,"text":"7. A mapping from one account to\n"},{"number":1908,"text":"   another is a transformation: what it preserves, the law that licenses\n"},{"number":1909,"text":"   it, and whether it is exact or approximate with its adequacy relation\n"},{"number":1910,"text":"   and end-to-end bound, are stated and discharged under\n"},{"number":1911,"text":"   [ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement), and where it is\n"},{"number":1912,"text":"   recorded in a_c its record is\n"},{"number":1913,"text":"   [AC-013](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-013-transformation). A project may add `planned` or\n"},{"number":218,"text":"`cancelled`; those states do not replace close review.\n"},{"number":219,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":233,"heading":"TICKETS/3. It may not batch away intake triage:\n"},{"number":229,"text":"substantive included tickets still record their lawful `change_class` and\n"},{"number":230,"text":"`re_entry_point` (§4, Triage metadata). Manifest-local iteration entries\n"},{"number":231,"text":"may rely on the sprint's declared class only while they remain inside the\n"},{"number":232,"text":"sprint scope and excluded boundaries (P4b).\n"},{"number":233,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":260,"heading":"TICKETS/3. Deferred compliance is not\n"},{"number":241,"text":"silent debt: it is escrow held by the sprint, and\n"},{"number":242,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#sprint-execution-boundary) states that\n"},{"number":243,"text":"escrow satisfies no method, release or product closure until paid down,\n"},{"number":244,"text":"accepted or repriced (P2, P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":245,"text":"\n"},{"number":246,"text":"The following may be eligible for escrow when the governing method allows\n"},{"number":247,"text":"it: screenshots or\n"},{"number":248,"text":"walkthrough capture; visual review; accessibility cleanup; replay proof for\n"},{"number":249,"text":"product-meaningful user-interface interactions; design wording cleanup; trace cleanup;\n"},{"number":250,"text":"local realisation cleanup. The following may not be hidden in escrow: new\n"},{"number":251,"text":"product truth; new\n"},{"number":252,"text":"or changed data contracts; new runtime, governance, closure, provenance or\n"},{"number":253,"text":"evidence semantics; missing constructive carriers; changed public\n"},{"number":254,"text":"published-function or public carrier contracts; law-changing work that\n"},{"number":255,"text":"needs `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice`, `product_reprice`,\n"},{"number":256,"text":"`requirement_reprice` or `design_reframe`. If one of those appears during\n"},{"number":257,"text":"the sprint, the sprint records the finding and the work exits the sprint\n"},{"number":258,"text":"path through a standalone ticket, a repricing action or sprint supersession\n"},{"number":259,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":260,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":324,"heading":"TICKETS/3. Sprint rules/Close review","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F3.%20Sprint%20rules%2FClose%20review","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"33c990decea01bb9b815dc2d50cfc53fc5f7e4c897865328740e241df5dc0e87","start_line":261,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":261,"text":"### Close review\n"},{"number":262,"text":"\n"},{"number":263,"text":"Sprint close begins by moving the manifest to `status: closing`. While\n"},{"number":264,"text":"closing: new iteration inside that sprint is frozen; every included ticket\n"},{"number":265,"text":"or iteration entry is reviewed against the manifest; accumulated evidence\n"},{"number":266,"text":"is checked for durability; changed surfaces are walked against cited\n"},{"number":267,"text":"authority; deferred compliance is classified; paydown tickets are opened\n"},{"number":268,"text":"where debt must survive past the close review (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":269,"text":"\n"},{"number":270,"text":"Each reviewed item is classified as one of `accepted` (compliant under the\n"},{"number":271,"text":"sprint authority), `local_paydown` (local debt remains and is captured by a\n"},{"number":272,"text":"paydown ticket), `design_reframe` (the work needs design repricing),\n"},{"number":273,"text":"`requirement_reprice` (the work needs requirement repricing),\n"},{"number":274,"text":"`product_reprice` (the work changes product definition) or `remove` (the\n"},{"number":275,"text":"work should be backed out or kept out of closure) (P5). A sprint may move to\n"},{"number":276,"text":"`closed` only when every item and every debt entry is classified and the\n"},{"number":277,"text":"resulting paydown or repricing work is durable. Sprint close can accept\n"},{"number":278,"text":"local paydown debt only when the governing method allows that debt to\n"},{"number":279,"text":"survive as explicit follow-up; it cannot accept hidden authority drift\n"},{"number":280,"text":"(P6).\n"},{"number":281,"text":"\n"},{"number":282,"text":"Close classifications and the core. A close classification is the\n"},{"number":283,"text":"outcome of close review for one reviewed item, made against the sprint\n"},{"number":284,"text":"authority the manifest cites; the close review must classify, under that\n"},{"number":285,"text":"authority. The classification uses\n"},{"number":286,"text":"[ACTIVATION §3 Disposition](ACTIVATION.md#disposition) only for its\n"},{"number":287,"text":"result mapping: the candidate is the reviewed item, its boundary is the\n"},{"number":288,"text":"sprint's close under the cited authority, and the classification consumes\n"},{"number":289,"text":"the core results of the item's review and stays separate from them, as\n"},{"number":290,"text":"acceptance stays separate from assessment\n"},{"number":291,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)). Each classification\n"},{"number":292,"text":"takes exactly one core value, for the predicate \"the reviewed item is\n"},{"number":293,"text":"accepted as compliant under the sprint authority\", and the table names\n"},{"number":294,"text":"the disposition whose condition it matches, where one does (P5, P6):\n"},{"number":295,"text":"\n"},{"number":296,"text":"| Classification | Matching disposition | Core value | Ground, and how it narrows or differs from the disposition's condition |\n"},{"number":297,"text":"|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":298,"text":"| `accepted` | `accept` | satisfied | the item is compliant under the sprint authority |\n"},{"number":299,"text":"| `local_paydown` | `local_repair` | falsified | local debt remains and is captured by a paydown ticket; the debt is the counterexample. The governing relation stays coherent, because an item whose governing authority must change takes a repricing classification instead. It differs from `local_repair` in where the repair is carried: by the paydown ticket, which survives the close where the method allows that debt to survive |\n"},{"number":300,"text":"| `design_reframe` | `re_enter` | invalid_basis | the accepted design that governs the item must change, so the authority the sprint cites cannot support accepting it |\n"},{"number":301,"text":"| `requirement_reprice` | `re_enter` | invalid_basis | a governing requirement must change, with the same consequence |\n"},{"number":302,"text":"| `product_reprice` | `re_enter` | invalid_basis | the work changes the product definition, which the authority the sprint cites cannot support |\n"},{"number":303,"text":"| `remove` | none | falsified | the work is backed out or kept out of closure; the reason for removal is the counterexample. No disposition of ACTIVATION §3 has this condition, because removal does not require a violated governing relation or a competing truth path |\n"},{"number":304,"text":"\n"},{"number":305,"text":"The layer that `design_reframe`, `requirement_reprice` and\n"},{"number":306,"text":"`product_reprice` name is a declared fact, not a further result: it is\n"},{"number":307,"text":"the change class of [SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) at\n"},{"number":308,"text":"which the work re-enters, and it travels with the core value as the\n"},{"number":309,"text":"domain outcome (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Recording). The outcome of a\n"},{"number":310,"text":"debt entry, accepted, ticketed, repriced or removed (Sprint status,\n"},{"number":311,"text":"`closed`), is likewise classified by the close review and mapped at the\n"},{"number":312,"text":"close boundary, for the predicate \"the debt entry is accepted under the\n"},{"number":313,"text":"sprint authority\": accepted matches `accept` (`satisfied`), ticketed\n"},{"number":314,"text":"matches `local_repair` (`falsified`), removed takes `falsified` with no\n"},{"number":315,"text":"matching disposition, and repriced matches `re_enter`\n"},{"number":316,"text":"(`invalid_basis`), on the grounds of `accepted`, `local_paydown`,\n"},{"number":317,"text":"`remove` and the repricing classifications respectively. The mappings\n"},{"number":318,"text":"add no disposition and no core value. The condition for `closed`\n"},{"number":319,"text":"above requires an outcome for every item and debt entry, not a\n"},{"number":320,"text":"`satisfied` one. \n"},{"number":321,"text":"Purpose and material relation: a consumer that combines close outcomes\n"},{"number":322,"text":"with other results cannot read remaining debt, needed repricing or\n"},{"number":323,"text":"removal as compliance (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":324,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":326,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/One durable record per ticket","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FOne%20durable%20record%20per%20ticket","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"ec86e51e8af1f7a46ecd388a187e38a27df14dde5bc3634b18f459486cac0427","start_line":327,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":327,"text":"### One durable record per ticket\n"},{"number":328,"text":"\n"},{"number":329,"text":"Each ticket has one durable authoritative record; the default carrier is\n"},{"number":330,"text":"one markdown file. A repository or external tracker carrier is lawful only\n"},{"number":331,"text":"when it preserves the required ticket contract, history, state transition,\n"},{"number":332,"text":"stable identity, searchability and closure semantics without a co-equal\n"},{"number":333,"text":"local copy (P3, P4b). For a local\n"},{"number":334,"text":"file, the filename should carry a stable id and a short slug. Recommended\n"},{"number":335,"text":"local-file naming:\n"},{"number":336,"text":"`T-001-add-product-layer.md`, `B-002-fix-reset-manifest-id.md`,\n"},{"number":337,"text":"`S-003-evaluate-integration-capability.md`,\n"},{"number":338,"text":"`C-004-clean-up-trace-tags.md`.\n"},{"number":339,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":386,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Multi-build-tenant independence","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FMulti-build-tenant%20independence","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"16e37dffd298e0a19ec78869656b90150ca21b3bf6e0577d6e6b4235660daa55","start_line":340,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":340,"text":"### Multi-build-tenant independence\n"},{"number":341,"text":"\n"},{"number":342,"text":"This clause consumes the build-tenancy bounded context\n"},{"number":343,"text":"`urn:stdo:bounded-context:build-tenancy` declared by PRODUCT_DEFINITION §8.\n"},{"number":344,"text":"This member owns the multi-build-tenant work-item and ticket-lifecycle\n"},{"number":345,"text":"relation inside that context; it does not redefine build-tenant identity or\n"},{"number":346,"text":"realisation meaning (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":347,"text":"\n"},{"number":348,"text":"A multi-build-tenant work item is one admitted upstream work item with more\n"},{"number":349,"text":"than one build-tenant execution line. The upstream authority and each\n"},{"number":350,"text":"tenant-local ticket retain distinct identities and lifecycles. If one\n"},{"number":351,"text":"source, product or design work item must be realised in more than one build\n"},{"number":352,"text":"tenant, its tenant realisations are not tracked inside one ticket\n"},{"number":353,"text":"lifecycle. The rule governs backlog and active tickets; it is not\n"},{"number":354,"text":"retroactive for completed tickets unless a completed ticket is reopened or\n"},{"number":355,"text":"explicitly repriced. It does not make every ticket multi-tenant: tenant\n"},{"number":356,"text":"duplication is used only when the same admitted work item genuinely has\n"},{"number":357,"text":"more than one tenant execution line (P3).\n"},{"number":358,"text":"\n"},{"number":359,"text":"The three lawful cases: an upstream-only ticket (source, product or design\n"},{"number":360,"text":"authority only; no tenant duplicate yet); a single-tenant ticket (one\n"},{"number":361,"text":"tenant-local execution line; no sibling duplicate required); a multi-tenant\n"},{"number":362,"text":"work item (one upstream authority ticket and one suffixed tenant-local\n"},{"number":363,"text":"ticket per tenant execution line). For the multi-tenant case: keep the\n"},{"number":364,"text":"upstream source, product or design ticket as its own authority surface;\n"},{"number":365,"text":"duplicate the work item into one tenant-local ticket per build tenant;\n"},{"number":366,"text":"append a build-tenant mnemonic to the base ticket id and filename; keep\n"},{"number":367,"text":"status, proof, closure and reopen logic independent for each tenant.\n"},{"number":368,"text":"Recommended examples: `B-030-publish-capability-profile...` as the\n"},{"number":369,"text":"source ticket,\n"},{"number":370,"text":"`B-030-T1-publish-capability-profile...` and\n"},{"number":371,"text":"`B-030-T2-publish-capability-profile...` as the tenant tickets.\n"},{"number":372,"text":"\n"},{"number":373,"text":"The law: one ticket does not claim closure for more than one build-tenant\n"},{"number":374,"text":"lifecycle; a tenant-local blocker or false closure in one tenant is not\n"},{"number":375,"text":"hidden by green status in another; tenant-local proof, repricing and\n"},{"number":376,"text":"reopening remain tenant-local (P3, P6). If a tenant-local duplicate\n"},{"number":377,"text":"exists, it should record `source_ticket` and `build_tenant`. The\n"},{"number":378,"text":"`build_tenant` value identifies the\n"},{"number":379,"text":"applicable entry in the product's `how.build_tenants` definition; a path\n"},{"number":380,"text":"name, display alias or tracker label does not replace that identity unless\n"},{"number":381,"text":"the product definition binds it as the identity. The unsuffixed base ticket\n"},{"number":382,"text":"may remain the upstream product or design authority. If the work item is\n"},{"number":383,"text":"multi-tenant, tenant execution and closure for backlog and active work live\n"},{"number":384,"text":"on the suffixed duplicates; if it is single-tenant, no sibling duplicate is\n"},{"number":385,"text":"required.\n"},{"number":386,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":407,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Required fields","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FRequired%20fields","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"53f0aa90552029aa7e49134b6585bebcae51fa8aefe78d3503545fd171896751","start_line":387,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":387,"text":"### Required fields\n"},{"number":388,"text":"\n"},{"number":389,"text":"Each ticket records at least `id`, `title`, `type`, `ticket_category`,\n"},{"number":390,"text":"`status`, `goal`, `change_intent`, `change_class`, `re_entry_point`,\n"},{"number":391,"text":"`triaged_at`, `created_at` and `updated_at` (P4b, P3). Recommended additional fields: `priority`,\n"},{"number":392,"text":"`dependencies`, `links`, `intake_source`, `affected_boundary`,\n"},{"number":393,"text":"`source_ticket` when the ticket duplicates or derives from another ticket,\n"},{"number":394,"text":"and `build_tenant` when the ticket is tenant-local.\n"},{"number":395,"text":"\n"},{"number":396,"text":"For `ticket_category: implementation_migration` the ticket also carries\n"},{"number":397,"text":"`migration_strategy` and `library_usage`; `governing_library` when\n"},{"number":398,"text":"`library_usage` is `consume` or `extend`; and `library_rationale` when\n"},{"number":399,"text":"`library_usage` is `none` (§6). A tenant-local implementation migration\n"},{"number":400,"text":"also carries `build_tenant`, and `source_ticket` when it duplicates or\n"},{"number":401,"text":"derives from an upstream source, product or design ticket.\n"},{"number":402,"text":"\n"},{"number":403,"text":"For execution-contract admission the runtime-drafted contract should also\n"},{"number":404,"text":"carry, at minimum, `target_truth`, `superseded_truth` when relevant,\n"},{"number":405,"text":"`closure_law`, `evaluation_criteria`, `non_closure_conditions` and\n"},{"number":406,"text":"`proof_surface` (§5).\n"},{"number":407,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":414,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Types","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FTypes","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"0e76a7066ccccc3c71e071f53b5359832c7e022ff7881d89d7d515737837a587","start_line":408,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":408,"text":"### Types\n"},{"number":409,"text":"\n"},{"number":410,"text":"The minimum common set of ticket types is `feature`, `bug`, `spike` and\n"},{"number":411,"text":"`chore`. A project may add more; the default set should be enough for\n"},{"number":412,"text":"most cases\n"},{"number":413,"text":"(P3).\n"},{"number":414,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":429,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Category","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FCategory","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"38b57140e8797e7666363f8114ec4fa8da93dec432fcf13c63438b2304f07388","start_line":415,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":415,"text":"### Category\n"},{"number":416,"text":"\n"},{"number":417,"text":"Ticket category is orthogonal to ticket type: type answers what kind of\n"},{"number":418,"text":"work record this is; category answers what execution or migration\n"},{"number":419,"text":"discipline governs the ticket (P3, P1). The minimum\n"},{"number":420,"text":"common set is `ordinary` and `implementation_migration`, so a `feature`,\n"},{"number":421,"text":"`bug`, `spike` or `chore` may carry either. `implementation_migration` is\n"},{"number":422,"text":"used when the ticket is not \"change code until tests pass\" but a governed\n"},{"number":423,"text":"replacement of one implementation truth path with another across producers,\n"},{"number":424,"text":"consumers, projections and proof surfaces: a bug ticket that replaces an old\n"},{"number":425,"text":"tracker or read-model family with one new authoritative carrier; a feature\n"},{"number":426,"text":"ticket that introduces a new public interface and requires every producer\n"},{"number":427,"text":"and consumer to migrate before closure; a refactor ticket that removes a\n"},{"number":428,"text":"bridge path or compatibility facade from an authoritative contract family.\n"},{"number":429,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":445,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Inside-out sequencing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FInside-out%20sequencing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"de25586f41cf86d9ab367c9c707fa0eb485b8e9fdd41939f1a8113a5fa6f56cb","start_line":430,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":430,"text":"### Inside-out sequencing\n"},{"number":431,"text":"\n"},{"number":432,"text":"For `ticket_category: implementation_migration`, ticket sequencing reflects\n"},{"number":433,"text":"the inside-out rule of\n"},{"number":434,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §7](SPEC_METHOD.md#inside-out-first-sequencing) (P4b, P6). Tickets that publish or admit\n"},{"number":435,"text":"the new authoritative source carrier are the upstream tickets in the wave.\n"},{"number":436,"text":"Tickets that harden prompt assembly, projections, reports, dossiers, review\n"},{"number":437,"text":"surfaces or other downstream consumers depend on those upstream source\n"},{"number":438,"text":"tickets. A downstream ticket may carry exploratory work while the source\n"},{"number":439,"text":"ticket is active, but that work is non-closure evidence until the source\n"},{"number":440,"text":"carrier is admitted and authoritative. A downstream ticket does not close\n"},{"number":441,"text":"while its upstream source-carrier ticket remains open. When one migration\n"},{"number":442,"text":"wave introduces a new source carrier and then its prompt, projection or\n"},{"number":443,"text":"read-model consumers, the dependency chain runs `source carrier ->\n"},{"number":444,"text":"downstream consumers`, never the reverse.\n"},{"number":445,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":467,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Change class","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FChange%20class","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"333ed79e25c2aa34728f97c8c2d2150f472cfb623b36da5f017ba06a0aacbf84","start_line":446,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":446,"text":"### Change class\n"},{"number":447,"text":"\n"},{"number":448,"text":"Ticket type and change class are orthogonal: type answers what kind of\n"},{"number":449,"text":"work record this is; change class answers where the change lawfully\n"},{"number":450,"text":"re-enters the constitutional chain. A ticket records the `change_class`\n"},{"number":451,"text":"declared by intake triage, using the classes of\n"},{"number":452,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) (P4b, P2).\n"},{"number":453,"text":"\n"},{"number":454,"text":"Common pairings: `feature` with `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice`,\n"},{"number":455,"text":"`product_reprice`, `requirement_reprice` or `design_reframe`; `bug` with\n"},{"number":456,"text":"`requirement_reprice`, `design_reframe` or `realization_refactor`; `chore`\n"},{"number":457,"text":"with `design_reframe` or `realization_refactor`; `spike` as exploratory\n"},{"number":458,"text":"work that still carries the current triage class and should terminate\n"},{"number":459,"text":"either in a more specific downstream ticket or in an explicit decision\n"},{"number":460,"text":"that no further substantive change is required.\n"},{"number":461,"text":"\n"},{"number":462,"text":"Ticket category and change class are also orthogonal: `change_class`\n"},{"number":463,"text":"governs lawful constitutional re-entry; `ticket_category` governs ticket\n"},{"number":464,"text":"execution and closure discipline. A ticket may therefore be `type: bug`,\n"},{"number":465,"text":"`ticket_category: implementation_migration`, `change_class: design_reframe`\n"},{"number":466,"text":"without contradiction (P3).\n"},{"number":467,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":507,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Upward propagation check","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FUpward%20propagation%20check","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"6b07cc59a69d2d6c7c19d53089ca6d7828266f084a6ded0b7a0b858599bacc8d","start_line":468,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":468,"text":"### Upward propagation check\n"},{"number":469,"text":"\n"},{"number":470,"text":"Triage consumes the computed classification of\n"},{"number":471,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment) for\n"},{"number":472,"text":"the declared owner and layer traversal, the complete relevant public\n"},{"number":473,"text":"membership and value delta, the accepted-design scope and trace coverage,\n"},{"number":474,"text":"and the rule-determined treatment. The owning work carrier references that\n"},{"number":475,"text":"exact result and its residuals; a new role does not repeat an unchanged\n"},{"number":476,"text":"walk (P4b, P2).\n"},{"number":477,"text":"\n"},{"number":478,"text":"Before declaring `realization_refactor` for a bug, establish that the\n"},{"number":479,"text":"current requirement and the accepted realising design govern the affected\n"},{"number":480,"text":"behaviour and remain sufficient for the authorised outcome. Their presence\n"},{"number":481,"text":"proves no coverage. Missing or ambiguous evidence leaves the affected\n"},{"number":482,"text":"treatment unknown; it is not proof that the governing layer itself is\n"},{"number":483,"text":"absent (P6).\n"},{"number":484,"text":"\n"},{"number":485,"text":"The re-entry rule is SPEC_METHOD §4's: the\n"},{"number":486,"text":"[change classes](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes) with their re-entry\n"},{"number":487,"text":"points, and the smallest lawful re-entry that step 4 of\n"},{"number":488,"text":"[Computed classification and treatment](SPEC_METHOD.md#computed-classification-and-treatment)\n"},{"number":489,"text":"exposes, with the paragraph after the four steps: a candidate's public\n"},{"number":490,"text":"violation does not select a new contract, and the governing owner is\n"},{"number":491,"text":"re-entered only for an explicitly changed desired outcome or an\n"},{"number":492,"text":"established governing insufficiency. For a bug, this check\n"},{"number":493,"text":"refines that rule into an upward walk from the realised surface that\n"},{"number":494,"text":"checks each layer and stops at the highest layer found missing or\n"},{"number":495,"text":"insufficient for the authorised outcome, and the class is the one that\n"},{"number":496,"text":"re-enters there:\n"},{"number":497,"text":"\n"},{"number":498,"text":"| Where the walk stops | Change class | Action |\n"},{"number":499,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":500,"text":"| the governing requirement is missing or insufficient | `requirement_reprice` | re-enter the requirement's owner |\n"},{"number":501,"text":"| the requirement is sufficient, and the realising design is missing or insufficient | `design_reframe` | re-enter Design |\n"},{"number":502,"text":"| an actual upstream Goal, Intent or Product change | `goal_reprice`, `intent_reprice` or `product_reprice` | follow the change to its owner rather than stopping at a familiar file |\n"},{"number":503,"text":"| the current requirement and accepted design suffice, and the implementation deviates | `realization_refactor` | repair or reject the candidate |\n"},{"number":504,"text":"\n"},{"number":505,"text":"Unresolved meaning remains J and a reserved choice remains O, as that\n"},{"number":506,"text":"paragraph states (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":507,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":516,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Triage metadata","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FTriage%20metadata","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"46b6aac6dab500d7eb9f7fe6a408ecc8194762389681e0c960b784016b4d12b3","start_line":508,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":508,"text":"### Triage metadata\n"},{"number":509,"text":"\n"},{"number":510,"text":"Because tickets are the durable authority surface for work tracking, a\n"},{"number":511,"text":"ticket for substantive work carries the minimum metadata required by the\n"},{"number":512,"text":"intake triage of [SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#universal-intake-triage):\n"},{"number":513,"text":"the declared `change_intent`, the lawful `change_class`, the lawful\n"},{"number":514,"text":"`re_entry_point`, and when triage occurred in `triaged_at` (P4b, P2). The recorded values are those intake triage declared\n"},{"number":515,"text":"(Change class and Upward propagation check above).\n"},{"number":516,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":535,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Ticket rules/Status","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md#TICKETS%2F4.%20Ticket%20rules%2FStatus","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","sha256":"be47599b7605c08341618c1a27a9b5cece5061c400a212479a7788154e2e21d5","start_line":517,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/TICKETS.md","lines":[{"number":517,"text":"### Status\n"},{"number":518,"text":"\n"},{"number":519,"text":"The minimum ticket status model is `backlog`, `active` and `completed`. A\n"},{"number":520,"text":"project may add `blocked`, `cancelled` or other explicit local states; the\n"},{"number":521,"text":"base method starts with the three (P5, P3).\n"},{"number":522,"text":"\n"},{"number":523,"text":"The ticket statuses, any local state a project adds, the lanes below, the\n"},{"number":524,"text":"sprint statuses of §3 and the `migration_strategy` and `library_usage`\n"},{"number":525,"text":"values of §6 are declared states of their carriers, not results, and map\n"},{"number":526,"text":"to no core value; the recorded `change_class` is a declared state under\n"},{"number":527,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §4](SPEC_METHOD.md#change-classes). The close\n"},{"number":528,"text":"classifications and debt-entry outcomes of §3\n"},{"number":529,"text":"Close review are results, mapped there. An evaluation that reads a\n"},{"number":530,"text":"declared state returns its own core value with its predicate under\n"},{"number":531,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Purpose and material\n"},{"number":532,"text":"relation: a declared state is never combined as an evaluation result, so\n"},{"number":533,"text":"a ticket marked `completed`, or a sprint marked `closed`, cannot stand in\n"},{"number":534,"text":"for a `satisfied` result (P5, P1).\n"},{"number":535,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":578,"heading":"TICKETS/4. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no\n"},{"number":542,"text":"findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may\n"},{"number":543,"text":"carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).\n"},{"number":544,"text":"\n"},{"number":545,"text":"The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact\n"},{"number":546,"text":"artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a\n"},{"number":547,"text":"lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or\n"},{"number":548,"text":"closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility\n"},{"number":549,"text":"restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the\n"},{"number":550,"text":"same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The\n"},{"number":551,"text":"Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to\n"},{"number":552,"text":"its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces\n"},{"number":553,"text":"nothing and grants no additional read (P6).\n"},{"number":554,"text":"\n"},{"number":555,"text":"After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work\n"},{"number":556,"text":"item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,\n"},{"number":557,"text":"original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,\n"},{"number":558,"text":"source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical\n"},{"number":559,"text":"finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session\n"},{"number":560,"text":"index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work\n"},{"number":561,"text":"to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).\n"},{"number":562,"text":"\n"},{"number":563,"text":"| Item state | Required trace |\n"},{"number":564,"text":"|---|---|\n"},{"number":565,"text":"| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |\n"},{"number":566,"text":"| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |\n"},{"number":567,"text":"| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |\n"},{"number":568,"text":"\n"},{"number":569,"text":"These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required\n"},{"number":570,"text":"recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is\n"},{"number":571,"text":"available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when\n"},{"number":572,"text":"the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is\n"},{"number":573,"text":"[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).\n"},{"number":574,"text":"Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or\n"},{"number":575,"text":"transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.\n"},{"number":576,"text":"Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,\n"},{"number":577,"text":"P4b).\n"},{"number":578,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":592,"heading":"TICKETS/4. The required lifetime of the work or obligation selects the\n"},{"number":676,"text":"smallest lawful source carrier: first establish the applicable upstream\n"},{"number":677,"text":"work authority, then select the first matching row below. For work inside\n"},{"number":678,"text":"an admitted sprint the local carrier boundary is that sprint; otherwise it\n"},{"number":679,"text":"is the current run (P2, P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":680,"text":"\n"},{"number":681,"text":"| Condition | Execution-contract source | Durable-ticket decision |\n"},{"number":682,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":683,"text":"| no applicable upstream work authority exists | no execution contract is admitted | do not create a ticket as substitute authority; stop or re-enter |\n"},{"number":684,"text":"| applicable authority exists and an existing admitted ticket covers the exact work | derive the run-scoped contract from that ticket | reuse it; do not create another ticket |\n"},{"number":685,"text":"| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work or an open obligation needs independent state beyond the local carrier boundary | one durable ticket plus the run-scoped contract | create or update the ticket only under ticket-state authority |\n"},{"number":686,"text":"| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket covers the work, and the work stays inside one admitted sprint with no state required after sprint close | the sprint manifest plus one manifest-local iteration entry | do not create a durable ticket |\n"},{"number":687,"text":"| applicable authority exists, no exact admitted ticket or sprint covers the work, and the work ends in the current run with no independent surviving state | an intake-drafted run-scoped contract | do not create a durable ticket |\n"},{"number":688,"text":"\n"},{"number":689,"text":"\"Ticket-shaped\" describes the categorisation, closure criteria, proof\n"},{"number":690,"text":"surface, non-closure conditions and the other required execution-contract\n"},{"number":691,"text":"fields (§4, Required fields). It creates no durable ticket identity and no\n"},{"number":692,"text":"ticket-lane state (P3).\n"},{"number":693,"text":"\n"},{"number":694,"text":"Absence of a durable ticket neither requires nor authorises creating one.\n"},{"number":695,"text":"An exact product-authorised work instruction may supply the upstream work\n"},{"number":696,"text":"authority for a one-run contract; a generic request or a model-widened\n"},{"number":697,"text":"scope cannot. A durable ticket is created or updated only when the table\n"},{"number":698,"text":"requires surviving state and the actor holds ticket-state authority. An\n"},{"number":699,"text":"explicit instruction from ticket-state authority to create a durable record\n"},{"number":700,"text":"selects that durability; it does not admit an execution contract or widen\n"},{"number":701,"text":"its upstream work authority (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":702,"text":"\n"},{"number":703,"text":"The step side of admission is [ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#admission) and\n"},{"number":704,"text":"is defined there once: drafting versus admission inside one invocation, the\n"},{"number":705,"text":"condition under which execution may begin, what admission may never be\n"},{"number":706,"text":"inferred from (including ticket or sprint presence, lane placement and\n"},{"number":707,"text":"`active` status), the coordinates an admitted result carries, the recording\n"},{"number":708,"text":"of every result, withheld closure and residual obligation before return,\n"},{"number":709,"text":"and refusal when no durable result and evidence surface is available. This\n"},{"number":710,"text":"member adds the carrier side (P6, P4b). The admission mechanism and the\n"},{"number":711,"text":"durable result and evidence surface are the ones the product definition\n"},{"number":712,"text":"binds. When that surface is the ticket or the sprint manifest, the admitted\n"},{"number":713,"text":"result with its coordinates is recorded there. A carrier's lane, status or\n"},{"number":714,"text":"prose that asserts admission without those coordinates is not admission\n"},{"number":715,"text":"evidence, and the contract it describes remains drafted or rejected.\n"},{"number":716,"text":"\n"},{"number":717,"text":"When admission is absent or rejected, ACTIVATION §1 returns the missing\n"},{"number":718,"text":"work authority without execution. Before that return, an obligation that\n"},{"number":719,"text":"must survive the run is carried as follows (P4b, P6): it becomes a\n"},{"number":720,"text":"sprint-local entry when its lifetime stays inside the admitted sprint;\n"},{"number":721,"text":"otherwise it is recorded as a durable ticket, only under ticket-state\n"},{"number":722,"text":"authority; where that authority is absent, it is retained in the\n"},{"number":723,"text":"contract's named durable result and evidence surface or in an\n"},{"number":724,"text":"already-authorised enclosing carrier, closure is marked withheld on\n"},{"number":725,"text":"ticket-state authority, and the required re-entry is returned.\n"},{"number":726,"text":"\n"},{"number":727,"text":"Execution and closure use the same admitted categorisation, criteria,\n"},{"number":728,"text":"proof surface and non-closure conditions. The resulting state still flows\n"},{"number":729,"text":"through proof, gap analysis and repricing (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":730,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":754,"heading":"TICKETS/5. An admitted execution contract\n"},{"number":737,"text":"should be recorded on the selected durable work carrier, including an event log\n"},{"number":738,"text":"where the execution binding requires one. It is available to prompt assembly\n"},{"number":739,"text":"where applicable, and to later closure checking, so that execution and\n"},{"number":740,"text":"closure read the same admitted basis. A binding that requires an event log\n"},{"number":741,"text":"still requires that log; a human or mixed binding may select another durable\n"},{"number":742,"text":"carrier under [SPEC_METHOD §11](SPEC_METHOD.md#11-build-tenant-binding)\n"},{"number":743,"text":"(P6, P4b). The refusal of self-certification\n"},{"number":744,"text":"is ACTIVATION §1.\n"},{"number":745,"text":"\n"},{"number":746,"text":"Admission validates a contract against its cited product outcome,\n"},{"number":747,"text":"prerequisite or experiment basis and does not admit that basis (ACTIVATION\n"},{"number":748,"text":"§1). Admission or renewal of the basis belongs to the authority owning the\n"},{"number":749,"text":"selected goals work wave, or its explicitly bounded proxy, and stays\n"},{"number":750,"text":"durably legible in the existing goals or ticket authority\n"},{"number":751,"text":"([SPEC_METHOD §3](SPEC_METHOD.md#3-outcome-conservation)). A ticket's\n"},{"number":752,"text":"`active` status, its lane, or an admitted or retained contract is therefore\n"},{"number":753,"text":"never the admission of a growth basis (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":754,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":776,"heading":"TICKETS/5. At minimum it should make `evaluation_criteria` and\n"},{"number":760,"text":"`non_closure_conditions` visible. These are the local gain function for\n"},{"number":761,"text":"the work (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":762,"text":"\n"},{"number":763,"text":"For implementation migrations, typical non-closure conditions are: the old\n"},{"number":764,"text":"authoritative path still passes in normal execution within the declared\n"},{"number":765,"text":"affected scope; mixed old and new proof is still accepted; a proxy or\n"},{"number":766,"text":"partial interface implementation still stands in the acceptance path;\n"},{"number":767,"text":"competing or ambiguous executable authority remains reachable on the\n"},{"number":768,"text":"claimed product acceptance path; ticket wording, product wording and proof\n"},{"number":769,"text":"wording are not reconciled. These conditions are not optional commentary;\n"},{"number":770,"text":"they are the anti-self-deception surface for execution (P6).\n"},{"number":771,"text":"\n"},{"number":772,"text":"Residual implementation debt outside the claimed acceptance path is not by\n"},{"number":773,"text":"itself a non-closure condition. It may be deferred only under the\n"},{"number":774,"text":"path-relative authority and explicit disposition rules of\n"},{"number":775,"text":"[SPEC_METHOD §7](SPEC_METHOD.md#constitutional-migration-options) (P2).\n"},{"number":776,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":795,"heading":"TICKETS/5. A ticket may use an\n"},{"number":781,"text":"unqualified term when its cited product, re-entry surface, execution basis\n"},{"number":782,"text":"and affected scope select exactly one bounded-context meaning (P1, P3).\n"},{"number":783,"text":"\n"},{"number":784,"text":"When a ticket spans contexts, or a material term has competing meanings,\n"},{"number":785,"text":"the ticket cites the applicable product-definition disambiguation or the\n"},{"number":786,"text":"owner-authorised import, translation, equivalence or disambiguation\n"},{"number":787,"text":"carrier; it may reference that relation rather than duplicate it. Ticket\n"},{"number":788,"text":"prose, actor familiarity, a matching glossary heading, tenant placement or\n"},{"number":789,"text":"comment context cannot select meaning or transfer authority (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":790,"text":"\n"},{"number":791,"text":"An unresolved or multiply resolved material term blocks execution-contract\n"},{"number":792,"text":"admission and closure for the affected claim. Opening or updating the\n"},{"number":793,"text":"ticket records the pressure and does not cure it; resolution re-enters at\n"},{"number":794,"text":"the authority that owns the missing context or semantic relation (P1, P5).\n"},{"number":795,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":797,"heading":"TICKETS/6.
