Process model\n"},{"number":242,"text":"\n"},{"number":243,"text":"The constitutional process model is the Elm Architecture (P0, P1):\n"},{"number":244,"text":"\n"},{"number":245,"text":"- State: the typed state shape, held by the runtime, not by the view;\n"},{"number":246,"text":"- Msg: the typed message algebra naming every action a user or system can\n"},{"number":247,"text":"  emit;\n"},{"number":248,"text":"- Update: the pure reducer of signature `(Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`; it\n"},{"number":249,"text":"  describes side effects as Cmd values and does not perform them;\n"},{"number":250,"text":"- View: the pure function of signature `State → ViewTree`; given the same\n"},{"number":251,"text":"  state, it produces the same output;\n"},{"number":252,"text":"- Cmd and Sub: typed descriptions of side effects to schedule and of\n"},{"number":253,"text":"  external sources to subscribe to, interpreted by the runtime at the\n"},{"number":254,"text":"  effect membrane.\n"},{"number":255,"text":"\n"},{"number":256,"text":"The runtime owns the loop (P0):\n"},{"number":257,"text":"\n"},{"number":258,"text":"`current State → render View → user emits Msg → Update produces new State and Cmds → runtime interprets Cmds → repeat`\n"},{"number":259,"text":"\n"},{"number":260,"text":"This loop is the Elm Architecture and the constitutional process model of\n"},{"number":261,"text":"UX work under this profile (P1).\n"},{"number":262,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":297,"heading":"UX/4. Process model/Process model without stack mandate","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F4.%20Process%20model%2FProcess%20model%20without%20stack%20mandate","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"e6dcbb46a03f7d4e73693733ea7e1a1242be6b92c6b813bc8e2cc4bc8c1811c5","start_line":263,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":263,"text":"### Process model without stack mandate\n"},{"number":264,"text":"\n"},{"number":265,"text":"The process model is the Elm Architecture; the implementation stack is\n"},{"number":266,"text":"the project's choice, recorded in its design module. This mirrors\n"},{"number":267,"text":"DESIGN_MODULE §4 Functional bias without language mandate: the process\n"},{"number":268,"text":"model is constitutional and not negotiable; the stack is project-local\n"},{"number":269,"text":"and free, provided it preserves the model (P1, P6). Any\n"},{"number":270,"text":"realisation that preserves §4 to §8 is compliant with this profile. This\n"},{"number":271,"text":"test differs from the test of §4 Realisation discretion; §15 states which\n"},{"number":272,"text":"test applies under §1 Authority's fail-closed rule, with the ambiguity\n"},{"number":273,"text":"retained for the governing authority.\n"},{"number":274,"text":"Examples (non-normative):\n"},{"number":275,"text":"\n"},{"number":276,"text":"- a language-integrated reducer runtime, which enables typed state,\n"},{"number":277,"text":"  message, update, command and view relations as native runtime\n"},{"number":278,"text":"  capabilities;\n"},{"number":279,"text":"- a typed reducer with an effect interpreter, which enables a\n"},{"number":280,"text":"  host-language UI stack to preserve pure update and an explicit effect\n"},{"number":281,"text":"  membrane;\n"},{"number":282,"text":"- a reactive-signal realisation behind a reducer, which enables reactive\n"},{"number":283,"text":"  projection while forbidding signal mutation outside the reducer;\n"},{"number":284,"text":"- a server-rendered hypermedia realisation, which enables server-side\n"},{"number":285,"text":"  state derivation as the reducer and uses the request and response\n"},{"number":286,"text":"  boundary as the effect membrane.\n"},{"number":287,"text":"\n"},{"number":288,"text":"Constitutionally rejected: any realisation that lets the view own state\n"},{"number":289,"text":"continuation, performs side effects in render code, mutates state outside\n"},{"number":290,"text":"a typed reducer, or carries multi-step view-local state machines that\n"},{"number":291,"text":"bypass Msg. Two-way binding without Msg emission, imperative DOM\n"},{"number":292,"text":"manipulation in render code, and effect handlers used as controllers are\n"},{"number":293,"text":"violations regardless of stack (P6). A project that selects a framework\n"},{"number":294,"text":"records the choice in its design module with a short justification of how\n"},{"number":295,"text":"the framework preserves the §4 process model. The profile does not rank\n"},{"number":296,"text":"frameworks; it tests realisations against §4 to §8 (P1).\n"},{"number":297,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":319,"heading":"UX/4. Process model/Realisation discretion","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F4.%20Process%20model%2FRealisation%20discretion","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"ce3fadfbd3b6f0b313463725cd8e911cf6d4b4b6faa63dcb9bc5aab810419bf8","start_line":298,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":298,"text":"### Realisation discretion\n"},{"number":299,"text":"\n"},{"number":300,"text":"The profile is opinionated about the process model and not about the\n"},{"number":301,"text":"realisation stack (P1, P2). The project\n"},{"number":302,"text":"chooses:\n"},{"number":303,"text":"\n"},{"number":304,"text":"- the language;\n"},{"number":305,"text":"- the framework or runtime;\n"},{"number":306,"text":"- the state-container library, if any;\n"},{"number":307,"text":"- the effect-interpreter mechanism;\n"},{"number":308,"text":"- the runtime validator, if any;\n"},{"number":309,"text":"- the build, bundling and deployment toolchain.\n"},{"number":310,"text":"\n"},{"number":311,"text":"The project records its choices in the design module with a short\n"},{"number":312,"text":"justification of how each choice preserves the §4 Elm process model and\n"},{"number":313,"text":"the §6 effect-membrane rule. The profile does not rank stacks; it tests\n"},{"number":314,"text":"realisations. A realisation is compliant with this profile when §4 to §10\n"},{"number":315,"text":"hold under inspection and the §13 failure patterns are absent (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":316,"text":"This test differs from the test of §4 Process model without stack\n"},{"number":317,"text":"mandate; §15 states which test applies under §1 Authority's fail-closed\n"},{"number":318,"text":"rule, with the ambiguity retained for the governing authority.\n"},{"number":319,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":369,"heading":"UX/5. State transitions","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F5.%20State%20transitions","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"d10ca223a671b7db5a9c67cf6ab2c259621d6da16f688277020c529da24845be","start_line":320,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":320,"text":"## 5. State transitions\n"},{"number":321,"text":"\n"},{"number":322,"text":"State changes through typed messages applied by the pure reducer, the\n"},{"number":323,"text":"Update of §4 (P4a, P1). A UX surface\n"},{"number":324,"text":"declares:\n"},{"number":325,"text":"\n"},{"number":326,"text":"- its State shape;\n"},{"number":327,"text":"- its Msg algebra;\n"},{"number":328,"text":"- its `Update : (Msg, State) → (State, Cmd)`;\n"},{"number":329,"text":"- its Cmd algebra;\n"},{"number":330,"text":"- its Sub algebra when the surface subscribes to external or runtime\n"},{"number":331,"text":"  events.\n"},{"number":332,"text":"\n"},{"number":333,"text":"Each Cmd declaration names (P5, P4b):\n"},{"number":334,"text":"\n"},{"number":335,"text":"- the effect kind;\n"},{"number":336,"text":"- the typed input payload;\n"},{"number":337,"text":"- the admitted carrier or external boundary it targets;\n"},{"number":338,"text":"- a typed outcome Msg family covering every materially possible observed\n"},{"number":339,"text":"  or unresolved outcome of the effect, including success and failure;\n"},{"number":340,"text":"- the evidence by which an outcome Msg is selected and the observations\n"},{"number":341,"text":"  required to resolve an uncertain outcome;\n"},{"number":342,"text":"- any deterministic correlation key required to connect the Cmd, its\n"},{"number":343,"text":"  invocation, outcome messages and replay.\n"},{"number":344,"text":"\n"},{"number":345,"text":"An outcome Msg represents the available effect evidence. For an intended\n"},{"number":346,"text":"effect, its meaning uses the three effect values of\n"},{"number":347,"text":"[ACTIVATION §3 Effects](ACTIVATION.md#effects): `completed`,\n"},{"number":348,"text":"`not_effected` and `completion_unknown`. These are effect results for\n"},{"number":349,"text":"the predicate \"the intended effect occurred\", not a replacement for the\n"},{"number":350,"text":"product's typed message vocabulary. A lost or failed transport reply alone\n"},{"number":351,"text":"establishes neither completion nor non-completion. Sufficient independent\n"},{"number":352,"text":"observations may decide the outcome; otherwise the message and State\n"},{"number":353,"text":"retain `completion_unknown`, its correlation and the missing observation\n"},{"number":354,"text":"(P5, P4b).\n"},{"number":355,"text":"\n"},{"number":356,"text":"The reducer is pure: it does not perform I/O, log to side channels or\n"},{"number":357,"text":"mutate global state. Effects scheduled by Cmd are interpreted by the\n"},{"number":358,"text":"runtime at the effect membrane (§6) (P0, P1).\n"},{"number":359,"text":"\n"},{"number":360,"text":"View-local ephemera (open or closed flags, hover state, draft input) may\n"},{"number":361,"text":"be held in implementation-local state cells where the framework provides\n"},{"number":362,"text":"them, but only when the value is genuinely view-local: not observed by\n"},{"number":363,"text":"other views, not part of the product's state surface, and not\n"},{"number":364,"text":"consequential after the view unmounts. Product-meaningful state goes\n"},{"number":365,"text":"through the reducer without exception (P6, P3). The discipline test for\n"},{"number":366,"text":"whether state belongs in the reducer or in view-local ephemera: if losing\n"},{"number":367,"text":"the value on unmount changes the product's behaviour or another part of\n"},{"number":368,"text":"the UI's view, it belongs in the reducer (P3).\n"},{"number":369,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":397,"heading":"UX/6. Effect membrane","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F6.%20Effect%20membrane","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"b2396946feb82cdbb55355afab589be95aa193aa54eae140af2c10dd9fe71538","start_line":370,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":370,"text":"## 6. Effect membrane\n"},{"number":371,"text":"\n"},{"number":372,"text":"Side effects are isolated to a declared effect membrane, which refines\n"},{"number":373,"text":"DESIGN_MODULE §10 Effect edge for UX surfaces (P0, P5). The membrane interprets Cmd values\n"},{"number":374,"text":"produced by the reducer and translates side-effect outcomes back into Msg\n"},{"number":375,"text":"values delivered to the reducer. Inside the membrane, I/O, subscriptions\n"},{"number":376,"text":"to external sources, and imperative interop with the host platform (DOM,\n"},{"number":377,"text":"file system, native APIs) are allowed. Outside it, in render code, in\n"},{"number":378,"text":"pure helpers consumed by render, and in the reducer, there is no I/O, no\n"},{"number":379,"text":"subscription and no imperative platform manipulation (P0).\n"},{"number":380,"text":"\n"},{"number":381,"text":"The membrane has one job: interpret declared Cmd values. It is not where\n"},{"number":382,"text":"logic lives. Branching, conditional state derivation and multi-step\n"},{"number":383,"text":"business decisions belong in the reducer; the membrane interprets a\n"},{"number":384,"text":"single declared Cmd per effect (P6). An unresolved outcome returns through\n"},{"number":385,"text":"the typed outcome Msg family; it is not converted into ordinary failure\n"},{"number":386,"text":"or success merely to keep the UI moving. Before a repeat or dependent\n"},{"number":387,"text":"effect whose safety depends on the outcome, the product observes the\n"},{"number":388,"text":"owning state and follows [ACTIVATION §5 Recovery](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart),\n"},{"number":389,"text":"with the current authority and effect territory retained. Recovery is an\n"},{"number":390,"text":"explicit Cmd/Msg interaction, not hidden membrane continuation (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":391,"text":"A platform-specific effect handler,\n"},{"number":392,"text":"whatever name the chosen framework gives it (`useEffect`,\n"},{"number":393,"text":"`createEffect`, `onMount`, `subscribe`, a server-action handler), is part\n"},{"number":394,"text":"of the membrane only when it interprets a declared Cmd. A handler that\n"},{"number":395,"text":"contains conditional logic deciding state transitions is a violation: the\n"},{"number":396,"text":"logic moves to the reducer, and the handler interprets one Cmd (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":397,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":436,"heading":"UX/7. Carrier binding","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F7.%20Carrier%20binding","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"5d7bfa21b81815ea924be3817a283ddee66a10d239f535d288b2636747200f7b","start_line":398,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":398,"text":"## 7. Carrier binding\n"},{"number":399,"text":"\n"},{"number":400,"text":"When the product publishes typed asset surfaces under the graph-execution\n"},{"number":401,"text":"profile's carrier law and the local product's design, a UX surface binds\n"},{"number":402,"text":"to one or more AssetSurface contracts as its data source and action\n"},{"number":403,"text":"target (P6, P3). Binding requirements:\n"},{"number":404,"text":"\n"},{"number":405,"text":"- the surface's State is derived from AssetSurface projections, not from\n"},{"number":406,"text":"  a UX-local re-declaration of the asset shape;\n"},{"number":407,"text":"- its product-truth-changing Msg variants map one to one to AssetSurface\n"},{"number":408,"text":"  action-registry entries, or wrap them through a documented projection\n"},{"number":409,"text":"  with no hidden semantic change;\n"},{"number":410,"text":"- UX-local Msg variants are reserved for view-local concerns (open or\n"},{"number":411,"text":"  closed, sort order, filter input);\n"},{"number":412,"text":"- selection within the surface emits a Context update, or equivalent,\n"},{"number":413,"text":"  consistent with the product's selection contract;\n"},{"number":414,"text":"- writes from the surface go through the AssetSurface action registry,\n"},{"number":415,"text":"  not through direct file or service calls.\n"},{"number":416,"text":"\n"},{"number":417,"text":"This is the rule that produces strong functional consistency between\n"},{"number":418,"text":"front end and back end: the same typed contract is the ground truth on\n"},{"number":419,"text":"both sides (P1, P3). If the product does not publish AssetSurface\n"},{"number":420,"text":"contracts, the design module names the equivalent typed contract and\n"},{"number":421,"text":"applies the same binding law to that contract. Absence of an admitted\n"},{"number":422,"text":"contract blocks product-truth-changing UX actions (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":423,"text":"\n"},{"number":424,"text":"A prompt for UI or operator-surface work must carry the governing UX law\n"},{"number":425,"text":"the task needs, acquired as\n"},{"number":426,"text":"[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)\n"},{"number":427,"text":"Acquisition states: a current derived surface or projected frame of this\n"},{"number":428,"text":"member where one serves the task, otherwise the deciding sections of this\n"},{"number":429,"text":"member carried in the prompt, rather than require the worker to rediscover\n"},{"number":430,"text":"it from the raw member. If a worker\n"},{"number":431,"text":"changes product truth through UI behaviour, the prompt must name the\n"},{"number":432,"text":"admitted carrier and action path. If the prompt cannot identify that\n"},{"number":433,"text":"carrier and action path, the correct result is a block or re-entry, not\n"},{"number":434,"text":"local UI invention (P6, P5; prompt construction is\n"},{"number":435,"text":"[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope)).\n"},{"number":436,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":457,"heading":"UX/8. Continuation and replay","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F8.%20Continuation%20and%20replay","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"2994e84b6eb56c5f6a9e8d335853608c7eafd0a8072c50b64ee0f6d77a8a077b","start_line":437,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":437,"text":"## 8. Continuation and replay\n"},{"number":438,"text":"\n"},{"number":439,"text":"In the graph-execution profile the runtime owns continuation (PROFILES\n"},{"number":440,"text":"§2) and the product is a cooperative bounded-step subsystem. The UX\n"},{"number":441,"text":"twin: the view does not own state continuation (P0, P6). State\n"},{"number":442,"text":"transitions flow through declared Msg actions interpreted by the reducer.\n"},{"number":443,"text":"A view does not:\n"},{"number":444,"text":"\n"},{"number":445,"text":"- decide on its own what the next state will be after a user event;\n"},{"number":446,"text":"- chain several state updates locally without emitting them as separate\n"},{"number":447,"text":"  Msg values;\n"},{"number":448,"text":"- carry hidden inter-event state in refs, closures or module-level\n"},{"number":449,"text":"  variables.\n"},{"number":450,"text":"\n"},{"number":451,"text":"If a view appears to need a multi-step local state machine, that machine\n"},{"number":452,"text":"belongs in the reducer as part of State, with explicit Msg transitions\n"},{"number":453,"text":"between phases; the view becomes a pure projection of which phase it is\n"},{"number":454,"text":"in (P1). The discipline test is the Msg-replay test: can the view's\n"},{"number":455,"text":"behaviour be replayed by replaying its Msg log against an empty State? If\n"},{"number":456,"text":"the answer is no, continuation has leaked into the view (P4b).\n"},{"number":457,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":499,"heading":"UX/8. Continuation and replay/Msg-replay proof","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F8.%20Continuation%20and%20replay%2FMsg-replay%20proof","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"bb0d20b2ffe3399f4cf7787afcaa5dfe6a710753fe3853370985ddc50b13504e","start_line":458,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":458,"text":"### Msg-replay proof\n"},{"number":459,"text":"\n"},{"number":460,"text":"Every product UX surface carries at least one executable Msg-replay proof\n"},{"number":461,"text":"for each product-meaningful interaction family before claiming closure\n"},{"number":462,"text":"under this profile (P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":463,"text":"Purpose and material relation: the Msg log is the surface's recorded work\n"},{"number":464,"text":"state, and replay is resumption from it\n"},{"number":465,"text":"([ACTIVATION §5 The workspace and an actor's account](ACTIVATION.md#the-workspace-and-an-actors-account)).\n"},{"number":466,"text":"A surface whose behaviour cannot be reproduced from its log holds state\n"},{"number":467,"text":"that no later actor or session can recover or check, so the proof is the\n"},{"number":468,"text":"evidence that the view owns no hidden continuation (P0, P4b). A\n"},{"number":469,"text":"replay proof includes:\n"},{"number":470,"text":"\n"},{"number":471,"text":"- an initial State fixture;\n"},{"number":472,"text":"- an ordered Msg log;\n"},{"number":473,"text":"- the expected final State;\n"},{"number":474,"text":"- the expected ordered Cmd values;\n"},{"number":475,"text":"- the typed outcome Msg values returned by interpreted Cmds, including\n"},{"number":476,"text":"  every materially possible unresolved outcome and its recovery messages;\n"},{"number":477,"text":"- injected deterministic values for time, randomness, generated ids and\n"},{"number":478,"text":"  external payloads.\n"},{"number":479,"text":"\n"},{"number":480,"text":"The proof fails if correctness depends on (P5, P4b):\n"},{"number":481,"text":"\n"},{"number":482,"text":"- DOM state not represented in State;\n"},{"number":483,"text":"- mutable refs, module variables, closures, timers or effect-handler\n"},{"number":484,"text":"  memory;\n"},{"number":485,"text":"- network or file results that bypass typed Msg;\n"},{"number":486,"text":"- view-local state that changes product behaviour after unmount or\n"},{"number":487,"text":"  replay.\n"},{"number":488,"text":"\n"},{"number":489,"text":"For an interaction whose external effect can be unresolved, the proof\n"},{"number":490,"text":"covers the correlated unresolved message, its retained State and the\n"},{"number":491,"text":"recovery path, including the prohibition on an outcome-dependent repeat\n"},{"number":492,"text":"before the required observation. Reproducing that State establishes the\n"},{"number":493,"text":"replay predicate only. It does not establish that the external effect\n"},{"number":494,"text":"completed; `replay_passes` can coexist with `completion_unknown` for the\n"},{"number":495,"text":"effect predicate (P5, P4b).\n"},{"number":496,"text":"\n"},{"number":497,"text":"For a pure projection-only surface, the replay proof may be a no-effect\n"},{"number":498,"text":"proof: a Msg log plus the final State and an empty Cmd sequence (P2).\n"},{"number":499,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":520,"heading":"UX/9. View shape","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F9.%20View%20shape","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"b8c3527ff2efbcc6116d53190a0b307cb73e55591abf9188105363f6328d02cf","start_line":500,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":500,"text":"## 9. View shape\n"},{"number":501,"text":"\n"},{"number":502,"text":"A view is a pure function from typed state to a view tree (P1). The view:\n"},{"number":503,"text":"\n"},{"number":504,"text":"- accepts typed input (state, props, context);\n"},{"number":505,"text":"- returns a typed view tree;\n"},{"number":506,"text":"- declares its consumed inputs explicitly;\n"},{"number":507,"text":"- does not capture mutable state in closures across renders;\n"},{"number":508,"text":"- does not read from sources outside its declared input.\n"},{"number":509,"text":"\n"},{"number":510,"text":"Whether the implementation expresses this as a function, a function\n"},{"number":511,"text":"component, a template, a server-rendered handler, a signal-derived\n"},{"number":512,"text":"expression or another framework-specific shape is a stack decision\n"},{"number":513,"text":"recorded in the design module. The constitutional rule is the function\n"},{"number":514,"text":"signature `State → ViewTree` and the absence of side effects in the body\n"},{"number":515,"text":"(P1, P0). A view that depends on out-of-render mutation, for example a\n"},{"number":516,"text":"ref written from inside an effect handler and read during render,\n"},{"number":517,"text":"violates §6 unless the mutation is part of the declared effect membrane,\n"},{"number":518,"text":"for example a platform handle for imperative interop already named in the\n"},{"number":519,"text":"design module (P6).\n"},{"number":520,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":545,"heading":"UX/10. Type sharing","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F10.%20Type%20sharing","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"ae8534aa740ea5ba0aa520320ac41081fc8c9ab62daec9ab431bffec895391ed","start_line":521,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":521,"text":"## 10. Type sharing\n"},{"number":522,"text":"\n"},{"number":523,"text":"UX-consumed types come from the shared front-end and back-end contract\n"},{"number":524,"text":"(P3, P1). A UX surface does not re-declare\n"},{"number":525,"text":"back-end record shapes; it imports them from the shared contract module,\n"},{"number":526,"text":"typically the same package or a dedicated `contracts/` package.\n"},{"number":527,"text":"\n"},{"number":528,"text":"Runtime validation is mandatory at every untrusted or out-of-process seam\n"},{"number":529,"text":"(P6; it makes DESIGN_MODULE §4's preference for parsing and admitting\n"},{"number":530,"text":"foreign data once at ingress an obligation at these seams):\n"},{"number":531,"text":"\n"},{"number":532,"text":"- HTTP or RPC responses;\n"},{"number":533,"text":"- MCP payloads;\n"},{"number":534,"text":"- file-loaded records;\n"},{"number":535,"text":"- websocket or event-stream messages;\n"},{"number":536,"text":"- agent or worker outputs;\n"},{"number":537,"text":"- URL, storage, clipboard or browser integration payloads.\n"},{"number":538,"text":"\n"},{"number":539,"text":"The project uses a typed-schema mechanism so that the same type\n"},{"number":540,"text":"definition is the source of both compile-time types and runtime\n"},{"number":541,"text":"validators; the mechanism choice is project-local. Compile-time\n"},{"number":542,"text":"TypeScript alone is not sufficient at these seams (P6, P1). UX-local types\n"},{"number":543,"text":"are allowed for view-local concerns: form input draft state, sort order\n"},{"number":544,"text":"enums, filter strings. UX-local types do not shadow back-end types (P3).\n"},{"number":545,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":567,"heading":"UX/11. Accessibility minimum","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F11.%20Accessibility%20minimum","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"aeebc29569666dbba1c9050b5b4743e9ea161201b600252f0076859c29c585aa","start_line":546,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":546,"text":"## 11. Accessibility minimum\n"},{"number":547,"text":"\n"},{"number":548,"text":"A UX surface that is the public face of a product capability declares\n"},{"number":549,"text":"(P2, P6):\n"},{"number":550,"text":"\n"},{"number":551,"text":"- semantic structure (heading levels, landmarks, lists, or\n"},{"number":552,"text":"  platform-equivalent affordances);\n"},{"number":553,"text":"- keyboard or platform-equivalent navigability for every action that has\n"},{"number":554,"text":"  a pointer interaction;\n"},{"number":555,"text":"- focus management on dynamic content changes;\n"},{"number":556,"text":"- accessibility annotations for any custom interactive element that lacks\n"},{"number":557,"text":"  a native semantic equivalent;\n"},{"number":558,"text":"- colour contrast at the project's declared accessibility standard (WCAG\n"},{"number":559,"text":"  AA is the recommended default for web).\n"},{"number":560,"text":"\n"},{"number":561,"text":"Accessibility is not optional for product capabilities. It is optional\n"},{"number":562,"text":"for internal-only debug surfaces, and the design module records the\n"},{"number":563,"text":"exemption (P2, P6). This section is intentionally minimal. Projects with\n"},{"number":564,"text":"stricter accessibility obligations (regulated industry, public-sector\n"},{"number":565,"text":"procurement) author a project-local accessibility refinement and cite it\n"},{"number":566,"text":"from their design modules (P2).\n"},{"number":567,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":591,"heading":"UX/12. Adoption","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F12.%20Adoption","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"7b081b4cd6cabd6ab7c17efe929906b51aaf1bc74c5c4883f6043083eec78772","start_line":568,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":568,"text":"## 12. Adoption\n"},{"number":569,"text":"\n"},{"number":570,"text":"Product authority adopts this profile for a project (§1 Authority), and\n"},{"number":571,"text":"the adoption is recorded by (P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":572,"text":"\n"},{"number":573,"text":"1. naming the profile in the project's UX-related design modules;\n"},{"number":574,"text":"2. recording the realisation stack choice (§4 Realisation discretion) and\n"},{"number":575,"text":"   the justification;\n"},{"number":576,"text":"3. declaring the irreducible architectural carrier set and the structural\n"},{"number":577,"text":"   carrier diagram the design profile requires (DESIGN_MODULE §6 and §7);\n"},{"number":578,"text":"4. declaring the State, Msg, Update, Cmd and Sub shapes for each UX\n"},{"number":579,"text":"   surface in the design module before implementation;\n"},{"number":580,"text":"5. declaring the AssetSurface or equivalent typed-contract bindings (§7)\n"},{"number":581,"text":"   the surface consumes and emits to;\n"},{"number":582,"text":"6. naming the effect-membrane mechanism (§6) and the Cmd algebra it\n"},{"number":583,"text":"   interprets;\n"},{"number":584,"text":"7. naming the executable Msg-replay proof surface required by §8;\n"},{"number":585,"text":"8. naming any §11 accessibility refinement the project requires;\n"},{"number":586,"text":"9. noting any §9 view-shape or §6 effect-membrane exemptions explicitly.\n"},{"number":587,"text":"\n"},{"number":588,"text":"Adoption is per project. A project may adopt this profile only for some\n"},{"number":589,"text":"UX surfaces, for example the production UI but not internal debug tools,\n"},{"number":590,"text":"with the scope recorded in the design module (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":591,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":619,"heading":"UX/12. Adoption/Scaffold and exemption","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F12.%20Adoption%2FScaffold%20and%20exemption","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"de036af1144bc2172ce202224c5a89a76bfa1bc0ed2010eaa3a70b0f7e7fadca","start_line":592,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":592,"text":"### Scaffold and exemption\n"},{"number":593,"text":"\n"},{"number":594,"text":"A UX surface is governed by this profile by default when any of these are\n"},{"number":595,"text":"true (P6, P5):\n"},{"number":596,"text":"\n"},{"number":597,"text":"- it is reachable from the product shell;\n"},{"number":598,"text":"- it is used as proof for a ticket, requirement, design module, release or\n"},{"number":599,"text":"  review;\n"},{"number":600,"text":"- it can mutate product truth;\n"},{"number":601,"text":"- it can spawn, attach, resume or dispatch work;\n"},{"number":602,"text":"- it can change Context, selection authority, closure, continuation,\n"},{"number":603,"text":"  evidence or provenance.\n"},{"number":604,"text":"\n"},{"number":605,"text":"A scaffold, prototype, debug pane or temporary proof surface may be\n"},{"number":606,"text":"exempt only when the design module or ticket records (P6, P4b):\n"},{"number":607,"text":"\n"},{"number":608,"text":"- the exemption scope;\n"},{"number":609,"text":"- the permitted operations;\n"},{"number":610,"text":"- whether mutation is forbidden or explicitly bounded;\n"},{"number":611,"text":"- a visible scaffold or debug label where user-facing;\n"},{"number":612,"text":"- the authoritative surface that will supersede it;\n"},{"number":613,"text":"- the retirement condition and owning ticket;\n"},{"number":614,"text":"- the non-closure condition preventing release if the scaffold remains.\n"},{"number":615,"text":"\n"},{"number":616,"text":"An exempt scaffold cannot become the production UX by accumulation. It is\n"},{"number":617,"text":"retired, repriced into a governed UX surface, or kept outside product\n"},{"number":618,"text":"closure (P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":619,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":684,"heading":"UX/12. Adoption/UX sprint compliance escrow","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F12.%20Adoption%2FUX%20sprint%20compliance%20escrow","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"fac4183c082300bb1e6e814d255c4f759e8048367dc2b38fb876cd39aabbf938","start_line":620,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":620,"text":"### UX sprint compliance escrow\n"},{"number":621,"text":"\n"},{"number":622,"text":"UX is the primary governed use case for sprint compliance escrow. This\n"},{"number":623,"text":"subsection is the profile's statement, which SPEC_METHOD §4 Sprint\n"},{"number":624,"text":"execution boundary admits, of when that escrow is an appropriate cost\n"},{"number":625,"text":"optimisation for UX; the generic escrow law and the close mechanics are\n"},{"number":626,"text":"TICKETS §3 Compliance escrow and Close review (P2, P6). A UX sprint may defer local UX\n"},{"number":627,"text":"compliance proof during a short iteration window when per-change proof\n"},{"number":628,"text":"cost is higher than expected correction cost. This is a cost-optimisation\n"},{"number":629,"text":"rule; it does not weaken the UX process model (P2).\n"},{"number":630,"text":"\n"},{"number":631,"text":"A UX sprint may escrow (P2, P4b):\n"},{"number":632,"text":"\n"},{"number":633,"text":"- screenshots or walkthrough capture;\n"},{"number":634,"text":"- visual review;\n"},{"number":635,"text":"- copy, spacing, density and layout cleanup;\n"},{"number":636,"text":"- accessibility review and remediation;\n"},{"number":637,"text":"- Msg-replay proof updates for product-meaningful interaction families;\n"},{"number":638,"text":"- design-module wording cleanup;\n"},{"number":639,"text":"- trace cleanup between changed UX states and governing authority.\n"},{"number":640,"text":"\n"},{"number":641,"text":"A UX sprint may not escrow (P6):\n"},{"number":642,"text":"\n"},{"number":643,"text":"- product-truth-changing Msg variants that lack an admitted carrier;\n"},{"number":644,"text":"- new or changed AssetSurface contracts or equivalent typed product\n"},{"number":645,"text":"  contracts;\n"},{"number":646,"text":"- new navigation, information architecture or selection authority that\n"},{"number":647,"text":"  changes product meaning;\n"},{"number":648,"text":"- runtime, governance, closure, continuation, lineage, provenance or\n"},{"number":649,"text":"  evidence semantics;\n"},{"number":650,"text":"- release criteria or method law.\n"},{"number":651,"text":"\n"},{"number":652,"text":"If one of those appears, the sprint records the finding and the work\n"},{"number":653,"text":"exits the UX sprint path through standalone repricing or sprint\n"},{"number":654,"text":"supersession. The UX layer still does not become the hidden constructive\n"},{"number":655,"text":"carrier (P6; §3).\n"},{"number":656,"text":"\n"},{"number":657,"text":"A UX sprint should close when continued iteration is more expensive or\n"},{"number":658,"text":"less trustworthy than review. Valid close triggers include (P2, P6):\n"},{"number":659,"text":"\n"},{"number":660,"text":"- the declared timebox ends;\n"},{"number":661,"text":"- accumulated changed states are too numerous for casual review;\n"},{"number":662,"text":"- screenshots or walkthrough evidence no longer explain the current\n"},{"number":663,"text":"  surface;\n"},{"number":664,"text":"- interaction behaviour changed beyond visual polish;\n"},{"number":665,"text":"- reviewer uncertainty makes more iteration unsafe without\n"},{"number":666,"text":"  reconciliation.\n"},{"number":667,"text":"\n"},{"number":668,"text":"UX sprint close is a forensic walkthrough: it reviews each changed\n"},{"number":669,"text":"screen, state and product-meaningful interaction against the cited\n"},{"number":670,"text":"authority (P6). Each finding takes one of the six classifications of\n"},{"number":671,"text":"TICKETS §3 Close review (`accepted`, `local_paydown`, `design_reframe`,\n"},{"number":672,"text":"`requirement_reprice`, `product_reprice`, `remove`); for a UX finding,\n"},{"number":673,"text":"`accepted` reads as compliant with this profile and the cited design,\n"},{"number":674,"text":"and `local_paydown` as local UX debt captured by a paydown ticket (P6,\n"},{"number":675,"text":"P5). The sprint may close with explicit local paydown tickets only where\n"},{"number":676,"text":"the debt is local to UX realisation and the governing method allows\n"},{"number":677,"text":"follow-up. It may not close while product-truth carrier gaps, hidden\n"},{"number":678,"text":"state continuation or authority drift remain unclassified (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":679,"text":"\n"},{"number":680,"text":"Closure under this profile for a product UX surface still requires the\n"},{"number":681,"text":"§8 Msg-replay proof and the §11 accessibility obligations unless an\n"},{"number":682,"text":"explicit exemption is recorded. The sprint can defer those obligations\n"},{"number":683,"text":"during iteration; it cannot erase them (P4b, P6).\n"},{"number":684,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":726,"heading":"UX/13. Failure patterns","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F13.%20Failure%20patterns","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"de908e8c4c1d2838e1f42c2558eb6460904143ba1d8cdd15c323b862eb976b09","start_line":685,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":685,"text":"## 13. Failure patterns\n"},{"number":686,"text":"\n"},{"number":687,"text":"A UX surface violates this profile when any of these are true (P6, P5):\n"},{"number":688,"text":"\n"},{"number":689,"text":"1. render code mutates state directly (assignments inside the render\n"},{"number":690,"text":"   body, mutating a prop or context value);\n"},{"number":691,"text":"2. view-local state cells carry product-meaningful state instead of\n"},{"number":692,"text":"   view-local ephemera;\n"},{"number":693,"text":"3. an effect handler contains conditional logic that decides state\n"},{"number":694,"text":"   transitions;\n"},{"number":695,"text":"4. multi-step state machines live in the view rather than in the reducer;\n"},{"number":696,"text":"5. mutable refs are read during render outside the declared effect\n"},{"number":697,"text":"   membrane;\n"},{"number":698,"text":"6. UX-local types shadow or re-declare back-end types instead of\n"},{"number":699,"text":"   importing from the shared contract;\n"},{"number":700,"text":"7. selection or action emission writes to file or network without going\n"},{"number":701,"text":"   through an AssetSurface action;\n"},{"number":702,"text":"8. view-shape exemptions (§9) are taken without a recorded design-module\n"},{"number":703,"text":"   entry;\n"},{"number":704,"text":"9. accessibility is omitted on a public product capability without a\n"},{"number":705,"text":"   recorded exemption;\n"},{"number":706,"text":"10. two-way binding emits no typed Msg action and the reducer is\n"},{"number":707,"text":"    bypassed;\n"},{"number":708,"text":"11. logic that should be a Cmd is implemented imperatively inside an\n"},{"number":709,"text":"    effect handler;\n"},{"number":710,"text":"12. the view's behaviour cannot be replayed by replaying its Msg log\n"},{"number":711,"text":"    against an empty State;\n"},{"number":712,"text":"13. a product-truth-changing UX message has no admitted carrier, graph\n"},{"number":713,"text":"    function, runtime command or typed product contract;\n"},{"number":714,"text":"14. external data crosses into UX state without runtime validation;\n"},{"number":715,"text":"15. a scaffold or debug surface is reachable, mutating or used as proof\n"},{"number":716,"text":"    without the exemption record of §12 Scaffold and exemption;\n"},{"number":717,"text":"16. a project-local ADR, component convention or existing code pattern is\n"},{"number":718,"text":"    used to weaken this profile;\n"},{"number":719,"text":"17. a UX sprint claims closure while deferred proof, accessibility,\n"},{"number":720,"text":"    carrier, scaffold or authority debt remains unclassified or\n"},{"number":721,"text":"    un-ticketed.\n"},{"number":722,"text":"\n"},{"number":723,"text":"Any of these is a violation of this profile. Repeated violations are not\n"},{"number":724,"text":"normalised by usage; they are repaired or the surface is repriced (P6,\n"},{"number":725,"text":"P4b).\n"},{"number":726,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":756,"heading":"UX/14. Review questions","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F14.%20Review%20questions","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"effbf37c633a966885c34a618f89f5c33fbe4b6e87b302dd1c86a9f9e76e8b23","start_line":727,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":727,"text":"## 14. Review questions\n"},{"number":728,"text":"\n"},{"number":729,"text":"A UX surface review under this profile should answer (P6, P2):\n"},{"number":730,"text":"\n"},{"number":731,"text":"1. What is the surface's State, Msg and Update?\n"},{"number":732,"text":"2. What is the surface's Cmd and Sub algebra?\n"},{"number":733,"text":"3. Which AssetSurface or equivalent typed contracts does it bind to?\n"},{"number":734,"text":"4. Which product-truth-changing messages map to admitted carriers?\n"},{"number":735,"text":"5. Where is the effect membrane, and what Cmd values does it interpret?\n"},{"number":736,"text":"6. Is `View = f(State)` provably pure for this surface?\n"},{"number":737,"text":"7. Can the surface's behaviour be replayed from a Msg log (the Msg-replay\n"},{"number":738,"text":"   proof of §8)?\n"},{"number":739,"text":"8. Are all UX-consumed types imported from the shared contract?\n"},{"number":740,"text":"9. Are all out-of-process payloads runtime-validated before entering UX\n"},{"number":741,"text":"   state?\n"},{"number":742,"text":"10. Are view-shape, effect-membrane, accessibility, scaffold or debug\n"},{"number":743,"text":"    exemptions documented?\n"},{"number":744,"text":"11. What realisation stack is chosen, and how does it preserve the §4 Elm\n"},{"number":745,"text":"    process model?\n"},{"number":746,"text":"12. Does the surface honour the §8 rule that the view does not own\n"},{"number":747,"text":"    continuation under user replay?\n"},{"number":748,"text":"13. Does the design module include the design profile's carrier set and\n"},{"number":749,"text":"    structural carrier diagram required for closure (DESIGN_MODULE §6 and\n"},{"number":750,"text":"    §7)?\n"},{"number":751,"text":"14. If the work used a UX sprint, did close review classify every deferred\n"},{"number":752,"text":"    proof, accessibility, carrier, scaffold and authority finding?\n"},{"number":753,"text":"\n"},{"number":754,"text":"If any of these cannot be answered, the design module is incomplete (P6,\n"},{"number":755,"text":"P5).\n"},{"number":756,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":826,"heading":"UX/15. Results of this profile","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md#UX%2F15.%20Results%20of%20this%20profile","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","sha256":"28aa4d683ed2170b49cbfc1395a71af2f3901f43806020a5c8df0dbfda9903c1","start_line":757,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/UX.md","lines":[{"number":757,"text":"## 15. Results of this profile\n"},{"number":758,"text":"\n"},{"number":759,"text":"This section owns this profile's refinements of the core result algebra\n"},{"number":760,"text":"of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Each refinement names\n"},{"number":761,"text":"the question it answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps\n"},{"number":762,"text":"each of its values to exactly one core value. The predicate travels with\n"},{"number":763,"text":"the value, so a `satisfied` for one predicate never counts toward another\n"},{"number":764,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),\n"},{"number":765,"text":"and no mapping raises a result's standing: nothing is coerced to\n"},{"number":766,"text":"`satisfied` (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: this profile's verdicts decide closure of a UX surface\n"},{"number":767,"text":"and enter conjunctions with the results of other members, which combine\n"},{"number":768,"text":"only in the core, so a review, a proof, a closure claim and a carrier\n"},{"number":769,"text":"check are each read for their own predicate and none is read as another\n"},{"number":770,"text":"(P5, P6).\n"},{"number":771,"text":"\n"},{"number":772,"text":"| Refinement | Question | Predicate of the mapping |\n"},{"number":773,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":774,"text":"| surface review | does the surface comply with this profile (§4 Realisation discretion, §13, §14) | the UX surface complies with this profile on the exact basis |\n"},{"number":775,"text":"| replay proof | does a Msg-replay proof hold (§8 Msg-replay proof) | the Msg-replay proof reproduces its expected final State and ordered Cmd values, and its correctness depends on nothing that §8 Msg-replay proof lists |\n"},{"number":776,"text":"| closure obligations | where closure of a product UX surface is claimed, are the obligations met that closure requires (§12 UX sprint compliance escrow) | each product-meaningful interaction family of the surface carries its Msg-replay proof and the surface carries its §11 declarations, unless a recorded exemption covers the obligation |\n"},{"number":777,"text":"| carrier admission | does each product-truth-changing message have an admitted carrier (§3, §7) | every product-truth-changing message or action of the surface maps to an admitted product carrier or typed product contract |\n"},{"number":778,"text":"\n"},{"number":779,"text":"| Refinement | Value | Core value | Ground |\n"},{"number":780,"text":"|---|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":781,"text":"| surface review | `compliant` | satisfied | §4 to §10 hold under inspection and no §13 failure pattern is present (§4 Realisation discretion), and every §14 review question is answered from the design module. The first part is the stricter of the two compliance tests of §4, which disagree: §4 Process model without stack mandate counts a realisation that preserves §4 to §8 as compliant. The tests differ in scope; this mapping applies the stricter under the fail-closed rule of §1 Authority and retains the ambiguity for the governing authority. The last part, every §14 review question answered from the design module, is in neither test: it is the basis condition that separates `compliant` from `design_module_incomplete` |\n"},{"number":782,"text":"| surface review | `violation` | falsified | the test of `compliant` fails: a §13 failure pattern is present, a realisation that §4 Process model without stack mandate rejects is used, or a rule of §4 to §10 does not hold under inspection; the pattern, realisation or rule is the counterexample |\n"},{"number":783,"text":"| surface review | `design_module_incomplete` | invalid_basis | no counterexample of `violation` is found, and a §14 review question cannot be answered from the design module, so the design module, on which the review rests, cannot support the evaluation; the value names the unanswered question |\n"},{"number":784,"text":"| replay proof | `replay_passes` | satisfied | the proof reproduces its expected final State and ordered Cmd values on its injected deterministic values, and no dependency that §8 lists decides its correctness; reproducing an unresolved outcome proves replay only and does not establish external completion |\n"},{"number":785,"text":"| replay proof | `replay_fails` | falsified | the proof diverges from its expected final State or Cmd values, or its correctness depends on something §8 lists; the divergence or the dependency is the counterexample |\n"},{"number":786,"text":"| closure obligations | `closure_obligations_met` | satisfied | every product-meaningful interaction family carries its Msg-replay proof and the surface its accessibility declarations, or a recorded exemption covers the obligation |\n"},{"number":787,"text":"| closure obligations | `closure_unproven` | falsified | an interaction family lacks its proof or the surface an accessibility declaration, with no recorded exemption; that family or obligation is the counterexample. Inside an open UX sprint closure is not claimed, and a deferred obligation is escrow under §12 |\n"},{"number":788,"text":"| carrier admission | `carrier_admitted` | satisfied | each product-truth-changing message or action maps to an admitted carrier of §3 and binds under §7 to an AssetSurface contract where the product publishes one, otherwise to the equivalent typed contract its design module names |\n"},{"number":789,"text":"| carrier admission | `carrier_missing` | falsified | a product-truth-changing message or action has no admitted carrier or typed contract (§13 pattern 13); that message or action is the counterexample |\n"},{"number":790,"text":"\n"},{"number":791,"text":"Where none of these values applies, the evaluation returns a core value\n"},{"number":792,"text":"directly under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results):\n"},{"number":793,"text":"`indeterminate` where the admissible evidence cannot decide its predicate,\n"},{"number":794,"text":"naming the evidence that would decide; `out_of_frame` where its claim\n"},{"number":795,"text":"needs a relation or capability that its frame does not declare; and\n"},{"number":796,"text":"`invalid_basis` where its subject or basis cannot support it on a ground\n"},{"number":797,"text":"other than `design_module_incomplete` (P5).\n"},{"number":798,"text":"\n"},{"number":799,"text":"Fail closed (§1 Authority). The\n"},{"number":35,"text":"graph-execution profile is [ODD](ODD.md), indexed in\n"},{"number":36,"text":"[PROFILES §2](PROFILES.md#2-graph-execution) (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":37,"text":"\n"},{"number":38,"text":"This profile's own terms are those of §6 Units (App, Builder Project,\n"},{"number":39,"text":"Published Domain Artifact, Fragment, World Model Object, Assurance,\n"},{"number":40,"text":"Attribute Ledger, Markov Object, Entity Cut, Markov-Object Overlay,\n"},{"number":41,"text":"Treatment Surface, Covariance Edge, Adjoint Mapping, Temporal Reference\n"},{"number":42,"text":"Artifact, Composed World Model, Projection, Query Plane), with effective\n"},{"number":43,"text":"blanket, identity direction, null peer, core and coat, representation\n"},{"number":44,"text":"space, epistemic overlay, semantic kernel, publication ledger, control\n"},{"number":45,"text":"plane and data plane. Position\n"},{"number":61,"text":"\n"},{"number":62,"text":"Most institutional systems preserve values and lose the semantic context\n"},{"number":63,"text":"needed to interpret them. World-model work builds a governed semantic\n"},{"number":64,"text":"layer over authoritative source systems, which enact bounded domain\n"},{"number":65,"text":"function through code paths, events, records, APIs, schedules,\n"},{"number":66,"text":"configurations, documents and downstream obligations (P1, P6). The profile starts from these claims:\n"},{"number":67,"text":"\n"},{"number":68,"text":"- source systems enact domain function and remain sovereign for\n"},{"number":69,"text":"  operational truth;\n"},{"number":70,"text":"- domains are defined by bounded function and authority;\n"},{"number":71,"text":"- records are intelligible only through function, provenance and\n"},{"number":72,"text":"  treatment context;\n"},{"number":73,"text":"- mappings are semantic treatments over governed meaning;\n"},{"number":74,"text":"- catalogs and schemas are explanatory projections over deeper semantic\n"},{"number":75,"text":"  structure;\n"},{"number":76,"text":"- the world model traces authoritative source surfaces, records accepted\n"},{"number":77,"text":"  semantic claims in ledgers, and publishes bounded semantic cuts;\n"},{"number":78,"text":"- the published semantic layer gives probabilistic systems a governed\n"},{"number":79,"text":"  substrate for reasoning and correspondence.\n"},{"number":80,"text":"\n"},{"number":81,"text":"The profile builds inspectable, versioned, machine-reasonable domain truth\n"},{"number":82,"text":"(P3, P6). §5 states each core claim in full.\n"},{"number":83,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":93,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/1. Query, traversal and serving over\n"},{"number":89,"text":"those artifacts are important delivery concerns, but they do not define\n"},{"number":90,"text":"the constitutional identity of this profile. Manifesto\n"},{"number":95,"text":"\n"},{"number":96,"text":"The manifesto states the commitments the profile holds itself to (P1, vocabularies;\n"},{"number":103,"text":"- treat data as evidence of function, never as meaning in isolation;\n"},{"number":104,"text":"- recover the objects, boundaries, states, transitions, domains;\n"},{"number":114,"text":"- use fully qualified naming to remove preventable aliasing before arguing\n"},{"number":115,"text":"  about deeper semantic grounded.\n"},{"number":129,"text":"\n"},{"number":130,"text":"If these claims do not hold, the work is not genuinely\n"},{"number":131,"text":"world-model-driven What a world model is\n"},{"number":301,"text":"\n"},{"number":302,"text":"A world model is a governed semantic layer built over existing source\n"},{"number":303,"text":"systems. It is descriptive before it is generative (P3, P6). Its primary semantic unit is the published\n"},{"number":304,"text":"entity cut (§6 Units). Generic references to a \"world-model object\" are\n"},{"number":305,"text":"shorthand for this unit unless the text explicitly names a looser\n"},{"number":306,"text":"candidate or intermediate surface. A world model should make explicit:\n"},{"number":307,"text":"\n"},{"number":308,"text":"- what objects are treated as real in a bounded context;\n"},{"number":309,"text":"- what boundaries make those objects coherent;\n"},{"number":310,"text":"- what state and transition surfaces matter;\n"},{"number":311,"text":"- what evidence supports those claims;\n"},{"number":312,"text":"- what value lists or classifications govern interpretation;\n"},{"number":313,"text":"- how adjacent domains reinterpret the objects;\n"},{"number":314,"text":"- what co-varies across those domains;\n"},{"number":315,"text":"- what is preserved, changed, aggregated, delayed or lost.\n"},{"number":316,"text":"\n"},{"number":317,"text":"A world model is not a replacement system of record; a central monolith\n"},{"number":318,"text":"that erases local semantics; a generic catalog entry; a copied data\n"},{"number":319,"text":"warehouse; or a schema registry pretending to be comprehension (P6).\n"},{"number":320,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":336,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/3. That layer consists of\n"},{"number":341,"text":"published domain artifacts; their bounded fragments and published entity\n"},{"number":342,"text":"cuts; explicit treatments, covariance edges, adjoint mappings and\n"},{"number":343,"text":"temporal reference artifacts; and composed world models built by\n"},{"number":344,"text":"reference from those published artifacts. Everything else is downstream\n"},{"number":345,"text":"or supporting: epistemic overlays, query planes, mapping reports and\n"},{"number":346,"text":"compiled deterministic execution artifacts. Those surfaces may be\n"},{"number":347,"text":"important; they do not create a second truth surface (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":348,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":365,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/3.
