Preferred hierarchy:\n"},{"number":353,"text":"\n"},{"number":354,"text":"1. realised system behaviour and emitted records or events;\n"},{"number":355,"text":"2. source code, rules and configuration when available;\n"},{"number":356,"text":"3. interfaces and schemas;\n"},{"number":357,"text":"4. large-scale observational data evidence;\n"},{"number":358,"text":"5. documentation, catalogs and operator testimony.\n"},{"number":359,"text":"\n"},{"number":360,"text":"Code is a high-fidelity explanatory surface when available. Realised\n"},{"number":361,"text":"behaviour remains the broader truth surface because some systems are\n"},{"number":362,"text":"proprietary, partially visible, or only intelligible through their\n"},{"number":363,"text":"outputs and effects. The profile therefore never depends on code\n"},{"number":364,"text":"availability as a prerequisite for comprehension (P6, P0).\n"},{"number":365,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":385,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F4.%20The%20Markov-object%20construct","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"1b5a6fd23722efc89a15ced997138b5ea30fdfd11af0e1b598e2f1e3e5c476dc","start_line":366,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":366,"text":"## 4. The Markov-object construct\n"},{"number":367,"text":"\n"},{"number":368,"text":"The profile treats \"Markov object\" as a load-bearing construct, not as\n"},{"number":369,"text":"borrowed vocabulary (P3, P1). A Markov object is\n"},{"number":370,"text":"a stable self-bounding pattern in a constraint structure whose internal\n"},{"number":371,"text":"state can be reasoned about through its effective blanket. The term is\n"},{"number":372,"text":"substrate-neutral: the same topology is expected wherever a constraint\n"},{"number":373,"text":"structure admits stable configurations, in biological systems, in the natural-language traces those systems emit, in\n"},{"number":374,"text":"learned representations built over those traces (LLMs), and in the\n"},{"number":375,"text":"engineered institutional systems descended from both. The working claim\n"},{"number":376,"text":"is that world-model construction is possible because this topology\n"},{"number":377,"text":"propagates across substrates: what domain experts recognise as \"objects\"\n"},{"number":378,"text":"in an institutional system is the same kind of stable constraint\n"},{"number":379,"text":"structure hypothesised for biological systems, re-expressed through\n"},{"number":380,"text":"another substrate. The profile is the practice of making that structure explicit,\n"},{"number":381,"text":"traceable and publishable (P3, P6). The generic law for boundary claims,\n"},{"number":382,"text":"their evidence and the limit on stronger Markov claims is\n"},{"number":383,"text":"[IDENTITY §2 Boundaries and sufficiency claims](IDENTITY.md#boundaries-and-sufficiency-claims);\n"},{"number":384,"text":"this section refines it for the Markov-object construct.\n"},{"number":385,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":414,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Effective blanket","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F4.%20The%20Markov-object%20construct%2FEffective%20blanket","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"a33377dd5e5aecf1593b8868b85790efbcc0c5dbb315c976e97645e6b4cad8c0","start_line":386,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":386,"text":"### Effective blanket\n"},{"number":387,"text":"\n"},{"number":388,"text":"The naive reading of \"blanket\" is set-theoretic: a fixed set of member\n"},{"number":389,"text":"states partitioning internal from external. That reading does not survive\n"},{"number":390,"text":"contact with real representations (P1, P3):\n"},{"number":391,"text":"\n"},{"number":392,"text":"- for any attribute basis over a domain (schema columns, SAE dictionary,\n"},{"number":393,"text":"  feature set, vocabulary), the set of attributes that \"fire\" for an\n"},{"number":394,"text":"  object is not a crisp partition, and overwriting attributes outside\n"},{"number":395,"text":"  that apparent set still leaks partial identity transfer;\n"},{"number":396,"text":"- the attributes that do fire have only partial alignment with the\n"},{"number":397,"text":"  object's identity; each alone is insufficient, and the basis distributes\n"},{"number":398,"text":"  object identity across many atoms.\n"},{"number":399,"text":"\n"},{"number":400,"text":"The load-bearing reading is geometric (P3):\n"},{"number":401,"text":"\n"},{"number":402,"text":"- the effective blanket is a low-rank projection in the representation\n"},{"number":403,"text":"  space along which object identity is preserved under treatment;\n"},{"number":404,"text":"- the attribute basis is evidence for that projection; the projection is\n"},{"number":405,"text":"  not a column-membership predicate;\n"},{"number":406,"text":"- a published Markov-object overlay is an identity direction together\n"},{"number":407,"text":"  with the distributed attribute evidence supporting it.\n"},{"number":408,"text":"\n"},{"number":409,"text":"This reading is a working hypothesis. Direction-level and behavioural\n"},{"number":410,"text":"evidence can support an overlay without establishing the formal\n"},{"number":411,"text":"conditional-independence condition for a Markov blanket. The construct\n"},{"number":412,"text":"remains candidate-class under the promotion gate in Epistemic status\n"},{"number":413,"text":"below (P6).\n"},{"number":414,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":451,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Four working refinements","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F4.%20The%20Markov-object%20construct%2FFour%20working%20refinements","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"46d7b2b61c78c5294a8a10ca83690c98872fe0b16038149f1d2b4953dd7462e2","start_line":415,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":415,"text":"### Four working refinements\n"},{"number":416,"text":"\n"},{"number":417,"text":"Four working refinements constrain how this profile treats Markov\n"},{"number":418,"text":"objects. They are adopted commitments of this profile at candidate\n"},{"number":419,"text":"standing, not formal closure of the construct. An application records\n"},{"number":420,"text":"its own evidence for the boundaries and overlays it publishes; no\n"},{"number":421,"text":"refinement replaces the promotion gate (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":422,"text":"\n"},{"number":423,"text":"1. Effective blanket is geometric, not set-theoretic. A boundary\n"},{"number":424,"text":"   stated as attribute-column membership leaks under bypass. The\n"},{"number":425,"text":"   load-bearing structure is the identity axis, and a set-valued boundary\n"},{"number":426,"text":"   over columns is an epistemic convenience rather than the object. The\n"},{"number":427,"text":"   Representation law (§8) is read this way: the test is whether identity\n"},{"number":428,"text":"   survives treatment, not which attributes are in the member set.\n"},{"number":429,"text":"2. Attribute schemas sense and fragment; they do not isolate. Any fixed\n"},{"number":430,"text":"   attribute basis partially aligns with a given object's identity and\n"},{"number":431,"text":"   partially distributes it. Where a Markov-object overlay is published,\n"},{"number":432,"text":"   it exposes the identity axis, not only the attribute profile. Schemas\n"},{"number":433,"text":"   are evidence, not ontology.\n"},{"number":434,"text":"3. Core identity, not core size, is the discriminator of objecthood. A sparse invariant with semantically loaded content is a\n"},{"number":435,"text":"   lawful object; a rich attribute cluster with nothing invariant under\n"},{"number":436,"text":"   context variation is not. More columns do not buy more objecthood.\n"},{"number":437,"text":"   This is why sparse first publication remains lawful under the\n"},{"number":438,"text":"   Saturation law (§11).\n"},{"number":439,"text":"4. Identity is a DC shift, not a principal-variance axis. Object\n"},{"number":440,"text":"   identity appears as a mean offset in representation space, not as the\n"},{"number":441,"text":"   dominant-variance direction. Characterisation by \"the biggest source of\n"},{"number":442,"text":"   variance in the attribute set\" systematically misses identity;\n"},{"number":443,"text":"   characterise by typical offset from a null peer instead. This is the\n"},{"number":444,"text":"   basis for excluding principal-component and maximum-variance\n"},{"number":445,"text":"   constructions as identity directions (§10).\n"},{"number":446,"text":"\n"},{"number":447,"text":"These refinements do not weaken the construct; they sharpen it into one\n"},{"number":448,"text":"that can be operationally validated and reproduced in published overlays.\n"},{"number":449,"text":"They constrain the construct and overlays built on it. They are not\n"},{"number":450,"text":"admissibility conditions for entity cuts, which §9 governs (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":451,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":484,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Epistemic status","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F4.%20The%20Markov-object%20construct%2FEpistemic%20status","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"6a8c4ef5ffc9d4f8dea50c7e1f529ce21ecaa731058e0158dbd2108e8f95ffcf","start_line":452,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":452,"text":"### Epistemic status\n"},{"number":453,"text":"\n"},{"number":454,"text":"The profile commits to the Markov-object construct as load-bearing\n"},{"number":455,"text":"working vocabulary at candidate status. Its geometric-blanket reading\n"},{"number":456,"text":"does not by itself establish the conditional-independence condition for\n"},{"number":457,"text":"a Markov object in the statistical sense;\n"},{"number":458,"text":"[FOUNDATIONS §5](FOUNDATIONS.md#5-hypotheses) carries that condition as a\n"},{"number":459,"text":"hypothesis. Adopting this profile does not require the hypothesis to be\n"},{"number":460,"text":"established. Claims that an overlay is the blanket rather than a\n"},{"number":461,"text":"candidate for it remain working commitments until the promotion gate is\n"},{"number":462,"text":"met for their exact subject and basis (P6, P5).\n"},{"number":463,"text":"\n"},{"number":464,"text":"Promotion gate. The experimental result that would promote the construct\n"},{"number":465,"text":"from candidate to established is a direction-native\n"},{"number":466,"text":"conditional-independence test: given the identity projection, residual\n"},{"number":467,"text":"variation along remaining components should be independent of the target\n"},{"number":468,"text":"under plausible treatments. Candidate standing persists without a\n"},{"number":469,"text":"result that meets this predicate on the claimed subject and basis. A\n"},{"number":470,"text":"failed run falsifies that run's predicate; it does not relocate the gate\n"},{"number":471,"text":"or by itself falsify the construct (P6).\n"},{"number":472,"text":"\n"},{"number":473,"text":"This status attaches to the construct and to overlays built on it. A\n"},{"number":474,"text":"published Markov-object overlay is a candidate-class overlay of a\n"},{"number":475,"text":"candidate construct, not a certified blanket of a formally established\n"},{"number":476,"text":"object. It does not attach to entity cuts: an entity cut is lawful\n"},{"number":477,"text":"published truth on its own admissibility test (§9) and does not inherit\n"},{"number":478,"text":"the construct's candidate status. A candidate entity that has not met\n"},{"number":479,"text":"that test is a candidate; a published entity cut is not (P3, P6). The\n"},{"number":480,"text":"status is inherited downstream: tooling that materialises Markov-object\n"},{"number":481,"text":"overlays under this profile should default to a candidate-class\n"},{"number":482,"text":"publication kind and reserve any formally closed publication kind for\n"},{"number":483,"text":"cuts backed by a real promotion-gate result (P6).\n"},{"number":484,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":507,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/4. The Markov-object construct/Relation to the design profile","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F4.%20The%20Markov-object%20construct%2FRelation%20to%20the%20design%20profile","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"99ec7d73ca4a1feab4e1918ea1cc646887699fcba2a753b1683002edda1f7720","start_line":485,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":485,"text":"### Relation to the design profile\n"},{"number":486,"text":"\n"},{"number":487,"text":"The Markov-object framing gives a theoretical account of a design\n"},{"number":488,"text":"pressure that also appears in DESIGN_MODULE, whose §8 Theoretical framing\n"},{"number":489,"text":"names the analogues from its side (P3, P2). If a Markov object is read as a\n"},{"number":490,"text":"candidate identity-bearing cut, good software boundary design should\n"},{"number":491,"text":"prefer:\n"},{"number":492,"text":"\n"},{"number":493,"text":"- the smallest lawful carrier set that preserves the boundary's real\n"},{"number":494,"text":"  authority;\n"},{"number":495,"text":"- subordinate payloads staying subordinate unless they carry independent\n"},{"number":496,"text":"  authority;\n"},{"number":497,"text":"- resistance to boundary inflation, where many sensed fragments are\n"},{"number":498,"text":"  promoted into peer objects without irreducible need;\n"},{"number":499,"text":"- strongly typed semantic boundaries, so identity-bearing cuts are not\n"},{"number":500,"text":"  left fuzzy, reconstructive or controller-owned.\n"},{"number":501,"text":"\n"},{"number":502,"text":"This profile does not make established Markov-object theory a\n"},{"number":503,"text":"prerequisite for all design work. The relation runs the other way: this\n"},{"number":504,"text":"profile gives one theoretical framing for why these boundary disciplines\n"},{"number":505,"text":"are sound, and DESIGN_MODULE gives the general engineering law that\n"},{"number":506,"text":"remains valid even outside world-model products (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":507,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":562,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/5. Core claims","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F5.%20Core%20claims","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"24bbfcf84b7202abb6dfe6c86a9b64b4c0c829406c3d4bfcaded726e15b04282","start_line":508,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":508,"text":"## 5. Core claims\n"},{"number":509,"text":"\n"},{"number":510,"text":"Source systems remain sovereign. Operational truth remains with the\n"},{"number":511,"text":"systems that enact it. The world model is a derived semantic layer over\n"},{"number":512,"text":"those systems, not a replacement operational source (P6).\n"},{"number":513,"text":"\n"},{"number":514,"text":"Domains are functional surfaces. A domain is defined by coherent\n"},{"number":515,"text":"function: what enters, what changes, what is owned, what is guaranteed,\n"},{"number":516,"text":"what leaves, and what adjacent domains can rely on (P3).\n"},{"number":517,"text":"\n"},{"number":518,"text":"Data is evidence, not meaning by itself. Data is a trace of constrained\n"},{"number":519,"text":"function execution; it is invalid in isolation from context (P1, P6).\n"},{"number":520,"text":"\n"},{"number":521,"text":"World models externalise expert cognition. The world model is the\n"},{"number":522,"text":"inspectable form of the domain understanding that experts already carry\n"},{"number":523,"text":"implicitly (P6).\n"},{"number":524,"text":"\n"},{"number":525,"text":"Mappings are semantic treatments. Cross-domain transformation is not\n"},{"number":526,"text":"plain structural rewrite. Every treatment declares preserved structure,\n"},{"number":527,"text":"changed meaning, loss, surplus and ambiguity (P1, P4b). A treatment is a refinement or\n"},{"number":528,"text":"rewrite step of\n"},{"number":529,"text":"[ACTIVATION §4 Refinement](ACTIVATION.md#refinement): what it preserves\n"},{"number":530,"text":"and its licensing law are that section's, and a treatment that changes\n"},{"number":531,"text":"meaning is an approximate step with its adequacy relation. The five\n"},{"number":532,"text":"declared fields are this profile's domain fields for that statement;\n"},{"number":533,"text":"preserved structure is what the step preserves, and changed meaning,\n"},{"number":534,"text":"loss, surplus and ambiguity state where and how it is not exact.\n"},{"number":535,"text":"\n"},{"number":536,"text":"Fully qualified naming is mandatory. Many cross-domain failures are\n"},{"number":537,"text":"preventable naming collisions. Fully qualified naming removes aliasing,\n"},{"number":538,"text":"so the remaining hard work is real semantic transformation; IDENTITY §2\n"},{"number":539,"text":"states the scoped identity it applies (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":540,"text":"\n"},{"number":541,"text":"Value lists are domain artifacts too. Changing code sets,\n"},{"number":542,"text":"classifications and value lists are governed temporal reference\n"},{"number":543,"text":"artifacts, not static enum decorations (P3).\n"},{"number":544,"text":"\n"},{"number":545,"text":"The world model sits above APIs and schemas. API contracts and schema\n"},{"number":546,"text":"contracts are projections over the world model. They are useful because\n"},{"number":547,"text":"they publish structure and function; they are not the highest semantic\n"},{"number":548,"text":"authority (P6, P1).\n"},{"number":549,"text":"\n"},{"number":550,"text":"Probability belongs in the epistemic overlay. The canonical published\n"},{"number":551,"text":"entity cut should remain semantic and bounded. Probability belongs in\n"},{"number":552,"text":"uncertainty, ranking, anomaly and alignment overlays, not in the\n"},{"number":553,"text":"ontological identity of the published object itself (P3, P6). That overlay may\n"},{"number":554,"text":"include correspondence candidates; confidence and ranking; ambiguity\n"},{"number":555,"text":"registers; anomaly and surprise signals; and candidate mappings or\n"},{"number":556,"text":"treatment suggestions. The overlay is useful because it lets\n"},{"number":557,"text":"probabilistic reasoning operate over a governed semantic substrate rather\n"},{"number":558,"text":"than over detached strings, schemas or raw tables. But the overlay is not\n"},{"number":559,"text":"the same thing as published semantic truth: accepted semantic treatments,\n"},{"number":560,"text":"published domain artifacts and compiled deterministic execution artifacts\n"},{"number":561,"text":"remain distinct from probabilistic overlays (P6, P0).\n"},{"number":562,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":615,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/6. Units","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F6.%20Units","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"5af2073a32a34828f5b0070e06dc9ef27fabbc16b4d5238ac739b19258cc6ada","start_line":563,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":563,"text":"## 6. Units\n"},{"number":564,"text":"\n"},{"number":565,"text":"The profile's units (P3):\n"},{"number":566,"text":"\n"},{"number":567,"text":"| Unit | Definition | Requires |\n"},{"number":568,"text":"|---|---|---|\n"},{"number":569,"text":"| App | a world-model builder application | P3 |\n"},{"number":570,"text":"| Builder Project | concept identity `urn:stdo:concept:world-model:builder-project`; a configured project instance of the builder with its own source inputs, settings and publication lane; its relation to Source Project is the directional specialisation of §2 Builder Project specialisation, and this clause is not read as an unchanged import or general equivalence | P3, P1 |\n"},{"number":571,"text":"| Published Domain Artifact | a published immutable world-model output built by a builder project | P3, P4b |\n"},{"number":572,"text":"| Fragment | a bounded published slice inside a published domain artifact | P3 |\n"},{"number":573,"text":"| World Model Object | a generic shorthand for something treated as real in the institutional operating model; intentionally weaker than Markov Object; useful during observation, extraction, review and discussion; not the preferred name for the primary published semantic unit once the builder has constructed a governed identity-bearing cut | P3, P1 |\n"},{"number":574,"text":"| Assurance | the governed basis on which a traced source observation is accepted as a qualified semantic claim; it answers why a claim is lawful world-model truth rather than merely a raw observation | P6 |\n"},{"number":575,"text":"| Attribute Ledger | an append-only ordered record of qualified attribute claims over a stable object identity; entries may carry observed values, derived values, interpreted meanings, rule or constraint claims, topology or relation claims, provenance and authority claims, and effective, observed and publication coordinates | P4b, P3 |\n"},{"number":576,"text":"| Markov Object | below | P3 |\n"},{"number":577,"text":"| Entity Cut | below | P3, P6 |\n"},{"number":578,"text":"| Markov-Object Overlay | an optional geometric overlay on an entity cut, admissible only where a declared representation space exists; it adds an identity direction, projection support and effective coordinate, constructed and verified under §10; the overlay strengthens an entity cut, and its absence does not weaken one | P3, P6 |\n"},{"number":579,"text":"| Treatment Surface | a semantic reinterpretation from one domain into another | P1 |\n"},{"number":580,"text":"| Covariance Edge | a declared relation showing how changes in one object correspond to changes in another | P1, P3 |\n"},{"number":581,"text":"| Adjoint Mapping | the interpret-back contract for a treatment | P1 |\n"},{"number":582,"text":"| Temporal Reference Artifact | a changing value list, code set or classification set whose semantics matter for object interpretation | P3, P1 |\n"},{"number":583,"text":"| Composed World Model | a higher-order world model built by referencing and stitching published domain artifacts while preserving their identity, version and local authority | P4a, P6 |\n"},{"number":584,"text":"| Projection | a user-facing or downstream-facing artifact derived from the semantic kernel | P1 |\n"},{"number":585,"text":"| Query Plane | an optional downstream serving surface that makes published domain artifacts or composed world models queryable or traversable without becoming the constitutional publication authority | P6 |\n"},{"number":586,"text":"\n"},{"number":587,"text":"Markov Object. A stable self-bounding world-model object whose internal\n"},{"number":588,"text":"state can be reasoned about through its effective blanket (§4). The\n"},{"number":589,"text":"published Markov object is an immutable object cut projected from the\n"},{"number":590,"text":"attribute ledger, not an in-place mutable record; the cut is an identity\n"},{"number":591,"text":"direction together with the distributed attribute evidence that supports\n"},{"number":592,"text":"it, not an enumeration of member columns (P3, P4b).\n"},{"number":593,"text":"The Markov object is the theoretical account of why a discovered boundary\n"},{"number":594,"text":"is a real object rather than an arbitrary cluster. It is not a claim that\n"},{"number":595,"text":"the builder invents the object: institutional entities are already\n"},{"number":596,"text":"committed by people, implicitly in code paths, records and workflows or\n"},{"number":597,"text":"explicitly in schemas and policy, and the profile's practical work is to\n"},{"number":598,"text":"trawl existing systems and recover them. A recovered entity is published\n"},{"number":599,"text":"as an Entity Cut; where the builder additionally operates over a\n"},{"number":600,"text":"representation space in which identity is a geometric direction, the\n"},{"number":601,"text":"entity cut may carry a Markov-object overlay. The theory is §4, the\n"},{"number":602,"text":"discovery obligations §9, and the representation-substrate obligations\n"},{"number":603,"text":"§10 (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":604,"text":"\n"},{"number":605,"text":"Entity Cut. The primary published semantic unit: an identity-bearing,\n"},{"number":606,"text":"bounded, evidence-backed cut of a recovered entity, projected from the\n"},{"number":607,"text":"attribute ledger (P3, P6). An entity cut is lawful\n"},{"number":608,"text":"without an identity direction. It publishes identity, boundary,\n"},{"number":609,"text":"authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity, each\n"},{"number":610,"text":"traced to ledger entries and their assurance basis. Builder projects may\n"},{"number":611,"text":"begin with looser object candidates; world-model publication converges\n"},{"number":612,"text":"them into entity cuts, or explicitly leaves them as non-object artifacts\n"},{"number":613,"text":"such as treatment surfaces, covariance edges or temporal reference\n"},{"number":614,"text":"artifacts (P3, P5).\n"},{"number":615,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":684,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/7. Flow","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F7.%20Flow","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"52406d778ff36f4becaa482429cc836349a2c8c8470e3e172a9e24d92f9163af","start_line":616,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":616,"text":"## 7. Flow\n"},{"number":617,"text":"\n"},{"number":618,"text":"The profile proceeds through these stages (P4b, P6):\n"},{"number":619,"text":"\n"},{"number":620,"text":"1. Observe. Gather source evidence from the strongest available surfaces\n"},{"number":621,"text":"   (§3 Evidence hierarchy): runtime behaviour; source records and events;\n"},{"number":622,"text":"   code and configuration when available; interfaces and schemas; docs and\n"},{"number":623,"text":"   metadata.\n"},{"number":624,"text":"2. Trace. Index and locate the source surfaces that may support semantic\n"},{"number":625,"text":"   claims. Tracing should make it possible to point from a later\n"},{"number":626,"text":"   world-model attribute claim back to the concrete source span, field,\n"},{"number":627,"text":"   locator, code path or record that supports it.\n"},{"number":628,"text":"3. Extract. Produce reviewable intermediate surfaces from traced source\n"},{"number":629,"text":"   objects: source inventories; object candidates; event and lifecycle\n"},{"number":630,"text":"   candidates; treatment candidates; authority candidates; ambiguity\n"},{"number":631,"text":"   registers. These are not the world model yet; they are the auditable\n"},{"number":632,"text":"   path toward it.\n"},{"number":633,"text":"4. Assure. Qualify traced observations into lawful world-model claims.\n"},{"number":634,"text":"   Assurance should make explicit what is being claimed; whether the\n"},{"number":635,"text":"   claim is observed, derived, interpreted or composed; which source\n"},{"number":636,"text":"   surfaces support it; which source is authoritative for which aspect of\n"},{"number":637,"text":"   the claim; and what ambiguity or missingness remains.\n"},{"number":638,"text":"5. Ledger. Write the accepted qualified claims into the attribute ledger.\n"},{"number":639,"text":"   The ledger is append-only: new understanding is recorded as new\n"},{"number":640,"text":"   qualified claims and later object cuts, not by mutating prior accepted\n"},{"number":641,"text":"   entries in place.\n"},{"number":642,"text":"6. Bound. Identify bounded contexts and the candidate entities that\n"},{"number":643,"text":"   actually cohere inside them. Reject schema-first modelling and\n"},{"number":644,"text":"   vocabulary-cluster modelling. Define local boundaries in terms of\n"},{"number":645,"text":"   function, authority, state and adjacency.\n"},{"number":646,"text":"7. Materialise. Project entity cuts from the attribute ledger with enough\n"},{"number":647,"text":"   semantic context for alignment and reasoning. Sparse first publication\n"},{"number":648,"text":"   is lawful if the object is bounded, distinguishable and evidence-backed\n"},{"number":649,"text":"   (§9 Admissibility).\n"},{"number":650,"text":"8. Relate. Add treatment surfaces, covariance edges, adjoint mappings and\n"},{"number":651,"text":"   temporal reference artifacts. This is where cross-domain meaning\n"},{"number":652,"text":"   becomes explicit.\n"},{"number":653,"text":"9. Publish. Publish immutable cuts of the published domain artifact; do\n"},{"number":654,"text":"   not mutate prior published truth in place. In the low-volume lane, Git\n"},{"number":655,"text":"   and the filesystem are sufficient as publication authority (§8\n"},{"number":656,"text":"   Publication law).\n"},{"number":657,"text":"10. Compose. Stitch published domain artifacts, their fragments and their\n"},{"number":658,"text":"    published entity cuts into higher-order world models without erasing\n"},{"number":659,"text":"    local authority. Composition is recursive, inspectable and bounded\n"},{"number":660,"text":"    (§11 Composition law).\n"},{"number":661,"text":"11. Align (optional). Use the semantic kernel as a tether for\n"},{"number":662,"text":"    probabilistic alignment across domains, entity cuts, artifacts and\n"},{"number":663,"text":"    projections. This stage may produce correspondence candidates,\n"},{"number":664,"text":"    confidence-ranked alignments, ambiguity overlays, mapping suggestions,\n"},{"number":665,"text":"    and anomaly or mismatch overlays. These outputs are epistemic\n"},{"number":666,"text":"    overlays, not yet published semantic truth.\n"},{"number":667,"text":"12. Project. Emit familiar outputs from the same semantic kernel: tables;\n"},{"number":668,"text":"    schema contracts; API contracts; event contracts; mapping documents;\n"},{"number":669,"text":"    transformation specifications; covariant transforms; tests and\n"},{"number":670,"text":"    application scaffolds where applicable.\n"},{"number":671,"text":"13. Compile (optional). Where delivery requires real execution, compile\n"},{"number":672,"text":"    accepted semantic understanding into deterministic executable\n"},{"number":673,"text":"    artifacts. Examples may include data-movement specifications,\n"},{"number":674,"text":"    transformation jobs, high-volume ETL or ELT plans, deterministic\n"},{"number":675,"text":"    mapping-tool records and generated implementation artifacts. The\n"},{"number":676,"text":"    important rule: probabilistic correspondence may help comprehension;\n"},{"number":677,"text":"    accepted semantic understanding governs compilation; execution at\n"},{"number":678,"text":"    scale should run through deterministic compiled artifacts rather than\n"},{"number":679,"text":"    through row-by-row probabilistic inference (P0, P6).\n"},{"number":680,"text":"14. Serve or query (optional). If delivery needs justify it, expose\n"},{"number":681,"text":"    traversal or query capability over published domain artifacts and\n"},{"number":682,"text":"    composed world models. This may remain filesystem-first in the\n"},{"number":683,"text":"    low-volume lane or later move behind a dedicated query plane.\n"},{"number":684,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":686,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/8. Representation and publication","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F8.%20Representation%20and%20publication","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"6dcb7a3c901cd72a300da31d1b892278b8907fce56e59a2824d641af1d75b405","start_line":685,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":685,"text":"## 8. Representation and publication\n"},{"number":686,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":703,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/8. Representation and publication/Representation law","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F8.%20Representation%20and%20publication%2FRepresentation%20law","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"f2818dd03c0cf65dee5eae4abfd36d26685f8dd47bf467839557c847ed6d7db7","start_line":687,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":687,"text":"### Representation law\n"},{"number":688,"text":"\n"},{"number":689,"text":"Every published entity cut is prompt-sufficient for reasoning (P3, P1). At minimum, the cut should make visible\n"},{"number":690,"text":"identity, boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and\n"},{"number":691,"text":"ambiguity. \"Make the effective blanket explicit\" means: state the\n"},{"number":692,"text":"boundary at which the entity's identity survives reinterpretation, not\n"},{"number":693,"text":"enumerate a set of member attribute columns. Attribute schemas are\n"},{"number":694,"text":"evidence for identity, not identity itself. The boundary is\n"},{"number":695,"text":"interventional, not structural: the test is \"does this identity survive\n"},{"number":696,"text":"treatment across its adjacent domains?\", never \"which attributes are in\n"},{"number":697,"text":"the member set?\" (P3). Where a declared representation space exists, that\n"},{"number":698,"text":"boundary takes its geometric form, the low-rank projection along which\n"},{"number":699,"text":"identity is preserved under treatment, and a Markov-object overlay should\n"},{"number":700,"text":"then expose both the distributed attribute evidence and the projection\n"},{"number":701,"text":"that recovers identity from it. Outside such a space the same law is\n"},{"number":702,"text":"discharged semantically under §9 (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":703,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":735,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/8. Representation and publication/Materialisation law","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F8.%20Representation%20and%20publication%2FMaterialisation%20law","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"3e97567a5fbea32298ecbb0b3d377337a8ec73dcb67c3c76b0f9bcd46cb4f15d","start_line":704,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":704,"text":"### Materialisation law\n"},{"number":705,"text":"\n"},{"number":706,"text":"The materialised entity cut is an artifact of the world-model builder,\n"},{"number":707,"text":"not a raw artifact of the source system (P6). The governing split: source systems remain\n"},{"number":708,"text":"sovereign for operational truth (§5); the builder observes and\n"},{"number":709,"text":"comprehends that truth; the published entity cut is the canonical\n"},{"number":710,"text":"object-level truth of the world-model layer; projections are derived from\n"},{"number":711,"text":"that semantic artifact. This is why published domain artifacts should be\n"},{"number":712,"text":"versioned and superseded explicitly: the versioned cut is the builder's\n"},{"number":713,"text":"governed understanding of reality, not a claim that the source system\n"},{"number":714,"text":"emitted the object directly (P6, P4b). More specifically:\n"},{"number":715,"text":"\n"},{"number":716,"text":"`source -> tracing -> assurance -> attribute ledger -> entity cut`\n"},{"number":717,"text":"\n"},{"number":718,"text":"The entity cut is the immutable projection, not the mutable source of\n"},{"number":719,"text":"truth. \"Projection\" is literal: the cut selects one bounded identity and\n"},{"number":720,"text":"boundary over the distributed evidence in the ledger, accompanied by that\n"},{"number":721,"text":"evidence and the basis on which it was accepted; §9 states the\n"},{"number":722,"text":"obligation, and §10 applies where the selection is expressed\n"},{"number":723,"text":"geometrically in a declared representation space (P3). The attribute\n"},{"number":724,"text":"ledger is the accepted semantic record over which the entity cut is\n"},{"number":725,"text":"projected. A single ledger state can support many different cuts at\n"},{"number":726,"text":"different identities, boundaries and context scopes; the cut records\n"},{"number":727,"text":"which selection was taken, not that the ledger is the cut (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":728,"text":"\n"},{"number":729,"text":"Every accepted object attribute should therefore be recoverable through\n"},{"number":730,"text":"the object cut that contains it; the attribute-ledger entries that\n"},{"number":731,"text":"justify it; the assurance basis that accepted those entries; and the\n"},{"number":732,"text":"traced source surfaces that support the assurance. No object attribute\n"},{"number":733,"text":"should exist without ledger support; no ledger entry should exist without\n"},{"number":734,"text":"assurance; no assurance should exist without traceable source (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":735,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":750,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/8. Representation and publication/Publication law","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F8.%20Representation%20and%20publication%2FPublication%20law","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"16b10e14fb25e550dd2e7c884e7952cbe7c180df3a55c22a5fc5c63ad1fc8bbe","start_line":736,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":736,"text":"### Publication law\n"},{"number":737,"text":"\n"},{"number":738,"text":"Published world-model truth should be immutable per cut; reviewable by\n"},{"number":739,"text":"diff; traceable to evidence; and superseded by explicit later cuts rather\n"},{"number":740,"text":"than silently overwritten (P4b, P3). The\n"},{"number":741,"text":"filesystem and Git are sufficient for the publication plane in the\n"},{"number":742,"text":"initial lane. A database, if introduced later, is a query-plane\n"},{"number":743,"text":"complement rather than the constitutional publication authority. In other\n"},{"number":744,"text":"words: Git is the publication ledger; a database is the query plane\n"},{"number":745,"text":"(P6). This publication ledger is distinct from the attribute ledger: the\n"},{"number":746,"text":"attribute ledger records qualified semantic claims over object identity,\n"},{"number":747,"text":"and the publication ledger records immutable published cuts of domain\n"},{"number":748,"text":"artifacts and object projections. Both should remain append-only and\n"},{"number":749,"text":"replayable (P4b).\n"},{"number":750,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":763,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/8. Representation and publication/Attribute ledger law","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F8.%20Representation%20and%20publication%2FAttribute%20ledger%20law","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"e1f22a9dc7532b44ee89fea0aeac059b4421a4f05d6977e6d28c78b13984fc64","start_line":751,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":751,"text":"### Attribute ledger law\n"},{"number":752,"text":"\n"},{"number":753,"text":"The attribute ledger is the immediate semantic source of an entity cut\n"},{"number":754,"text":"(P4b, P6). Every entry should be a fully\n"},{"number":755,"text":"qualified claim, potentially including a value or measured quantity; a\n"},{"number":756,"text":"rule or constraint; a classification; a topology or relation claim;\n"},{"number":757,"text":"provenance and authority information; and effective, observed and\n"},{"number":758,"text":"publication coordinates. The ledger may be supported by one or more\n"},{"number":759,"text":"evidence surfaces, including documents for declared semantics or policy,\n"},{"number":760,"text":"code for derivation logic or invariants, and data for observed state or\n"},{"number":761,"text":"emitted values. The profile does not assume one source per attribute; it\n"},{"number":762,"text":"assumes one lawful claim record per accepted attribute fact (P6, P3).\n"},{"number":763,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":770,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/9. Entity cut construction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F9.%20Entity%20cut%20construction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"0fc9cff78dcbdf7d3a6966b0aab93b11465505ce55addbe960894833b25dc0f6","start_line":764,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":764,"text":"## 9. Entity cut construction\n"},{"number":765,"text":"\n"},{"number":766,"text":"Entities are recovered, not invented. A builder project constructs an\n"},{"number":767,"text":"entity cut by trawling authoritative source surfaces for the boundaries\n"},{"number":768,"text":"the operating model already commits to, then qualifying them into\n"},{"number":769,"text":"published truth (P3, P6).\n"},{"number":770,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":792,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/9. Entity cut construction/Admissibility","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F9.%20Entity%20cut%20construction%2FAdmissibility","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"52b8e6a97b94c63f99b3a706be880e85fe7ad0d10a1a6069edf5d7916547eb44","start_line":771,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":771,"text":"### Admissibility\n"},{"number":772,"text":"\n"},{"number":773,"text":"An entity cut is admissible when its identity, boundary, authority,\n"},{"number":774,"text":"state, evidence, treatment, covariance and ambiguity are explicit,\n"},{"number":775,"text":"traceable, and discriminated from plausible alternatives at evidence\n"},{"number":776,"text":"altitude proportional to the claim (P3, P6). That is\n"},{"number":777,"text":"the whole constitutional test. It binds what is true of a published cut;\n"},{"number":778,"text":"it does not prescribe how a builder establishes it (P0).\n"},{"number":779,"text":"\n"},{"number":780,"text":"\"Explicit\" admits three lawful values on every surface: a stated value,\n"},{"number":781,"text":"stated absence, or stated non-applicability with its reason. A cut whose\n"},{"number":782,"text":"entity has no adjacent-domain treatment says so; it does not manufacture\n"},{"number":783,"text":"one. This keeps the predicate whole without adding evidence machinery\n"},{"number":784,"text":"(P5).\n"},{"number":785,"text":"\n"},{"number":786,"text":"Sparse first publication remains lawful. A unique, historical,\n"},{"number":787,"text":"single-context, inaccessible or regulated entity is publishable when the\n"},{"number":788,"text":"test above holds and its residual ambiguity is declared. Absence of a\n"},{"number":789,"text":"comparison population, of repeated contexts, or of permission to\n"},{"number":790,"text":"intervene is a bound on evidence altitude to be stated, not a bar to\n"},{"number":791,"text":"publication (P5, P2).\n"},{"number":792,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":822,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/9. Entity cut construction/Discrimination","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F9.%20Entity%20cut%20construction%2FDiscrimination","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"6696b8751768b7db51ca514060ef3f796f2e788e75ee8db89eb32891b4b9ec8c","start_line":793,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":793,"text":"### Discrimination\n"},{"number":794,"text":"\n"},{"number":795,"text":"\"Discriminated from plausible alternatives\" means the cut states why\n"},{"number":796,"text":"this boundary rather than a nearby one the operating model would treat\n"},{"number":797,"text":"differently. The claim carries its own discrimination; a stronger claim\n"},{"number":798,"text":"needs stronger discrimination (P3, P6). Techniques\n"},{"number":799,"text":"that serve this, none of them mandatory and none of them exhaustive:\n"},{"number":800,"text":"\n"},{"number":801,"text":"- cross-context invariance: separate what holds wherever the entity\n"},{"number":802,"text":"  appears from what a particular context adds, where multiple contexts\n"},{"number":803,"text":"  exist;\n"},{"number":804,"text":"- null-peer comparison: name a structurally similar entity the operating\n"},{"number":805,"text":"  model treats differently, and state what separates them;\n"},{"number":806,"text":"- adjoint round-trip: interpret the entity through an adjacent domain's\n"},{"number":807,"text":"  treatment surface and back through its adjoint mapping, and show the\n"},{"number":808,"text":"  identity claim survives;\n"},{"number":809,"text":"- transplant: show what a neighbouring entity would have to acquire to be\n"},{"number":810,"text":"  treated as this one;\n"},{"number":811,"text":"- coat stripping: vary or remove contextual claims and show identity\n"},{"number":812,"text":"  survives; vary an identity claim and show it does not.\n"},{"number":813,"text":"\n"},{"number":814,"text":"The adjoint round-trip performs, at semantic altitude, the discrimination\n"},{"number":815,"text":"the geometric boundary test performs in a representation space. Where a\n"},{"number":816,"text":"builder can intervene, interventional evidence discriminates more\n"},{"number":817,"text":"strongly than declarative evidence, and a cut should say which kind it\n"},{"number":818,"text":"rests on (P6). Boundary is interventional in character, not structural.\n"},{"number":819,"text":"A cut that states its boundary only as a set of source fields has made a\n"},{"number":820,"text":"weaker claim than one that states the reinterpretations under which\n"},{"number":821,"text":"identity survives, and should be read as such (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":822,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":834,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/9. Entity cut construction/Publishing a cut","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F9.%20Entity%20cut%20construction%2FPublishing%20a%20cut","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"ed9b03e22d45968ce38742112d92a1a586cd017e15b61a2e43f6e9c8fe821b85","start_line":823,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":823,"text":"### Publishing a cut\n"},{"number":824,"text":"\n"},{"number":825,"text":"A published entity cut makes the eight admissibility surfaces (identity,\n"},{"number":826,"text":"boundary, authority, state, evidence, treatment, covariance and\n"},{"number":827,"text":"ambiguity) visible and traceable, each as a stated value, stated absence\n"},{"number":828,"text":"or stated non-applicability, and records the basis on which identity was\n"},{"number":829,"text":"discriminated (P3, P6). Cuts are immutable: revising\n"},{"number":830,"text":"identity or boundary produces a new cut that supersedes the prior one\n"},{"number":831,"text":"(P4b). Concrete carriers, layouts, schemas and storage topology are\n"},{"number":832,"text":"consumer realisation; this profile requires that the published surfaces\n"},{"number":833,"text":"survive and does not select the form they are stored in (P0, P2).\n"},{"number":834,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":848,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"4d6ba837243296c6259bb5b1c40fcc5fb2d0a76d82ced73402380dc98bee9b05","start_line":835,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":835,"text":"## 10. Markov-object overlay construction\n"},{"number":836,"text":"\n"},{"number":837,"text":"This law is the representation-substrate specialisation of §9. It\n"},{"number":838,"text":"applies only where the builder operates over a declared representation\n"},{"number":839,"text":"space in which identity is a geometric direction (a learned\n"},{"number":840,"text":"representation, an embedding over ledger claims, or an equivalent metric\n"},{"number":841,"text":"space); it is not required for ordinary institutional recovery (P3, P2). Where it applies, a builder\n"},{"number":842,"text":"project constructs the overlay by a directional, interventional\n"},{"number":843,"text":"procedure. The steps below are both how the overlay is built and the\n"},{"number":844,"text":"minimum structure that is stored when it is published. The declared\n"},{"number":845,"text":"representation space is part of the overlay: an identity direction is\n"},{"number":846,"text":"uninterpretable without the space it lives in, and directions computed in\n"},{"number":847,"text":"different spaces do not compose (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":848,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":863,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Paired evidence collection","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FPaired%20evidence%20collection","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"24e34dfe4d0990c30f18cb4676b52e1967f7bc92d888fb5d29a06bf2bd15f1aa","start_line":849,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":849,"text":"### Paired evidence collection\n"},{"number":850,"text":"\n"},{"number":851,"text":"For a candidate object, assemble attribute-ledger evidence across context\n"},{"number":852,"text":"variation together with evidence for at least one null peer (P3, P6):\n"},{"number":853,"text":"\n"},{"number":854,"text":"- multiple contexts in which the candidate is instantiated;\n"},{"number":855,"text":"- a null-peer instance: a structurally similar thing that lacks the\n"},{"number":856,"text":"  candidate's identity content, observed in the same contexts;\n"},{"number":857,"text":"- paired ledger entries covering `(candidate, context)` and\n"},{"number":858,"text":"  `(null, context)`, so identity-carrying signal can be separated from\n"},{"number":859,"text":"  context-carrying signal.\n"},{"number":860,"text":"\n"},{"number":861,"text":"The paired evidence is the raw material of the cut. The ledger entries\n"},{"number":862,"text":"remain distributed; they are not the object (P3).\n"},{"number":863,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":879,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Identity-direction extraction","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FIdentity-direction%20extraction","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"cf76867f6b8b563bdafd4dde2f641d77ea42417150460f97253dcc7c19ae68a0","start_line":864,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":864,"text":"### Identity-direction extraction\n"},{"number":865,"text":"\n"},{"number":866,"text":"Derive the identity axis as a low-rank projection over the paired\n"},{"number":867,"text":"evidence (P3, P1). The canonical\n"},{"number":868,"text":"form is the mean offset\n"},{"number":869,"text":"\n"},{"number":870,"text":"`d(object) = μ(evidence_object) − μ(evidence_null)`\n"},{"number":871,"text":"\n"},{"number":872,"text":"taken across contexts. Supervised variants (linear discriminant,\n"},{"number":873,"text":"logistic-regression normal, difference-in-conditional-means) are\n"},{"number":874,"text":"admissible when they target mean offset rather than within-class\n"},{"number":875,"text":"variance. Principal-component and maximum-variance constructions are not\n"},{"number":876,"text":"admissible as identity directions: they capture within-pair variation,\n"},{"number":877,"text":"not the identity offset. The identity direction is not an attribute\n"},{"number":878,"text":"column; it is a geometric combination over columns (P3).\n"},{"number":879,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":901,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Verification by treatment","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FVerification%20by%20treatment","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"b3a2603a3ffd0046f876ae1a48039207c4011520eeb9fac576a189d151076609","start_line":880,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":880,"text":"### Verification by treatment\n"},{"number":881,"text":"\n"},{"number":882,"text":"A candidate identity direction is accepted only if projection along it\n"},{"number":883,"text":"preserves object identity under held-out treatments. The builder records\n"},{"number":884,"text":"at least one acceptable verification (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":885,"text":"\n"},{"number":886,"text":"- α-sweep: apply `x − α · d` on held-out contexts, and show the expected\n"},{"number":887,"text":"  identity shift and its saturation behaviour;\n"},{"number":888,"text":"- transplant: apply `x + α · d` to null-peer instances, and show identity\n"},{"number":889,"text":"  acquisition;\n"},{"number":890,"text":"- boundary test: overwrite attributes outside the projection support and\n"},{"number":891,"text":"  show identity survives (this is what discriminates a geometric blanket\n"},{"number":892,"text":"  from a set-membership blanket).\n"},{"number":893,"text":"\n"},{"number":894,"text":"A direction that has no acceptable verification is a candidate, not an\n"},{"number":895,"text":"accepted overlay. Publishing an unverified direction violates the\n"},{"number":896,"text":"Representation law (§8). The underlying entity cut remains lawful and\n"},{"number":897,"text":"publishable without the overlay (P6, P3). Passing this battery establishes\n"},{"number":898,"text":"that a direction is verified for\n"},{"number":899,"text":"publication under this profile; it does not establish a formally closed\n"},{"number":900,"text":"Markov blanket (§4 Epistemic status) (P6).\n"},{"number":901,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":911,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Core and coat decomposition","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FCore%20and%20coat%20decomposition","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"2f26f23f44c508b2aca31e32058ffb887362ab9c4ecde02102a902a14b0e8f10","start_line":902,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":902,"text":"### Core and coat decomposition\n"},{"number":903,"text":"\n"},{"number":904,"text":"For candidates that appear in multiple contexts, decompose the attribute\n"},{"number":905,"text":"evidence into an invariant core, the attributes whose contribution to the\n"},{"number":906,"text":"identity direction is stable across ≥ N of N contexts, and a context\n"},{"number":907,"text":"coat, the attributes selected by the specific context, carrying\n"},{"number":908,"text":"contextual reinterpretation rather than identity per se (P3). Both are evidence. The core carries\n"},{"number":909,"text":"identity; the coat carries treatment. The coat to core ratio is a\n"},{"number":910,"text":"characterisation, not a quality metric (P3, P1).\n"},{"number":911,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":927,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Null-peer discrimination","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FNull-peer%20discrimination","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"d8947f0de6e8de910b4f18f9a01264c1a259449e115ebc2622e8f73da70c6282","start_line":912,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":912,"text":"### Null-peer discrimination\n"},{"number":913,"text":"\n"},{"number":914,"text":"Before publication, discriminate an accepted Markov object from an\n"},{"number":915,"text":"incidental attribute cluster by null-peer comparison (P3, P6):\n"},{"number":916,"text":"\n"},{"number":917,"text":"- is the candidate's core size in a range that null peers also hit? Yes\n"},{"number":918,"text":"  is expected and acceptable; size is not diagnostic;\n"},{"number":919,"text":"- are the identity-loaded attributes in the core unique to the candidate\n"},{"number":920,"text":"  among its null peers? They should be;\n"},{"number":921,"text":"- does the candidate's identity direction transfer more cleanly than a\n"},{"number":922,"text":"  random diagonal in the representation? It should.\n"},{"number":923,"text":"\n"},{"number":924,"text":"Failure on the uniqueness and transfer tests means the cluster is not yet\n"},{"number":925,"text":"a lawful Markov object, even if its invariants are internally consistent\n"},{"number":926,"text":"(P3, P5).\n"},{"number":927,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":952,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Overlay publication","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FOverlay%20publication","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"9fff324b5c5f2ef60a51e0b57bda31420d852b280f48af7bbfd7a75e4d6d2538","start_line":928,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":928,"text":"### Overlay publication\n"},{"number":929,"text":"\n"},{"number":930,"text":"A published Markov-object overlay makes visible, at minimum (P6, P3):\n"},{"number":931,"text":"\n"},{"number":932,"text":"- representation space: the declared space and attribute basis the\n"},{"number":933,"text":"  direction is expressed in, versioned so a later re-fit is detectable;\n"},{"number":934,"text":"- identity direction: the projection (a representation-space vector or\n"},{"number":935,"text":"  equivalent geometric description);\n"},{"number":936,"text":"- attribute evidence: core and coat, traced to ledger entries;\n"},{"number":937,"text":"- verification record: treatments used, outcomes observed, held-out\n"},{"number":938,"text":"  contexts evaluated;\n"},{"number":939,"text":"- boundary characterisation: the projection support on which identity was\n"},{"number":940,"text":"  preserved under treatment;\n"},{"number":941,"text":"- null-peer comparison: what similar things were tested, what was\n"},{"number":942,"text":"  accepted, what was rejected;\n"},{"number":943,"text":"- effective coordinate: α along the direction for this instance, where\n"},{"number":944,"text":"  applicable.\n"},{"number":945,"text":"\n"},{"number":946,"text":"An overlay is an immutable projection. Revising the identity direction,\n"},{"number":947,"text":"because new contexts, new evidence or a re-fitted representation space\n"},{"number":948,"text":"became available, produces a new overlay that supersedes the prior one.\n"},{"number":949,"text":"A change of representation space changes every direction expressed in it\n"},{"number":950,"text":"and is therefore a supersession even when no ledger entry changed. Prior\n"},{"number":951,"text":"overlays are never mutated in place (§8 Publication law) (P4b, P3).\n"},{"number":952,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":970,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/10. Markov-object overlay construction/Storage shape","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F10.%20Markov-object%20overlay%20construction%2FStorage%20shape","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"2f12954d0aa47b7fcfdff21ce103848ac1e5b11c76aba674a5e3111501690c2a","start_line":953,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":953,"text":"### Storage shape\n"},{"number":954,"text":"\n"},{"number":955,"text":"The stored overlay is not a row in a table and not a membership list. It\n"},{"number":956,"text":"is a package attached to its entity cut (P4b, P6):\n"},{"number":957,"text":"\n"},{"number":958,"text":"- the declared representation space and its version;\n"},{"number":959,"text":"- the geometric object (identity direction and projection support);\n"},{"number":960,"text":"- the distributed evidence (pointers into the attribute ledger);\n"},{"number":961,"text":"- the verification trace (treatments, contexts, outcomes);\n"},{"number":962,"text":"- the provenance and authority record (who accepted, on what assurance\n"},{"number":963,"text":"  basis);\n"},{"number":964,"text":"- the supersession record (which overlay this replaces, if any).\n"},{"number":965,"text":"\n"},{"number":966,"text":"A storage layout that loses any of these surfaces is not a lawful\n"},{"number":967,"text":"Markov-object storage layout. Query planes and projection surfaces\n"},{"number":968,"text":"derived from stored cuts are downstream conveniences and do not\n"},{"number":969,"text":"substitute for this storage shape (P6, P4b).\n"},{"number":970,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":972,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/11. Saturation, composition and projection","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F11.%20Saturation%2C%20composition%20and%20projection","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"77bf5bed8c7d50c7b05aee48d4a47e3e9bbc5096741a345b886b3bb974d20e8f","start_line":971,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":971,"text":"## 11. Saturation, composition and projection/Saturation law","id":"urn:a-c:project:8ae07eeca101a93be143e873f9d12ab43e316ef0359058c0c9fa71380880d2d5/source/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md#WORLD_MODEL%2F11.%20Saturation%2C%20composition%20and%20projection%2FSaturation%20law","path":"build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","sha256":"efad94037be3fcaf8ee0b70ab12996087f06e33c1ef90c9a74bc917ce90b296c","start_line":973,"source_file":"/Users/jim/src/apps/specification_methodology/stdo_representation/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/run-coherent-003/generation/corpus/build_tenants/a_c/representation/stdo-v3.0.5/source/standards/WORLD_MODEL.md","lines":[{"number":973,"text":"### Saturation law\n"},{"number":974,"text":"\n"},{"number":975,"text":"World-model construction is iterative. Builder projects may work a\n"},{"number":976,"text":"bounded source-object set repeatedly until the resulting attribute ledger\n"},{"number":977,"text":"is judged sufficiently saturated for publication (P2, P5). Sufficient saturation means: materially important\n"},{"number":978,"text":"attributes have traceable support; remaining gaps are explicit\n"},{"number":979,"text":"ambiguities rather than silent misses; and the resulting object cut is\n"},{"number":980,"text":"stable enough to publish and supersede later if needed. Sparse first\n"},{"number":981,"text":"publication remains lawful (§9 Admissibility); silent unsupported\n"},{"number":982,"text":"attribute creation does not (P5, P6).\n"},{"number":983,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":995,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/11. Build local published domain\n"},{"number":987,"text":"artifacts and their entity cuts, then stitch them (P4a, P6). Composition preserves fragment authority,\n"},{"number":988,"text":"bounded-context meaning, treatment semantics, declared loss and\n"},{"number":989,"text":"ambiguity. Higher-order models are composed from published domain\n"},{"number":990,"text":"artifacts; they do not erase them (P4a, P4b). The preferred end state is\n"},{"number":991,"text":"a federated world-model mesh rather than a single flattened enterprise\n"},{"number":992,"text":"model. Detailed mesh topology may remain product-local while the line is\n"},{"number":993,"text":"still being developed; profile-level mesh law should be ratified only\n"},{"number":994,"text":"once the reusable node and edge model is stable (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":995,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1010,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/11. All\n"},{"number":1000,"text":"projections should remain traceable back to governing objects; evidence;\n"},{"number":1001,"text":"treatments; covariance edges; adjoint mappings; and temporal reference\n"},{"number":1002,"text":"artifacts where applicable. Tables, schemas, APIs, mapping documents and\n"},{"number":1003,"text":"covariant transforms are all publication forms over the same semantic\n"},{"number":1004,"text":"kernel (P1). Because an API usually carries more business semantics than\n"},{"number":1005,"text":"a bare schema, the preferred structural order is\n"},{"number":1006,"text":"`world model -> API contract -> schema contract`. Query and traversal are\n"},{"number":1007,"text":"also downstream-facing conveniences in this sense: they may be a\n"},{"number":1008,"text":"first-class delivery pillar without becoming the constitutional core of\n"},{"number":1009,"text":"this profile (P6, P2).\n"},{"number":1010,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1012,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/12. The semantic\n"},{"number":1017,"text":"control plane consists of published domain artifacts; composed world\n"},{"number":1018,"text":"models; treatments, covariance edges and adjoint mappings; and epistemic\n"},{"number":1019,"text":"overlays for correspondence, ranking and ambiguity. The high-volume data\n"},{"number":1020,"text":"plane consists of deterministic executable artifacts compiled from\n"},{"number":1021,"text":"accepted semantic understanding. That means: world-model artifacts carry\n"},{"number":1022,"text":"semantic truth; epistemic overlays carry probabilistic correspondence and\n"},{"number":1023,"text":"uncertainty; compiled execution artifacts carry deterministic runtime\n"},{"number":1024,"text":"behaviour. This is a plane split, not a truth split; the semantic truth\n"},{"number":1025,"text":"surface remains the published world-model layer (§3 Single truth\n"},{"number":1026,"text":"surface) (P6).\n"},{"number":1027,"text":"\n"},{"number":1028,"text":"LLMs and other probabilistic systems belong primarily on the semantic\n"},{"number":1029,"text":"control plane. They should help with comprehension, candidate alignment,\n"},{"number":1030,"text":"ambiguity reduction and correspondence ranking. They should not be the\n"},{"number":1031,"text":"row-by-row execution engine for large-scale data movement when the\n"},{"number":1032,"text":"semantic understanding has already been accepted and can be compiled\n"},{"number":1033,"text":"(P0, P2).\n"},{"number":1034,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1055,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/12. Preferred wedge:\n"},{"number":1039,"text":"\n"},{"number":1040,"text":"1. comprehend one bounded source slice;\n"},{"number":1041,"text":"2. publish one fragment;\n"},{"number":1042,"text":"3. stitch one adjacent fragment;\n"},{"number":1043,"text":"4. answer one painful question the incumbent pipeline cannot answer\n"},{"number":1044,"text":"   cleanly;\n"},{"number":1045,"text":"5. emit both conventional and covariant outputs side by side.\n"},{"number":1046,"text":"\n"},{"number":1047,"text":"This is incremental semantic capture, not a demand for immediate central\n"},{"number":1048,"text":"convergence. The proof obligation is practical: build the world model\n"},{"number":1049,"text":"once, then show that the same semantic substrate can emit the legacy\n"},{"number":1050,"text":"artifacts the organisation expects and the richer covariant outputs the\n"},{"number":1051,"text":"profile makes possible. Where the line is mature enough, the proof should\n"},{"number":1052,"text":"also show that accepted semantic understanding can be compiled into\n"},{"number":1053,"text":"deterministic executable pipelines without losing the traceability and\n"},{"number":1054,"text":"challengeability of the governing world model (P2, P6).\n"},{"number":1055,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1073,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/12. A sufficiently well-formed world model can therefore project\n"},{"number":1061,"text":"large parts of an application surface without requiring duplicated\n"},{"number":1062,"text":"semantic re-authoring downstream (P2, P1). Preferred relationship:\n"},{"number":1063,"text":"\n"},{"number":1064,"text":"`world model -> epistemic correspondence overlay -> deterministic compiled artifacts -> implementation`\n"},{"number":1065,"text":"\n"},{"number":1066,"text":"For simpler lines the shorter compression still holds:\n"},{"number":1067,"text":"`world model -> application projections -> implementation`. Use\n"},{"number":1068,"text":"normative application specs where the problem is primarily user\n"},{"number":1069,"text":"interaction, workflow choice, non-domain behaviour, or operational policy\n"},{"number":1070,"text":"beyond the domain semantics themselves. Use the world model as the\n"},{"number":1071,"text":"semantic substrate wherever the software is mainly an interface over\n"},{"number":1072,"text":"stable domain reality (P2, P1).\n"},{"number":1073,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1075,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/13. The result is:\n"},{"number":1079,"text":"\n"},{"number":1080,"text":"- published domain artifacts as the durable semantic publication units;\n"},{"number":1081,"text":"- composed world models built from those published artifacts;\n"},{"number":1082,"text":"- published entity cuts as the primary semantic units;\n"},{"number":1083,"text":"- inspectable Markov-object overlays where a representation space is\n"},{"number":1084,"text":"  selected;\n"},{"number":1085,"text":"- explicit treatment and covariance semantics;\n"},{"number":1086,"text":"- epistemic correspondence overlays grounded in the same semantic\n"},{"number":1087,"text":"  substrate;\n"},{"number":1088,"text":"- temporal reference artifacts for changing domain enumerations;\n"},{"number":1089,"text":"- familiar projections emitted from the same semantic substrate;\n"},{"number":1090,"text":"- deterministic compiled execution artifacts where the line must move\n"},{"number":1091,"text":"  real volume safely;\n"},{"number":1092,"text":"- a basis for AI reasoning over real institutional meaning.\n"},{"number":1093,"text":"\n"}]},{"end_line":1108,"heading":"WORLD_MODEL/13. Results of this profile\n"},{"number":1110,"text":"\n"},{"number":1111,"text":"This section owns this profile's refinements of the core result algebra\n"},{"number":1112,"text":"of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). Each refinement names\n"},{"number":1113,"text":"the question it answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps\n"},{"number":1114,"text":"each of its values to exactly one core value. The predicate travels with\n"},{"number":1115,"text":"the value, so a `satisfied` for one predicate never counts toward another\n"},{"number":1116,"text":"([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)),\n"},{"number":1117,"text":"and no mapping raises a result's standing: nothing is coerced to\n"},{"number":1118,"text":"`satisfied` (P5, P6). other\n"},{"number":1120,"text":"members, which combine only in the core, so an inadmissible cut, an\n"},{"number":1121,"text":"unverified direction or a failed gate run is never read as
